The key insight is that existing 4-bit quantizers preserve generated actions but degrade the predicted future through which errors propagate; LAQ introduces a reader metric measuring how faithfully the predicted future is written, stored, and read. This improves deployment fidelity for onboard robot inference.

entry.title: One Schedule Does Not Fit All: Adaptive Inference Schedules for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Rabimba Karanjai, Linsey Pang, Hemanth Hegadehalli Madhavarao, Richard Williamson, Uma Kona, Prakhar Mehrotra

entry.summary: The paper shows that the cheapest quality-preserving denoising schedule for diffusion language models depends on task, model, and sampler, and proposes TCDA, a deployment rule that uses one-sided bootstrap bounds to certify which candidate schedules meet utility and guardrail criteria with an explicit error guarantee. It then deploys the cheapest certified candidate, including options like early prefix decoding and state-reusing continuation.

entry.title: SAM 3 Sees More Than It Detects: Promptable Concept Maps Beyond Categories

author.name: Yu-Huan Wu, Yun Liu, Liangli Zhen

entry.summary: The paper introduces promptable concept maps (PCM), extending SAM 3's promptable concept segmentation from noun instances to dense maps of concepts named by short noun phrases such as transparent objects, and presents PCM-Bench grouping test sets of seven dense prediction tasks. Analysis shows SAM 3's semantic path responds to many concepts that its detection output blocks via a low image-level presence score.

entry.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild

author.name: Sean Tang, Peiran Wang, Ying Li, Esha Shivakumar, Tao Meng, Yuan Tian

entry.summary: GEOHunter measures a paid generative-engine-optimization operation across three major Chinese UGC platforms, uncovering 1,985 accounts and 466,357 inferred promotional placements designed to game AI-generated answers and rankings. The study documents coordinated cross-category promotion campaigns, highlighting risks in medical and financial domains where misleading AI-surfaced advice can cause harm. It provides the first large-scale empirical map of GEO manipulation in the wild.

entry.title: Cross-Question Reliable Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hector G. Rodriguez, Marcus Rohrbach

entry.summary: The paper critiques per-question confidence post-training of LLMs, noting that individually reinforced confidence scores do not yield useful selective prediction when users have risk tolerances, and proposes cross-question reliable RL that optimizes confidence for selection across question sets. This aligns confidence training with its actual downstream use in abstention and deferral to humans or stronger models.

entry.title: Gradient Boosting with Kolmogorov-Arnold Units for Interpretable Regression beyond Pairwise Interactions

author.name: Minjong Cheon, Hanseon Joo, Eunji Lee

entry.summary: Introduces MJBoost, a gradient boosting method using single Kolmogorov-Arnold units with penalized splines as weak learners, allowing fully plottable additive models that capture three-way and higher interactions beyond the EBM's pairwise restriction. Units are fitted in closed form and handle categorical and missing inputs directly.

entry.title: Identity World Model: Recognizing People in an Imagined Latent World

author.name: Dingqiang Ye, Kartik Narayan, Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: IDWorld reframes whole-body person recognition as a counterfactual prediction problem: instead of learning to ignore transient cues like clothing and pose, the model imagines how a person would be represented under changed conditions such as a fixed view or bare silhouette, predicting these counterfactual features in a single forward pass. This aims to make recognition robust to real-world appearance variation.

entry.title: LoopedWAM: Looped World Action Models for Elastic Inference

author.name: Anh Dao, Xinxin Liu, Hang Yu, Jeffrey A Chan Santiago, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: Presents a compact world action model for robotics that recurrently applies a shared six-block core, executing 30 transformer layers while storing only 12 blocks per expert, with video and action experts at different depths reflecting their asymmetric costs. An elastic self-distillation scheme trains a single checkpoint that operates across action-depth and sampling-step budgets, at only 0.58B policy parameters. This targets practical deployment of generative video-plus-action models on robots.

entry.title: SEEC: A Large-Scale Dataset and Benchmark for Self-Supervised External-Eye Representation Learning

author.name: George R. Nahass, Michelle Fleishaker, Sanjay Ganesh, Sasha Hubschman, R. V. Paul Chan, Chad A. Purnell, Pete Setabutr, Ann Q. Tran, Sathya N. Ravi

entry.summary: SEEC provides a 4.35-million-image standardized external-eye corpus built from fourteen public face datasets, plus a benchmark for self-supervised periocular representation learning. Evaluation spans embedding geometry, anatomical probe sets, and clinical disease classification including ptosis, thyroid eye disease, and craniofacial syndromes.

entry.title: Trajectory-Calibrated Merging of Embodied Policies

author.name: Wenshuo Chen, Honglei Jin, Le Yang, Jianfei Song, Shaofeng Liang, Lei Wang, Junze Zhu, Kailong Wang, Zhengxi Jin, Haozhe Jia, Honglin Chu, Songning Lai, Xiucheng Wang, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: Trajectory-Calibrated Regression is an execution-aware, gradient-free framework for merging multiple robot task specialists into a single policy. It collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts and intermediate states at two timescales so that merged behavior is preserved during closed-loop execution, addressing the failure of parameter-space merging proxies to guarantee behavior at uncalibrated states. This tackles capability fragmentation in robot foundation models.

entry.title: Learning Ankle Exoskeleton Control for Reactive Standing Balance Through Neuromusculoskeletal Simulation

author.name: Maria T. Tagliaferri, Inseung Kang

entry.summary: The authors propose a sim-to-real framework combining motion imitation and reinforcement learning in a muscle-driven neuromusculoskeletal model to develop balance-assistive ankle exoskeleton controllers. This avoids the need for repeated destabilizing perturbation trials on human subjects, addressing fall-risk reduction for older adults and people with neuromuscular impairments.

entry.title: Beyond the Sink Interpretation: Radial Attention in Flow-Based VLA Policies

author.name: Yuxi Zheng, Yueqian Lin, Yudong Liu, Zijia Tang, Junyu Pan, Yiheng Wang, Hai Helen Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: This paper tests whether the so-called radial action sink in flow-based VLA policies matches the language-model attention-sink profile, analyzing one pi0.5 checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. It finds the first and last action tokens do not fit the sink profile: rotary positional encoding, not sink behavior, produces their modest attention excess, challenging prior horizon-setting heuristics based on that interpretation.

entry.title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization

author.name: BoHao Chen

entry.summary: This work studies domain specialization of LLM agents by evolving the agent harness (system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, planning scaffolding) with the policy frozen, casting harness evolution as an RL-style outer loop using GEPA. Harness adapters require no GPU training, load per domain, and show consistent gains with a Claude Code-style agent on SWE-bench Verified, OfficeBench, and Terminal-Bench.

entry.title: DMT-Attack: Diffusion-Prior Texture Search for Closed-Loop Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Jun Xia, Shangwen Wang, Jun Ma, Ruichao Ren, Zhouyang Jia, Xin Zhao, Huijun Liu, Jie Yu

entry.summary: DMT-Attack is a gradient-free gray-box attack on vision-language-action policies that generates natural-looking disruptive textures on ordinary scene objects by searching the structured distribution of a frozen text-conditioned diffusion model, using closed-loop feedback and an eight-expert selection mechanism. Unlike optimized adversarial patterns, these textures blend into surroundings, making them stealthy and persistent. This exposes a robustness gap in VLA manipulation policies.

entry.title: HabitusMem: Belief Memory over Evolving User Preferences for LLM Agents

author.name: Yifan Lu, Gaoyang Guo, Wen Chen, Ziyun Zou, Jian Wu, Han Zhu, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: HabitusMem reframes agent memory as the assistant's evolving belief about the user, modeled as a latent preference state that each interaction both reveals and updates, drawing on Bourdieu's notion of habitus. This contrasts with conventional content-storage memory systems, which often lead agents to act on outdated or misapplied preferences.

entry.title: Validation-driven Deployment of LLM Inference Platforms for Agentic Workloads

author.name: Shai Gretz, Alon Halfon, Yoav Katz, Lena Dankin, Michal Jacovi, Rachel Tzoref-Brill, Kfir Toledo, Elron Bandel, Natan Ergas, Michal Malka, Pravein Govindan Kannan, Maroon Ayoub, Michal Shmueli-Scheuer

entry.summary: An IBM team presents an end-to-end validation pipeline for enterprises deploying agentic workloads on their own open-weight model infrastructure, spanning small-scale testing through sizing and pre-production to production. Key results show trace replay reproduces per-session load far better than live re-runs (1.18x versus 4.98x at the 95th percentile of input tokens), enabling repeatable load testing.

entry.title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement

author.name: Yinhao Tang, Youqing Fang, Yanan Sun, Xintian Shen, Hanyu Sun, Wenran Liu, Yue Wu, Weiming Zhang, Bin Liu, Wenwei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces AdaObs, an observation-side mechanism for recursive self-improvement loops that keeps the anchor benchmark objective fixed while adaptively refining the observation: at plateaus a controller increases diagnostic granularity, escalates difficulty, and adds new signals. This addresses the problem that stalled progress may reflect exhausted observations rather than exhausted capability.

entry.title: DVBench: End-to-End Benchmark for Real-World UVM Design Verification Agents

author.name: Jiaru Qian, Jiawei Li, Xiaolong Hu, Zheng Shen, LiMing Zhao, Xin Zhang, Siyuan Jiang, Yongqiang Wei, Dong Liu, Jianyang Li, Yihua Chen, Yangxu Liao, Yuxin Wu, Jing Liang, Bin Wen, Junjie Zhang, Yongsheng Han, Yihong Dong, Ge Li

entry.summary: Introduces DVBench, the first end-to-end benchmark for LLM-based agents performing UVM hardware design verification, comprising 95 tasks across 9 functional domains and 5 difficulty levels. Unlike prior benchmarks of decoupled subtasks, agents must complete the full verification workflow independently. Targets the labor-intensive design-verification bottleneck in hardware development.

entry.title: Dune: A Zeroth-Order Optimizer with Time-Conditioned Historical Error Regression for VLA Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Chengyang Dong, Ze Chen, Kai Ye, Chutian Wang, Heng Xu, Wei Mo, Maomao Li, Jiayan Xu, Jiayuan Wu, Yihao Xiao, Linhua Ye, Zhonghua Peng, Ruize Han, Jialong Sun

entry.summary: Dune enables memory-efficient test-time adaptation of vision-language-action models on resource-constrained robots using zeroth-order optimization, stabilizing long-horizon adaptation by coupling online historical error prediction with current perturbation observations. It targets the known failure where ZO methods gain quickly but stall or degrade due to noisy gradient estimates, while backprop-based adaptation is too memory-heavy for robot deployment. This addresses practical distribution shift handling during deployment.

entry.title: Raptor: Rejection-aware Adaptive Tree based on Speculative Decoding

author.name: Qishu Hu, Haozhao Wang, Zicong Hong, Yufeng Zhan, Yuanqing Xia

entry.summary: Raptor is a training-free framework that uses rejection feedback from speculative decoding to jointly regulate candidate coverage and drafting effort in tree-based speculative decoding for vision-language models. Its key insight is that acceptance length alone cannot distinguish insufficient coverage from excessive deep expansion, and the two require different allocation decisions.

entry.title: Erasing the Wrong Thing: Conditional Attribute Leakage and Concept Erasure in Shared Foundation-Model Embeddings

author.name: Haijun He, Fei Li, Donghong Ji, Junjun He

entry.summary: Focusing on shared medical-image embeddings, the paper proves an impossibility result: when task and sensitive labels are associated, global and task-conditional linear guardedness cannot both hold while preserving a nonzero linear task signal, so global concept erasure must either destroy task utility or retain conditional leakage. It also derives a closed-form prediction of erasure's utility cost for linear readers.

entry.title: Fast-JEPA: Advancing the Success-Latency Frontier for Latent World Models

author.name: Yao Zhang, Bin Yu, Shijie Lian, Haishan Liu, Changti Wu, Yu Wu, Kai Chen

entry.summary: Fast-JEPA is a latent world model planning framework that predicts outcomes of complete candidate action sequences directly instead of recursively rolling out states during refinement. It uses a goal-directed plan to guide search, achieving 96.5% average success with 2.41x faster planning than INTACT across four control environments.

entry.title: The Stability Gap in Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sebastian Pusch, Matthia Sabatelli, Gido M. van de Ven

entry.summary: This work introduces a simple continual RL benchmark varying observation representations while holding environment dynamics and rewards fixed, and demonstrates the stability gap in CRL: a substantial drop in prior-task performance after new tasks arrive, followed by partial or complete recovery, even with full access to old data. Final aggregate metrics can hide this temporary degradation.

entry.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)

author.name: Mengxiao Wang, Mahbub Alam, Kalyan Nakka, Nitesh Saxena

entry.summary: ROGUE-AI is a multi-agent framework that reproduces real-world reported LLM agent incidents (such as the Replit coding agent deleting a production database) offline together with matched controls, to validate incidents and test root-cause hypotheses. Existing incident catalogs and benchmarks only record or report failures without replication or causal investigation. This brings scientific rigor to a space currently dominated by unverified media narratives.

entry.title: Learning to Read Events for Exact State Tracking with Frozen Language Models

author.name: Jeonghoon Lee (Attractor Dynamics Inc.)

entry.summary: This work trains a selector on a frozen language model, with API-only access, to read event transitions which an external integer register composes in order for exact state tracking, with confidence rules for flagging uncertain updates. The task is proven hard for fixed-depth transformers under standard complexity conjectures, and a frozen 0.8B model with a trained selector dramatically outperforms much larger models without intermediate reasoning.

entry.title: A Sparse Low-Rank Biclique Decomposition for Graphs

author.name: Antoine Vialle, Sergei Gerasimov, Aref Einizade, Antonio Ortega, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros, Jhony H. Giraldo

entry.summary: Proposes signed biclique decomposition (SBD), a sparse low-rank decomposition for integer-weighted graphs using sums of sparse signed binary rank-one factors plus a sparse residual, preserving discreteness, interpretability, and graph combinatorial properties. Includes fixed-rank and greedy objectives with algorithmic guarantees.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Self-supervised Vision Backbones Survives Distribution Shift in Radar Micro-Doppler HAR

author.name: Keryan Chelouche (ETIS UMR 8051, CY Cergy Paris Universit\'e, ENSEA, CNRS, Cergy, France, Fondation L\'eonie Chaptal, Sarcelles, France), Petr Dobias (ETIS UMR 8051, CY Cergy Paris Universit\'e, ENSEA, CNRS, Cergy, France), Nistor Grozavu (ETIS UMR 8051, CY Cergy Paris Universit\'e, ENSEA, CNRS, Cergy, France), Olivier Romain (ETIS UMR 8051, CY Cergy Paris Universit\'e, ENSEA, CNRS, Cergy, France)

entry.summary: Compares full fine-tuning, frozen probing, and PEFT for human activity recognition from radar micro-Doppler signatures, finding only PEFT avoids both negative cross-dataset transfer and under-adaptation. Applies DINOv3 with PiSSA adaptation, reportedly the first use of a self-supervised image foundation backbone in this domain, and ranks first among PEFT methods.

entry.title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift

author.name: Ziyao Mou, Andrea Wynn, Eric Nalisnick

entry.summary: The paper proposes Expert-Drift-Adapted Learning-to-Defer (EDA-L2D), which extends the learning-to-defer framework to model temporal fluctuations in human expert reliability caused by fatigue and cognitive biases. The deferral head is conditioned on expert state over time, addressing a realistic gap in prior work that assumes fixed expert performance across radiology, aviation, judicial, and annotation settings.

entry.title: From Self-Play RL to Constrained Control: Distilling DiffMPC Students with DAgger

author.name: Luca M. Hartmann, Parinaz Naghizadeh

entry.summary: The paper adds explicit safety constraints to self-play RL driving policies by replacing a PPO teacher's action head with differentiable model predictive control that enforces road boundary and collision constraints, then distilling the student via DAgger in the teacher's simulator. The constrained student of a smaller teacher matches its teacher on nuPlan and outperforms it on CARLA and out-of-distribution Waymo scenes.

entry.title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery

author.name: Ryotaro Okabe, Shoki Kishida, Abhijatmedhi Chotrattanapituk, Dominic Bollettieri, Takuya Isogawa, Yongqiang Cheng, Mingda Li, Masaki Adachi

entry.summary: This paper reframes reward misalignment as a discovery tool in generative materials design: systematic disagreements between expert judgment and a numerical flat-band score are learned from pairwise comparisons and used to guide a crystal diffusion model. The learned preferences and the score agree on the flattest bands but diverge elsewhere, surfacing candidate materials the original reward overlooked.

entry.title: Perfumer: A Large Language Model-based Agentic Framework Accelerating Structural Relaxation and Electronic Band Prediction for First-Principle Calculation

author.name: Zhiwei Li, Yuhao Zhou, Yikai Yang, Haonan Wang, Qing Ye, Jiancheng Lv, Kazunari Matsuda

entry.summary: Perfumer is an LLM-based agentic framework that orchestrates Quantum ESPRESSO alongside learned surrogate models to accelerate first-principles materials calculations. It achieves a 2.75-fold speedup for structural relaxation, and its periodic graph neural network band predictor, trained on 125,153 curated band structures, predicts 12 band energies at arbitrary wavevectors while preserving lattice periodicity and time-reversal symmetry.

entry.title: TRAC: Efficient Diffusion Language Models for Machine Translation via Length-Aware Decoding

author.name: Tianyuan Li, Xihan Yang, Chenglong Wang, Yuzhang Wu, Jingbo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: TRAC is a training-free adaptive decoding method for diffusion LLMs in machine translation that tackles two sources of waste: fixed target lengths and premature confidence thresholds that delay already-stable tokens. By adapting generation length and commitment timing, it reduces redundant computation while preserving translation quality.

entry.title: Can World Models Predict Rice Growth? Toward Agricultural World Models

author.name: Wenkai Ji, Zeteng Li, Yinkun Guo, Jie Zhou, Liang He, Zhenong Jin

entry.summary: The paper defines agricultural world modeling as predicting how a plant will look days to months into the future from a single photo, cultivar, and camera view, showing that state-of-the-art image generators fail at this long-horizon prediction. The proposed AgroWM explicitly infers developmental state before generating future plant appearance, targeting a real need in crop management.

entry.title: Real Cameras are Radiometric

author.name: Ties Harder, Felix Seegr\"aber, David Nakath, Hendrik Sauer, Kevin K\"oser, James Pritts

entry.summary: The authors propose a radiometric camera model that lifts any central geometric camera model to include finite aperture, a free-form focus surface, and generic vignetting, calibrated by inverse rendering on sensor irradiance without feature detection. The resulting calibrations achieve lower held-out reprojection errors than feature-based geometric calibration and extend defocus modeling beyond the thin lens.

entry.title: Fold the Loop: Decoding-Time KV Memory for Looped Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kun Zhou, Wenmian Yang, Zhensheng Wang, Yanzeng Li, Weijia Jia

entry.summary: FoldCache addresses the growing KV-cache memory of looped vision-language models by compressing visual KV states along the recurrent axis, reusing the final visual KV of grouped recurrent steps within each weight-tied module. This preserves exact prefill computation while allowing larger images and batch sizes within a fixed memory budget.

entry.title: TwoPass: Draft-Guided Few-Step Video Prediction for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yijun Liu, Shijia Ge, Tongtong Feng, Xin Wang, Yuan Meng, Yuwei Liu, Zhi Wang, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces TwoPass, a self-conditioned video prediction framework for robots that reuses the model's own clean-video draft estimate as conditioning at the same noisy state, using draft training and a refinement-only late adapter under standard flow matching. Draft-reuse iterative refinement reduces required network evaluations while improving prediction of manipulated objects. Better action-conditioned prediction directly supports robot planning and policy evaluation.

entry.title: Suppressing the Shortcut Hidden Behind the Gains of VideoLLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Youngwoo Shin, Jongsuk Kim, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: Shows that supervised fine-tuning of VideoLLMs induces a textual shortcut that lets models answer from data regularities without using the video, costing generalization under distribution shift, and proposes VETO, which intervenes on the fine-tuning update via orthogonal projection to suppress shortcut directions. The shortcut forms regardless of epoch, data size, or backbone and is hidden behind in-distribution accuracy gains. A robustness contribution to the most common VideoLLM training stage.

entry.title: Does It Depend on the Split? Frozen Satellite Features vs. Fine-Tuned CNNs for Tree Species Mapping

author.name: Dharani Deivasihamani, Nandakishore Puttashamachar

entry.summary: Tests the claim that self-supervised foundation models need fewer labels by comparing a frozen DINOv3 model with a linear classifier against a fine-tuned ImageNet ResNet-50 on TreeSatAI tree species classification. The authors find 28.8% of the official test patches overlap training/validation patches, so they construct a spatial split holding out whole 2 km squares with buffers. Under this corrected split the comparison outcomes change substantially, exposing spatial leakage in the benchmark.

entry.title: SpatialScout-V2: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore Real-World 3D Scenes and Localize Objects?

author.name: Zhaoxi Zhang, Hao Liang, Linxuan Wu, Yiming Xu, Yifu Yuan, Kun Liang, Chenming Tang, Meiyi Qiang, Wentao Zhang, Weikang Li, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: SpatialScout-V2 extends active 3D scene mapping benchmarks from simulation to real residential scenes, built from 100 homes with 3,171 objects across 29 categories. Agents must autonomously select recorded viewpoints, integrate calibrated RGB observations, and iteratively refine object localizations under a fixed interaction budget.

entry.title: Training Vision Models for LLM-Driven Weight-Space Programming

author.name: Timo Ropinski, Sebastian Kranz

entry.summary: This paper benchmarks LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, with five LLMs editing CNNs and vision transformers across relabeling and error-correction tasks on four datasets, covering more than 2,600 scored edit processes. It compares standard, label-smoothing, gradient-based editable, and other training regimes to determine how training choices affect editability by weight-space programming LLMs.

entry.title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video

author.name: Yiyan Ji, Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Zhuoran Zhang, Yifan Xu, Tengfei Liu, Yuqi Tang, Xiaohan Zhang, Shujie Li, Jiafu Tang, Xuanyu Zhu, Xinyu Liu, Yan He, Yushuo Guan, Zihao Wang, Xianghua Ying, Shixuan Liu, Haotian Wang, Wenjing Yang, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies the Code2Video paradigm, in which agent-authored 3D proxies guide video generation, through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation of proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. Findings reveal task-dependent trade-offs, such as coarse proxies favoring natural motion while medium-grained proxies improve consistency. Based on these findings, the authors build Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework that selects the appropriate proxy strategy.

entry.title: Learning What Actions Change: Action Effect Matching for Dynamics-Faithful World Models

author.name: John Won, Yonghoon Dong, Jinwoo Shin

entry.summary: AFFECT is an auxiliary training objective that improves the action-sensitivity of world models, which despite realistic videos often fail to capture how small action changes alter future observations. The method learns the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations by injecting temporally correlated noise into actions of a policy trained on human teleoperation. This targets applications like robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning.

entry.title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning

author.name: Dijia Zhan, Jinyi Li, Xuemiao Xu, Yan Zhou, Yu Liu, Shaoshan Liu, Jie Tang

entry.summary: RefreshGrad is an online adaptive data-sampling framework for training VLA policies from demonstrations, which periodically scores temporal windows using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts sampling weights during training. It exploits the observation that demonstration value varies sharply across time and evolves over the course of training.

entry.title: GNetSS: Towards Learning GNSS Corrections without Ground Truth

author.name: JiaXu Chee, Simon Denman, Fahira Afzal Maken, Qingqing Cheng, Amir Khodabandeh, Milad Ramezani

entry.summary: GNetSS is a self-supervised framework that predicts satellite-wise pseudorange corrections using a transformer combined with a differentiable positioning solver, training from GNSS measurement consistency rather than ground-truth locations. It improves robustness of single point positioning without labeled data.

entry.title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL

author.name: Wei Dai, Jinkun Liu, Jiayi Chen, Han Liu, Wenbo Ding, Shaolun Huang

entry.summary: EmbodyAgent presents an end-to-end post-training stack that turns open-weight vision-language models into robot-use agents that write and execute control code through tool interfaces. It combines black-box teacher data synthesis under a think-then-code contract, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to fix failures at interactive tool contracts and rollout distribution shift.

entry.title: EverydayBench: Evaluating Satisfactory Completion of Live User-Facing Digital Work

author.name: Fangrui Huang, Bingyang Wang, Chuhan Li, Yijiang Li, Arpandeep Khatua, Austin Shen, Riki R Z Choi, Cuiyuanxiu Chen, Jin Huang, Zachary Robertson, Kate Lin, Akshay Paruchuri, Sijun Tan, Xin Liu, Zhengmin Ni, Sanmi Koyejo, Ehsan Adeli

entry.summary: EverydayBench is a benchmark of 77 human-authored tasks across eight everyday life and work domains that evaluates whether AI agents deliver useful outcomes on the live web, integrating predefined success criteria, current evidence verification, and deliverable-quality assessment. It addresses the challenge that multiple valid results may exist and web content changes over time.

entry.title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models

author.name: LoongForge Team

entry.summary: LoongForge-Embodied is a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates training of heterogeneous Vision-Language-Action models and World-Action Models via a common abstraction layer decoupling model-specific implementations from shared training infrastructure. It enables cross-model reuse of system optimizations without constraining individual architectures.

entry.title: Efficient Multimodal Agents for Auditing 3D Worlds

author.name: Jingbo Yang, Ziyan Jiang, Li An, Jiabao Ji, Yujian Liu, Tommi Jaakkola, Yang Zhang, Shiyu Chang

entry.summary: This paper studies automatic auditing of AI-generated 3D worlds and games for glitches like floating objects and walk-through walls, identifying three required capabilities: navigation, glitch triggering, and recognition. The authors show a 4B vision-language model can be fine-tuned to handle much of the audit pipeline, balancing accuracy against cost. This enables scalable reward signals for world-building agents.

entry.title: Anchor and Check: Deterministic Cross-Prompt, Cross-Model Reconciliation for Auditable LLM Decisions

author.name: Sivakameswara Reddy Chejarla

entry.summary: This paper defines a reconciliation contract for unattended LLM decisions: commit the target model's greedy answer as an anchor, verify it with greedy checks via alternate prompts or other model families, and map the result to one of five deterministic outcomes with only Agree acted upon. Across 48,000 evaluations, pooling samples from another model family measurably improves semantic entropy's AUROC for detecting unreliable answers.

entry.title: ZeroVLN: Learning to Navigate without Supervised Fine-Tuning of the VLM Brain

author.name: Zixuan Huang, Yang Zhou, Guli Zhang, Sunzhu Li, Hongyan Xie, Zehao Chen, Fuzhen Zhuang, Kaixuan Wang, Xiaozhi Chen, Yikun Ban, Deqing Wang

entry.summary: ZeroVLN achieves vision-language navigation with zero navigation-domain supervised fine-tuning of the VLM, instead equipping the frozen VLM with a semantic tool-calling interface through which it issues natural-language movement requests to a separately trained action expert. The slow-fast framework avoids degrading base VLM general visual capabilities while still jointly improving navigation performance.

entry.title: FLUID: Flexible, Evidence-Grounded Situated Task Guidance

author.name: Yunqi Zhao, Run Peng, Ze Dong, Ryan Lu, Yinpei Dai, Joyce Chai

entry.summary: Presents FLUID, a framework for modeling and evaluating flexible real-time multimodal task guidance, where multiple responses and timings can be appropriate and silence is sometimes best. It grounds interventions in evidence, necessity, and timing flexibility using human-human guidance data from WTaG and HoloAssist. Addresses a real gap in benchmarks that treat synthesized dialogue as fixed targets.

entry.title: MADJEPA: Enhanced Multi-Stage Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture for Medical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Ioana-Sabina Stoian, Florinel-Alin Croitoru, Vlad Hondru, Andreea Iuliana Ionescu, Andrei Paun, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: MADJEPA adapts JEPA-style world models to unsupervised medical anomaly detection, training on healthy patient data only via a multi-stage pipeline combining image-level and video-level JEPA stages to model normality. The work leverages world models' ability to build internal representations of an environment, here the space of healthy medical investigations. It targets a clinically important setting where labeled anomalies are scarce.

entry.title: Planning Width Is Hard to Approximate Even Given the Unique Optimal Plan

author.name: Viet Bac Nguyen

entry.summary: This theory paper settles an open question about the approximability of planning width by constructing STRIPS tasks with a unique optimal plan where distinguishing width 1 from Theta(N) is NP-hard for set, chain, and goal-admissible widths. The construction uses positive preconditions, binary branching, and constant-size actions with all reachable states near-goal.

entry.title: Does the Workspace Do the Work? A Causal Protocol for Verifying Global-Workspace Computation in a Language Model

author.name: Diaoxuan He, Linqian Wu

entry.summary: The authors introduce a causal protocol for determining who computes what when modules in a network communicate, tested in the context of Global Workspace Theory implementations in language models. The key test transplants a message from another input so that ignoring, relaying and recombining it predict three different answers, distinguishing genuine workspace computation from mere forwarding.

entry.title: Flow Matching from Non-Gaussian Sources: A Theory of Efficient Sampling

author.name: Yuchen Zhou, Lili Zheng, Yuxin Chen, Gen Li

entry.summary: This paper establishes nonasymptotic convergence guarantees for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation when the source distribution is non-Gaussian (e.g., heavy-tailed or multimodal), under mild smoothness and variance conditions. Prior finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources were limited. The theory formalizes when flexible source choices in flow matching remain statistically and computationally reliable.

entry.title: Sequential Probability Assignment against Smoothed Adversaries with Unknown Base Measure

author.name: Ziyi Liu, Daniel M. Roy

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies sequential probability assignment (online log-loss learning) under smoothed adversaries where the fixed base measure constraining the adversary is unknown to the learner, removing assumptions from prior work. It handles the unknown-base-measure setting without Lipschitz conditions, addressing a notable gap in bypassing worst-case adversarial hardness results.

entry.title: Approximate Adjoint Models for Memory and Compute-Efficient Online Learning of Hybrid Models

author.name: Emilio Gonz\'alez-Zamora, Pierre Tandeo, Laurent Debreu, Said Ouala

entry.summary: Proposes approximate adjoint methods that reduce the memory and compute cost of gradient computation for online calibration of hybrid numerical-neural models, addressing limitations of truncated BPTT which introduces bias and drops long-range dependencies. Targets realistic geophysical applications where trajectory length and resolution are bottlenecks.

entry.title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action

author.name: Linfeng Dong, Jianwei Niu, Jiuyi Zhao, Ruibing Feng, Xinghao Wu, Wu Yang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Mu Li

entry.summary: ActMem is an in-context memory framework for vision-language-action models that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone with native video understanding. Motivated by cognitive science distinctions between reconstructive memory and perception, it infers what past experience implies for current tasks while preventing history from crowding out current perception in long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: MoGloss: Joint Motion and Pseudo-Gloss Pretraining for American Sign Language Understanding

author.name: Rui Hong, Jana Ko\v{s}eck\'a

entry.summary: MoGloss proposes a two-stage pretraining for sign language motion encoders: masked motion reconstruction followed by joint masked prediction of pseudo-gloss units derived from captions via an LLM. The authors curate roughly 1,100 hours of American Sign Language video from five public datasets with estimated 2D poses and a standardized evaluation protocol, then reproduce and compare state-of-the-art translation methods under consistent splits.

entry.title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI

author.name: Qiman Wu, Hanlin Chen, Yuhua Wei, Mingyuan Wang, Shaman Tang, Minghao Li, Rui Xin, Xingye Liu, Zhichao Yang, Yiqi Yu, Hongyan Pei, Xiaowen Tian, YingYing Liu, Shiwen Liu, Jiahui Hu, Yizhao Wang, Yuheng Zhang, Anhua Liu, Yue He, Shuang Su, Da Zhu, Hua Zhou, Pengfei Diao, Haojie Yang, Weichao Huang, Hang Zhang, Honggou Yang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: TuringPAI is a family of compact models for on-device physical AI: a 0.65B vision-language backbone (TuringPAI-VL) built on a hybrid convolutional-Transformer architecture with multi-scale latent queries, specialized into TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Towards High-Fidelity Learned Video Compression

author.name: Bumyoon Kim, Yongseong Kim, Inhyuk Jeong, Byeungwoo Jeon

entry.summary: Quantifies how little of the professional video quality range recent learned codecs cover, showing they reach only 24-38% of the span from VVC QP 37 up to high-grade 4:2:2 ProRes on 10-bit YCbCr test content, constrained by fixed latent capacity of at most 0.25. Proposes a learned inter-frame codec with a searched encoder to extend the achievable quality range. Important grounding for a field often evaluated only on standard low-quality test conditions.

entry.title: StreamEgo: Streaming Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation

author.name: Tianyi Xu, Boyang Lyu, Yunkai Tang, Kairan Ding, Jiahang Li, Weiyu Guo, Yandong Guo, Shuchen Weng, Boxin Shi

entry.summary: StreamEgo is a real-time framework for unbounded, streaming conversion of third-person video into first-person egocentric viewpoints, targeting AR/VR and embodied robotics demonstration synthesis. A streaming dual-branch prior provides pixel-aligned guidance for manipulation regions, overcoming fixed-length clip limitations of prior Exo2Ego methods.

entry.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action

author.name: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhibo Pang

entry.summary: TacInno addresses inconsistent gains from tactile sensing in VLA models by isolating tactile innovation: the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot already explain. A tokenizer conditioned on visual observations and actions compresses only this residual tactile signal, which is then used as the training target. This makes tactile input informative rather than redundant, improving contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Cognitive-Horizon Action Chunking: Memory-Guided Adaptive Reasoning for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Weile Gong, Zijian Lu, Jiahao Zheng, Bo Xu, Yiping Zuo, Jiajia Guo, Xin He, Weijun Wang, Weibei Fan

entry.summary: CHAC is a training-free framework that adaptively decides how many cached waypoints a robot executes before refreshing its VLM prediction, using retained visual context, completion cues, and controller feedback to set the cognitive horizon. It cuts VLM calls by 33.4 to 64.7 percent on HM3D-OVON and R2R-CE with modest success-rate tradeoffs.

entry.title: One View, One Action: Spatially Generalizable VLAs through Observation-Aligned Experts and Cross Graph Consistency

author.name: Jinxi Liu, Ruifeng Zhai, Hao Liu, Guangrun Wang

entry.summary: OVOA-VLA improves spatial generalization in multi-view vision-language-action models by predicting actions in each camera's frame instead of only the robot base frame, training a base-frame expert plus view-specific experts with observation-aligned supervision. Consistency constraints tie the experts together, improving robustness to camera viewpoint and initial-state changes.

entry.title: Generalist Meets Specialists: An Evolving Multimodal Agent with Persistent Tool Orchestration for Traffic Scenario Understanding

author.name: Linjia Kang, Binhan Jiang, Juan Yang, Zhiqin Song, Xiangsen Wu, Qionglin Ren, Jiang Liu, Zhongjiang He, Hao Sun

entry.summary: StarTV-Agent is a tool-augmented vision-language agent for traffic scenario understanding that combines policy learning with experience evolution, echoing a fast-slow cognition split: adaptive reasoning when needed and reuse of prior experience when possible. Its Role-Sensitive Process Optimization blends process advantages with terminal rewards to give better training signal for intermediate tool decisions, and it persists experience across similar tasks to cut repeated planning cost.

entry.title: When Agents Play Differently: Localizing Human--Agent Behavioral Divergence with Conditional Distributional Testing

author.name: Oleg Smirnov, John Pertoft, Sara Karimi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a stratified statistical framework that computes nonparametric discrepancy statistics within contextual cells and discovers subgroup rules pinpointing where agent behavior diverges from human play, showing that outcome-level metrics like win/loss carry little signal while process-level metrics such as move efficiency reveal real differences. Applied to a commercial match-3 game, it finds a playtesting bot diverges substantially from humans in specific game modes that aggregate metrics miss.

entry.title: ClosureBench: A Benchmark for Reasoning under Closure Assumptions

author.name: Francesco Belardinelli, Flavio Corradini, Matteo Leonesi

entry.summary: ClosureBench tests whether LLM agents correctly handle missing information under open-world, closed-world, and local closed-world assumptions, with verified base scenarios where only the treatment of missingness varies between variants. It also includes agent extensions covering action choice, source scope, and updates, isolating a reasoning dimension current evaluations conflate with other demands.

entry.title: LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Yu-Hung Wu, Shao-Xiang Yuan, Chan-Hung Yu, Zih-Ching Chen, Kuan-Hao Huang, Shao-Hua Sun

entry.summary: Framing LLM inference through computational complexity theory, this paper uses generated-token count as an observable proxy for inference-time compute and shows empirically that token usage does not align monotonically with classical time complexity. It demonstrates a fundamental divergence rooted in how LLMs allocate computation at inference. Offers a conceptual framework for reasoning-efficiency analysis.

entry.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification

author.name: Meenakshi Rajpurohit, Anna Phan, Ravikumar Komandur Narayanan, Gunanidhi Ramakrishnan, Nathan Howland

entry.summary: Presents FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent financial QA prototype over SEC filings and live market data featuring a compact routing model, Python for all computations, retrieval and MCP-based tools, Mistral-7B for cited answer writing, and a code validator checking citation and numeric consistency. Live experiments show the typed routing model outperforming larger alternatives. Emphasizes provenance and verification in a domain where LLMs miscompute and hallucinate confidently.

entry.title: CRAFT: Constrained Route planning with Adaptive Framework and Template-based code generation

author.name: Shahd Elmahallawy, Ahmed Eldawy

entry.summary: CRAFT handles natural-language routing queries with multiple constraints (ordered stops, time budgets, EV charging) by having an LLM generate search functions that a generic graph-search engine executes on real road networks. It formalizes the underlying problem as State-Expanded RCSP, unifying many distinct routing problem variants. This replaces the classical need for a bespoke solver per constraint combination.

entry.title: Intelligent Embedding Pruning for Large-Scale Recommendation Models

author.name: Anish Khazane, Alex Saad-Falcon, Guanchu Wu, Marcio Porto, Jasper Shan, Fei Yu, Eugene Shulga, Intaik Park, Yongzhe Zhang, Xiaoyu Deng, Sheng Luo, Xiaoya Wang

entry.summary: FI-ITEP improves in-training embedding pruning for recommendation systems by using feature importance signals rather than size-based heuristics to set per-table pruning ratios. Across three large-scale recommendation models it achieves 20-40% memory reduction while matching or improving accuracy. The work addresses the dominant memory pressure from sparse embedding layers mapping high-cardinality categorical features.

entry.title: Online Mistake Detection in Instruction-Conditioned Procedural Video

author.name: Amit Feldman, Ilan Shimshoni, Rotem Dror

entry.summary: This paper studies online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric procedural video, identifying and localizing completed action attempts and classifying them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions using only observed video, instructions, and prior predictions. It fills a gap between offline instruction-conditioned methods and online detectors that ignore instruction text.

entry.title: A$^2$-VLA: Adapting Vision-Language-Action Policies to New Tools through Agentic Affordance Discovery

author.name: Chenyuan Zhou, Chaoyi Huang, Zibo Wang, Zhiyuan Li, Yong-Lu Li

entry.summary: A2-VLA is a tool-adaptation framework combining an embodied agent with a VLA policy, treating tool affordances as hypotheses the agent constructs, tests, and revises in simulation from a few teleoperated demonstrations. The goal is transferring manipulation skills across geometrically different tools by discovering shared task-relevant affordances.

entry.title: AltRA-Test: An Alternative Annotator Test for LLM Judges Without Shared Annotators

author.name: Nagham Omar, Rotem Dror, Almog Gueta, Avigdor Gal, Roi Reichart, Nitay Calderon

entry.summary: AltRA-Test is a statistical test for deciding when LLM judges can replace human annotators in realistic sparse annotation settings where items are labeled by different annotator subsets. It uses bootstrap resampling of items and substitution of one human annotation to extend the prior Alt-Test beyond dense shared-annotator settings.

entry.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes

author.name: Francesco Caporali, Jason M. Altschuler, Boris Hanin

entry.summary: The authors propose critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes, which multiply the classical Polyak rule by 4 and a damping factor, biasing gradient descent toward flatter minima. The factor 4 induces equioscillations around the minimizer manifold, operating at the edge of stability while adapting to local curvature. The paper establishes the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives.

entry.title: Rate-distortion Assessment for Hierarchical Content Summarization

author.name: Yunye Gong, Indranil Sur, Jared Claypoole, Pritish Sahu, Ajay Divakaran

entry.summary: Inspired by Shannon rate-distortion theory, this work formalizes hierarchical content summarization as an information encoding problem, extracting the semantic hierarchy of source content to quantitatively characterize the trade-off between compression efficiency and fidelity. This moves summarization quality assessment from subjective judgment toward a principled quantitative framework.

entry.title: Differentially Private Score Estimation with Applications to Score-Based Generative Models

author.name: Mengxiao Gao, Elly K. H. Hung, Yuchen Wu, Yi Yu

entry.summary: This paper studies the statistical limits of score function estimation under differential privacy, motivated by memorization and privacy-attack risks in score-based generative models. The authors establish minimax results for private score estimation in d-dimensional settings and connect them to training differentially private score-based generative models.

entry.title: The Depth of a Prediction: Where Language Models Resolve a Word Predicts Human Reading Time

author.name: Donato Riccio, Fabrizio Maturo

entry.summary: Using the tuned lens to read word predictions at every layer across GPT-2, OPT, and Pythia models and eight eye-tracking/self-paced reading corpora, the paper introduces resolution depth, the layer around which a word's surprisal trajectory changes. Words resolved later, and the words following them, are read more slowly, and resolution depth improves held-out reading-time prediction beyond final-layer surprisal and entropy.

entry.title: Scaling classical hardware for accurate real-time quantum error correction

author.name: Chenyang Jin, Susanne F. Yelin, Andi Gu

entry.summary: Rapids is a streaming neural decoder for quantum error correction co-designed with an FPGA so that its operations and integer-arithmetic training map cheaply onto the hardware, achieving both the low latency required by superconducting processors and high decoding accuracy. This alleviates the speed-accuracy trade-off that otherwise forces larger surface codes and more physical qubits.

entry.title: MV-JEPA: Post-Training Video Encoders for Cross-View Understanding

author.name: Yangchen Zhao, Ali Payani, Caiwen Ding

entry.summary: MV-JEPA introduces multi-view predictive post-training for JEPA-based video encoders, jointly predicting latent tokens of masked regions and paired camera views to strengthen cross-view instance and temporal correspondence while retaining single-view inference. This addresses the limitation that standard JEPA pretraining never exploits paired views of the same moment.

entry.title: Wearable Logo, Silent Hijack: Stealthy Cross-Modal Semantic Attacks on Visible--Infrared Vision-Language Models

author.name: Qike Zhang, Jiaju Han, Xuelian Shi, Xiang Chen, Dehe Zhao, Banglong Nong, Wenhao Zheng, Lei Wang, Jiahuan Long, Jiujiang Guo, Chengyin Hu

entry.summary: This paper presents LoSA, a score-based black-box attack that repurposes real logos on clothing and objects to mount targeted semantic attacks against visible-infrared vision-language models, keeping the logo outline intact for stealth. It demonstrates coordinated cross-modal attacks in realistic physical settings.

entry.title: UniReFP: Robust Unified Fingerprinting for Vision Models against Cross-Task Repurposing Attacks

author.name: Ziye Geng, Guang Yang, Yihang Chen, Lingfeng Yao, Xing Shi, Miao Pan, Xin Fu, Changqing Luo

entry.summary: Identifies a new model modification attack, cross-task repurposing, that invalidates existing vision model fingerprints, and proposes UniReFP, a unified fingerprinting framework that verifies ownership via a shared class-level semantic space instead of task-specific outputs. By repurposing the protected model to build a surrogate classifier, fingerprints survive when a stolen model is adapted to a different task with heterogeneous outputs. This strengthens model IP protection against an underexplored evasion route.

entry.title: Fast and Accurate Body Estimation in Pixels, World Space and Scenes

author.name: Jinkun Cao

entry.summary: Introduces FAB, a human body estimator that directly predicts skeleton joints and dense surface points alongside a parametric MHR head, fitting SMPL via one learned pass plus two Gauss-Newton steps. A ViT-L student distilled from a fine-tuned SAM 3D Body runs in real time on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER at 4.6x the speed of SAM 3D Body's body-only path while improving accuracy on most camera-space benchmarks, with the same network working across pixel, world, and scene spaces. Combines efficiency and fidelity advances in a single system.

entry.title: ContextRenderer: Dynamic-Context Video Generation for Interactive Game Worlds

author.name: Runze Wang, Fei Zha, Bing He, Ke Xu, Zhongyuan Wu, Yuxuan Xie, Wenzheng Wu, Zhongyuan Liu, Youcheng Cai, Ligang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ContextRenderer, an autoregressive video diffusion framework for rendering engine-provided game scene representations into detailed video observations during sustained interactive gameplay. It couples Dynamic-Context Learning for chunk-level interaction supervision with Recurrent History Compression to follow condition updates while preserving visual continuity under a bounded token budget. The work targets cross-proxy generalization in world model renderers.

entry.title: Better Retrieval, Not Better Binding: Pretraining Exposure in Egocentric Video Retrieval

author.name: Yuqi Guo, Michael Wray

entry.summary: The authors introduce Ego-ExBind, a diagnostic protocol that disentangles pretraining exposure from compositional verb-noun binding in egocentric video-text retrieval. Using an Exposure Ledger over the EgoClip corpus, they create Seen Composition, Unseen Composition, and Unseen Atom splits to test whether video-language models truly understand compositional relationships.

entry.title: AdaPixFlow: Learning Continuous-Time 3D Dynamics Across Scenes from Sparse Multi-view Observations

author.name: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: AdaPixFlow learns a continuous-time dynamics operator that maps multi-view RGB-D observations to 3D object kinematics without per-scene optimization or predefined physical motion models. Observations from all cameras are fused into a shared world-coordinate voxel grid from which a network predicts a continuous-time velocity field. This enables predicting object positions at unobserved times across scenes, a step toward generalizable dynamic scene understanding.

entry.title: Solomonoff induction with reflective oracles

author.name: Cole Wyeth

entry.summary: A linkpost discussing a PIBBSS fellow's arXiv paper on reflective-oracle Solomonoff induction (rOSI), which uses reflective oracles to build a sequence predictor that can extract computable structure from partially uncomputable sequences. The post frames this as a clean demonstration that self-reflection can overcome unrealizability, with properties reminiscent of logical induction but in a more compact and accessible form.

entry.title: From Cases to Criteria: Reusing Evaluation Knowledge for Task-Specific Rubric Generation

author.name: Qiyan Deng, Long-Kai Huang, Kangfei Zhao

entry.summary: RubricDuo organizes historical query-rubric pairs into a Rubric Knowledge Graph linking evaluation dimensions, shared concepts, and criterion-level evidence, enabling generation of task-specific rubrics that connect recurring evaluation requirements to their source context. This avoids the failure modes of reusing whole cases (irrelevant details) or aggregated criteria (lost structure) in LLM-as-judge setups.

entry.title: DeepQuest: From Knowledge Gaps to Scientific Discovery in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Chunbo Jiang, Yifei Chen, Beining Wu, Fuyou Mao, Weihong Chen, Enyu Bao, Mingxuan Liu, Feiwei Qin, Qiyuan Tian

entry.summary: DeepQuest is a knowledge-gap-driven AI scientist framework for Alzheimer's research that converts unresolved questions from domain reviews into traceable, testable hypotheses, prioritized via data feasibility screening and groupwise Elo ranking. It couples iterative experimentation with two-level auditing against frozen literature corpora and produces 42 feasible hypotheses on the OASIS-3 dataset.

entry.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images

author.name: Adri\`a Ciurana Lanau, Harleen Hanspal, Lusine Abrahamyan, Emilio Tylson Baixauli, Yu Cao, Danai Triantafyllidou, Stefano Zorzi, Gustavo Zanoni Felipe, Peter Griger, Stefan Sietzen, Petru-Daniel Tudosiu

entry.summary: Presents ProtoDiffusion, a latent diffusion framework for generating layered graphic designs, built on ProtoVAE which encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype plus one candidate vector per RGBA layer. This reduces representation size from N*HW tokens for full grids to HW+N tokens, enabling scalable layered image generation. Targets the graphic-design domain where layer separability enables editing and reuse.

entry.title: Joint Language Modeling for In-the-Wild Speech-Scene Generation with Distinct Token Representations

author.name: Semin Kim, Ju Yeon Kang, Sunghwan Ahn, Seonuk Kim, Nam Soo Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes an LLM-based framework for generating coherent speech scenes that jointly models distinct speech and environment token streams using a source-aware neural audio codec, trained on in-the-wild rather than simulated mixed scenes. It addresses the failure of single mixed acoustic representations to capture the different characteristics of speech and environmental audio.

entry.title: Splice-Core: Low-Order-Bit-Splicing GEMM for Highly Energy-Efficient AI Inference Accelerators

author.name: Prabhu Vellaisamy, Hsien-Fu Hung, Andrew Kim, Shawn Blanton, John Paul Shen

entry.summary: Splice-Core is a temporal-unary/binary hybrid GEMM accelerator design that minimizes low-order accumulation latency while retaining value-dependent execution for high-order bits. Its two processing element variants achieve roughly 77% geometric-mean tile energy reductions versus a binary systolic array across INT4 CNN and LLM workloads, with Splice-LUT also boosting throughput 44% and cutting energy-delay product over 6x.

entry.title: Multi-View Transformer with Geometry-Guided Multi-Modal ControlNet for 3D Virtual Try-On

author.name: Sarthak Batra, Armin Mustafa, Adrian Hilton

entry.summary: GS-VTON-MVT is a three-stage framework for consistent 3D virtual try-on on Gaussian Splatting captures, combining implicit and explicit 3D reasoning. A multi-view inpainting transformer jointly edits training views with cross-view attention, and a geometry-guided ControlNet preserves garment detail, addressing texture drift and implausible geometry in novel views.

entry.title: SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills

author.name: Anjie Xu, Zixing Wang, Yifeng Cai, Leye Wang

entry.summary: SkillBridge is a contract-based workflow of static analysis, dynamic validation and repair for diagnosing cross-OS failures in executable agent skills, screening 3,270 skill-target-OS cases covering 1,090 skills across Linux, macOS and Windows. It reduces the cost of running every skill on every OS before identifying genuinely OS-related failures.

entry.title: One Framework to Diagnose Them All: A Stratified Benchmark for Bengali LLM Hallucination

author.name: Asif Shahriyar Sushmit, Shefayat E Shams Adib, Abdullah Al Jubaer Gem, Ahmed Shafin Ruhan, MD. Nazmuddoha Ansary, Biplab Kumar Sarkar, Syed Rifat Raiyan, Ajwad Abrar, Abdullah Bin Hasan, Adib Sakhawat, M. Sakeef Hossain, Ahmed Alfey Sani, Arefin Mizan, Sourab Chakma, Quazi Adibur Rahman Adib, Wassie Haque, Sanjay Kumar Sen, Saad Tahmid, Mohammad Mamun Or Rashid

entry.summary: Alikbachan is a large Bengali hallucination-detection benchmark stratified by cultural distance, six task types, and a 32-mode hallucination taxonomy, comprising a 2,516-item harvested test set and a 5,000-item gold-labeled set. Community-scale competitions (99 and 32 systems across phases) reveal over 30 macro-F1 variation across strata for zero-shot LLM judges, demonstrating diagnostic value of stratification. The paper advocates consolidating fragmented low-resource-language hallucination research into comparable resources.

entry.title: HapBO: Harnessed $\alpha$-$\pi$ Bayesian Optimization via Expert Natural Language Priors

author.name: Jean-S\'ebastien Giroux, Rose Guay Hottin, Marco Bonizzato

entry.summary: HapBO elicits prior beliefs once from a human expert, an LLM, or both in natural language, then deterministically compiles them into a structured, reusable belief function for prior-guided Bayesian optimization. This bridges the gap between language-expressed knowledge and the probability distributions that prior-guided BO methods require, while being robust to misleading information.

entry.title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models

author.name: Alireza Moayedikia

entry.summary: The paper formalizes model merging composability as a property of task-vector collections, proving that excess loss of a merged model is controlled by an interference functional of cross-task curvature overlap and signed update alignment. It derives a curvature-metric angle criterion that is both necessary and sufficient in the quadratic regime, and proposes a curvature-guided regularizer for merge-aware fine-tuning.

entry.title: Beyond Alignment: Whitening Geometry, Profile Synthesis, and Heterogeneous Ensembles for Cross-Environment WiFi Action Recognition

author.name: Lei Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes cross-environment WiFi action recognition collapse under leave-one-domain-out evaluation, showing via ceiling analysis and a pre-registered falsification chain that the failure is encoder extrapolation rather than a domain alignment problem. Proposes whitening geometry, profile synthesis, and heterogeneous ensembles as alternatives that beat alignment methods like CORAL.

entry.title: When Do Rankings Beat Signs? Gradient Direction Recovery under Even Nuisance

author.name: Zhuangzhuang Pan, Yan Xia, Chee Seng Chan

entry.summary: Provides a theoretical analysis of gradient direction recovery from ranking versus sign feedback in the presence of unknown even nuisance functions, defining an information hierarchy (Mirror, Reverse, Full) and a relative shell variation condition. Under that condition, ranking-based queries localize directions to angular accuracy with provable evaluation-complexity advantages.

entry.title: Time Series Structure Learning with Local Causal Parent Discovery

author.name: Jacqueline Maasch, Shu Wan, Hank Zhu, Huan Liu, Zhiguang Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD), a sound and complete constraint-based algorithm for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. It uses a local-to-global strategy, discovering each variable's parent set sequentially and exploiting temporal structure to mitigate the high computational and sample complexity of causal discovery.

entry.title: Stability Bands for Feature Attribution: The Core, the Nucleolus and the Bargaining Set of Explained-Variance Games

author.name: Fernando Delbianco, Fernando Tohm\'e

entry.summary: The authors reinterpret feature attribution through cooperative game theory, defining an explained-variance game and reporting for each feature a stability band derived from the core, least core, nucleolus, and bargaining set rather than a single Shapley number. This reveals whether feature coalitions could contest the attribution and provides certificates that allocations admit no justified objection.

entry.title: Hierarchical Spatiotemporal World Modeling with Content-Adaptive Spatial Addressing

author.name: Tiantian Li, Junfeng Lu, Yifei Wang, Zhaoyang Zhang, Lei Wang, Tianyi Qian

entry.summary: HiSTFormer is a hierarchical spatiotemporal world model inspired by hippocampal episodic memory and grid-cell coding, combining local and multi-periodic spatial RoPE with content-conditioned address offsets and a fixed-capacity memory that bounds KV storage and attention cost as sequences grow. It outperforms strong world-model baselines on MemoryMaze and HM3D within the training setup.

entry.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation

author.name: Zhixiong Hu, Meng Li, Maggie Zhang, Deborshi Goswami, David Bailey, James Bradley

entry.summary: This paper presents LSER, a production content recommendation system at Autodesk that derives session- and history-level user embeddings from a pretrained LLM and adds them as auxiliary features in the retrieval-stage user tower alongside learned sequence encoders, with mechanisms for keeping embeddings fresh under real-time behavior. It reports on reconciling heterogeneous content types with sparse, fast-changing user behavior at scale.

entry.title: Exact Bayesian layers via characteristic functions

author.name: William H. W. Thompson, Guillaume St-Onge, Laurent H\'ebert-Dufresne, Jean-Gabriel Young

entry.summary: CF-Prop propagates uncertainty through Bayesian ReLU layers exactly using characteristic functions, avoiding both Monte Carlo sampling and the Gaussian-output assumptions of prior sampling-free variational inference. This allows closed-form evidence lower bounds for a broad class of likelihoods, improving the tractability and accuracy of Bayesian neural network training.

entry.title: Same Judgement, Different Scores: Numerical Scoring Topology in LLM-as-a-Judge Evaluation

author.name: Doyun Kim, Chanwoo Kim, Jiwoo Kum, Minsoo Song, Chanjun Park

entry.summary: This paper defines numerical scoring topology, covering scale width, granularity, offset, symmetry, and boundary placement of scoring schemes, and conducts the first systematic study of how these design choices affect zero-shot LLM-as-a-judge evaluation. Results show scoring topology systematically influences judge scores, calibration, and robustness.

entry.title: Do Deep Stereo Models Learn Shape Priors?

author.name: Linbo Tang, Aneel Damaraju, Todd Zickler

entry.summary: Using a synthetic stereo dataset from a tightly constrained family of shapes, the authors show that several state-of-the-art stereo models retain systematic boundary errors even when finetuned or trained from scratch, indicating they fail to internalize simple shape priors. They propose a generative stereo model that jointly predicts disparity and a signed distance field, improving boundary consistency.

entry.title: DiLE: Discrimination-Aware Latent-Space Learning for Universal Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Ben Kang, Junda Wang, Yuxuan Yuan, Hang Li, Yuhan Liu, Xin Chen, Wanting Geng, Tong Lin, Pei Fu, Dong Wang, Jian Luan, Huchuan Lu

entry.summary: DiLE improves universal multimodal embeddings built on MLLMs by preserving discriminative evidence needed to separate relevant items from confusable alternatives. It combines task guidance via learnable latent queries and answer-generation supervision with on-policy retrieval feedback drawn from retrieval mistakes.

entry.title: CaT-Movie: Balancing Global Planning and Local Rendering for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Jinpeng Lu, Haoyuan Shi, Yuanshen Guan, Jiyuan Xia, Bin Wu, Yinda Chen, Zhiwei Xiong

entry.summary: Proposes a system for long multi-shot movie generation combining an LLM-driven global story planner with a local window renderer that uses deterministic code to maintain storyboards and reference frames across shots. Reference-routed sparse self-attention and shot-wise cross-cut techniques preserve narrative progression and visual identity where naive segment stitching drifts. This addresses a core limitation of current video generators, which render only short clips per pass.

entry.title: D3-Cache: Accelerating Diffusion Models with Dynamic Mode Decomposition

author.name: Yanbo Li, An Xiang, Xiaoxin Hu, Feng Wang, Cheng-zhong Xu, Kejiang Ye, Xitong Gao

entry.summary: Applies Dynamic Mode Decomposition to diffusion transformer sampling by fitting DMD to a short history of exact network velocities and forecasting the velocity the scheduler consumes, with a horizon-aware gate that triggers full network evaluation when forecast error grows. This training-free caching approach avoids per-model calibrated skip criteria and per-layer prediction histories used by prior cache methods. Targets cheaper image and video generation with diffusion transformers.

entry.title: FlexVSR: Continuous-Scale Super-Resolution for Streaming Video Generation

author.name: Ji Wang, Haonan An, Jiasheng Zhang, Renlong Chen

entry.summary: FlexVSR enables continuous-scale generative video super-resolution for streaming applications, allowing flexible target resolutions without retraining a diffusion transformer per scale. It decouples scaling from the generative prior, supervising at only a few scales to avoid redundant downsampling costs.

entry.title: Risk-Controlled Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zixuan Liu, Hashem Haghbayan, Zizhan Zheng, Siavash Khajavi

entry.summary: R2-VLA is a risk-controlled framework for retrieval-augmented vision-language-action models that guarantees a user-specified task success rate with minimal expert assistance during test-time adaptation. It learns an uncertainty predictor over predicted actions given retrieved demonstrations and intervenes with expert help only when risk exceeds a threshold. This brings conformal-style statistical guarantees to robot policy adaptation.

entry.title: From Sequence to Space: Explicit Spatial Belief with Vision-Language Distillation for Active Geo-Localization

author.name: Ziyang Xu, Peng Han, Hai Zhou

entry.summary: EAGLE tackles active geo-localization by distilling spatial context from a frozen Qwen2.5-VL-7B teacher into a lightweight Swin student that maintains an explicit spatial belief over a masked aerial search grid. This replaces large sequential Transformers and dense distance rewards that depend on hidden goal locations, improving navigation to targets specified by images or text.

entry.title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zilang Cen, Chao Tang, Fangcheng Liu, Weishi Mi, Wei Hao, JiaYu Xu, Dehao Huang, Yehui Tang, Xiaohui Cui, Tingguang Li, Xiaoyuan Zhang

entry.summary: RoC reduces latency and token costs in long-horizon manipulation by using an online task-state monitor combining temporal visual observations with interaction memory to predict subtask progress and successors, triggering high-level agent review only on events. This event-triggered design coordinates a low-level policy with a reasoning agent, deciding whether errors need execution repair, replanning, or both.

entry.title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration

author.name: Fangxu Yu, Tao Feng, Xuying Ning, Haolin Yang, Jiaxuan You, Tianyi Zhou

entry.summary: EpiCompass is a plug-and-play scaffold for research agents that maintains an epistemic state via a tree linking hypotheses, evidence, beliefs, and revisions, reassessing hypotheses as evidence accumulates. It targets known failure modes: unsupported claims, narrow hypothesis exploration, and belief retention despite conflicting evidence.

entry.title: COVERAGE-TRACE: Source-Side Counterfactual Tracing for Detecting Omissions in LLM Summaries

author.name: Ali Karkehabadi, Jamshid Hassanpour, Rafael E. Banchs

entry.summary: COVERAGE-TRACE detects omissions in LLM summaries by replacing a target atomic source fact with type-matched alternatives while holding the summary fixed, then measuring changes in teacher-forced, length-normalized likelihood. Summaries that cover the fact should respond more strongly than those omitting it, and aggregation across counterfactuals reduces sensitivity. This addresses the hard problem that missing information leaves no output span to inspect.

entry.title: ADAPT: Adaptive Decision and Abstention with Pool-Size-Aware Thresholds for Service Routing

author.name: Manile Srun, Muntasir Adnan, Arslan Shaukat, Carlos C. N. Kuhn

entry.summary: This paper introduces ADAPT, a lightweight retrieval-based routing architecture for directing queries to specialized services, with an explicit abstention/fallback option when no suitable service exists. Its key empirical insight is that routing confidence distributions shift systematically with the size of the candidate pool K, so fixed abstention thresholds degrade as services scale.

entry.title: Serialization Tax in Shared-Latent Exchangeable Decisions

author.name: Siming Zhang, Zhehui Shen, Shijie Chen, Xinle Gu, Yansen Yu, Hang Yu

entry.summary: This theory paper identifies the serialization tax: the error that arises when systems score items independently while acting on group-level decisions over items sharing an uncertain latent state. Using convex-order comparisons, the authors quantify variance and total-variation gaps between the true dispersed count law and independent approximations, and connect posterior approximation error to decision regret via threshold separation results.

entry.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models

author.name: Jinzhe Li, Qi Wang, Dandan Guo, Li Liu, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: Introduces MM-SystemOneBias, a benchmark evaluating 13 multimodal decision models on 5,323 instances from nine datasets and 11 task scenarios using six paired interventions such as option order, option labels, and external judgments. It provides a unified protocol comparing decision models to their backbones on robustness to presentation changes and irrelevant additions. Fills a gap between separate study of decision-interface bias and multimodal behavior.

entry.title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Woongkyu Lee, Jungwook Choi

entry.summary: Introduces CANDID, an execution-control framework for local computer-use agents in resource-constrained settings, targeting failure modes like rigid action loops and premature DONE decisions. It repurposes parallel test-time scaling as sparse, execution-level intervention, with loop-recovery candidate filtering and unanimous DONE gating. Aimed at improving reliability of on-device agents without textual reflection overhead.

entry.title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models

author.name: Sion Israel Sion

entry.summary: This framework distinguishes future-directed content, prospective computation, and causal guidance when probing whether language models internally represent unchosen alternatives, drawing on prospection and hippocampal forward-sweep research. A preregistered low-rank probe evaluated once on a sealed test set failed its criterion (0.020 vs 0.195 baseline accuracy), and the paper honestly reports this negative result. It contributes methodological rigor for interpretability claims about prospective representations.

entry.title: LLMs Are Already Confidence-Aware Zero-Shot Classifiers

author.name: Owen Cook, Xingyi Song

entry.summary: This empirical study compares black-box confidence methods (verbalized confidence, sampling) with white-box token-probability methods for LLM zero-shot text classification across eleven open-weight models (1B-32B) on five datasets with 3-151 labels. Confidence method choice rarely changes accuracy, but logit-based scoring yields much better discrimination (AUROC 0.74-0.77) than verbalized approaches. The title's claim is that LLMs already possess usable calibrated confidence signals if you read the right signals.

entry.title: SGLayout: Schema-Guided Closed-Loop Refinement for LLM-Driven Parameterized Layout Generation

author.name: Siyang Chen, Yuan Pu, Yuhan Qin, Zhaotan Lin, Siyuan Liang, Zhuolun He, Lining Zhang, Bei Yu

entry.summary: SGLayout is a self-refining framework for LLM-driven parameterized layout generation that uses a structured schema to link code-level instances to their geometric attributes, enabling evaluation feedback to translate into actionable code fixes. This closes the loop between geometric-domain evaluation and code-level refinement, avoiding blind refactoring.

entry.title: The Coverage Selection Gap: Ranking, Not Generation, Limits LLM Rubric Construction

author.name: Ali Karkehabadi, Jamshid Hassanpour, Rafael E. Banchs

entry.summary: This paper studies automatic rubric construction for evaluating open-ended LLM outputs in professional M&A due diligence, introducing a multi-axis generation framework and a coverage-selection decomposition that separates criterion discovery failures from candidate selection failures. Its central finding is that ranking, not generation, is the bottleneck for rubric coverage.

entry.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember

author.name: Aryan Jain, Abhishek Jha, Anish Nediyanchath, Promod Yenigalla

entry.summary: STARK is a dual-graph long-term memory architecture for personalized agents, maintaining an Episodic Graph of temporally, causally, and semantically linked interactions and an Insight Graph of LLM-extracted behavioral patterns. Events serve both as nodes and as edges connecting behavioral insights, enabling agents to retain why experiences mattered, not just what happened.

entry.title: Closing Performance Gap for Diffusion Language Models under Low Inference Budgets

author.name: Hao Wu, Sipeng Chen, Jingwen Fu, Yuwang Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces CaRR (Commitment-aware Refinement and Recovery), a training-free framework that improves generation quality of editable diffusion language models at low inference budgets by recovering useful intermediate results lost before final submission via updated-context refill and trajectory-based recovery. It targets the quality decline that occurs when denoising steps are reduced below autoregressive parity.

entry.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature

author.name: Pangjing Wu, Xu Yuan, Wenqi Fan, Qing Li

entry.summary: LINEAGE is a benchmark for retrieving empirical lineage relations in AI literature, where a prior paper serves as an explicit comparison baseline for a source paper. It moves beyond topical relevance and citation links to capture which methods researchers actually benchmark against, supporting literature synthesis and experiment planning agents.

entry.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving

author.name: Changtao Zhao, Yingxue Guan, Li Wang, Shijie Zhao, Yuhang Zhang, Shengkai Zhang, Qing Wang, Ziying Song

entry.summary: FastRoverVLA decouples visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution in off-road VLA driving models, maintaining decoded plans between visual predictions via a training-free interface. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion and advanced incrementally, reducing expensive multimodal inference frequency while correcting for vehicle motion.

entry.title: A Control-Theoretic Approximation to Predictive Coding Dynamics

author.name: Ryan Fayyazi, Kyle Daruwalla, Mitra Javadzadeh

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that deep feedback control (DFC) arises as a local approximation to predictive coding (PC) dynamics near fixed points, establishing exact equivalence in shallow linear networks and characterizing deviations with depth, nonlinearity, and distance from equilibrium. It connects two biologically plausible alternatives to backpropagation within a control-theoretic framework. The analysis clarifies the previously murky relationship between these local-learning methods.

entry.title: AURA: AUdio-dRiven streaming Avatar

author.name: Nathaniel Cohen, Nicolas Dufour, Am\'elie Royer, Alasdair Newson, Patrick P\'erez

entry.summary: AURA is an audio-driven streaming video diffusion model that generates talking-avatar video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the current audio chunk rather than multi-second look-ahead.
