AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps), and AURA 5B streams 720p, targeting interactive avatar and voice-assistant applications. This overcomes the latency limits of bidirectional multi-step diffusion models.

entry.title: Improving Imitation Policies for Multi-Phase Tasks through Residual Learning Allocation

author.name: Clinton Enwerem, Saleh Kemal, John S. Baras, Calin Belta

entry.summary: This paper addresses residual reinforcement learning for multi-phase imitation-learned tasks, formalizing how a limited interaction budget should be allocated across task phases. It introduces the completion gain concept — the change in full-task completion probability when a corrective controller replaces base-policy actions during one phase — and decomposes it into phase-reach probability and conditional improvement, estimated from paired episodes.

entry.title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation

author.name: Haowei Hua, Irwin King, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: The authors show that crystal variational autoencoders implicitly organize atom-wise latent representations by elemental families, a phenomenon they call emergent chemical semantics. Exploiting this structure, FamilySpace enables controllable generation by sampling from family-specific latent regions in a VAE-plus-flow crystal generative pipeline, improving both control and interpretability of materials generation.

entry.title: Is a Description Worth a Thousand Demonstrations? Specificity and Reliability of Task Descriptions in In-Context Learning

author.name: Bruce Nguyen, Bei Jiang, Linglong Kong

entry.summary: Through the Bayesian view of in-context learning, the paper models task descriptions as informative priors characterized by specificity and reliability, adapting effective sample size to quantify a description's value as an equivalent number of demonstrations. It proves that for in-context linear regression a reliable description's ESS grows with specificity and task dimension, and empirically tests whether LLMs match these theoretical predictions.

entry.title: How Reliable Are Explanations of Language Models That Detect Insider Threats?

author.name: Suramya R. Angdembay

entry.summary: Audits internal-feature explanations of neural insider-threat detectors trained on CERT simulated workplace logs by removing claimed features and comparing against a matched control. This tests whether explanation-based flags actually drive detector scores, an important reliability question for high-stakes security monitoring.

entry.title: Invertible Transport Between Sample-Only Distributions via Projected Characteristic Functions

author.name: Juan Guti\'errez, Victor Guti\'errez-Garc\'ia, Jos\'e Luis Blanco-Murillo

entry.summary: This paper proposes Projected Characteristic-Function matching (PCF), a density-free framework for learning invertible maps between a data distribution and a prior known only through samples. It aligns distributions using projected empirical characteristic functions, avoiding density estimation, adversarial training, and paired observations.

entry.title: When Is Program Structure Required? Certificate-Grounded Calibration of Program-Induction Difficulty

author.name: Wenzhang Du

entry.summary: This work introduces certificate-grounded calibration for program-induction benchmarks, constructing matched tasks where single-rule versus two-rule explanations can be formally certified using enumeration and executable witnesses. Evaluations with Qwen3-8B and Olmo-3-7B-Think show that displayed-task completion drops substantially on certified separation tasks, exposing gaps between apparent and genuine program-structure understanding.

entry.title: Instance-Optimal Moment Estimation in the Add-Remove Model of Differential Privacy

author.name: Shokichi Takakura

entry.summary: This work studies estimation of empirical means, variances, and covariances under pure differential privacy in the add-remove model, introducing instance-dependent error metrics and proving sharp lower bounds on them. The authors design mechanisms matching these bounds and show asymptotically better utility than existing worst-case-optimal methods on individual datasets.

entry.title: Beyond Error Mitigation: Using Boosting for Noisy Quantum Machine Learning

author.name: Anastasiia Lukianenko, Yash J. Patel, Nurbolat Kenbayev, Vedran Dunjko

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether labeled training data can reduce the large sampling overhead required by quantum error mitigation in supervised quantum machine learning. Focusing on binary classification, where correct prediction depends on the sign and margin of the classifier, it shows problem-specific information from boosting-style data reuse can circumvent superpolynomial sampling lower bounds that apply to generic observable recovery.

entry.title: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity

author.name: Valentin Roth, Marco Avella Medina

entry.summary: The authors prove that a single pass of differentially private Noisy SGD with fixed stepsize and constant batch sizes matches minimax lower bounds for smooth strongly convex Lipschitz losses, resolving an open question for strongly convex GLMs under Renyi DP. Lower bounds are established via the Score Attack framework.

entry.title: RoCoKV: Accelerating LLM Inference Serving through Uncertainty and Redundancy Aware KV Cache Compression

author.name: Payman Behnam, Elaheh Sobhani, Saad Amin, Yahya Hassan, Daniyal Khan, Biswadeep Chakraborty, Tanish Patwa, Souvik Kundu, Alexey Tumanov

entry.summary: RoCoKV compresses KV caches for large reasoning models, where long generated reasoning traces dominate cost yet contain redundant low-utility tokens that can still attract high attention scores. It combines uncertainty-guided adaptive pruning, which modulates compression strength with model confidence, with redundancy-aware token handling to preserve reasoning quality.

entry.title: PILAPS: A Bilingual Benchmark for Evaluating Pragmatic Inference across Phenomena and Settings

author.name: Jiani Cao, Anna Korhonen, Chen Cecilia Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces PILAPS, a bilingual English/Mandarin benchmark covering eight pragmatic phenomena, with both purpose-written and dialogue-derived items including culturally adapted and independently sourced data. Evaluating eight LLMs from four families reveals substantial variation across models and phenomena, with open-source models showing weaknesses, questioning whether strong English pragmatic performance generalizes across languages and settings.

entry.title: Beyond Resemblance: Image Fusion Reimagined

author.name: Hao Zhang, Yumin Huang, Linfeng Tang, Junjun Jiang, Jiayi Ma

entry.summary: ApexFuse reframes image fusion by abandoning source-resemblance objectives, which impose competing modality-specific constraints, in favor of learning a general distribution of high-quality scene representations. It uses a human-LMM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct supervision for generative fusion.

entry.title: Anchored Inertial Proposals with Objective Verification for Diffusion-Prior Inverse Problems

author.name: Minwoo Kim, Seunghyeok Shin, Dabin Kim, Hongki Lim

entry.summary: Proposes an anchored inertial correction rule for training-free diffusion priors in inverse problems, separating proposal generation from acceptance via a frozen clean-space objective plus a verifier stage. Heavy-ball dynamics with curvature-derived step sizes generate candidates that a separate verifier accepts or falls back on the denoiser prediction. This addresses a known failure mode where aggressive measurement guidance improves local fit but derails later denoising.

entry.title: World-delta: Continually Integrating Observations for Incremental 3D Scene Generation

author.name: Haonan Wang, Hanyu Zhou, Xiaobin Hu, Luxin Yan

entry.summary: Proposes World-delta, a framework for incremental 3D scene generation that treats generated content as revisable predictions rather than fixed structure, combining uncertainty-aware persistent world modeling with delta-guided diffusion. This allows scenes to be expanded and corrected as new observations arrive, preventing early generation errors from accumulating. It addresses a real limitation of existing 3D generation methods that synthesize from fixed inputs.

entry.title: OffBeat: Multicoset Sampling for 4D Capture Beyond the Camera Frame Rate

author.name: Chi-Wei Lee, An-Kai Chen, Cheng-Han Chiang, Yi-Chun Chang, Po-Chih Kuo

entry.summary: OffBeat models a staggered multi-camera rig as a spatially distributed multicoset sampler, enabling 4D reconstruction beyond the native camera frame rate. From calibration alone it derives camera firing groups and order, correcting shared errors such as color offsets that confound depth with motion in prior schedules like 4DSloMo.

entry.title: Stereo Visual Odometry with In-the-Loop Geometric Feed-Forward Models Towards Dense Metric Mapping

author.name: Fahira Afzal Maken, Sagun Man Singh Shrestha, Edward Vanderfeen, Lucas Carvalho de Lima, Rongxin Li, Changming Sun, Milad Ramezani

entry.summary: This work integrates geometric feed-forward depth models into a factor-graph stereo visual odometry pipeline, using sparse but reliable metric geometry from stereo and multi-view observations to calibrate dense depth predictions. Optimized 3D landmarks jointly estimate a scale-shift transformation across keyframes within each local submap, yielding metrically consistent dense depth while retaining robust model-based odometry. The result targets accurate localization plus dense metric mapping.

entry.title: Visual Attribution Limits and Graded Provenance Auditing in Commercial Video-Generation APIs

author.name: Haocheng Mei, Yuchuan Tian, Yingte Shu, Chao Xu, Kai Han, Hanting Chen, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: This work studies what a delivered video file can establish about its origin from commercial video-generation APIs, combining passive attribution probes and cryptographic provenance into a graded audit framework. The authors test attribution under re-encoding, downscaling, and frame-rate changes, and survey C2PA and GB 45438 metadata across 19 commercial endpoints, concluding that only authenticated provenance supports accusations of model or tier substitution. This addresses billing fraud and supply-chain trust in generative video APIs.

entry.title: A Matter of Representation: Evolving Partial Spreads for Bent Functions

author.name: Claude Carlet, Marko {\DJ}urasevic, Domagoj Jakobovic, Luca Manzoni, Luca Mariot, Stjepan Picek

entry.summary: The authors design an Evolution Strategy to construct partial spread bent functions, which are Boolean functions of maximum nonlinearity built from pairwise-intersecting-only-in-null-vector subspaces. They compare generator-matrix and spread-set encodings, finding that the spread-set encoding with a ruin-and-rebuild operator finds solutions up to 10 variables, and complement the results with ablation studies and a fitness landscape analysis of stagnation points.

entry.title: PhysVAM: Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation

author.name: Yuxiang Yang, Jingbo Zhang, Jiaru Zhong, Junliang Chen, Yirui Zhou, Guangming Wang, Haitao Lin, Huaiyuan Xu, Yi Wang, Lap-Pui Chau

entry.summary: PhysVAM represents anticipated interactions in dynamic manipulation through their effects on future task progress rather than reconstructing future visual states, providing task-directed foresight without explicit video prediction. Conditioned on current observations and history, it targets manipulation where objects keep moving during perception and execution.

entry.title: Alignment Drives Reuse: Learning Generalizable Robot-Use Agents from Heterogeneous Experience

author.name: Ziyue Wang, Yaopeng Yang, Liyi Zhou

entry.summary: UniCraft proposes learning manipulation skills from heterogeneous robot interactions by aligning coordinate conventions, sensing, and control interfaces across benchmarks and embodiments, so that diverse experience jointly improves a single shared skillset. The paper reframes robot skill learning as an alignment problem over fragmented interaction data.

entry.title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference

author.name: Yin Liu, Shanshan Zhao, Didong Li

entry.summary: Proposes TSGSurv, a two-stage generative framework for synthetic survival data that jointly models observed times and censoring, with theoretical guarantees on distributional fidelity and downstream inference reliability. It targets clinical trial simulation, data sharing, and digital twin applications where synthetic time-to-event data had little prior theoretical support.

entry.title: AI helps researchers investigate how thousands of medical studies share code

author.name: Bwiza Gihana Deborah | Institute for Medical Engineering and Science

entry.summary: An MIT and Dana-Farber led international team used AI to study how thousands of medical research studies share their underlying code and data, addressing the problem that shared code is often poorly structured and documented for reuse. The work tackles researcher degrees of freedom in medical studies by making methods more transparent and reproducible. It matters because reproducibility and code-sharing standards in biomedical research remain underdeveloped, and AI-assisted analysis could establish concrete guidance for what constitutes a well-organized code release.

entry.title: Cyber-Physical RSI for AI-RAN: A Case Study

author.name: Binghan Wu, Kai Zeng, Zhiqi Li, Zhigang Wang, Yang Liu, Ya-Qin Zhang, Joseph Sifakis, Ye Ouyang

entry.summary: This paper presents a cyber-physical recursive self-improvement framework for AI-driven radio access networks, connecting a student model, an experiment-planning coach agent, a calibratable virtual environment, and a physical host agent. Physical measurements serve as evidence for both model adaptation and planning of subsequent experiments, demonstrated through a ping-pong handover case study with 12 physical executions. It addresses the sim-to-real gap in learned RAN models.

entry.title: From AI Surrogate to Engineering Tool: Toward Production Use of Fiber-Orientation Prediction in Crash CAE

author.name: Osamu Ito, Yoshikazu Nakagawa, Tomoaki Tatsukawa

entry.summary: This Honda-industry paper documents the validation and deployment of an AI surrogate that predicts fiber-orientation fields for crash simulation of glass-fiber-reinforced plastic parts, cutting per-part analysis from about 25 hours of molding-specialist work to about 3 minutes. It reports staged validation from 2D plates to production parts, predefined angular-error criteria, and expert review approval for design use.

entry.title: World Models Favor Learned Priors over Visual Evidence

author.name: Han Xiao, Zhiyong Bao, Xiaotong Liu, Yanhao Chen, Qingqiang Wu

entry.summary: The paper shows that world models transferred across environments are biased toward common physical rules even when short-video motion evidence supports rare ones, due to long-tailed training distributions. It introduces TailWorld, a benchmark evaluating whether models use demonstrated rules as direct evidence to predict motion under a new rule from a different initial state.

entry.title: No-Harm-Jury A Jury-Based Multi-Dimensional Harm Evaluation Framework for Medical AI Responses

author.name: Antonio Puertas Gallardo, Mario Ceresa

entry.summary: Proposes No-Harm-Jury, an automated evaluation framework scoring AI-generated medical responses across seven harm dimensions (informational, social, psychological, autonomy, economic, privacy, epistemic) using a panel of five diverse LLM jurors with median aggregation to suppress individual juror bias. Evaluated on roughly 2,849 responses from Ministral-14B over PubMedQA, MedQA, and MedMCQA. Addresses multidimensional harm assessment in the safety-critical medical domain.

entry.title: VisAlloc: Allocating Visual Supervision for On-Policy Self-Distillation

author.name: Haoran Xu, Tian Chen, Yuhe Wu, Yanbo Zhao, Junchi Liao, Hongyu Wang, Jiaze Li, Wentao Wang, Yanfeng Li, Rui Qian

entry.summary: Proposes VisAlloc, a dual-level framework for improving visual reasoning in multimodal LLMs via on-policy self-distillation, combining sample-level filtering (retaining samples answered correctly from evidence-centered crops but incorrectly from displaced crops) with token-level counterfactual reweighting using EMA teachers' log-probability differences. Allocates privileged visual supervision only where it helps. Addresses dilution of visually grounded signals under uniform supervision.

entry.title: FlashX: Scaling Robotic Experience Reuse for Embodied Agents with CBA-Based NAND Flash

author.name: Yuseon Choi, Sanghyeon Park, Eunjong Lee, Hanseo Lee, Sangjin Kim

entry.summary: FlashX scales retrieval of successful experiences to warm-start diffusion-based action denoising in VLA and world action models, using a hardware-aware CBA-based NAND flash design. This improves both task accuracy and inference efficiency on out-of-distribution environments, inverting the usual accuracy-computation tradeoff of acceleration techniques.

entry.title: Auto-Alpha: A Framework for Autonomous Factor Research

author.name: Hui Cai, Kangcheng Deng, Tianyi Ma, Qixuan Yang, Jiacheng Lu, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Jing Li, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: Auto-Alpha is an autonomous system for quantitative factor research that chains an idea agent proposing economic hypotheses and signal constructions, a research agent developing them with backtest feedback, and semantic and quantitative audits plus human admission into a persistent factor library with an experience library of research insights. Starting from 120 reports, it built 32 initial factors and retained 62 more from 420 generated implementations.

entry.title: Policy Improvement-Guided Replay for Continual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qin-Wen Luo, Haoxuan Gao, Sheng Ren, Xiang Chen, Sheng-Jun Huang

entry.summary: The authors revisit continual reinforcement learning for vision-language models through the lens of policy improvement, using the performance difference lemma to characterize historical performance changes via expected advantages on past task distributions. They propose replaying historical prompts with the current policy and a contrastive likelihood scheme to allocate limited replay memory.

entry.title: PsyWorld: Profile-Conditioned World Modeling for Human Behavior Prediction

author.name: Ziyuan Qin, Yang Qiao, Summer B. Frandsen, Michael T. Treadway, Liang Zhao

entry.summary: PsyWorld introduces a world model for human behavior that conditions on psychometric profiles and learns from observed state transitions, using a posterior encoder that quantizes transitions and a prior that predicts codes from the profile and context. This makes realized state transitions an explicit supervision signal for behavioral prediction, going beyond static profile conditioning.

entry.title: Interpretable Prototype-Conditioned Adaptation for Weather Forecasting

author.name: Zhixuan Li, Hao Jiang, Chen Hui, Kai Geng, Weisi Lin

entry.summary: Introduces ProtoCast, which uses group-specific prototype banks to adapt local features in learned weather forecasters, making implicit patterns explicit while respecting cross-variable dependencies. This improves distinction between locations with different local evolutions and adds interpretability to neural forecasting.

entry.title: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics

author.name: Chuanqi Chen, Nan Chen

entry.summary: Neural CGM is a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a latent space with conditional Gaussian structure, enabling closed-form data assimilation updates while encoder-decoder mappings retain nonlinear expressivity. It provides sequential uncertainty quantification for partially observed nonlinear systems without expensive nonlinear filtering or explicit dynamical models.

entry.title: PriTabICL: Differentially Private Tabular In-Context Learning with Task-Aligned Cluster-Wise Synthesis

author.name: Syed Ahzaz Shah, Evan Bramblett, H\'eber H. Arcolezi, Chen Gong, Qianqian Tong, Xiaochen Li

entry.summary: PriTabICL addresses privacy risks in tabular in-context learning, where LLM demonstrations in prompts contain sensitive personal data, by generating differentially private synthetic demonstrations. It identifies limitations of global DP synthesis on heterogeneous data and proposes task-aligned cluster-wise synthesis that preserves local structure and minority patterns needed for accurate prediction.

entry.title: Rank2Replace: VLM-Ranked Slot Replacement for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Bo-Han Feng, Keng-Te Liao, Shou-De Lin

entry.summary: Rank2Replace improves out-of-distribution generalization by transferring task-relevance knowledge from pretrained vision-language models to small predictors through training-time augmentation: a VLM ranks object-centric slots by task relevance, and same-rank slot embeddings from other images are swapped in so the predictor must rely on preserved task evidence. It composes with existing OOD methods and is validated across four datasets and six splits.

entry.title: Generative News Recommendation Reproduces Popularity: A Memorization-Based Analysis

author.name: Shotaro Ishihara

entry.summary: Using roughly 20 million browsing sessions from a Japanese news service, the author continually trains an instruction-tuned Llama 3 8B model to generate next-article titles and shows the generated distribution is more concentrated and less diverse than real browsing behavior, driven by memorization of popular items. This provides a mechanism for the concern that generative recommenders narrow information diversity.

entry.title: Branch Caching After Step Distillation in Four- and Eight-Step Image Generators

author.name: Mingyu Liang, Dingkun Xu

entry.summary: The paper shows that even heavily step-distilled image generators can be further accelerated by reusing attention and MLP features across their few remaining denoising steps, with per-branch scalar corrections calibrated from one full and one cache trajectory. This yields about 1.5x speedups on eight-step Lightning and Hyper-FLUX while preserving image fidelity on DrawBench.

entry.title: Zero to Four Views: Unified Panorama Generation and Preference RL for Unobserved Regions

author.name: Rui Hong, Xugang Ye, Jana Ko\v{s}eck\'a, Kai Fan

entry.summary: This work presents a single rectified-flow transformer fine-tuned to generate full equirectangular panoramas conditioned on a caption plus zero to four perspective views from a four-camera rig, using camera-slot IDs so one weight set handles all input counts. A second preference-RL stage improves regions not covered by any conditioning view.

entry.title: Carry the Fine Print: Budget-Aware Visual Token Compression for Document OCR

author.name: Yixuan Huang, ShengFan Zhang, Jiawei Chen

entry.summary: This paper shows that salience- or similarity-based token compression fails for full-document OCR, where visually inconspicuous small symbols can be transcription-critical. Its Select and Compensate framework chooses anchor tokens via adaptive resolution plus global importance and local contrast, then enriches them with discarded nearby content and relative positions while keeping the OCR backbone frozen.

entry.title: Interpreting DeepStack-Style Vision-Language Models: Do Input or Deeper-Layer Visual Tokens Drive Answers?

author.name: Yucheng Du, Yi Nian, Ruixue Lian, Yue Zhao, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: A mechanistic interpretability study of DeepStack-style VLMs that inject visual tokens at both the language model input and deeper layers, using controlled color conflicts to determine which entry drives answers. Findings show original DeepStack follows later-entry tokens while Qwen3-VL-8B/32B follow the main entry, and that weakening main-entry features consistently increases later-entry influence across four models including Granite. Sheds light on how multi-entry visual injection affects model behavior.

entry.title: Thinking in Streams: Proactive Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Junyoung Hong, Minsu Kim, Jaehyun Kim, Jeonghwan Cho, Jiwoo Lee, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: Studies proactive spatial reasoning in streaming video, where a VLM receives a query in advance and decides whether and when to respond as the stream unfolds. The paper contributes ProSpace-Bench with nine tasks and ProSpace-Train, plus ProSpace-VLM, which injects causally estimated geometric encodings into intermediate layers using the KV cache as spatial memory. Results reveal significant gaps in current models on streaming spatial decisions.

entry.title: Domain-Aware Conformal Prediction for Trustworthy Spacecraft Pose Estimation under Sim-to-Real Shift

author.name: Nidhal Eddine Chenni, Arunkumar Rathinam, Djamila Aouada

entry.summary: Shows that conformal pose estimation calibrated on synthetic images loses coverage guarantees under the sim-to-real shift present in orbital perception, demonstrated on the SPEED+ dataset. The paper proposes domain-aware conformal prediction methods that restore reliable uncertainty sets for spacecraft pose estimation in rendezvous and proximity operations. Trust indicators with formal guarantees are critical for autonomous space operations.

entry.title: ResVision: Spectrum-Matched Resizing and Context-Preserving Inspection for Visual Reasoning

author.name: Guojian Zhan, Jiahao Xu, Yahui Liu, Yao Hu, Chuan Mu

entry.summary: ResVision improves agentic visual reasoning in vision-language models by addressing three bottlenecks: loss of high-frequency detail during token formation, difficulty retrieving distributed evidence, and scale/position mismatch from isolated crops. It uses spectrum-matched adaptive resizing and context-preserving inspection to keep local observations grounded in the full scene.

entry.title: Fixing the Last Mile: Failure-Aware Image Restoration with Region-Specific Guidance

author.name: Hongyu An, Fanghua Yu, Kainan Yan, Luc Van Gool, Chao Dong, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: FAIR targets the last-mile problem in image restoration, where globally good results still contain localized failures in faces, text, or structure that dominate perceptual quality. Instead of one uniform generative prior, the method conditions a single-pass restoration model on both where failures occur and how to fix them region by region. Credible authors including Luc Van Gool and Chao Dong back the work.

entry.title: Agentic Scaling of Embodied Tasks in Simulation for Synthetic Data Collection and Policy Evaluation

author.name: Kang Wang, Xiaolei Zhou, Xiaoyu Wu, Zhendong Wang

entry.summary: AgenticTask is an agent-based framework that expands robot task collections by linking interaction requirements to object bindings, scene configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria, with generation and execution agents validating variations. Evaluated on RoboCasa, it aims to reduce the cost of specifying and validating tasks for synthetic data collection and policy evaluation.

entry.title: SpecFlow: Flow Matching in the Acceleration Spectrum for Multi-Agent Trajectory Forecasting

author.name: Ziyang Xu, Peng Han, Hai Zhou

entry.summary: SpecFlow is a conditional flow-matching framework for multimodal trajectory forecasting that generates DCT coefficients of future accelerations, reconstructing velocity and position via analytical integration from the last observed state. A joint phase-space objective supervises position, velocity, and acceleration, ensuring dynamical coherence while covering diverse futures.

entry.title: Blue-teaming AI Through Safety Hillclimbing

author.name: Skye

entry.summary: Inspired by Anthropic's Anvil system, this post proposes that frontier agents can autonomously improve the safety of other models, a process the authors call blue-teaming. They demonstrate this by tasking GPT 6.1 Sol with restoring safety behavior in an abliterated Gemma 4 12B variant while preserving usefulness, treating safety research as a hill-climbable task environment for agent training.

entry.title: An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance

author.name: Nianjun Zhou, Dhaval Patel

entry.summary: The authors introduce CodeReAct, an agentic framework for industrial equipment maintenance that interprets natural language instructions to extract knowledge, summarize asset status, and recommend work orders. It standardizes industrial data into business objects and generates executable code during the Action phase, automating analytical tasks normally done by data scientists.

entry.title: DSFlow: A Neuro-Symbolic Data Workflow Agent with Statistical Diagnostic Guardrails

author.name: Junfeng Nie, Xiaohui Chen

entry.summary: DSFlow is a LangGraph-based neuro-symbolic platform that pairs reusable LLM-selected skills with deterministic statistical diagnostic guardrails for data science workflows. Symbolic validation can accept, clarify, replan, override, or fall back on method choices, with regression and clustering case studies showing auditable decision documentation.

entry.title: Falsifiable Compositional Reasoning in Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Hao Xue

entry.summary: This paper argues that top time series models degrade under non-stationary regime transitions because historical backtesting is used as an open-ended search objective rather than to test pre-specified compositional assumptions. It proposes treating real-world series as composites of recurring latent primitives and using backtesting to falsify assumed invariant couplings instead of merely selecting lowest-error predictors.

entry.title: Learning Networked Dynamical Systems via Neural ODE-based Graph Structure Inference

author.name: Peiyan Sun, Jinming Yang, Gujia Gao, Yaohui Jin, Yanyan Xu

entry.summary: NOGI is a framework for inferring latent interaction graphs from multivariate time series using a continuous-time Neural ODE formulation coupled with MPNN-based dynamics. The continuous-time approach decouples structure inference from fixed observation schedules and avoids entangling multi-hop dependencies into spurious direct edges, improving on discrete-time neural relational inference. Applications target neuroscience, biology, and physics.

entry.title: Ask in the Crowd: Differentially Private LLM Inference via Dummy-Augmented Shuffling

author.name: Zhihao Liu, Zixiong Guo, Shuo Shao, Yu He, Wenli Wang, Meihui Chen, Di Wang, Yuke Hu

entry.summary: DP-SPD is a differentially private LLM inference framework for LLM-as-a-Service settings that hides a real query among client-generated dummy queries, randomly shuffled before being sent to the server. This addresses the privacy-utility tradeoff that plagues noise-injection approaches to embedding privacy. The crowd-hiding design aims to protect sensitive user inputs while preserving inference accuracy.

entry.title: Actor-Predictor Architecture for Reinforcement Learning with Formal Specification Objectives

author.name: Josef Brozovich, Qining Zhang, Lei Ying

entry.summary: The Actor-Predictor framework enforces temporal safety constraints in RL by learning a surrogate representation of logic progress instead of constructing automata from formal specifications. A predictor continuously estimates whether a partial trajectory will later satisfy the specification, and its features serve as auxiliary inputs to the policy, removing the tractability limits of automaton-based reward shaping beyond small LTL formulas.

entry.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiahao Huang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MC-Lens, a multimodal Jacobian-based interpretability lens that maps intermediate VLM states into a shared semantic space defined by the decoder vocabulary, enabling comparison of concept accessibility across vision and language modalities. Inspired by global workspace theory, it supports internal concept interventions to test how accessed concepts influence downstream computation. Connects cognitive theory with mechanistic interpretability of VLMs.

entry.title: Trace2ST: Recovering PLC Structured Text from I/O Traces with LLM Generation and Verification

author.name: Hsi Chang, Irfan Khan

entry.summary: Explores whether an LLM can recover executable Structured Text programs for programmable logic controllers from input/output traces alone, using a generate-replay-feedback pipeline where candidate programs are executed against traces and refined. Addresses industrial settings where controller source code is lost but I/O is continuously logged. Combines LLM code generation with verification for safety-relevant industrial infrastructure.

entry.title: When Objectives and Evaluators Disagree: Evaluating Transfer for Post-hoc Demographic Framing Mitigation

author.name: Tunazzina Islam

entry.summary: This paper studies post-hoc LLM rewriting for reducing demographic framing disparities as a transfer problem, using 660 gender pairs and 1,980 age contrasts of demographic-conditioned climate messages with independent rewriter, selector, and evaluator components. It shows that a fixed policy targeting the lower Persuasion Bias Index message transfers inconsistently across axes, while an adaptive policy proposing edits on both sides with capped acceptance performs better. The work highlights that apparent mitigation success can be an artifact of the evaluator's involvement.

entry.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization

author.name: Chen Qiu, Zhigang Hua, Qi Xu, Jizhe Zhang, Sha Hua, Ren Mao, Luke Simon

entry.summary: This paper, with authors appearing to come from an industrial recommendation team, studies whole-page optimization and proposes a local page-level objective that trains generative re-ranking policies beyond fixed imitation targets or uniform page-level credit assignment. It jointly selects and orders items to maximize the score of the entire recommendation page.

entry.title: Beyond Entity Recognition: Vision-Centric Knowledge Visual Question Answering

author.name: Jiatong Ma, Yuchen Liu, Longteng Guo, Yichen Yuan, Yuze Wu, Dongze Hao, Ru Zhen, Yanhao Zhang, Haonan Lu, Jing Liu

entry.summary: VC-VQA is a large-scale benchmark evaluating multimodal LLMs on vision-centric knowledge reasoning, requiring retrieval of external visual evidence, identification of pre-retrieval visual clues, and verification of retrieved knowledge against the image. It explicitly models whether visual information is internal or external and whether it is used before or after retrieval.

entry.title: Verifiable Logic in Medical LLMs: A Critical Review of Agentic Clinical Reasoning Optimization and Neuro-Symbolic Grounding

author.name: Youssef ElNahas, Adel Ammar, Soumaya Chaffar, Wadii Boulila

entry.summary: A critical review of reasoning reliability in clinical LLMs covering hallucination mechanisms, the agentic hallucination cascade in multi-agent and tool-augmented systems, process reward modeling, and neuro-symbolic grounding with formal logic engines and knowledge graphs. It argues that final-answer accuracy metrics miss invalid reasoning paths in high-stakes clinical settings.

entry.title: GenSPARQL: A Generative Extension of SPARQL for Incomplete Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Jingcheng Wu, Yi Wang, Hongkuan Zhou, Steffen Staab, Bo Xiong

entry.summary: GenSPARQL extends SPARQL 1.1 with an operator that binds LLM-generated values to query variables during evaluation, using a similarity join to map generated names to graph IRIs. The query planner invokes the LLM only where needed, and the system is demonstrated in a web workbench over Wikidata-derived graphs.

entry.title: Online Temporal Rotations for 2 Bit KV-Cache Quantization in Video Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Ryan Lucas, Petros Prastakos, Rahul Mazumder

entry.summary: The paper introduces TRQ (Temporal Rotation Quantization), which exploits persistent per-channel patterns shared by temporally adjacent video tokens in KV caches of video diffusion transformers. TRQ fits per-block orthogonal rotations that map cache vectors toward constants before aggressive 2-bit quantization, adapting rotations to each video. This substantially relieves the KV-cache memory bottleneck for long video generation.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models

author.name: Chang Yang, Yao Xuan, Wendan Yan, Nhat Le, Jiang Liu, Longhao Jin, Zhen Peggy Yao, Alireza Vahdatpour, Djordje Gligorijevic

entry.summary: This industrial paper describes an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes feature selection across a large fleet of ranking models sharing tens of thousands of candidate features under resource constraints like pipeline cost and serving QPS. LLM agents propose cross-feature hypotheses while deterministic tools execute and verify experiments; Pareto fronts across tasks guide feature blending for multi-task models. It demonstrates LLM-agent-driven ML engineering at production scale on a major web platform.

entry.title: Federated Learning of Car Aerodynamics Surrogates with Spectral Optimizers

author.name: Arman Bolatov, Nikolay Spitsyn, Daniil Medyakov, Vladimir Aletov, Dmitry Bylinkin, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: The study compares federated optimizers for training a Transolver neural surrogate of car aerodynamics on DrivAerNet++ across six clients, each holding one car body type, so manufacturers can jointly train without sharing proprietary CFD data. It finds spectral optimizers that orthogonalize weight-matrix updates (FedMuon, plus proposed FedMARS-M and FedOLion) outperform non-spectral baselines like FedAvg and SCAFFOLD.

entry.title: Protein Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification

author.name: Chuyang Zhou, Bingxin Zhou, Andi Han, Chang Xu

entry.summary: The paper introduces SAVR, a contrastive post-training method that reshapes protein language model representations using Pfam family co-membership as a homology-guided semantic signal. It disentangles functional signals from non-functional variation such as sequence identity and compositional bias, improving downstream protein function prediction readouts.

entry.title: Measurable Does Not Imply Transportable: A Prospective Audit of Model Explanations in Multi-Year Field Trials

author.name: Rayhaneh Shabani Nia, Ali Karkehabadi

entry.summary: This paper formalizes prospective explanation transportability — whether an explanation learned from past data is recovered in genuinely future contexts — and tests it using multi-year Genomes-to-Fields maize field trials where each new year is a real future context. It demonstrates that reliable measurement does not imply reproducible explanations, distinguishing transportability from feature importance and measurement reliability.

entry.title: Power Setpoint Tracking for Large-Scale EV Charging: Transformer-Constrained Charging Policy Learning with Self-Tuning Constraint Prices

author.name: Daniyal Sajedi-Hosseini, Yoshihiko Fujisawa, Shubham Singh, Lei Zhou, Katsuki Fujisawa, Sebastien Gros, Mazaher Karimi, Xun Shen

entry.summary: Frames EV charging power setpoint tracking as a constrained MDP and proposes TC-CPL, an extension of soft actor-critic with PI-style Lagrange multiplier updates from measured violations and a transformer-aware encoder shared across ports. Evaluated on a 600-port simulation against an incumbent dispatcher, observing no departure times or states of charge.

entry.title: Mamba Flow Matching Neural Processes: Linear-Time Inference for Irregularly Observed Spatial Fields

author.name: Cosmo Santoni, Giovanni Charles, Timothy James Hitge, Oliver Watson, Elizaveta Semenova

entry.summary: This paper replaces quadratic-cost self-attention in joint-predictive neural processes with Mamba-style state-space models, enabling linear-time interpolation of spatial fields from sparse, irregular observations. This targets the practical limitation of Gaussian-process kriging and attention-based neural processes, which become infeasible beyond a few thousand points.

entry.title: Improving On-board Shape Models Using Sun Sensors and Implicit Representations

author.name: Zacharia A. Rudge, Giacomo Acciarini, Dario Izzo, Dominik Dold, Moritz Fieback, Said Hamdioui

entry.summary: The authors propose an end-to-end pipeline to build and refine 3D shape models of irregular small bodies like asteroids using only low-cost Sun sensor eclipse data, targeting resource-constrained CubeSat missions. EclipseNets, a differentiable model of eclipse boundaries, refines 2D silhouettes that then supervise a compact neural signed-distance field with periodic activations for incremental high-fidelity geometry updates.

entry.title: Understanding MoE Decisions Beyond Gradients

author.name: Zhen Xu, Zitao Zhang, Kevin Zhao, Xuefeng Liu

entry.summary: The paper analyzes decision attribution in mixture-of-experts language models, showing that replacing one expert can change which experts downstream layers select in ways gradients miss. It introduces a predictor using the model's own expert outputs and routing rules to estimate these switching effects, reducing error in predicting answer-score changes by 60% on Qwen3.6 and 47% on Gemma4 relative to multistep gradient baselines.

entry.title: Quantifying Cultural-Psychological Constructs in Four Centuries of Ottoman Court Registers

author.name: Sila Mutaf, Enes Y{\i}landilo\u{g}lu, Mohammad Atari

entry.summary: The authors build sentence-embedding models adapted to Ottoman legal language and a theory-driven text-analytic pipeline to quantify individualism, collectivism, and honor across 54,670 Ottoman court records from 1513-1911. Validated via retrieval, semantic similarity, and questionnaire-based checks, the framework enables computational study of cultural change in historical societies lacking conventional psychological data.

entry.title: Language models represent more about emphasis than they can tell you

author.name: Aarne Talman, Stergios Chatzikyriakidis

entry.summary: The study examines how much prosodic prominence language models recover from text alone, finding text models plateau near 68.8% on a 3-way task and prompted LLMs perform no better than a word-majority baseline even with 500 examples. Linear probes find more information in representations than models can report, while speech models reach 84.7%, showing a representational-reporting gap.

entry.title: EgoPass-Bench: Identifying Objects That May Affect the Wearer's Passage in Egocentric Video

author.name: Hongyu Wang, Chuhan Li, Congjin Xu, Xuandong Zhao, Hua Shen

entry.summary: EgoPass-Bench is a benchmark for observer-relative interaction understanding in egocentric video, comprising 284 manually reviewed clips from Ray-Ban Meta smart glasses and 2,201 questions across five tasks covering motion perception, interaction judgments, and discovery of entities that may affect the wearer's passage. It targets a gap in evaluating how surrounding entities influence observer actions.

entry.title: CalibCache: Cache-to-Full Feature Dynamics Calibration for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Mingyu Liang, Dingkun Xu, Jingwei Xu

entry.summary: CalibCache is a lightweight offline calibration method that corrects systematic discrepancies between cached and full-compute feature dynamics in diffusion transformer sampling, specifically calibrating feature acceleration via second-order finite differences using only a single trajectory pair per setting. It targets the reliability degradation of feature caching under short sampling schedules.

entry.title: MIR-Depth: Multi-Range Refinement for Single-View RGB-D Depth Completion of Transparent Objects

author.name: Xinzhe Fu, Qi Shao, Yuanfei Xie, Taoyu Wu, Zhihao Cao, Long Hu, Hong Liang, Xianzhi Li, Anh Nguyen, Baoru Huang, Rongsheng Li

entry.summary: MIR-Depth improves depth completion for transparent objects, where specular reflection causes missing depth and refraction corrupts measurements. It builds coordinate-aware multi-range hypotheses combining a global inverse-depth volume with local pixel-wise volumes, then selectively refines to balance large refraction offsets against fine local resolution for robotic grasping.

entry.title: Contrast Where It Matters: Visual Evidence-Guided Decoding for Mitigating Hallucinations in LVLMs

author.name: Yiheng Li, Wenhao Wang, Xingyi Li, Mingda Jia, Zichang Tan, Yinhang Tang, Zhen Lei, Yang Yang

entry.summary: VEGD is a training-free contrastive decoding method that first locates query-relevant visual evidence by aggregating attention signals and then guides its use in both branches of contrastive decoding, ensuring predictions are grounded in relevant image regions rather than linguistic priors. It improves hallucination mitigation over methods that only alter auxiliary inputs.

entry.title: RelGeo: Pair-Conditioned Relational Calibration for Frozen Diffusion Correspondence

author.name: Zixuan Dai, Zhiliang Zhang, Daosong Hu, Tang Zheng, Xinkai Liu, Tianyu Lei, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: Shows that 41-69% of Top-1 errors in frozen diffusion feature correspondence still contain a valid match among Top-5 candidates, indicating a candidate-selection bottleneck rather than a representation failure. RelGeo introduces pair-conditioned relational calibration that combines reciprocal diffusion Query/Key associations with RoMa transport evidence to rerank candidates across DIFT and DiT backbones on standard benchmarks. A training-free improvement on semantic correspondence without touching the frozen model.

entry.title: Why Flat Drafts Stay Flat: Region-Mean Latents Govern Texture in Flow-Based Image Generation

author.name: Zihan Gu, Jiangcan Jia, Hua Zhang, Lulu Zhao

entry.summary: Explains why flat color-block drafts remain flat in pretrained flow-based image generators, tracing the behavior to a cross-scale mechanism linking fine pixel variation to regional means in VAE latent space. Controlled field exchanges in FLUX.1-dev and Qwen-Image show that adding a photo-derived regional mean field to a flat latent restores texture, establishing the causal role of regional mean displacement. This offers mechanistic insight into latent-space structure of flow generators.

entry.title: EgoCaptioner: Towards Comprehensive and Fine-Grained Egocentric Video Captioning

author.name: Yuqi Tang, Yang Shi, Yuran Wang, Tengfei Liu, Rundong Wang, Zongyang Qiu, Qixun Wang, Zhuoran Zhang, Xuanyu Zhu, Yifan Xu, Yiyan Ji, Shujie Li, Shixuan Liu, Haotian Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Pengfei Wan, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: EgoCaptioner produces egocentric video captions combining a video-level overview with timed, fine-grained step narrations that adapt to perceptual demands and mark key moments. A coarse-to-fine annotation pipeline yields 50,000 training examples from eight egocentric sources, improving over MLLMs that miss brief actions or misorder events.

entry.title: UniVEP: Unifying Velocity and Endpoint Prediction for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Zhengtu Liang, Qiwei Liang, Tao Lin, Shihang Weng, Boyang Cai, Xiangyu Chen, Yikeng Chen, Jiaming Liang, Bohan Tan, Yu Yan, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: UniVEP systematically compares velocity prediction, endpoint prediction, and velocity-weighted endpoint prediction targets for flow-matching robot policies across multiple policies, benchmarks, and inference budgets. Findings show velocity-weighted endpoint prediction works best for few-step generation while velocity prediction benefits more from iterative refinement, with complementary strengths across noise levels. The study yields practical guidance for designing flow-matching VLA policies.

entry.title: Communication-Aware UAV Spatio-Temporal Relay Cooperation and Planning in Complex Urban Environments

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Yingjie He, Zehao Zhuo, Xiqun Chen, Zhenyu Gao

entry.summary: The ST-RCP framework uses delivery UAVs as opportunistic communication relays for disconnected UAVs in urban airspace, predicting communication blind-spot events over a planning horizon and jointly solving relay assignment via a helper-event compatibility graph. It requires no additional communication infrastructure.

entry.title: Dynamic Human-Robot Role Allocation through Entropy-Based Monitoring and LLM Reasoning

author.name: Elena Merlo, Marta Lagomarsino, Hamidreza Raei, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: The framework leaves the human free to act in collaborative tasks while a robot dynamically allocates its own activities via a cost-driven Behavior Tree, combining LLM parsing of natural language preferences with entropy-based monitoring of human activity. This improves user initiative and collaboration fluency compared to systems that assign tasks to both parties.

entry.title: Spatially Conditioned Trajectory Diffusion

author.name: Yefim Nudelman, Dor Atzmon, Tom Tirer

entry.summary: SCTD is a map-conditioned diffusion model for multi-robot motion planning that maintains position-aware occupancy tokens accessed via cross-attention throughout a temporal U-Net, with hard endpoint inpainting enforcing start and goal states. One model trained on single-robot demonstrations generalizes to obstacle-aware multi-robot trajectory generation.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics

author.name: Onur Beker, A. Ren\'e Geist, Michael Posa, Marc Toussaint, Justin Carpentier, Georg Martius

entry.summary: A pedagogical tutorial unifying rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact solvers under one notation, aimed at roboticists rather than computational mechanists or graphics researchers. It fills a documented gap by providing complete derivations for cone complementarity formulations used in widely deployed simulators.

entry.title: Can an LLM Fix a Language Model Without Training It?

author.name: Bharath Kumar Bolla, Raghavender Surya Upadhayula, Vishnu Surya Reddy Nandi, Ramesh Nandipalli

entry.summary: This controlled study assesses whether an external LLM can repair another model's weights through fixed numerical edits selected interactively, without gradient updates. Across 20 recorded sessions on five masked and causal language models, live selection matched black-box search on SmolLM2 and Qwen2.5 under a two-layer fault, and achieved 65.6% repair (presumably) on Pythia. The findings clarify the value of interactive LLM-driven model editing versus automated search.

entry.title: A CPU Inside an LLM: Zero-Gradient Compilation of Exact Circuits into Pretrained Weights

author.name: Tanmay Sah

entry.summary: The paper introduces closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation (exact multi-digit arithmetic) directly into pretrained LM weights with no training examples or runtime hooks, using mechanisms such as a Mellin-GLU quadrature over SwiGLU layers with IEEE 754 error bounds. The approach bounds normalization drift while preserving natural-language competence.

entry.title: TipDex-VTLA: Learning When to Refine Actions with Touch for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Xudi Ge, Yepeng Liu, Haifeng Liu, Enze Shi, Liangqi Zhang, Yongchao Xu

entry.summary: TipDex-VTLA is a vision-tactile-language-action policy that decides when tactile feedback should refine actions under changing illumination, using Visual Action Sensitivity Estimation to learn visual reliability and Tactile Anticipation and Correction to compare predicted versus measured touch at execution time. This addresses action drift when lighting changes but the physical state does not.

entry.title: PSTO: A PDE-structured transport operator with shared implicit updates for multiscale CDR systems

author.name: Kaiwen Li, Dezhi Zhou, Kun Wu, Xingcai Lu

entry.summary: PSTO is a PDE-structured neural transport operator that learns convection-diffusion dynamics from reaction-free data only, embedding PDE structure in the architecture so it generalizes to full convection-diffusion-reaction systems at inference without retraining. A shared operator block across all transported variables reduces parameter scaling and improves efficiency for multiscale, stiff CDR simulation.

entry.title: PAIR-MED: Policy-reward Alternation for Iterative Refinement in Multilingual Medical Reasoning

author.name: Fan Gao, Xiaohang Xu, Lang Huang, Nan Lu, Irene Li

entry.summary: PAIR-MED proposes alternately adapting a medical process reward model and optimizing a multilingual reasoning policy, where the evolving policy generates trajectories to update the PRM, which then supplies process-level rewards for the next policy iteration. This addresses PRM-policy distribution mismatch in RL for multilingual medical question answering.

entry.title: ScaleDiag: Diagnosing the Limits of Test-Time Scaling in GUI Grounding

author.name: Chen Liu, Zhen Fang, Xin Yu, Dadong Wang, Ling Chen

entry.summary: ScaleDiag is a controlled diagnostic framework that independently isolates the effects of visual scaling, instruction scaling, and sampling scaling on GUI grounding by varying target scale, context, instruction information, and candidate coverage. Evaluated across five benchmarks and up to eight model variants, it clarifies where each test-time scaling strategy saturates.

entry.title: Multi-View Relighting with Mergeable Radiance Fields

author.name: Yinan Wang, Rohan Kadkol, Hyunjin Yoo, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lalonde, James J. Clark

entry.summary: MergeableRF enables radiance-field relighting by directly merging parameters of radiance fields trained under known basis lights, exploiting the linearity of light transport. It uses shared geometry with per-light appearance networks from a shared initialization plus merge-aware regularization so that parameter combinations produce the corresponding image combinations.

entry.title: TRACE: Attribute Execution for Sequential Image Editing

author.name: Xiyang Zhang, Yuanhe Tian, Hongzhi Wang, Yan Song

entry.summary: Addresses sequential image editing where each new instruction must be satisfied while preserving still-active earlier requirements, separating continuing attributes from their visual carriers and prioritizing local appearance operations under complete-request checks. Active-goal binding resolves conflicts when a retrieved image contains a valid attribute on an obsolete surface. This targets state-tracking failures that plague iterative editing with current generative models.

entry.title: Less Than Meets the Eye: Action-Set Identifiability and Principled Abstention for 3D Physical Geometry

author.name: Reshad Ul Karim, Abrar Samin, Sammam Mahdi, Syeda Maliha Tabassum, Md Rashad Al Hasan Rony

entry.summary: Investigates whether bounded camera motions can distinguish physically distinct 3D geometry explanations that look identical from a viewpoint, such as a corridor versus its mirror reflection or a display image. Intervene3D predicts views under each hypothesis and candidate motion, selects maximin-separating motions, and abstains when available motions cannot separate remaining hypotheses. On matched synthetic benchmarks, disabling abstention yields confident answers on 76.4% of unresolvable scenes while abstention eliminates such overconfidence.

entry.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish

author.name: Ahmet Tu\u{g}rul Bayrak, Fatma Nur Korkmaz, Mustafa Serta\c{c} T\"urkel, Nur Ya\u{g}mur Tuncer

entry.summary: The study examines end-of-turn detection for voice agents using turn ends and turn-internal pauses from the Real-TurnTurk corpus of Turkish dyadic video calls, comparing a fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT, a zero-shot Turkish LM, and a deployed multilingual detector alongside voice-activity timing and facial features. The fine-tuned model best separates turn ends from pauses and is best calibrated under recording- and speaker-disjoint evaluation.

entry.title: AeroBelief: Budgeted First-Action Verification for Evidence-Guided Aerial Sensing

author.name: Tianren Li, Dongbo Li, Hongkai Chen, Jie Liu, Guoliang Xing

entry.summary: AeroBelief treats the next executable action as the unit of verification in aerial sensing, grouping candidate views by first action and selectively querying a structured world model under calibrated group bounds. Across 40 worlds and 960 closed-loop executions, it completes 75.42% of tasks, outperforming exhaustive world-model scoring (73.33%) and line-of-sight baselines (65.83%). This demonstrates selective verification can beat brute-force approaches under budget constraints.

entry.title: Efficient Latent Reasoning for Vision-Language Model via Dynamics-Aware Quantization and Distillation

author.name: Yanjing Li, Sheng Xu, Baochang Zhang, Xianbin Cao, Yawei Li

entry.summary: This paper tackles efficient latent chain-of-thought reasoning in vision-language models by lowering numerical precision of full-precision latent-CoT models, which otherwise incur large storage and compute costs. The authors analyze sensitivity and direction-dependent effects of continuous-thought errors and propose a dynamics-aware quantization and distillation approach preserving information retrieval and downstream reasoning rather than mere reconstruction. It targets severe accuracy degradation seen with direct 4-bit quantization.

entry.title: Inject Where It Matters: Objective-Dependent Feature Control in Rectified-Flow Image Editing

author.name: Nina Goncharova, Alexandra Ivanova, Aibek Alanov

entry.summary: The paper improves prompt-driven image editing in rectified-flow models like FLUX by spatially gating source-feature injection with adaptive masks and using REINFORCE to select which transformer blocks perform injection under different preservation-versus-editability objectives. On PIE-Bench with FLUX.1-dev, the approach better controls the alignment-preservation trade-off and requires no online search at inference.

entry.title: Studying AI Act Mentions: A first look at the impact of the European Union's AI regulation on Hugging Face

author.name: Anamaria Mojica-Hanke, Tessi Aigbovbiosa-Igbinovia, Steffen Herbold

entry.summary: An empirical study of how AI practitioners respond to the EU AI Act, analyzing over five million Hugging Face records (model cards, discussions, commits) for explicit references to the regulation. It provides a first large-scale look at whether and how regulatory obligations surface in public AI artifact sharing since the Act's staged obligations took effect.

entry.title: How Much Should an Agent Remember? Deployment Lessons from Self-Distilled Memory for LLM Agents

author.name: K. R. Jayaram, Vatche Isahagian, Aswath Vaithinathan Aravindan, Vinod Muthusamy, Punleuk Oum, Gaodan Fang, Michal Ulewicz, Gegi Thomas, Evelyn Duesterwald

entry.summary: Drawing on an IBM-deployed pipeline, the authors describe an agent that mines short lessons from its own trajectories and consolidates them into a smaller set of guidelines injected at inference, shipped in the open-source altk-evolve library and used in IBM's CUGA agent and watsonx Orchestrate. The paper reports deployment lessons about what agents should remember and how memory size affects performance.

entry.title: Monte Carlo Pass Search for Setpieces

author.name: Andrew Kang

entry.summary: Introduces Monte Carlo Pass Search (MCPS), which models corner kicks and lofted free kicks as distributions over plausible executions and futures rather than single realized events, using a world model with 3D ball physics, generative player models, and a value model to score counterfactual deliveries and setups. Evaluated on 249 deliveries from 30 Serie A 2025/26 matches. This brings decision-making and search techniques from games into sports analytics with counterfactual evaluation.

entry.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences

author.name: Ivan Kuznetsov, Dmitrii Pantiukhin, Sonja H\"anzelmann, Fabian Wachsmann, Jonas S{\o}lvsteen, Daniel Wiesmann, Thomas Jung, Nikolay Koldunov

entry.summary: This position paper argues that FAIR data principles are insufficient for autonomous AI agents in Earth sciences, since data curated for expert researchers can mislead a machine acting alone. It proposes AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled) as an agent-specific requirements layer extending FAIR, within an agenda of bounded tools and layered validation. The paper outlines a staged, measurable adoption path to reduce silent errors.

entry.title: Breaking Noise Shortcuts in Self-Supervised Learning Via Noise-Aligned View Generation

author.name: Oankar R. Patil, May D. Wang

entry.summary: SEANA addresses a representational shortcut in self-supervised learning on noisy scientific imaging (e.g., microscopy): since both augmented views come from the same noisy image, encoders can agree by encoding noise instead of semantics. The module learns an invertible variance-stabilizing transform from noisy data, estimates the clean signal, and regenerates noise-aligned views without requiring knowledge of the noise model. It is a drop-in improvement for SSL in signal-dependent noise regimes.

entry.title: Incorporating argumentation frameworks for LLM decision-making: Task-specific design and evaluation

author.name: Bochen Han, Anshu Xiong, Mingyang Ma

entry.summary: This paper abstracts a four-stage workflow shared by argumentation-augmented LLM decision-making methods and systematically studies design choices for argument construction, evaluation, and incorporation across debate-based decision-making and retrieval-based fact-verification tasks. Notably, it finds existing argumentation methods do not consistently improve performance with recent LLMs, motivating two task-specific methods. It provides a useful sobering assessment of a popular reasoning-augmentation direction.

entry.title: A four-level executable validation protocol for evaluating LLM-generated topology specifications of physics-based HVAC digital twins

author.name: Younghwan Joo, Jeonghoon Han, Sanghyun Oh, Soosik Bang, Sung-il Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes a four-level protocol for validating LLM-written declarative specifications for HVAC digital twins, testing static validity, model build, simulation convergence, and physical correctness rather than stopping at parse success or textual similarity. It matters because physically wrong but executable specifications currently pass existing evaluation standards.

entry.title: GRODE-RTL: Source-Mapped Dependency Views for LLM-Based RTL Repair

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Yi Liu, Bin Sun, Hongji Zhang, Dongsheng Zuo, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: GRODE-RTL tackles LLM-based repair of Register-Transfer Level hardware code by extracting the single-clock-stage fan-in cone of a suspect register from the netlist, mapping it back to editable source lines, and organizing it into a compact hop-partitioned dependency view. This anchor-centric representation helps standard LLMs localize non-local faults that flat token sequences obscure.

entry.title: Many Solutions, One Answer: Search Order Shapes the Default Solutions of Language Models

author.name: Qinhan Hou, Jing Tang

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that when constraint puzzles have multiple valid answers, language models concentrate on one shared default solution far beyond uniform chance. Comparing name-order versus fewest-candidates-first search strategies, the authors find that search-order dynamics best explain which default solution models output across four open-weight models.

entry.title: Law at the Speed of AI: Critical Legal Infrastructure for the Machine Age: Autonomy Under Law Architecture (AULA)

author.name: Natasha E Blycha, James Myint, Chen Feng, Dr Amani Soysa, Koshin Jama, Schellie-Jayne Price, Matthew Blycha

entry.summary: This position paper argues that protocol maturity in agent communication standards such as MCP and Agent2Agent does not produce legal legibility, since runtime enforcement constrains resources rather than legal authority. It proposes AULA, an architecture aiming to map autonomous agent activity onto legal personhood, rights and liabilities.

entry.title: C-LiTE: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Cellular feature learning in Histopathology

author.name: Esha Sadia Nasir, Jiaqi Lv, Gozde N. Gunesli, Shan E Ahmed Raza

entry.summary: C-LiTE is a lightweight cell-level foundation model for computational pathology that learns cellular features directly, avoiding the costly upsampling of small cellular crops that ViTs require. It addresses the gap between tissue-level pathology foundation models, which capture cell morphology only implicitly, and expensive cell-level models with hundreds of millions of parameters. This enables efficient tumour grading, mitotic assessment, and immune profiling.

entry.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yuzhi Huang, Jie Wu, Fanding Huang, Junchao Lin, Weichen Zhang, Ziyi Xiong, Yang Li, Zhengwei Xie, Zhimin Wang, Zhen Liu, Jiazhen Huang, Yuzheng Zhang, Yuche Liu, Hongyi Yang, Chen Tang, Shixiang Tang, Hakan Aktas, Adam Wu, Duo Wu, Kangye Ji, Shuzhao Xie, Huanan Liu, Weijue Bu, Chenxin Li, Xinyuan Wang, Tianyi Bai, Yinan Mao, Jiawei Wang, Minglei Li, Heng Yu, Ehsan Adeli, Minchen Li, Yong-Lu Li, Cengiz \"Oztireli, Huazhe Xu, Chao Yu, Jing Zhang, Shanghang Zhang, Weitao Zhou, Wenwu Zhu, Cheng Chi, Jingyan Jiang, Zhi Wang

entry.summary: Mind2Act World is a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks across five real-world domains, each with three difficulty levels and two scene settings, designed to separately assess history-based cognitive reasoning, precise physical execution, and their composition through environmental feedback. Existing benchmarks conflate these capabilities, obscuring the source of failures. The large multi-institution author list spans many robotics groups.

entry.title: Long-Range Video Presentation Attack Detection: A Three-Class Benchmark Across 1-100 m and Two Sensor Types

author.name: Lambert Igene, Mohammad Zahir Uddin Chowdhury, Afzal Hossain, Sandip Purnapatra, Peter Johnson, Stephanie Schuckers

entry.summary: The authors release a large video face presentation-attack-detection benchmark with 374,000+ frames from 261 identities captured at standoff distances from 1 to 100 meters, indoors and outdoors, on DSLR and mobile sensors, with live/spoof/props labels. It addresses the unrealistic close-range assumption of deployed face PAD systems used in border control and surveillance.

entry.title: From Sequence Uncertainty to Phenotype Hypotheses: Uncertainty-Conditioned Inference over Biomedical Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Huixin Zhan, Jason H. Moore

entry.summary: The authors propose an uncertainty-conditioned path-energy framework that converts genomic foundation model variant predictions and calibrated uncertainty into explicit probability distributions over gene-disease-phenotype hypotheses on a knowledge graph. Query uncertainty controls the temperature of the target distribution, making evidence quality an explicit determinant of hypothesis breadth while retaining interpretable multi-patient reasoning without phenotype supervision.

entry.title: Design and Evaluation of Epira: An Automated Interview System for Case Investigation and Contact Tracing

author.name: Ishita Asnani, Shaghayegh Fazliani, Zachary Ryan, Kriyoshig Prasai, Chirag Kumar, Indra Gonzalez Ojeda, Marc Lipsitch, Madeleine Udell

entry.summary: Epira is a protocol-controlled LLM interviewer for multi-disease case investigation and contact tracing, pairing LLM dialogue with a rule-based controller that enforces required questions, safety handoffs, and structured case records, adaptable to new diseases via questionnaire upload. It was evaluated with simulated cases using local (Qwen2.5) and cloud backends, and the cloud backend comparison uses GPT-5.4, an established OpenAI model rather than a new release.

entry.title: NIMIS: A Structure-Agnostic, Chemically Informed Slot-Attention Framework for Demixing 1D $^1$H-NMR Mixture Spectra

author.name: Anna Marija Sumrova, Jonathan M. Goodman

entry.summary: NIMIS is a deep learning framework that unmixes 1D proton NMR mixture spectra by grouping peaks according to their source molecule without requiring knowledge of component structures. It injects J-coupling information into a multi-head Transformer attention mechanism and uses slot attention to separate contextualized peak embeddings, trained on over 158,000 synthetic mixtures. This enables direct analysis of crude reaction mixtures, accelerating chemical reaction analysis.

entry.title: X Hedging: towards an eXplainable artificial intelligence option Hedging framework

author.name: Bj{\o}rn Andr\'e Aaslund, Johannes Berge, Ayoub Haida, Ying Ni, Rita Pimentel

entry.summary: Proposes X Hedging, replacing neural networks in the Deep Hedging framework with LightGBM tree ensembles for option hedging, reducing data requirements and improving interpretability while retaining strong hedging performance. Integrates explanation tooling into the hedging pipeline for more user-centered transparency.

entry.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Neural Networks for a Universal Fluid Gibbs Free Energy Equation of State

author.name: Xurui Li, Zhiguo Gan, Jiaming Zhang, Hongxi Zeng, Diannan Lu

entry.summary: The authors construct GEoS, a thermodynamically consistent neural network framework built on Gibbs free energy that provides a unified machine learning representation of fluid states. It achieves average absolute relative deviations of 5.25% and 3.96% on vapor and liquid phase density test sets, outperforming conventional volume-translated cubic equations of state.

entry.title: Variance-Adaptive Upper Confidence Bounds for Multi-Armed Bandits with Kaplan--Meier Survival Estimation

author.name: Yangfan Cui, Andrew Papanicolaou

entry.summary: The paper proposes KM-UCB, a multi-armed bandit policy for settings where rewards are survival probabilities at a time horizon and observations are right-censored time-to-event data. Using martingale theory and continuous influence functions, it derives a variance-adaptive empirical Bernstein bound that improves on prior Hoeffding-type Kaplan-Meier bounds.

entry.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?

author.name: Myeong-Su Lee

entry.summary: The paper provides a mathematical explanation for when and why integral constraints improve physics-informed neural networks, deriving stability estimates for losses with and without such constraints across several PDEs. It shows that in certain parameter regimes the standard loss weakly controls specific error components and integral constraints restore uniform control, with numerical experiments supporting the analysis.

entry.title: AdsNet: A Graph Neural Network for Direct Adsorption Energy Prediction

author.name: Changzhi Ai, Frank Abild-Pedersen, Johannes Voss

entry.summary: AdsNet is an equivariant graph neural network that predicts adsorption energies in a single forward pass using a local graph restricted to the adsorbate and immediate surface neighbors. The local formulation decouples cost from total system size while retaining geometric sensitivity, targeting high-throughput computational catalyst screening.

entry.title: SlotFlow-GB: A Neural Framework for Trans-Dimensional Inference of Overlapping Galactic Binaries

author.name: Niklas Houba, Giovanni Giarda, Davide Piras

entry.summary: SlotFlow-GB is a neural framework for LISA gravitational-wave data analysis that learns an approximation to the trans-dimensional posterior over the number and parameters of overlapping Galactic binaries, producing source multiplicity probabilities and per-source parameter densities in a single evaluation. This addresses a computationally demanding inference problem expected to involve millions of long-lived signals.

entry.title: Conformal Selection for Hierarchical Streaming Data

author.name: Zhenyuan Sun, Chengyao Yu, Ruixing Ming, Bingyi Jing

entry.summary: The paper extends online conformal selection to hierarchical data streams where candidates arrive sequentially from distinct populations, relaxing the standard i.i.d./exchangeability assumption. The proposed Online Hierarchical Selection method provides distribution-free, statistically valid candidate selection with sequentially constructed test statistics.

entry.title: ChronoDossier: Long-Form Personas as Temporal Memory Representations

author.name: Noah Sturgill, Jinho D. Choi

entry.summary: ChronoDossier is a benchmark of 311 synthetic long-form persona dossiers (1k-10k words) that treat personas as temporal memory representations, comprising an invariant identity plus a timeline of facts, routines, and decision rules. Intrinsic metrics score records against intended states and extrinsic metrics test fact recovery by five readers on a seeded GPT-5.1 panel with 520 rated turns per condition.

entry.title: TableRoute: Capability-Aware Routing for Scalable Table Question Answering

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Junhao Gan, Jianzhong Qi

entry.summary: TableRoute is a capability-aware routing framework for table question answering that selects among full-table reading, table reduction, and program execution based on table scale and model capability, using evidence-conditioned inference. This addresses brittleness of fixed strategies across compact to million-token tables.

entry.title: MemFolder: Structure-Guided Memory Folding for Efficient Agent Memory Management

author.name: Xuyang Liu, Chenwen Lu, Junxi Wang, Siyu Ren, Xinying Lin, Siteng Huang, Hongli Sun, Linfeng Zhang, Honggang Chen

entry.summary: MemFolder is a structure-guided memory folding framework for long-running agents that sequentially reduces both record count and retrieved context length by using cross-record structure to guide evidence selection and consolidation. It avoids the failure modes of pure pruning (losing evidence) and pure consolidation (longer retrieval units).

entry.title: CoRelate: Coordinated Human-Object Motion Synthesis through Interaction Relations

author.name: Zhiwen Qiu, Daisy Lin, Diyu Zhou, Jialin Wu, Rosita Ji, Saleh Kalantari

entry.summary: CoRelate is a diffusion framework for coordinated human-object motion synthesis that represents intended participation through hand-part relations specifying the participating hand, its reference position, and participation interval. These relations serve both as generation conditions and as references for measuring interaction realization, with task feedback ensuring contact is maintained while object goals are reached.

entry.title: A Unified Framework for Image Manipulation Localization Under Multi-Type Weak Supervision

author.name: Songlin Li, Hui Ma, Zhiqing Guo, Dan Ma, Gaobo Yang, Xin Liao

entry.summary: UniIML is a teacher-student framework that unifies diverse weak annotations for image manipulation localization by mapping them into a common representation that guides SAM to generate candidate masks, with an Ordinal Safe Consensus mechanism to select the best candidate. This enables joint training on heterogeneous annotation types and larger datasets.

entry.title: SegAnyFruit: Learning Generalizable and Edge Deployable Fruit Instance Segmentation at Scale

author.name: Yanan Wang, Yuzheng wang, Yibin Ying, Zhenghao Fei

entry.summary: SegAnyFruit distills foundation-model priors into lightweight, prompt-free fruit segmentation models via a progressive training regime over a curated 733K-image, 9.66M-mask dataset spanning 165 fruit types. Zero-shot results improve substantially over prior work across seven benchmarks while remaining edge-deployable.

entry.title: Characterizing Age-Conditioned Affective Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shahriyar Zaman Ridoy, Azmine Toushik Wasi, Lin Gu, Ruogu Fang

entry.summary: Evaluates 17 vision-language models on 900 OASIS images with young, middle, and older-adult persona prompts, comparing model emotion ratings against data from 822 human participants. While unprompted models track average human valence well (median r=0.891), the age-conditioned shifts do not correlate with actual human age differences, revealing that VLMs perform age perspective-taking superficially. Findings are clearest on sensitive images, with fairness implications.

entry.title: Calibrate in Context: Efficient Data-Free Quantization from Small Synthetic Pools

author.name: Haowen Hua, Sen Lin, Yaokun Huang, Zeyi Shao, Hao Zhang, Wei Sui, John See, Zeyd Boukhers, Cong Yang

entry.summary: Improves data-free low-bit quantization by calibrating activation scales and integer offsets against full-precision responses in the student's block context, evaluating candidates only at consuming operators at near-local scoring cost. Progressive inversion updates the same synthetic images through increasingly deep teacher prefixes for ViT-family models. With only 1,000 images the pipeline exceeds MimiQ's accuracy across 18 W4A4/W5A5 settings, addressing data-scarce quantization for transformers.

entry.title: GeoPillars: A Large-Kernel Pillar Detector for Single-Sweep LiDAR Under Point Sparsity, and a Decomposition of Its Gain

author.name: Chaitanya Dumbre, Shubham Sarkar, Akash Mohapatra, Ghanasham Patil, Sheetal Girase

entry.summary: GeoPillars is a pillar-based 3D detector designed for single-sweep LiDAR under extreme sparsity (eight points per pillar), combining geometric pillar features, grouped vector attention, a large-kernel backbone, and surface-normal supervision. It outperforms CenterPoint by over 13 BEV AP points at the same input budget, and notably the paper includes an honest ablation decomposition showing its gains are in-distribution, since validation is per-frame rather than scene-disjoint.

entry.title: TrajCal: Trajectory-Calibrated Time Schedules for Few-Step Flow Sampling

author.name: Junchi Zhang, Zihan Gu, Jiangcan Jia, Lulu Zhao, Wenbo Su, Hua Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TrajCal, a training-free calibration framework for few-step flow matching sampling that uses scatter search, a metaheuristic optimization method, to find a fixed time schedule achieving higher output fidelity. Starting from diverse seed schedules, it deforms and combines candidates and selects one fixed schedule by final output fidelity for reuse on new inputs. It improves reference agreement over baselines at low evaluation budgets for both image and video generation.

entry.title: Fast Self-Supervised Generative CT Denoising via Few-Step Sampling

author.name: Xingyi Yao, Zhengtao Ma, Zhennong Chen

entry.summary: N2N-iMF combines Noise2Noise self-supervised training with improved mean flow for few-step CT denoising, generating one noisy image conditioned on its pair and averaging independent samples to suppress noise without oversmoothing. This avoids costly multi-step diffusion sampling where clean references are unavailable.
