entry.title: Kernel Ridge Attention: Nonlinear Memory with Selective Forgetting

author.name: Haowei Chen, Yichen Wang, Congfu Xu

entry.summary: Proposes Kernel Ridge Attention (KRA), a recurrent sequence mixer that maintains a fixed-size memory via recursive ridge regression with covariance-guided updates and an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck transition for content-dependent forgetting. It offers an exact temporal-kernel interpretation, parallelizable training, and improves language-modeling quality over attention and recurrent baselines in controlled experiments.

entry.title: Probing agent overeagerness in realistic settings with continuation audits

author.name: Sean Lim, Clement Neo

entry.summary: Introduces Continuation Audits, a pipeline for probing coding-agent overeagerness (surprising or reckless actions beyond the user mandate, reported in frontier system cards) by grounding an auditor on a prefix from a real coding-agent transcript and steering the trajectory toward a seeded behavior. This avoids the synthetic setups that capable models increasingly recognize and game, and enables open-weight model evaluation without private deployment traffic. An independent-alignment-audit methodology paper.

entry.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Zhenqing Ling, Qirui Jiao, Daoyuan Chen, Cheng Chen, Xinji Mai, Haowen Gao, Zhuo Zhang, Xuchen Pan, Mengsu Ding, Jiaji Deng, Yuexiang Xie, Xiaoming Qin, Weirui Kuang, Zhaoyang Liu, Yaliang Li, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou

entry.summary: Piccolo is a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B-27B) that co-evolve capabilities and training data via agentic data engineering and recursive self-improvement, predicting probabilities over candidate answers for judgments, agent harnesses, workflows, and games. Piccolo-27B tops the Decision Index Vision Full leaderboard at 75.59, with research agents analyzing model behavior and constructing training data iteratively.

entry.title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws

author.name: Zhiyu Liu, Xinyu Yang

entry.summary: The authors rigorously test whether an LLM can audit black-box clinical prediction models by probing them through queries alone, using a blinded setup with 24 deliberately flawed copies of stroke-prediction models plus 8 clean ones. Using GPT-6 Astra, an existing frontier model, they evaluate whether the auditor can detect planted flaws such as under-predicted subgroups and reversed risk factors when ground truth is known. The work provides a rare controlled evaluation of LLM-based model auditing in a high-stakes medical setting.

entry.title: RSIBench-Infra: Can Agents Optimize Their Own Training and Inference Infrastructure at Production Scale?

author.name: Hanlin Wu, Yifei Wang, Zhicheng Cai, Huan-ang Gao, Wei-Ying Ma, Ya-Qin Zhang, Jingjing Liu, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: RSIBench-Infra is a benchmark of 20 training and inference infrastructure optimization tasks spanning model families and modalities, with deployments up to 32 accelerators on NVIDIA GPUs and Ascend NPUs, where agents can modify engine, kernel, and instruction levels from runnable baselines. An OCI image-layer protocol ensures reproducibility, targeting end-to-end rather than single-layer optimization.

entry.title: Cap-and-Track: Optimizing LLM Inference Request Dispatch Across Shifting Capacity

author.name: Benjamin Novotny, Doug Szeto, Chang Wang, Shicheng Chen, George Zhihua Yuan, Bob Kamma, Michael Ge, John Xin Zhou, Andrea Olgiati

entry.summary: Cap-and-Track is a system design for dispatching LLM inference requests across shifting provider and internal GPU capacity, using backend refusals as a fail-fast admission signal and durable priority queues to hold excess work. Meta's traffic shaper implements it in production for post and live-video understanding workloads.

entry.title: When Do LLMs Model the Right Target? Problem Formulation in High-Stakes Risk Prediction

author.name: Jennifer Zhang, Amanda Coston

entry.summary: The study evaluates whether LLMs can correctly formulate prediction problems under decision dependency, where historical decisions confound observed outcomes, across child-welfare, healthcare, and employment domains. Using 11 models from OpenAI and Anthropic under seven prompt conditions, it audits the statistical validity of LLM-generated analysis code and explanations.

entry.title: CurvDelta: Low-Curvature Delta Modeling For Surgical Learning and Unlearning

author.name: Zeguan Xiao, Zhuocheng Liang, Yun Chen, Yong Wang, Guanhua Chen, Pinyan Lu

entry.summary: Introduces CurvDelta, a framework that bakes capability-preservation constraints into the parameterization of model updates by constructing a low-curvature space where updates leave the preservation loss nearly invariant, made practical via K-FAC and factorized projection. Also proposes CurvLoRA, a low-rank variant for efficient adaptation and unlearning with preservation guarantees built into the geometry.

entry.title: Measuring and Charging for Retained Context in Long-Context LLM Services

author.name: Yi Lu, Qianshi Lin, Yumeng Yang, Hongxia Wang

entry.summary: This work examines how long-context LLM services bill repeated context, showing that current pricing weights do not reflect contribution to answer quality or true serving cost. A three-layer framework separates content relevance, observable proxies, and auditable positional weights, with measurements showing cache hits reduce repeated-prefix compute by over two orders of magnitude at 65,536 tokens. It has direct economic and policy implications for API pricing of long-context services.

entry.title: Keep the Reasoning, Read the Image: On-Demand Visual KV for Multi-Turn Reasoning VLMs

author.name: Ziyi Wang, Xiyue Zhang, Bing Hu, Guangmin Song, Chenyi Zhang, Li Wang

entry.summary: This paper identifies a critical failure in KV cache pruning for reasoning VLMs: because images and reasoning tokens share one eviction budget, growing reasoning crowds visual entries out, causing chart QA accuracy to drop from 8 to 24 points in multi-turn settings. The authors show a small protected visual reserve recovers most of the loss, and propose ShelfKV, a training-free mechanism for on-demand visual retention. This is a practical, high-leverage fix for multi-turn multimodal serving efficiency.

entry.title: VOL-Agent: Programming Your Film via Video Orchestration Language Agentic System

author.name: Hongji Yang, Yucheng Zhou, Lingting Zhu, Shengju Qian, Xinye Li, Huan Zheng, Dongyue Lu, Wei Chow, Xin Wang, Cheng-zhong Xu, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: VOL-Agent is a programmable video agent built on a Video Orchestration Language that compiles and verifies structural plans statically while loading skills dynamically at runtime. It decouples reliable story structure from flexible execution, resolving tools and user-defined skills from an open-world repository to orchestrate short clips into minute-level, story-coherent films. This pushes agentic video generation beyond brittle natural-language planning.

entry.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development

author.name: Xirui Jiang, Yuxi Chen, Rui Yang, Feng Luo, Pengcheng Wang, Bingxuan Li, Zihao Zhao, Yushan Li, Han Wang, Manling Li, Yang Zhang, Shiyu Chang, Tong Zhang, Huan Zhang

entry.summary: Game2Player co-develops game environments and playing agents at scale: a Builder agent adapts existing web games to expose internal state and define verifiable tasks, while coding and VLM player agents attempt them and report issues. This produces diverse gameplay experience with state-based success checks, addressing costly human gameplay data collection.

entry.title: LIC-Audit: How Comparable Are Reported Gains in Learned Image Compression?

author.name: Haisheng Fu, Jie Liang, Runyu Yang, Feng Ding, Xin Dong, Zixiao Jin, Jingning Han

entry.summary: Audits rate-distortion reporting practices in learned image compression, analyzing 353 released curves from 36 repositories and re-evaluating eight codec releases with 28,193 encode-decode records. Finds that changing VTM reference versions shifts BD-rates by up to 3.56 percentage points, making many published gains incomparable or misleading.

entry.title: RoboMorpher: Scaling Robot Morphology Representations for Cross-Embodiment Action Prediction

author.name: Wenwei Lin, Yan Qin, Weiliang Deng, Zixuan Li, Kaixuan Wang, Zanxin Chen, Yue Chen, Tianshuo Yang, Junting Chen, Zhixuan Liang, Yao Mu, Ximin Lyu, Renjing Xu, Ping Luo, Tianxing Chen

entry.summary: RoboMorpher is a morphology-conditioned action tokenizer that jointly reconstructs joint angles and link poses so that control coordinates are associated with their kinematic effects, addressing the problem that identical joint values mean different things on different robots. It is pretrained on 40 million morphology-state pairs using MorphGen-generated serial-arm descriptions and integrated as a frozen tokenizer into a vision-language-action policy, with a new benchmark introduced.

entry.title: Phoenix: Learning Scene Structure Representations for Generalizable World-Action Models

author.name: Yupeng Zheng, Chaoyue Li, Linbo Wang, Xiang Li, Yuhang Zheng, Xiaotong Su, Songen Gu, Yichen Zhang, Zebin Xing, Shuai Tian, Jingxiang Guo, Jing Li, Zhiyong Zhao, Zhongpu Xia, Qichao Zhang, Haoran Li, Shuicheng Yan, Dongbin Zhao

entry.summary: Phoenix learns scene-structure representations for world-action models by enriching DINOv3 features through dual-teacher distillation of geometric and spatiotemporal semantics, then compressing them with a causal VAE (CS-VAE) into generative latents that preserve spatial layout. The model jointly predicts these latents, appearance latents, and robot actions to link scene evolution with action generation for generalizable manipulation.

entry.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents

author.name: Tiancheng Bao, Riga Wu, Jan Wienhold, Sebastian Billig, Patrick Winnersbach, Hsuan-Chih Chen, Akis Giannoukos, Jiayang Li, Li Shen, Gary Weissman, Eduardo J. Mortani Barbosa Jr, Dyke Ferber, Jakob Nikolas Kather, Christos Davatzikos, Daniel Truhn, Tianyu Han

entry.summary: Decision2Care is a clinical decision agent that works up acutely ill patients without generating any free text, instead assigning probabilities to permitted EHR actions executed by fixed rules, making decisions auditable by construction. On 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases it matched a free-text agent's accuracy (86.5% vs 86.1%) at 2.2 seconds median per work-up. This demonstrates that structured, rule-governed agents can match text-based agents while solving the faithfulness-of-reasoning problem.

entry.title: 3D GameDev Arena: Benchmarking Coding Agents That Plan, Build, and Playtest extreme Long-Horizon Browser Games

author.name: Bizhe Bai, Jiliang Jian, Yuqing Yan, Tao Chen, Ying Wen

entry.summary: Introduces 3D GameDev Arena, a benchmark of 108 from-scratch 3D game development tasks across 14 genres, evaluated through an automated plan-implement-test-repair pipeline with runs averaging around 1,000 LLM calls (longest: 14,407 calls and 2.13B tokens). Evaluation covers objective correctness, code quality, and player enjoyment. Pushes coding agent benchmarks toward extreme long-horizon creative tasks.

entry.title: Ground, Iterate, Trace: Decomposing AI Research Ideation

author.name: Samson Yu, Qiran Zou, Jing Yu Lim, Rushi Shah, Anirudh Goyal, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces CAR (Creative AI Researcher), an agentic framework for research ideation that builds a semantic knowledge graph from retrieved literature and applies four conceptual operators — bisociation, analogy, exploration, elaboration — with structural acceptance checks and full traces of transformations and sources. This makes automated ideation more grounded and inspectable relative to unstructured LLM idea generation.

entry.title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents

author.name: Zhizhuo Kou, Sizai Hou, Jian Yang, Ge Sun, Junyu Luo, Wenkai Zhang, Sirui Han, Yike Guo

entry.summary: IDEA detects backdoor activation in GUI agents at inference time via an intent-evidence dominance inversion signature: on clean steps the instruction drives the action, whereas a trigger region on screen hijacks control of the decision state. This addresses supply-chain risk from downloaded open-weight GUI agents, a gap left by detectors built for image classifiers. A timely safety contribution for an emerging agent class.

entry.title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play

author.name: Akshay L Chandra, Iman Nematollahi, Lingyue Zhao, Daria Kulikova, Angela P. Schoellig, Fabien Despinoy, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: DiWALI learns and improves diffusion policies inside a world model trained on action-free human demonstrations plus robot play, inferring latent actions from consecutive frames with an inverse dynamics model and grounding them in robot commands via a separately trained decoder. Skill policies are trained over latent actions and refined with reinforcement learning in imagination, evaluated on the CALVIN benchmark.

entry.title: GUARD: Stabilizing Recursive Self-Improvement with Regret Guidance

author.name: Minghe Zhang, Xuetao Kang, Yifei Ming, Yanfei Chen, Han Yu, Yufan Zhuang, Chen-Yu Lee

entry.summary: GUARD is a closed-loop framework for grader-free recursive self-improvement of agent harnesses (prompts, skills, tool rules, memory) without weight updates. Its key insight is decomposing tasks into pre-execution self-checks and guiding harness updates via directional regret, separating what an edit newly broke from what remains unsolved. This addresses real failure modes of self-editing agents such as regression, skill forgetting, and memory bloat.

entry.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models

author.name: Wen Wang, Jindong Wang, Jiahua Bao, Tu Yongsiqi, Yihao Liu, Junwei He, Wenkui Fan

entry.summary: Presents Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), which improves RL for search-augmented language models by adding an auxiliary training signal measuring how retrieved documents increase the likelihood of a reference answer. This addresses the limitation that outcome-only rewards give identical credit to every search step and collapse when all rollouts fail. A targeted fix for a known weakness in outcome-supervised retrieval agents.

entry.title: GALA: Gallery-Level Alignment for Real-Life Vision Decoding from EEG

author.name: Philippe Forest, Giulia Lioi, Mai Pham Quyen, Alix Lamouroux, Javen Shi, Adrien Merlini

entry.summary: Proposes GALA for cross-subject EEG-based visual decoding, targeting the drop from over 80 percent intra-subject to about 32 percent unseen-subject accuracy on the THINGS-EEG-2 benchmark. It defines an incremental transductive setting where candidate outcomes form a known gallery and unlabeled user EEG accumulates naturally during device use, removing the labeled-data bottleneck for BCI deployment. A practical advance toward real-world brain-computer interfaces.

entry.title: Benchmarking LLM abilities on postdoc-level natural science problems

author.name: Alina Avanesyan, Alexey Boldyrev, Liqun Deng, Denis Derkach, Mary Godunova, Mikhail Hushchyn, Dmitry Ilvovsky, Irina Knyazeva, Irina Piontkovskaya, Dmitry Polubotko, Fedor Ratnikov, Ekaterina Trofimova, Zhenhe Zhang

entry.summary: STEMBench is a benchmark of twelve research problems in high-energy physics, astrophysics, and neuroscience, each scored by its own field's figure of merit rather than symbolic answer matching or unit tests. Each problem includes two measured anchors — a no-domain-knowledge submission and an expert reference reproducing a published method — enabling principled comparison of agent solutions against scientific standards.

entry.title: Repository-Grounded Rubrics for Execution-Free Evaluation of Coding Agents

author.name: Matej Gerek, Danylo Zahorulko, Samuel Budai, Chris Rupley, Thierry Donneau-Golencer

entry.summary: The paper adapts agentic rubrics into an execution-free evaluation measure for coding agents: an agent explores the repository before a change, writes weighted binary criteria, and a tool-free judge scores a diff by the weighted share of criteria satisfied. Validation against test outcomes on SWE-bench Verified using 7,291 labeled patches from fifteen systems shows strong ordering agreement where both resolved and unresolved patches exist. This addresses cases where tests are missing or environments are hard to build.

entry.title: Which Tokens, in What Order, and How Fast? A Theoretical Analysis of On-Policy Distillation Objectives

author.name: Hubert Strauss, Liam Fowl, Noam Razin

entry.summary: This theory paper analyzes on-policy distillation objectives for LLMs, showing how the choice between sequence-level and token-level objectives and divergence functions governs which tokens are prioritized and how fast learning proceeds. It identifies a future agreement bias in sequence-level OPD that induces a reverse learning order, which myopic token-level objectives avoid.

entry.title: Weight Space Programming for Vision Language Model Repair

author.name: Avinash Goutham Aluguvelly

entry.summary: This paper studies gradient-free repair of vision-language models where a coding agent directly edits network weights. Faults are planted in SmolVLM-256M and LFM2-VL-450M, and the agent locates corrupted projector rows and vision-encoder noise, infers unknown scale factors, and restores weights to near-original accuracy. Notably, repair programs generalize to unseen checkpoints without feedback.

entry.title: Grounding Radiology Reports in 3D Chest CT: Results of the ReXGrounding Challenge

author.name: Mohammed Baharoon, Mahmoud Hussain Alabbad, Sung Eun Kim, Xiaoman Zhang, Lucas Bijnens, Zirong Chen, Jiayu Wang, Xi Ouyang, Mingyang Yu, Weiqiu Jin, Xiaodan Ye, Dijia Wu, Kwang-Hyun Uhm, Inhwa Son, Rachel van 't Hull, Tim Veenboer, Cees Snoek, Kevin Groot Lipman, Daesung Kim, Junha Im, Youngjun Jun, Sangwon Lee, Katelyn Morrison, Adam Perer, Mijin Yun, Ali Piracha, Reem Alwasiah, Talal Yahyan, Abdulrahman Alamoudi, Mashael Alshehri, Rayan Alsager, Hannah Hancock, Anna M. Hunkem\"oller, Peter Youssef, Mona A. Alhammad, Afnan Aljumayan, Brecht Van Berkel, Eric Bijnens, Saud Alhussain, Maarten Steyvers, Rolf Symons, Bryan Eelen, Ayed Alaklubi, Maha Buraykan Alshammari, Amirah Fahad Alshammeri, Tomas Gilvydis, Ibrahim AlTurki, Monerah Almohideb, Ali Alburkani, Shahad Alhomaiani, Fatima Jabali, Maximilian Rokuss, Moritz Langenberg, Yannick Kirchhoff, Benjamin Hamm, Klaus Maier-Hein, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Sezgin Er, Michael Moritz, Hassan R. Alomaish, Luyang Luo, Pranav Rajpurkar

entry.summary: This paper reports results of the ReXGrounding Challenge at MICCAI 2026, the first challenge dedicated to segmenting each finding in a radiology report within 3D chest CT scans, enabling measurable, verifiable AI-generated reports. It used 2,992 training and 200 validation scans, with a held-out test set of 300 scans and 582 findings exhaustively annotated by board-certified radiologists, and drew 48 teams from 15 countries. The task advances verifiable medical report generation.

entry.title: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning and Out-of-Context Hallucination

author.name: Tianxiang Chen, Jingyuan Zhou, Guoyao Yang, Kaidi Yang

entry.summary: Provides a unified mechanistic study of in-context learning and out-of-context hallucination, observing that role information can be internally represented in a model without reliably constraining its output. The authors derive a first-order decomposition of role effects, showing that the influence of context depends on two factors, thereby connecting evidence faithfulness failures to ICL mechanics.

entry.title: Once Upon a Bias: Gender Stereotyping in LLM-Generated Children's Stories

author.name: Sayumi Muthukumarana, Roshan Godaliyadda, Parakrama Ekanayake, Roshan Ragel

entry.summary: A large-scale study of gender stereotyping in LLM-generated bedtime stories, analyzing 62,873 stories from 16 LLMs across 35 country settings and 12 narrator roles using matched daughter/son prompts and a five-generation design. The paper introduces a multi-level evaluation framework combining lexical rate contrasts, stereotype alignment metrics, human evaluation, and representation-level interventions. This matters because stories for children can shape perceptions of social roles.

entry.title: Harvesting Expert-Parallel Bubbles for Fine-Tuning

author.name: Oana Balmau, Saurav Banka, Jiaxuan Chen, Anne-Marie Kermarrec, Ramya Narasimha Prabhu, Rafael Pires, Mathis Randl, Martijn de Vos

entry.summary: BubbleTea is a colocation system that reclaims idle GPU time caused by load imbalance in expert-parallel MoE serving, using those bubbles (8-13% of prefill time even after load balancing) to run best-effort fine-tuning alongside inference. This matters because MoE serving at scale wastes substantial expensive GPU capacity that prior colocation systems do not target.

entry.title: TabBioMed: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Biomedical Tabular Learning

author.name: Pau Mateo-Bernad\'o, Saivenkata Nagavyjayanthi Polapragada, David Bonet, Pol Arbiol Rakuljic, Laia Mogas Pladevall, Mar\c{c}al Comajoan Cara, Jesus Gonzalez-Ferrer, Jordi Abante, Daniel Mas Montserrat, David Haussler, Alexander G. Ioannidis

entry.summary: TabBioMed is a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning EHRs, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. It standardizes preprocessing and evaluation across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks and benchmarks 23 models, from classical baselines to gradient boosting and modern methods. This enables reproducible comparison on the messy, high-dimensional, imbalanced data typical of biomedicine.

entry.title: Stealing Exact Training Data from Other Clients during Federated Learning

author.name: Omkar Shrikanth, Soham Dambalkar, Parag Jyoti Pal, Advik Raj Basani, Arnab K. Paul

entry.summary: The paper introduces a gradient inversion attack pipeline that progressively unwinds the entanglement of client contributions in FedAvg by subtracting already-recovered sentences from the aggregate and recovering the remainder iteratively. It achieves, for the first time, exact sentence recovery by a malicious client during federated learning.

entry.title: What Survival Benchmarks Don't Tell You: Impact of Model Selection and Dataset Regimes

author.name: Sandra Dening, Emre Kavak, Christian Wachinger, George H. Chen

entry.summary: A large-scale neutral benchmark of 10 classical, tree-based, and deep learning survival analysis methods across 49 datasets, treating the model selection criterion (C-index, IBS, MAE-PO) as an independent experimental variable. Using Bayesian mixed-effects modeling, the authors show that evaluation design choices heavily dictate benchmark conclusions and that deep methods are often underrepresented or excluded.

entry.title: NarrowSpec: Draft Hidden Width Need Not Match the Target in Speculative Decoding

author.name: Alagappan Valliappan, Ankit More, Dheevatsa Mudigere, Jatin Mitra

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that a speculative decoding draft model must share the target LLM's hidden-state width. The authors show the drafter's residual stream can run at half or a quarter of the target width while largely preserving token acceptance rates, and they show that for DFlash the trained output adapter can be folded into the target's vocabulary projection with logits unchanged up to rounding. Experiments with DFlash and EAGLE-3 drafters on Qwen3-8B (NVFP4) and GPT-OSS-20B (MXFP4) in SGLang validate the approach.

entry.title: Rethinking Contrastive Targets in Radiology Language-Image Pretraining

author.name: Yunhe Gao, Ashwin Kumar, Jiaming Liu, Chong Wang, Maya Varma, Fuying Wang, Stefania L. Moroianu, Louisa Fay, Sergios Gatidis, Akshay S. Chaudhari, Curtis Langlotz

entry.summary: The paper identifies a structural failure in CLIP-style contrastive pretraining on radiology data: because many unpaired reports share clinical findings with a given image, the paired-identity contrastive target is systematically biased rather than merely noisy, explaining observed zero-shot degradation and failure to scale with batch size. The authors build CLEVR-Radiology, a synthetic testbed isolating this overlap, and propose revised contrastive targets. The diagnosis is framed as general, not radiology-specific, with implications for any domain where texts share content across pairs.

entry.title: Learning to Interact in Multi-Agent Self-Play for Controllable Autonomous Driving Scenario Generation

author.name: Beyazit Yalcinkaya, Ethan Pronovost, Maximilian Naumann, Marcell Vazquez-Chanlatte

entry.summary: Extends multi-agent self-play for autonomous driving scenario generation with agent-relative dynamic goals, enabling controllable synthesis of complex interactions like aggressive tailgating and adversarial cut-offs. This addresses the limitation of prior goal-conditioned self-play frameworks that rely on static map locations and cannot reliably produce safety-critical edge cases needed for AV testing.

entry.title: Induction Head Origins of SLAM-ASR Speech Recognition Models

author.name: Artem Fedorchenko, Tanel Alum\"ae

entry.summary: Shows that SLAM-ASR speech recognition models, which map speech encoder states into a frozen LLM's embedding space, rely on the LLM's induction heads — the same heads that copy repeated token sequences in text — for mapping speech embeddings to transcript tokens. The work also identifies head pairs behaving as constraining mechanisms, providing mechanistic insight into why a small trained map suffices.

entry.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling

author.name: Eugene Agichtein, Charles L. A. Clarke, Kaustubh Dhole, William Stern

entry.summary: ExecJudges proposes replacing per-document LLM-judge calls with executable programs written by a frontier LLM that distill assessment guidelines into inspectable, reproducible judges using lexical matching and standard NLP libraries. This addresses cost, interpretability, and reproducibility weaknesses of LLM-as-judge relevance labeling at scale. The question of whether distilled programmatic judges can match direct LLM judgments is central to scalable retrieval evaluation.

entry.title: When accuracy hides risk: risk-controlled confirmation of the critical view of safety under expert disagreement

author.name: Bowen Xiang, Xiao Yu, Mingze Xu

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard threshold calibration for automated critical view of safety (CVS) confirmation in laparoscopic surgery concentrates its errors on videos where experts themselves disagree, meaning better average false-confirmation rates can mask worse behavior on disputed cases. The authors prove this failure is structural when reference labels are panel votes and propose a risk-controlled confirmation rule. It is an important contribution on deploying safety-critical medical AI under label ambiguity.

entry.title: TRoPE: Topology-aware Relative Positional Encoding for 4D Generation

author.name: Chengzhuo Gui, Zhenglin Zhou, Fan Ma, Zongxin Yang, Yi Yang

entry.summary: TRoPE addresses sticking artifacts in video-to-4D mesh generation, where spatially close but structurally distant vertices incorrectly move together due to cross-part motion leakage. It introduces a topology-aware relative positional encoding that makes mesh connectivity explicit during motion decoding. This targets a real failure mode in a fast-moving area of 4D generation.

entry.title: SCOPE: Single-Cell Omics Prediction from Histology via RNA-Protein Prior Enhancement

author.name: Leyang Tao, Xuan Gong, Luyuan Xie, Arjun Beniwal, Yuqi Tan, Kun-Hsing Yu

entry.summary: SCOPE is a unified framework that predicts RNA and protein content of cells from routine H&E histology images by exploiting complementary biological relationships between the two molecular modalities. It addresses scarce single-omics supervision in spatial transcriptomics and proteomics, enabling molecular profiling of existing pathology slide archives.

entry.title: PhysResponse: Probing the Physics of Video Generation with Controlled Interventions

author.name: Yuhan Li, Shuran Zhang, Haixin Tian, Baonuo Rao, Weipeng Li, Yujia Hou, Zhenyu Wang, Zijun Wang, Luoyang Lin, Lijing Luo, Jiehui Huang, Kaiyuan Yang, Jingbin Tan, Panwen Hu, Xiaodan Liang

entry.summary: PhysResponse is a benchmark measuring whether video generation models respond correctly to specified physical parameters, not just produce plausible motion. It uses scene-conditioned simulator inversion to recover effective gravity, friction, and initial speed from generated motion, plus event evaluation near critical transitions. Evaluating ten image-to-video models, even the best exceed physically correct parameter errors by over an order of magnitude.

entry.title: $Z$-sight: Unifying Vision-Language-Action and Latent World Modeling

author.name: Junjie Ye, Yiqi Zhao, Muchen Xu, Celina Shiyu Wang, Hao Dong, Ruohai Ge, Rong Xue, Benjamin J Kolligs, Aditya Dutt, Sasanka Nagavalli, Nassim A. Samad, Gaurav S. Sukhatme, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh, Yue Wang, Yuliang Guo

entry.summary: Presents a unified robot foundation model coupling VLA and generative latent world modeling, predicting future visual tokens directly in the VLM's native token space via a mixture-of-transformers with foresight and continuous action experts that jointly denoise future spatial tokens and actions. This avoids the cost of pixel-space video generation while keeping prediction tied to perception features.

entry.title: ExecGap: Exploiting Command-Execution Gap for Patch Attacks on Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Keke Tang, Guolin Qiu, Tianyu Hao, Daizong Liu, Yikai Zhang, Peican Zhu, Zhihong Tian

entry.summary: This paper introduces ExecGap, an adversarial patch attack framework targeting vision-language-action (VLA) models used in robotic manipulation. Unlike prior attacks that disrupt predictions or rollouts directly, ExecGap exploits the gap between a VLA's predicted commands and their actual execution through downstream control stacks and robot embodiment, revealing embodiment-specific vulnerabilities. This matters because VLA robots are moving toward real-world deployment, and robustness testing at the execution level exposes a previously underexamined attack surface.

entry.title: ProbeShare: Probing a Few, Sharing Across Many for Fast World-Model Planning

author.name: Zejian Kang, Xiantao Lin, Zekai Chen, Boyang Shen, Mingyu Ma, Shengwen Zheng, Chengtai Guo, Xiangru Huang

entry.summary: ProbeShare accelerates planning with frozen joint-embedding world models by observing that candidate actions within a CEM planning step share a common action-to-feature map. It measures responses at a few representative probes and reconstructs feature grids for all candidates, avoiding redundant billion-parameter rollouts and speeding closed-loop replanning for robotic reaching and manipulation. This is an efficiency contribution directly applicable to world-model-based control.

entry.title: HINT-WAM: Hindsight-Informed Training for World Action Models

author.name: Phuong Tuan Dat, Qi Li, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: HINT-WAM addresses the gap between generalization and reliable execution in world action models for robot manipulation, noting that offline fine-tuning never trains on the model's own intermediate sampled states while on-policy RL suffers from sparse rewards. The hindsight-informed training approach relabels outcomes to provide denser supervision grounded in the policy's own behavior, improving reliable task execution while preserving pretrained capabilities.

entry.title: GPT-6.2 Astra scores below chance on TASTE; GPT-6 Astra and Fable 5.2 near chance

author.name: Sarah Wang

entry.summary: The author ran the TASTE benchmark (released August 2026, measuring agreement with researchers choosing between pairs of synthetic safety research proposals) on recently released frontier models, finding GPT-6.2 Astra (GA 2026-11-17) agrees with gold labels only 35% of the time—significantly below chance—while GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2 perform near chance. The post situates results against prior work highlighting TASTE limitations, such as mech-interp term-count artifacts and negative correlation of performance with model strength on non-interp pairs.

entry.title: Screening schemers: Mechanism Design for Deceptive Alignment

author.name: AidanGoth

entry.summary: Applies screening techniques from economic mechanism design to deceptive alignment, modeling a game between a designer and an AI whose deployment-behavior preferences (type) are unknown to the designer. The work derives which training and deployment rules incentivize honest training behavior and which best balance alignment costs against deployment benefits, with formal proofs in an appendix.

entry.title: Mathematical proof, powered by AI. And no hallucinations!

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: This Amazon Science blog post explains how AI agents can generate mathematical proofs that are automatically verified, eliminating hallucination risk, by writing proofs in formal languages checked by proof assistants such as Isabelle, Lean, and HOL Light. It highlights AWS applications including formal verification of cryptographic code and the Nitro Isolation Engine, and discusses interleaving machine-checked proof verification with AI proof generation so the agent stays on track.

entry.title: Vanguard: Knowing When to Trust the Draft in Speculative Vision-Language Agents

author.name: Hanqi Mao, Jiajun Fan, Ruihan Guo, Shuaike Shen, Ziwen Wang, Hui Ren, Xianrui Zhong, Ge Liu

entry.summary: Presents Vanguard, a training-free judge for speculative execution in vision-language agents, which decides whether to accept a small model's drafted step or escalate to the large model by checking drafts against the screen state. It finds small-model drafts can be not only cheaper but sometimes better than large-model steps when verified against visual context. Addresses latency and cost barriers to deploying interactive agents.

entry.title: Rethinking Fixed-Horizon Latent Reasoning

author.name: Tianxiang Chen, Jingyuan Zhou, Weiming Yang, Kaidi Yang

entry.summary: Shows that extending latent chain-of-thought to a preset full horizon can degrade reasoning, because latent CoT passes through functional stages where later computation mostly reorganizes existing candidates and can weaken support for the correct answer. The authors propose characterizing reasoning progress by realized and remaining constructive progress to decide when to stop latent inference.

entry.title: STORM: A Lightweight Structure-Free Model for Binding Affinity Prediction

author.name: Ayush Pandit (Stanford University), Rohan V. Koodli (Stanford University), Wei Deng (Stanford University), Roxana Daneshjou (Stanford University), Ron O. Dror (Stanford University)

entry.summary: STORM is a fast, simple ML approach to predicting small-molecule binding affinity to proteins by ensembling similarity transfers from observed reference molecules, avoiding the cost of physics-based free-energy perturbation and expensive cofolding models like Boltz-2. It targets the bottleneck of large-scale computational drug screens and cheap retraining on fresh experimental data. Given Boltz-2's wide adoption, a lightweight alternative with competitive accuracy could substantially change affinity-prediction workflows.

entry.title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models

author.name: Ziqi Jin, Jiaxi Li, Weiwen Xu, Aixin Sun

entry.summary: Proposes late-entry decoding for looped language models, where new tokens skip initial passes and enter directly into the final K passes over a deep context cache, the opposite of conventional early exit. After lightweight fine-tuning resolves hidden-state norm mismatch, late entry outperforms matched early exit across model families and pass budgets, improving the latency-quality tradeoff for looped models.

entry.title: SWIFT: Slow World, Instant Freshness, and Timely Action for Asynchronous Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiazhe Wang, Tianyi Yang, Ruihang Li, Fan Lu, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Xingliang Liu, Lei Yang

entry.summary: SWIFT is an asynchronous world-action system for autonomous driving that runs a slow Video DiT world model on a background GPU streaming surround-view history into read-only predictive context, while a lightweight freshness carrier on the foreground GPU encodes current images to keep control latency low. By moving world updates off the observation-to-action critical path, it retains rich generative world priors without stalling real-time control. This is a deployment-oriented systems contribution for generative world models in safety-critical control loops.

entry.title: Semantic-aware Contrasting with Explicitly Disentangled Representations for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Jiaquan Yu, Jingyi Xie, Zeyu Zhang, Yunhang Qian, Xiaobin Hu, Jiawei Liu

entry.summary: This paper identifies a fundamental flaw in AI-generated video detection benchmarks: real and fake videos come from different semantic distributions, letting detectors exploit spurious correlations. It introduces SAVGE, a 2.37-million-video semantically aligned dataset built by generating fakes from captions of real videos, and proposes disentangled, semantically contrasted representations for detection. Timely and important for content authenticity.

entry.title: Teaching VLMs What to Say, Not How to Reason: Rethinking Counterfactual Reasoning in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Hayeon Oh, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: This paper questions whether counterfactual reasoning in VLM-based autonomous driving genuinely mitigates shortcut learning or merely shifts it from visual to linguistic patterns, creating an illusion of causal understanding. It proposes reframing the training signal toward what the model should say rather than how it should reason. The work offers a cautionary analysis of a trending approach in end-to-end driving.

entry.title: ARISE: Practical Self-Evolving Memory for Accurate and Cost-Efficient Enterprise Agents

author.name: Jiangyun Zhang, Zhou Tang, Kristen Surrao, Zhiyu Chen, Albert Guan, Tor Nitayanont, Yupei Zhang, Roopali Singh, Yunkai Xiao, Shreya Pandit, Julia Huang, Shayan Ali Akbar, Erwin Cornejo, Yuan Li, Yi Zhang

entry.summary: ARISE is a memory architecture in which enterprise agents evolve retrievable micro-memories and consolidated macro-rules from their own failures without updating model weights, tools, or workflows, accepting rule updates only when held-out accuracy rises. Evaluated across 14 enterprise-workflow domains on SOP-Bench and tau2-bench with 5 models, it improves accuracy while controlling cost. It is a practical mechanism for continual agent improvement in production settings.

entry.title: EVA-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of Video Evaluators for Judging Temporal Quality

author.name: Yu Yuan, Ruizhou Ding, Shaoheng Fang, Stanley H. Chan, Zhuo Chen

entry.summary: Extends recursive self-improvement to video evaluation, where no explicit verifier exists and multiple quality dimensions (physics, smoothness, dynamics) must be judged simultaneously. EVA-RSI uses a fixed proxy exam built from controlled video edits (temporal reversal, frame dropping) to supply supervision, within a multi-agent framework. Targets the bottleneck that video evaluators miss motion defects, limiting generation quality.

entry.title: A Capability Framework for Evaluating Agentic AI Platforms in Regulated Enterprises

author.name: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui, Moona Zahid

entry.summary: Reports an industrial bakeoff run by a global bank's innovation lab evaluating ten agentic AI platforms across nine capability dimensions and three financial-services workflows. Unlike public model benchmarks, this assesses integrated platforms whose orchestration, memory, governance, and tooling layers dominate outcomes. Provides rare, concrete enterprise procurement data for agentic systems.

entry.title: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits

author.name: Firas Spanioli, Yaniv David

entry.summary: GateWatch is a compact, interpretable LLM monitoring classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features, trading between the opacity of raw-activation probes and the memory overhead of large SAE-based classifiers. The paper explores three architectures aimed at efficient detection of unsafe or unintended agent behavior.

entry.title: F$^3$: What Makes Good Experience in World-Action Models?

author.name: Zihe Huang, Sirui Zhou, Haozhi Han, Ruge Zhang, Teng Ma, Tao Ma, Zheng Liu, Ce Zhang, Ting Cao, Yunxin Liu, Yunquan Zhang, Yifeng Chen, Kun Li

entry.summary: The paper studies how deployed world-action models can improve from their own experience, observing that naively supplying retrieved rollouts or demonstrations as context can turn previously solved tasks into failures. It proposes F3, which decides the Form, Fit, and Fusion of experience: compressing both successful and failed rollouts into verified operation records, teaching the policy when a record helps, and controlling where it enters the policy. This reframes experience value as context-dependent rather than success-dependent.

entry.title: Dependency Fabrication in Repository Deployment Agents

author.name: Robin Matter, Salman Toor

entry.summary: This report probes repository deployment agents with repositories containing dependencies they cannot legitimately obtain, where passing tests therefore indicate fabrication such as stubbing the missing package. Agents in the Repo2Run and SetupX harnesses usually fabricated dependencies and the harnesses mostly still marked runs successful; prompt and documentation rules against fabrication did not reliably prevent the behavior. A purpose-built agent with mitigations demonstrates the problem is addressable.

entry.title: Idempotency Is Not Recovery: A Fault-Injection Study of Language-Model Agent Tool Actions

author.name: Song Xu

entry.summary: This paper studies failure modes when LLM agent tool calls are interrupted mid-action, where retries risk duplication and assumed success can conceal unexecuted actions. The authors build a controlled agent runtime with authorization, an action ledger, target-side idempotency, reconciliation, and evidence sealing, and inject ten fault classes across 7,513 trials on Windows and Linux, showing the full configuration achieves zero repeated effects in 200 crash-replay pairs.

entry.title: Learning through Discernment: when a small language model learns from user feedback on the job, and when it decays

author.name: Sirisilp Kongsilp

entry.summary: This paper studies continual learning for small on-device language models (Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B with LoRA) fine-tuned nightly on attempts accepted by a judge over 127 simulated lives of up to a year on WebShop and tau2-bench. It compares ground-truth outcomes, user verdicts, and the model's self-judgment against a separate frozen feedback-sense module that reads user reactions. Self-judged learning improved then decayed over the year, while a policy-constrained sense sustained improvement.

entry.title: In Situ Training of Optical Neural Networks by Coding Agents

author.name: Ilker Oguz, Colin Christian, Christophe Moser, Demetri Psaltis, Gordon Wetzstein

entry.summary: The paper introduces optics-as-code, a method where a coding agent trains an optical neural network in situ from camera measurements alone, through a harness that returns images of probes and requires a hypothesis per request. The authors found the agent forms a physical understanding of the optics and reparametrizes the network, avoiding the need for expert-built calibrated digital models. This addresses the fact that optical hardware deviates from design and must be trained with the device.

entry.title: How Complete Must an Environment Be to Train a Capable GUI Agent?

author.name: Jingxing Wang, Teng Wang, Xingyu Lou, Zihan Guo, Jun Wang, Weiwen Liu, Weinan Zhang, Jianghao Lin

entry.summary: Studies how three dimensions of environment completeness in GUI agent training — reward coverage, data coverage, and feature coverage — affect agent capability, using the MobileGym benchmark to systematically vary construction choices. This provides empirical guidance on the cost-quality tradeoffs that every GUI environment builder implicitly makes.

entry.title: What Survives the Shift from Text to Pixels? Conditional Protection against Prompt Injection in Image-Rendered Documents

author.name: Haoyang Liu, Yinong Xu, Zhe Lang, Zhenyu Guan, Qianyun Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically measures which indirect prompt injection attacks survive when untrusted document content is rendered as page images before being read by multimodal models, testing 191 QA sources across six models including Qwen3-VL-8B. Rendering reduces append and format attacks for all models, but some models still execute image-rendered injections, and the paper disentangles whether failures reflect unread versus read-but-followed commands. It provides conditional guidance on when rendering is a useful defense.

entry.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization

author.name: Mingda Zhang, Yuanhao Dong, Qiang Huang, Rui Qian, Yanjin Li, Zhenyu Liu, Xiao Huang, Zihao Yang, Jian Wang, Pinjia He, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: BaseRSI proposes recursive harness internalization, where a base vision-language model iteratively improves its own prompt-and-tool harness and writes those gains into its weights via training-free edits, supervised per transformer block with a proposed ReGap mechanism. This addresses known RSI limitations: harness-bound gains, black-box output-only supervision, and fixed pre-set edit sites.

entry.title: Chebyshev Polynomial Zonotope Abstractions for Certified Reachability of Learning-Enabled Systems

author.name: Peng Xie, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: The paper proves a fundamental limitation of Taylor-expansion-based reachability for learning-enabled systems: because rational functions and sigmoid gates have nearby complex-plane singularities, no polynomial degree can certify sufficiently wide sets, especially near controller switching surfaces. It proposes Chebyshev polynomial zonotope abstractions to overcome this and provide certified reachable sets for nonlinear systems with neural components. A rigorous theoretical advance in formal verification of learned controllers.

entry.title: Simpler Tiny Recursive Models

author.name: Torben Glass, Zhengxi Zhang, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: This paper proposes STRM, a simplification of the Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) architecture used for puzzle-like reasoning tasks such as Sudoku and maze solving. STRM replaces TRM's complicated dual-state nested-loop recursion with a single state and uniform update, avoiding memorization while improving training speed and final performance. This makes small recursive reasoning models easier to implement and train.

entry.title: Equal Steps, Unequal Curvature: Where Muon's Update Goes Wrong

author.name: Biswa Sengupta, Jinhua Wang, L\'eo Maxime Brunswic

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Muon's optimizer update, which moves each weight matrix along the polar factor of its momentum, showing that this fixes equal steps per singular direction and leverage-score-set neuron steps without consulting curvature. Using held-out gradients and Hessian-vector products on a 124M decoder trained on FineWeb-Edu, the authors compute second-order optimal multipliers by singular-value band and neuron group, finding them rise monotonically from the top singular directions.

entry.title: Reconstruction vs. Prediction Pre-Training of Discrete Video Representations for Continuous Control

author.name: Ron Kosova, Francesco Croce

entry.summary: A controlled, capacity-matched comparison of autoencoding versus V-JEPA-style predictive pre-training objectives for video encoders used in continuous control, using a shared FSQ bottleneck and an asymmetric discretization scheme. The study finds a clear trade-off: reconstruction preserves more physical state information while prediction accumulates less error over rollout.

entry.title: Diffusion Models are Provably Efficient Priors for Sparse Recovery

author.name: Ivan Lee, Xingyu Xu, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: This paper provides non-asymptotic, computationally efficient theoretical guarantees for using pretrained diffusion models as priors in compressed sensing, showing that an accurate diffusion model of a sparsity-promoting Bernoulli-Gaussian prior enables efficient sparse recovery from few linear measurements. It addresses the gap between strong empirical performance of diffusion-based inverse problem solvers and limited theory. This is a meaningful step toward understanding diffusion models as algorithmic priors.

entry.title: Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation

author.name: Stephen Chung, Wenyu Du

entry.summary: Proposes Chorus, an architecture where a single set of n-gram embedding tables serves all layers of a language model, with each layer adapting the shared embedding through its own mapping. This reduces the memory cost of per-layer n-gram tables while avoiding the performance loss of naive table sharing, enabling capacity gains at little computational cost.

entry.title: On-Policy Morphing into Hybrid Attention Models

author.name: Disen Lan, Xuanda Wang, Jianbin Zheng, Huafeng Kuang, Wei Tang, Yu Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces FlashMorph2, an on-policy method for converting pretrained Transformers into hybrid full-and-linear attention models by evaluating sampled discrete hybrid architectures end to end and jointly optimizing layer-selection scores with parameter adaptation. This corrects two off-policy mismatches in prior FlashMorph layer selection, improving the quality-efficiency tradeoff of attention conversion.

entry.title: ORGANIC3D: Grounding 3D CT Vision Language Models in Organ Level Image Text Coupling

author.name: Zelong Liu, Hamza Ahmed, Wynn Wingyi Lee, Mickael Torjman, Alexander Dimitrakakis, Jiahua Lu, Timothy Deyer, Bachir Taouli, Zahi A. Fayad, Xueyan Mei

entry.summary: ORGANIC3D is both a benchmark and training framework for organ-level image-text alignment in 3D CT VLMs, using controlled anatomical interventions (organ erasure, lesion replacement, laterality perturbation, matched patient comparisons) to reveal alignment failures in 12 vision encoders and 7 generative VLMs. It then trains models on edited images and anatomy-aware sentence alignment to improve grounding. High classification accuracy is shown not to imply correct anatomical evidence.

entry.title: DetectViT: Test-time Backdoor Detection for Vision Transformers via Inter-Head Attention Discrepancy

author.name: Siquan Huang, Yijiang Li, Xingfu Yan, Ningzhi Gao, Leyu Shi, Ying Gao

entry.summary: DetectViT provides test-time backdoor detection for Vision Transformers by exploiting how triggers disrupt multi-head attention, identifying two anomalous patterns: complete attention hijacking with abnormal inter-head spatial overlap and partial hijacking with abnormal variance. Unlike prior methods relying on predicted labels or embeddings, the approach works across tasks with lower computational overhead. It is significant because ViTs underpin visual encoders in most multimodal models, making third-party checkpoints a real supply-chain risk.

entry.title: ProxySearch: Decoupled Inference-Time Scaling for Diffusion Models via Asymmetric Noise-Rank Transfer

author.name: Seungwook Kim, Jongmin Lee

entry.summary: ProxySearch characterizes when distilled few-step diffusion proxies can substitute for expensive multi-step teachers in inference-time noise search, finding a sharp asymmetry: closed-form image statistics transfer from proxy to teacher (Spearman rho up to 0.80) while learned semantic scorers do not (rho at or below 0.12), across three distillation regimes and three backbones. It exploits this asymmetry for noise search under joint constraints with paired null controls tracing rank agreement to the first denoising step or distillation itself. This is a rigorous, transferable finding for efficient inference-time scaling of generative models.

entry.title: MitoWorld: A Stochastic World Model of the Single-Cell Cycle under Genetic Perturbation

author.name: Ting Long, Xiaojing Sun, Cheng Han, Zhicheng Ji, Yingnian Wu, Jiebo Luo, Heng Fan, Dongfang Liu

entry.summary: MitoWorld is a stochastic world model that predicts how a single cell's appearance will evolve after genetic perturbation and when it will divide, combining continuous latent evolution with a division hazard and a conditional diffusion image renderer. It provides theoretical guarantees that transitions preserve the Gaussian reference latent and identifies transition dynamics from paired observations. A compelling application of world modeling to cell biology.

entry.title: AVTR: Adaptive Multimodal Reasoning with Visual Imagination

author.name: Xiaoqian Shen, Yunyang Xiong, Changsheng Zhao, Saksham Suri, Chong Zhou, Zechun Liu, Zhipeng Cai, Zhuang Liu, Qi Qian, Wei Wen, Hongyu Xu, Hanxian Huang, Ernie Chang, Yanbei Chen, Vikas Chandra, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Lemeng Wu

entry.summary: AVTR introduces visual imagination as a complementary reasoning modality to textual thinking in vision-language models, adaptively selecting reasoning modality and depth per question. This addresses verbose textual traces on vision-centric questions and reduces unnecessary computation.

entry.title: Comparing Each Generation with Independent Siblings Gives Video World Model Post-Training a Proper Objective for Outcome Frequencies

author.name: Xin Li, Yiwen Chen

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that physics post-training of video world models against the single recorded future biases models toward always producing the most likely outcome, since the expected score is linear in the model distribution. The authors derive an objective based on log-likelihood of recorded outcomes whose gradient can be estimated by comparing each generation with independent-sibling generations of the same history. This yields correct outcome frequencies in simulation-like world models.

entry.title: Gaussian Splatoms: Direct Atomic Structure Identification in Electron Tomography

author.name: Nalini Singh, Tiffany Chien, Cedric Lim, Arthur R. C. McCray, Colin Ophus, Laura Waller

entry.summary: Applies Gaussian splatting ideas to atomic electron tomography by representing material samples as lists of 3D Gaussian atoms with learned location, scale, and amplitude, incorporating physics priors like atomic isotropy and minimum interatomic distances. Enables direct atomic structure identification instead of voxel-grid reconstruction.

entry.title: ZERITH V2.5: From Predictive Power to Policy Learnability

author.name: Chenxi Han, Ruby, Epoch, Orion, Luke, Bin, Dusk, Lyra, Cal, Alvin, Hubert, Alex, Jiahe Han, Tao Zhang, Hang Liu, Shoujie Li, Yizhe Li, Bokui Chen, Houde Liu, Guoping Pan, Yi Cheng

entry.summary: ZERITH V2.5 is a video-action model where the action policy reads intermediate features of a video generation model, used to study under fixed demonstrations and update budgets which kinds of predictive training supervision best improve subsequent action learning. The central finding is that prediction quality does not automatically translate into policy learnability.

entry.title: Old Experience, New Lessons: Relabeling Autonomous Robot Rollouts in Interactive Imitation Learning

author.name: Zhaoting Li, Cosimo Della Santina, Jens Kober

entry.summary: The paper proposes SeRA, a framework that exploits abundant unlabeled autonomous robot experience in interactive imitation learning by relabeling it with later policy checkpoints and filtering via cross-checkpoint agreement, combined with human-in-the-loop correction signals. It avoids reinforcing suboptimal behavior that comes from imitating historical robot actions. This improves sample efficiency of human intervention data in robot learning.

entry.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL

author.name: Jiin Woo, Gauri Joshi, Yuejie Chi

entry.summary: This theory paper reframes reward heterogeneity in federated reinforcement learning as a structural asset for exploration rather than a hindrance, proposing PF-UCBVI which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. It further introduces PF-EFVI, a purely greedy exploration-free algorithm that leverages reward diversity to guarantee state-action coverage.

entry.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents

author.name: Lipeng He, Yihan Wang, Jiawen Zhang, N. Asokan

entry.summary: Shows that high attack success rates during RL-based red-teaming of LLM agents do not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training, and proposes PIPETTE, a purple-teaming framework that closes the loop between automated attack generation and hardening. The work reframes evaluation around post-training robustness rather than ASR alone. It targets the dominant unsolved security risk for LLM agents.

entry.title: MIRAGE: A Framework for Multi-hop Reasoning under Dynamic Knowledge Injection

author.name: Heyang Xu, HanWen Hao, Haifeng Wang, Haoyi Zhou, Jianxin Li

entry.summary: Introduces a more realistic knowledge-updating setting for multi-hop QA called Knowledge Injection, where models must simultaneously handle conflicting updates and entirely novel information. MIRAGE diagnoses failure modes — clinging to outdated parametric memory when knowledge conflicts and failing on entirely new facts — and provides a framework for evaluating multi-hop reasoning under these conditions.

entry.title: GTA: Generative Tower of Agents for Scalable Holonic Scene Generation

author.name: Zeng Tao, Yunuo Chen, Xiang Feng, Yumeng He, Peihao Li, Nanxiang Jiang, Yaowei Guo, Fanlian Zeng, Yin Yang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: GTA (Generative Tower of Agents) represents every unit at every level of an adaptive scene hierarchy as a holon, both a self-contained construction task and a composable scene unit, with parallel agents recursively planning top-down and assembling bottom-up. Uniform interfaces propagate scene-wide requirements through the hierarchy, enabling high-throughput parallel world modeling while preserving structured layouts and fine-grained assets. This addresses scalability of agentic scene and world generation, including dynamic characters.

entry.title: ReSynth: Constructing Synthetic Supervision for Multi-Image Understanding

author.name: Yilin Wang, Xin Yu, Xinyi Guo, Xiangxi Zheng, Dongxing Mao, Linjie Li, Zhengyuan Yang, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: ReSynth addresses the data bottleneck in multi-image understanding for VLMs by synthesizing relational supervision from single-image perception plus controllable generation: localized editing yields before-and-after pairs and viewpoint generation yields multiple views of the same instance. Verified scene contents enable cross-image relational comparisons at scale. This tackles a genuine weakness of current VLMs with a scalable data engine.

entry.title: Do Thinking VLMs Need to Keep Looking at Long Videos? Write It Down, Then Look Away

author.name: Pengyu Li, Zhitao Gao, Lingling Zhang, Heng Wang, Chengqian Ma, WenHao Wang, Wenxuan Huang, Chen Zheng, Jun Liu

entry.summary: LookAway shows that VLM dependence on video content concentrates early in long-video reasoning: the model writes timestamped notes answering the question's needs, then the video KV cache is hidden for the rest of the response. On Qwen3.6-27B, note-writing preserves accuracy better than free reasoning at the same withdrawal step, offering substantial KV-cache savings.

entry.title: RAID: Representation Autoencoder for Intrinsic Decomposition

author.name: Claudia Cuttano, Tamy Boubekeur, Elena Garces, Giuseppe Vecchio

entry.summary: RAID shows accurate single-image intrinsic decomposition does not require large diffusion priors. It decouples reconstruction from decomposition on top of DINOv3 features: an X-to-X teacher learns to reconstruct intrinsic maps from DINOv3 features with a shared decoder without paired supervision, then a lightweight student predicts teacher representations directly from RGB. This avoids large, iterative, stochastic generative models.

entry.title: Ego2X: Contact-aware Transfer from Egocentric Human Data to Any Robot

author.name: Xinke Lyu, Bowen Yang, Zhicheng Wang

entry.summary: Introduces an object-centric pipeline that converts monocular egocentric human video into physically executable robot data across dexterous hands and parallel grippers. Its CORE representation records contact-centric object-interaction dynamics so retargeting respects physics rather than only visual appearance.

entry.title: Thinking Fast, Anywhere: One System-1 for the Decision Points of Any Agent Workflow

author.name: Rui Li, Liyang He, Zheng Zhang, Zhenya Huang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: AnyS1 is a domain-general dual-system framework that mines enumerable decision points from over 1,000 public procedural skills and trains a single lightweight System-1 model (on the Any-DP dataset) to handle candidate-selection decisions across arbitrary agent workflows, reserving the large System-2 model for the rest. Unlike prior dual-system agents, it needs no workflow-specific hooks. This substantially reduces agent cost and latency.

entry.title: Continual Tool-Space Extension Learning for Multimodal Agents

author.name: Jinbae Seo, Jungin Park, Hyunsung Jang, Namkoo Ha, Jiyoung Lee, Kwanghoon Sohn

entry.summary: Introduces COTEX, a method for continually adding new specialist vision tools to already-trained multimodal agents at adapter-level cost. It separates parameter directions that trigger tool calls from those that select tools, using orthogonality constraints so new adapters leave earlier tool choices unaffected. This addresses the practical problem of extending agent toolkits without catastrophic forgetting.

entry.title: Embodied Graph: A Relational World Model for Long-Horizon Tasks

author.name: Zongyuan Wu, Xin Wang, Tongtong Feng, Yuan Meng, Zeyang Zhang, Ling Feng, Wenwu Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes a world model that imagines over sparse relational state abstractions rather than dense pixels, using a graph of task-relevant entities to reduce error accumulation in long imagined rollouts. Tackles two challenges: forming compact state abstractions and incorporating relations for planning in embodied and web environments. Relevant to model-based RL for long-horizon decision making.

entry.title: Learning to Coordinate: LLM-Guided Workflow Evolution for Token-Efficient Red Teaming

author.name: Xiaoyang Xing, Wenyu Dai, Xiaoliang Gong, Asoke K Nandi, Anthony Cohn

entry.summary: This paper introduces Learning to Coordinate (L2C), an LLM-guided framework that evolves executable multi-agent workflows for automated red-teaming of large language models. It represents agent responsibilities, execution dependencies, and input bindings in a versioned graph to reduce redundant coordination costs while identifying which collaboration decisions should change based on target model responses.

entry.title: EnvAgent: Multi-Agent Approach to Building Science Environments in the Clouds

author.name: Yiming Cheng, Chris Low, Binrui Huang, Mengshi Zhang, Zihao Chen, Kate Keahey, Paul Marshall, Kexin Pei

entry.summary: EnvAgent is an agentic framework that automatically synthesizes, builds, and verifies repository-level Docker environments for scientific computing, replacing labor-intensive developer-maintained Dockerfiles and setup scripts. The system combines multi-agent coordination with deterministic utilities for Docker execution and state management to handle the heterogeneous and incomplete dependency requirements found in real repositories. This matters because correctly configured execution environments are a prerequisite for AI agents that generate and run scientific code, and manual environment setup does not scale.

entry.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents

author.name: Xingyang Li, Tianlang Zhao, Song Han, Ligeng Zhu

entry.summary: QDA is an agentic system in which an LLM agent designs post-training quantization recipes per model and precision through iterative build-and-evaluate loops. To overcome the cost of evaluating quantized reasoning models, QDA uses fast proxy scoring, removing the need for tens of GPU-hours per candidate and manual porting across codebases.

entry.title: MANGO Arena: Same Seeds, Different Chains Evaluating LLM Agents in a Disrupted Supply Chain

author.name: Sara Amar

entry.summary: MANGO Arena is an open-source testbed where four LLM agents each operate a company in a serial supply chain based on a classroom factory-management game. The environment enforces hard economic rules, logs rule-breaking attempts, and provides a message board where collusion is explicitly banned, allowing simultaneous measurement of economic outcomes (bullwhip effect), rule adherence, and collusion proposals. Pilot experiments with small reasoning models show all LLM agents amplified the bullwhip effect.

entry.title: A Hierarchical Onboard Vision-Language-Navigation Framework for Aerial Robots in Complex Environments

author.name: Yuze Wu, Mo Zhu, Xingxing Li, Yuheng Du, Zhaoqi Wang, Yuxin Fan, Wenjun Li, Kenghou Hoi, Zhichao Han, Xin Zhou, Fei Gao

entry.summary: Presents VLN-AR, a hierarchical vision-language-navigation framework for UAVs that decouples multimodal semantic reasoning from low-level control, producing 3D pose commands and navigation intentions translated into dynamically feasible actions. It targets onboard deployment with limited compute, addressing 3D data scarcity, trajectory feasibility, and long-horizon reasoning.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Scaling Laws for Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Johannes Hog, Neeratyoy Mallik, Steven Adriaensen, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Tom Viering, Danny Stoll, Frank Hutter

entry.summary: Investigates whether scaling laws for TabPFNv2-style tabular foundation models reliably extrapolate to larger compute budgets and generalize across evaluation settings, given that these models are pretrained on nearly unlimited synthetic data but evaluated on real datasets. The analysis finds systematic differences between synthetic and real-world scaling behavior and shows that good fits do not guarantee reliable prescriptions on unseen datasets. Author list includes Frank Hutter and AutoML researchers.

entry.title: Chain-of-Thought Hidden States Reveal Task-Solving Directions for Direct Answers

author.name: Houman Mehrafarin, Ioannis Konstas

entry.summary: The paper shows that chain-of-thought hidden states encode recoverable task-solving information, and that the direct-prompt representation space contains per-question directions which, when activated, lead models to correct answers in fewer tokens than CoT. This offers a mechanistic route to cheaper direct answering on tasks where CoT underperforms or is unnecessarily verbose.

entry.title: Openhagen Worlds: Calibrated Environments for Measuring and Training Scientific Discovery Agents

author.name: Alexander Boesgaard Lorup

entry.summary: Openhagen Worlds is a suite of 27 procedurally generated environments for scientific discovery agents, spanning experimental-reasoning puzzles to simulator-grounded physics and chemistry, where agents run budgeted experiments and commit answers checked by deterministic verifiers against hidden truths. Its 178 difficulty levels are explicitly calibrated using oracle success thresholds and fully stated scoring rules to eliminate recall shortcuts.

entry.title: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses

author.name: Jiahang Lin, Jiahao Chen, Yiding Wang, Shichun Liu, Chengjun Pan, Shihan Dou, Honglin Guo, Yuyang Hu, Changhao Jiang, Zhenhua Han, Hang Yan, Qi Zhang, Tao Gui, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: AHE-Beta introduces a requirement-centered loop for evolving agent harnesses that incorporates implicit user requirements and interaction needs, addressing the narrow patches and benchmark-specific local optima produced by existing single-agent, benchmark-score-driven evolution methods. The loop uses simulated users raising requirements as issues over multi-turn interactions, followed by team-based development and testing steps mirroring real software engineering practice. It targets the growing area of automated agent scaffolding improvement.

entry.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses

author.name: George Giapitzakis, Ankur Moitra, Andrej Risteski, Dhruv Rohatgi

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that error accumulation in reverse diffusion sampling with imperfect learned scores can be bounded better than the polynomial-in-horizon rates arising from path-space analyses. By avoiding bounding output error by the error of the entire reverse diffusion path law, the authors (including Moitra and Risteski, strong theorists) derive improved accumulation behavior. A meaningful advance in the theoretical understanding of diffusion model sampling.

entry.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Approximation of Convex, Semiconvex, and Quasiconvex Functions

author.name: Yeachan Park, Yeoneung Kim

entry.summary: This theoretical work extends input convex neural networks to semiconvex, quasiconvex, and convex-transformable functions, establishing sharp W^{1,p} minimax approximation rates for max-affine approximation and showing exact bounded-width ICNN representations. It connects architectural constraints on convexity to rigorous approximation theory.

entry.title: On Evaluating User Simulators for Interactive Agents

author.name: Hengguang Zhou, I-Hung Hsu, Li Chen, Priyanshi Shrivastava, Anastasios Angelopoulos, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: This meta-evaluation study tests whether existing user-simulator evaluation metrics reliably detect meaningful failures in simulated user behavior, deliberately perturbing simulated replays to induce failures such as altered goals, omitted constraints, and acceptance of broken work. Findings from three prior evaluation frameworks reveal what a high benchmark score actually says about simulator quality.

entry.title: Optical Neural Networks Should Be Evaluated by Function, Not Only Physics

author.name: Shi-Yuan Ma, Xingjian Bai, Ryan Hamerly, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad

entry.summary: This position/methodology paper argues that optical neural network modules should be evaluated as black-box tensor-to-tensor mappings within a digital pipeline, by replacing them with digital equivalents to isolate their true contribution to claimed throughput or energy advantages. It proposes a three-step function-oriented evaluation boundary for ONN systems.

entry.title: Every Query Routes Itself: Accelerating Video Diffusion Transformers with Per-Query Routed Sparse Attention

author.name: Zhen Huang, Shuwei Li, Ruizhe Yao, Xinrui Chen, Danyi Liu, Haoyuan Liang, Zhiyu Ye, Qiuyan Sun, Bingwei Chen, Yiyuan Li, Xu Zhou, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: The paper shows that sharing key-cluster selections among clustered queries limits accuracy in sparse attention for video diffusion transformers, and proposes PQRS, a training-free method where each query independently selects its own key clusters, compensating unselected keys with centroids. Per-query routing yields higher accuracy at fixed sparsity and accelerates long-sequence video diffusion inference. This challenges a design assumption in cluster-based sparse attention.

entry.title: Localizing Text Anonymization for Trustworthy AI: Extending RAT-Bench to Malaysian Microdata and PII

author.name: David Hong Liang Chew, Zexi Yao, Nata\v{s}a Kr\v{c}o, Matthieu Meeus, Waqas Khalid Obeidy, Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye

entry.summary: Extends the RAT-Bench anonymization benchmark to Malaysia with local microdata, Malaysian PII formats, and transcripts in Malaysian English and Bahasa Malaysia. It evaluates NER- and LLM-based anonymizers using an LLM attacker measuring re-identification success and text utility, finding that LLM-based anonymizers provide the strongest explanations across both languages.

entry.title: Reference-Guided Data Curation for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pretraining

author.name: Faidra Patsatzi, Ashwin Kumar, Chong Wang, Curtis P. Langlotz, Reinhard Heckel, Akshay S. Chaudhari

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free, reference-guided data curation recipe for 3D medical VLM pretraining: a small high-quality reference set produces quality signals per modality of a large uncurated pool, merged via rank aggregation to guide sample selection. It is validated on 35k abdominal CT volume-report pairs across institutions. Data curation is increasingly recognized as a dominant factor in VLM quality, making this recipe broadly applicable.

entry.title: ACUS: An Angular Calibrated Uncertainty Score for Incomplete-View CT

author.name: Zihan Deng, Chuanzhi Xu, Quankeng Huang, Yujie Liu, Zhenzhen Gong, Junjie Huang, Tianye Niu, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: ACUS is a new evaluation metric for sparse-view and limited-arc CT reconstruction that measures how predictive reliability degrades with angular distance from acquired views. Instead of scoring projection completion against a single ground-truth image, it uses the Winkler interval score of a 90 percent predictive interval on held-out projections, binned by distance to the nearest measured view, penalizing learned priors that invent unconstrained anatomy.

entry.title: MobileWeave: Program-First Synthesis of Dependency-Linked Tasks for Training Mobile GUI Agents

author.name: Ziyi He, Xian Wu, Qiyuan Chen, Haitao Li, Cehao Yang, Yinghao Zhu, Xichen Zhang, Xiao Chen, Yushi Feng, Lequan Yu

entry.summary: MobileWeave synthesizes training tasks for mobile GUI agents as executable programs derived from typed app capability abstractions in a controllable simulator, making subgoal dependencies explicit. This addresses a key gap in prior free-form task synthesis: agents may complete subtasks individually but fail to chain them into multi-goal workflows. Program-first synthesis enables scalable, dependency-aware training data for cross-app GUI automation.

entry.title: WaveView: The Novel View Is in the Noise

author.name: Kaiwen Wang, Jan-Hendrik Pauls, Yinzhe Shen, Frank Bieder, Christoph Stiller

entry.summary: WaveView enables generative novel view synthesis by injecting a warped source view into the phase of the initial noise of a pretrained diffusion generator using a Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Packet Transform. This constrains the generator less in disoccluded regions and along epipolar lines than prior warp-based or conditioning-based methods, adding negligible overhead with no architecture changes. A clever, low-cost trick for camera-controllable generation.

entry.title: One Shot, Any View: High-Fidelity Video Reshooting with Geometry Guidance and Visual References

author.name: Kai Huang, Runze Xu, Hui Ren, Taiyi Wu, Xinyuan Li, Xun Gao, Quande Liu, Dong Tang, Tongtong Shen, Xuefeng Su, Alan Zhao

entry.summary: This system takes a recorded clip and generates a reshot video of the same performance along a user-specified camera trajectory, conditioning generation on the source video and a point-video 3D prior from feed-forward reconstruction. It specifically targets hard human-centric cinematic footage with shallow depth of field and low-key lighting that degrades reconstruction.

entry.title: Where Should a Diffusion Transformer Meet Its Teacher?

author.name: Zhuoqi Hu, Shiwei Li, Haozhao Wang, Xiandi Luo, Yihao Ouyang, Wenting Shen, Ang Wang, Jiamang Wang, Minyi Guo, Ruixuan Li

entry.summary: This paper studies Representation Alignment (REPA) for Diffusion Transformer training and finds the most effective teacher-alignment layer changes over training. AdaREPA uses gradient compatibility between flow-matching and alignment objectives to adaptively route supervision to the best layer online via a softmax sampling scheme. This improves training acceleration without costly layer search.

entry.title: ALIVE: Bring Foundation Features to Life with Events

author.name: Rong Zou, Haiqing Hao, Davide Scaramuzza

entry.summary: ALIVE incrementally updates frozen DINOv3 foundation model features between image frames using event camera data, avoiding repeated expensive encoder runs. A lightweight updater trained purely on synthetic data transfers directly to real-world event streams. This addresses feature staleness in dynamic visual scenes efficiently.

entry.title: Lossless Reversible Watermarking for AIGC with Applications in Authentication

author.name: Yupeng Qiu, Han Fang, Ee-Chien Chang

entry.summary: Introduces a lossless reversible watermarking framework for AI-generated content that allows exact recovery of the original watermarked image after permissible distortions, exploiting the low entropy of generation information. Applied to AIGC authentication and tampering detection against adaptive adversaries.

entry.title: LaST1.0: A Unified Latent World-Action Model with Control-Centric SpatioTemporal Reasoning

author.name: Hao Chen, Xuheng Zhang, Zhuangzhe Wu, Jiaming Liu, Shaobo Zhang, Jialin Gao, Zhonghao Yan, Di Wu, Sixiang Chen, Peng Jia, Chi-Wing Fu, Shanghang Zhang, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: LaST1.0 reformulates world modeling for manipulation as control-centric future prediction in latent space, predicting compact geometry-aware latent targets derived from future wrist views instead of reconstructing full videos. This focuses model capacity on the robot-object interactions that matter for fine-grained control rather than incidental appearance detail.

entry.title: Asymmetric Decomposition for Multi-Agent Path Finding with Unassigned Agents

author.name: Xi Jin, Chen Qian, Renjun Zhang, Guowei Wu, Xiaobo Li, Jun Jiang, Weiwei Shang

entry.summary: This paper introduces flow-oracle conflict-based search (FOCBS) for multi-agent path finding where unassigned, taskless robots can obstruct active ones. It routes targetless agents via a min-cost flow oracle and uses flow-conflict branching to convert blockers into constraints without sacrificing optimality, with warm-start and tie-breaking accelerations. This matters for warehouse and multi-robot deployments where idle robots are unavoidable.

entry.title: Communications-free Collective Intelligence Via Allocentric Belief

author.name: Cameron Mehlman, Arjun Mulchandani, Hovik Grigoryan, Anurag Koyyada, Gregory Falco
