entry.title: Taming the Tails of Stochastic Gradient Descent in the Interpolation Regime

author.name: Leonardo Galli, Daniela Angela Parletta, Andrea Paudice

entry.summary: The paper provides high-probability convergence guarantees for SGD in the smooth interpolation regime, complementing the usual in-expectation analyses. It proves fast rates of order log(1/beta)/n for convex objectives and a family of moment-based exponential bounds for strongly convex objectives, with matching lower bounds showing the tail deterioration is essentially unavoidable. This clarifies how heavy SGD tails must be in the regime underlying overparameterized learning.

entry.title: LipSpell: A Language-Independent Phonetic Scoring Framework for Spelling Correction Combining Distinctive-Feature Edit Distance, Keyboard Geometry, and Corpus Frequency

author.name: Leonardo Araujo

entry.summary: Presents LipSpell, a unified language-independent phonetic scoring engine for spelling correction that combines an IPA distinctive-feature phone-distance matrix, keyboard geometry, and corpus frequency priors, with swappable language-specific G2P frontends. This handles both typographical and phonetic misspellings, moving beyond English-centric phonetic hashes like Soundex and Metaphone.

entry.title: NIRJALA: Draining the Sea out of Gaussian Splatting with Three-Path Optics and Reversible Physics

author.name: Latchan Chhetri, Aman Kumar

entry.summary: NIRJALA is a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for underwater scene recovery with a three-path image formation model (TRIVENI) adding a range-saturating forward-scattering term to direct transmission and backscatter, preventing the unbounded inversion gain of exponential-transmission models. It jointly recovers water-free appearance and geometry. The physically grounded formulation addresses a real failure mode of prior underwater 3DGS methods.

entry.title: Image-Condition-Controlled Diffusion Network with Large-Scale CT Pretraining for CT-Free Attenuation Correction in Dynamic Cardiac PET

author.name: Zhejia Zhang, Scott M. Leonard, Jinkui Hao, Ryan J. Avery, Richard L. Weinberg, Bo Zhou

entry.summary: LUCID performs CT-free attenuation correction in dynamic cardiac PET using an image-condition-controlled diffusion network pretrained on large-scale unpaired CT data, avoiding the paired NAC-PET/CT data scarcity of supervised methods and the radiation and misregistration issues of CT-based mu-maps. This leverages abundant unpaired CT for pretraining in a clinically important quantitative imaging task. Cardiac PET quantification directly depends on attenuation correction quality.

entry.title: Mean Curvature Minimizing Foliations Of A Vector Field

author.name: Tabish A. Syed, Marc Theveneau, Benedikt Wirth, Rustum Choksi, Kaleem Siddiqi

entry.summary: This paper develops a mathematical model and algorithm for recovering smooth sheet-like foliations from a single vector field aligned with local orientations, targeting biological structures such as brain white matter fibre tracts and cardiac muscle cell arrangements. The model estimates a second orthonormal vector field while enforcing mean-curvature-minimizing properties to infer the underlying sheets. It addresses an open problem with relevance to diffusion MRI and biomechanics.

entry.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability

author.name: Michael Werman

entry.summary: This paper analyzes what image junctions of three perpendicular edges reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsics, showing each junction constrains a convex set of cameras and calibrating from many junctions becomes convex feasibility. It derives closed-form focal length intervals, characterizes identifiability, and provides certified bounds robust to measurement error. A theoretically clean contribution to classical camera self-calibration.

entry.title: Benchmarking Reasoning Reliability,Prior_Evidence Contrast,and Spectral Discrimination in Remote-Sensing Geological Image Interpretation

author.name: Jun Wang, Fengpeng Li, Wei Han, Yuxuan Li, Tianjin Huang, Jining Yan, Sheng Wang, Kan Sun, Lizhe Wang

entry.summary: HyGeoBench is a diagnostic benchmark of 10,000 questions based on hyperspectral satellite imagery for evaluating MLLM reliability in geological lithology interpretation across reasoning reliability, prior-evidence conflict, and spectral discrimination. It covers ten task types with multiple-choice and open-ended formats, exposing reasoning errors and cross-band inconsistencies in current models. Valuable for assessing where multimodal models fail in scientific remote sensing.

entry.title: PatchAdaNet: Unsupervised class incremental learning using local patches and global adapters

author.name: Kamel Aouaidjia, Yanchao Duan, Zihui Zhen, Xin Li, Yongfei Lv, Chongsheng Zhang

entry.summary: PatchAdaNet is an unsupervised class-incremental learning method that avoids replay buffers by continually updating feature representations with autoencoders over shared local image patches and global adapters. It is motivated by biological learning, aiming to integrate new experience with minimal interference without growing memory.

entry.title: CROMPT: Adapting CLIP via Cross-Modal Prompting for Robust Zero-Shot Generalization under Adverse Weather

author.name: Aniruddh Sikdar, Arya Kishor, Snehashis Dhibar, Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: This paper introduces CROMPT, a prompt-learning framework for zero-shot domain adaptation in semantic segmentation when target-domain images are unavailable, targeting ResNet-based CLIP backbones. It combines random visual prompting with hybrid textual prompting (CROMA) and uses vision-language models to generate descriptions of adverse target conditions. The work addresses robustness of open-vocabulary segmentation under weather shifts.

entry.title: RAPID: Reconstruction Accelerated by Polarization-Informed Depth for 2D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Daisong Ouyang, Linlin Xia, Liangkun Yan, Song Gu, Shedong Zhao, Xin Dai, Yi Zheng

entry.summary: RAPID is a geometry-first 3D surface reconstruction framework that uses multiview polarization cues to recover dense surface priors for 2D Gaussian splatting, avoiding sparse geometric initialization and costly densification. Surface normals are integrated into depth maps with sparse anchors and fused across views, with curvature-adaptive sampling supporting efficient optimization. The method targets reflective and weakly textured regions where standard splatting struggles.

entry.title: Predicting Species Splits: A Challenging Fine-Grained Benchmark for Category Discovery

author.name: Christian Lange, Joakim Bruslund Haurum, Bingchen Zhao, Oisin Mac Aodha

entry.summary: PS-SPLIT is a new large-scale benchmark for category discovery built from 257 real, expert-verified taxonomic splits, containing 79K bird images across 771 species with geographic metadata. It addresses saturation of existing category discovery benchmarks and reflects genuine real-world discovery difficulty. The benchmark enables long-term evaluation of novel category discovery methods.

entry.title: Ultimate3D: Teaching Multimodal LLMs 3D Camera-Object Relations by Large-Scale Visual Instruction Data

author.name: Liu He, Yizhi Song, Ruiqi Xu, Baris Sarper Tezcan, Xiao Zeng, Albert Y. C. Chen, Lu Xia, Shashwat Verma, Sankalp Dayal, Min Sun, Cheng-Hao Kuo, Daniel Aliaga

entry.summary: Ultimate3D introduces a pipeline combining 3D assets, rendering, diffusion-based image generation, and LLM-generated prompts to create large-scale photorealistic visual instruction data with precise camera-object relations. Fine-tuning on this data teaches MLLMs object orientation, camera viewpoint, and shot types they currently struggle with. This addresses a systematic weakness in spatial understanding of multimodal models.

entry.title: Efficient World-Model Planning via Physics-Guided Search Distillation

author.name: Hongyu Zhang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Heye Huang, Qingwen Meng, Wenjun Shi, Jianao Xu, Xin Hu, Xuanru Jin, Jingyi Zhang, Baicang Guo

entry.summary: Proposes PGSD, a single-view autonomous driving planner that combines execution-aware trajectory selection with a search teacher that generates beyond-pool corrections when all candidate trajectories violate road constraints, then distills these into the planner. This enables verified repair rather than mere re-ranking of an infeasible candidate pool.

entry.title: Hebbian self-organization of monosynaptic reflexes in a biologically realistic multiarticular limb

author.name: Jonathan Realmuto, Erfan Nozari, Gerald E. Loeb

entry.summary: Shows in a neuromechanical model that biologically realistic spinal monosynaptic reflex connectivity emerges spontaneously via Hebbian plasticity driven by motor babbling, without genetic specification. Identifies a sweet spot in babbling statistics and derives connectivity predictions grounded in limb biomechanics.

entry.title: Improve How You Improve: Recursive Policy Self-Improvement for Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Multi-Object Navigation

author.name: Yang Li, Ziju Han, Aming WU, Zihao Zhang, Sijia Zhang, Yahong Han, Qinghua Hu

entry.summary: The paper makes the mechanisms for diagnosing navigation failures and generating policy revisions themselves learnable and recursive, rather than fixed human-designed rules as in prior trajectory-reflection methods. This targets zero-shot open-vocabulary multi-object navigation in unseen environments.

entry.title: Emo-H2A: Driving a Facial Robot Directly from LLM Hidden States at Token Rate

author.name: Yige Liu, Jingcheng Huang, Hao Sun, Min Li, Zhouping Yin

entry.summary: Emo-H2A drives a facial robot directly from LLM hidden states during autoregressive decoding, so expression stays continuous, context-sensitive, and synchronized with speech without emotion labels. Its training-free instantiation, EmoManifold, extracts a valence-arousal-dominance coordinate from each hidden state and actuates the face at token rate.

entry.title: SearchDiffusion: Information-Guided Diffusion Planning for Object Search

author.name: Sausar Karaf, Dmitrii Plotnikov, Alexey Kotcov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: SearchDiffusion is a diffusion-based planner for object search in unknown environments, generating position and heading trajectories conditioned on a learned dense utility map capturing accessibility, visibility, and semantic progress, with guidance and validity checks for execution. It achieved 95.6 percent target detection across 90 simulated tasks on 24 map layouts at higher computational cost. It connects diffusion planning to active information gathering.

entry.title: TinyARM-X: A Series of Open-Source, Configurable, and Transparent Torque-Controlled Desktop-Scale Robotic Manipulators

author.name: Nicolas Kosanovic, Jean Chagas Vaz

entry.summary: TinyARM-X is a framework for low-cost (under 350 USD), torque-controllable, reconfigurable desktop serial manipulators with a shared hardware/software architecture allowing manual reconfiguration within 10 minutes. Torque control via actuator modeling and dynamic compensation enables applications like mixed-reality impedance-control teleoperation and simulator force feedback. It addresses the safety and simulation issues of servo-based cheap robot arms used for visuomotor policy research.

entry.title: Planner-Controller Interaction for Ackermann Navigation: A Matched Simulation and Hardware Benchmark

author.name: Moaiz Saeed, Marah Saleh, Mounis Shawgi, Mohamed Al Musleh

entry.summary: This benchmark study evaluates three geometric path-tracking controllers (Regulated Pure Pursuit, Stanley, Vector Pursuit) paired with two global planners (Hybrid A* and NavFn) on both a 1/10-scale Quanser QCar and a carefully matched Gazebo simulation, producing 60 trial comparisons. The work addresses whether simulation predicts hardware performance for planner-controller combinations, a question usually ignored since planners and controllers are evaluated independently.

entry.title: Quickly, There’s No Time

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi surveys recent AI timeline updates prompted by the METR report, covering new predictions from the AI Futures Project, Paul Christiano (who sees takeover risk within 6-12 months and calls for a pause), and Dwarkesh Patel (superintelligence by 2030), alongside skeptical counterpoints. The post aggregates and contextualizes a significant shift in prominent forecasters' expectations toward much shorter timelines.

entry.title: Solomonoff induction with reflective oracles

author.name: Cole Wyeth

entry.summary: This Alignment Forum linkpost by Cole Wyeth discusses a PIBBSS fellow's paper on reflective-oracle Solomonoff induction (rOSI), which adapts Solomonoff induction using reflective oracles to achieve strong sequence prediction even on partly uncomputable environments. The author argues the paper offers the clearest demonstration that self-reflection can overcome unrealizability, with properties reminiscent of logical induction but in a shorter, more accessible treatment.

entry.title: Modeling LLM Reasoning Dynamics with Structural Representations

author.name: Ilia Karpov, Andrey Atamanyuk, Dmitry Ilvovsky, Aleksandr Anokhin, Alex Elizov, Dmitry Zagorulkin, Sergei O. Kuznetsov

entry.summary: This paper studies the temporal structure of LLM reasoning, combining text, local events, and activity spans (T/E/S) to predict continuation and computation needs. Events and spans improve next-outcome prediction in the large majority of 76 evaluation groups, and the paper contributes budget-allocation counting formulations with proven counting-hardness results. It links reasoning-process structure to predictability and compute budgeting.

entry.title: Risk-Triggered Search: Behavior-Preserving Safe Control

author.name: Xinyu Deng, Bohao Lan, Kunpeng Li, Mingkai Yuan, Weihang Pan, Binbin Lin

entry.summary: Risk-Triggered Search (RTS) adds safety to frozen JEPA world models by unrolling action-conditioned future latent prefixes and training a lightweight risk head with process-violation supervision, enabling internal prediction of collision and forbidden-zone risk from purely visual interfaces. The goal is behavior-preserving safe control without analytical dynamics or explicit collision geometry.

entry.title: Rational Ensemble Logic for Cohort Discovery with Real-World Electrophysiology Data

author.name: Guo-Qiang Zhang, Xubing Hao, Yan Huang, Xiaojin Li, Licong Cui

entry.summary: The paper introduces Rational Ensemble Logic (QEL), a formal language for specifying temporal phenotypes in real-world electrophysiology data using three parameterized modal operators over rational time with Boolean connectives and quantification. Its Labeled Interval Ensemble semantics provides implementation-independent meaning, with connections to morphological operations and finite-state algorithms. The goal is transparent, reproducible clinical cohort discovery.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization: Fusing Expert Knowledge with Numerical Data

author.name: Dongjun Han, Mingyu Lee, Ikjin Lee

entry.summary: Adds an LLM component to multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization so that qualitative expert knowledge about omitted physics in low-fidelity models can be used to compare designs when high-fidelity data are too scarce to learn the LF-HF discrepancy numerically. The LLM interprets expert descriptions and augments the surrogate with this knowledge. An engineering-design-oriented hybrid of LLMs and Bayesian optimization.

entry.title: Learning Trajectories Leave Decodable Traces in Neural Network Weight Space and Internal Representations

author.name: Patrick Krauss, Achim Schilling, Andreas Maier, Thomas Kinfe, Claus Metzner

entry.summary: The study shows that final weights of trained networks encode information about their learning histories: all 30 trained networks could be matched to their initial weights among ten candidates, and networks sharing an initialization developed recognizable final hidden representations even under different batch schedules. This suggests weights preserve decodable traces of initialization and trajectory rather than merely representing alternative solutions.

entry.title: DuoCL: Dual-Path Online Continual Learning

author.name: Jebacyril Arockiaraj, Dhruv Parikh, Rajgopal Kannan, Viktor Prasanna

entry.summary: DuoCL is a dual-path online continual learning framework combining a fast analytic path that accumulates feature statistics from every incoming minibatch with a slow path that periodically adapts the backbone within the available compute budget. Feature alignment compensates for classifier-statistic drift caused by backbone updates. It addresses the real constraint that data arrival rates are independent of training speed in streaming settings.

entry.title: Continuous Noisy-Loop Models

author.name: An T. Le

entry.summary: This theory paper quantifies the gap between efficient learning and the existence of compact probabilistic circuits, using continuous noisy readings of latent spins on a grid. It establishes minimax squared Hellinger risk rates, shows a spline estimator achieves the rate under a reliability bound, and proves that nonnegative decomposable circuits need exponentially many nodes for fixed total-variation error even with bounded leaf supports. This provides new separation results between statistical and computational efficiency.

entry.title: How to Turn an Attention Neural Network into an Interpretable Hard-Logic Predicate Circuit: Truth-Table Predicate Extraction and State-Machine Merging under Ship-of-Theseus Replacement

author.name: Yuchen Li, Zongqi Fan, Xintong Li, Nguyen H. Tran, Ken-Tye Yong

entry.summary: The paper converts trained attention networks wholesale into hard-logic predicate circuits of 0/1 predicates and minimized truth tables, replacing blocks one at a time from the output down so the remaining soft part re-adapts to the frozen circuit. This yields an interpretable, exact-execution surrogate of the attention network including its attention mechanism.

entry.title: Uneven gains in protein-RNA affinity and mutation-effect prediction

author.name: Shangkun Sima, Tongfei Shen, Tianchi Lu

entry.summary: This study evaluates eleven method families for protein-RNA affinity prediction, showing that aggregate accuracy gains transfer unevenly to mutation-effect prediction, ordering, and local accuracy. A controlled CoPRA method reduces absolute-affinity MAE and improves mean-effect accuracy, with external validation across 220 mutation pairs and independent test sets.

entry.title: TangentPDE: Learning Local Operator Responses with Sparse Finite-Difference Supervision

author.name: Xinjian Xie, Ruxuan Chen, Jiashu Li, Tianyu Gao, Ye Wei

entry.summary: TangentPDE trains neural PDE operators to match not just state values but also local directional derivatives, using sparse finite-difference supervision from a reference solver. Its objective jointly constrains state fidelity, response-direction alignment, and response-magnitude calibration.

entry.title: Can LLMs Understand What They Predict? Evaluating Latent Causal Structure Inference in Financial Markets

author.name: Yixiang Zheng, Yuechen Jiang, Zhiwei Liu, Jimin Huang, Yuyan Wang, Sophia Ananiadou

entry.summary: This paper introduces LUCID, a benchmark testing whether LLMs can infer latent causal market structure from event descriptions and historical financial observations, evaluating generated event-induced causal graphs via a reconstruction-based framework. Across 6 open-weight and proprietary LLMs, results probe the assumption that predictive success implies mechanistic understanding.

entry.title: CoSlice: Coordinated Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for 5G Network Slicing Allocation

author.name: Pengxin Wang, Nakjung Choi, Jingdi Chen

entry.summary: CoSlice is a coordinated multi-agent RL framework for inter-slice radio resource block allocation in Open RAN, combining preference-conditioned slice agents for fast per-slice allocation with an LLM-based coordinator that adapts agent objectives using global information. It addresses the dual challenge of intra-slice SLA-efficiency trade-offs and inter-slice competition for shared radio resources. The LLM-as-coordinator design is a distinctive twist on standard MARL for network control.

entry.title: Mapping the Design Space of Feature Sampling for Optical Flow

author.name: Liping Zhang

entry.summary: This paper rethinks correlation-feature sampling for optical flow estimation, observing that RAFT-style fixed-radius cost-volume lookups and WAFT-style single-point indexing apply identical schemes to every position regardless of regional characteristics. The authors map the design space and propose adaptive, region-dependent sampling schemes. It is a focused architectural contribution to a mature task with potential efficiency and accuracy benefits.

entry.title: From Neural Tokens to Language: Dual-View EEG Semantic Bridging for Brain-to-Text Generation

author.name: YaoYang Liu, Jun Dai, ZhuoShi Tang, Weijun Sun, Xiaozhao Fang, Jie Wen

entry.summary: This paper proposes dual-view semantic token bridging for EEG-to-text generation, using raw and sketch images as complementary visual supervision to learn two EEG token streams interfaced with an LLM via branch-specific semantic query bridges. It aims to preserve richer visual semantics than single global EEG representations under noise and subject variability.

entry.title: Pixel2Perspective: A Benchmark for Multi-Modal and Multi-View Generalization in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Aditya Gandhamal, Aniruddh Sikdar, Arya Kishor, Suresh Sundaram

entry.summary: Pixel2Perspective is a benchmark for evaluating open-vocabulary semantic segmentation and multi-angle object localization in VLMs under varying viewpoints and outdoor conditions, motivated by embodied AI like drones and autonomous vehicles. It probes cross-domain generalization failures of CLIP-based segmentation models. The benchmark aims to expose gaps between image understanding and real-world deployment.

entry.title: EviScope: Evidence-Conditioned Sampling for Long-Range 3D Detection

author.name: Mingyang Lyu (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Yinqian Sun (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Gongce Cao (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Chujie Tang (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Yuhao Zhang (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, USA), Lu Jia (University of Science and Technology Beijing, Beijing, China), Qian Zhang (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Bo Wang (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China), Pin Lyu (Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China)

entry.summary: EviScope is a minimal module for query-based camera-radar 3D detection at 150 m range on MAN TruckScenes, where a non-learned bird's-eye evidence field from current radar returns lets each query scale its radial sampling extent and weight eight frames. It adds only 5,450 parameters (0.009%) to RaCFormer with no latency increase and exceeds the published TruckScenes mAP (25.9 vs 24.1). The work tests whether radar evidence should guide query sampling choices.

entry.title: Can Omni-modal LLMs Understand Spoken Intentions?

author.name: Zijie Xin, Tianyi Wang, Daoze Zhang, Jie Yang, Changli Tang, Qijie Wei, Fengyun Rao, Xirong Li

entry.summary: O-IN-Bench evaluates whether omni-modal LLMs understand spoken intentions from full videos with native speech, including when to remain silent and whether responses meet user needs. Unlike prior benchmarks that feed questions as separate text, it tests models in realistic interactive settings. This probes a critical capability gap for voice assistants.

entry.title: RoboDx: Repair and Diagnosis of Faults in Robot Software

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: RoboDx is a benchmark generator of 100 repair and diagnosis tasks for simulated robot navigation software with injected faults and a hidden verifier that only accepts repairs that drive correctly in unseen scenarios. It includes subtle cases like quiet faults that only fail when combined with other faults, plus a hypothesis-selection diagnosis track.

entry.title: Constructive Infinitely Differentiable Guidance Vector Fields for Robotic Control

author.name: Vinicius Mariano Goncalves, Peilin Wu, Adriano Rezende, Weijia Yao

entry.summary: The paper constructs infinitely differentiable guidance vector fields for path following and multi-robot coordination, parameterized by a smoothing parameter that recovers a prior GVF in the zero limit. The construction preserves smoothness under discretization and reduces computation time, making GVFs usable in cascaded controllers that require derivatives of the guidance signal. This removes a practical limitation of existing GVF approaches.

entry.title: Evaluating Governed LLM-Driven ML Experimentation: Lifecycle, Provenance, and Failure Metrics

author.name: Dowling Wong

entry.summary: The paper proposes evaluating autonomous ML-experimentation agents on process quality as well as outcome, introducing a governed harness with a control plane that owns trial lifecycles, checks edit scope, decides keeps/discards, and records an append-only provenance ledger. Governance metrics include invalid-action rate, repeated-bad rate, and provenance completeness. This reframes agent evaluation around accountability and traceability.

entry.title: Resolution as Attention for Efficient Agent Memory Perception

author.name: Siqi Xiang, Zhipeng Xu, Shengrui Liu, Zulong Chen, Chunyan Miao, Shijian Lu

entry.summary: Resolution as Attention (RAA) proposes allocating perceptual detail across an agent's interaction history by rendering past interactions at varying visual resolutions, treating resolution as a form of attention allocation. This complements existing memory-management work that focuses only on what to retain or retrieve, by controlling how much detail each memory carries.

entry.title: Response-Relevant Information Is Not Sufficient for Neural Training-State Equivalence

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh

entry.summary: The paper defines training-state equivalence operationally: two checkpoints are equivalent if they respond alike when training is perturbed and continued. Using one-layer transformers learning modular addition, it shows responses to a weight-decay pulse are highly reproducible, and finds that fifteen descriptors of weight spectra, representation geometry, and optimizer geometry carry response-relevant information beyond weight norm and loss. The negative result is that response-relevant information alone does not establish training-state equivalence.

entry.title: Neural Circuit Architectural Priors for Rat Locomotion

author.name: Nikhil X. Bhattasali, Jaron Cui, Lerrel Pinto, Grace W. Lindsay

entry.summary: This work develops embodied simulations of rat locomotion in which neural circuit models with biologically grounded architectural priors, informed by experimental connectivity and single-unit dynamics, control simulated bodies. It aims to enable study of increasingly complex bodies and circuits, advancing biologically realistic neuro-embodied simulation.

entry.title: TOGBench: Benchmarking and Improving Tiny-Object Generation Fidelity in Aerial Imagery

author.name: Chanhwi Jeong, Dongmin You, Seungwook Kim

entry.summary: TOGBench is an object-level benchmark measuring how faithfully generative models render tiny objects (vehicles, ships, aircraft) that dominate aerial imagery, a failure mode overlooked by prompt-following or human-preference evaluations. The paper also proposes two simple train- and inference-time techniques to improve tiny-object fidelity. It documents that existing generative models struggle substantially more with tiny objects.

entry.title: Fuse to Recognize the Unseen: Class-Relative Infrared-Visible Fusion for Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Zehao Gao, Jie Feng, Wenda Zhao, Junpeng Zhang, Ronghua Shang, Weisheng Dong

entry.summary: Shows that naively injecting infrared cues into CLIP-based open-vocabulary segmentation can disrupt RGB-language alignment, and proposes an RGB-anchored, class-relative strategy that applies thermal corrections only where they fix RGB misclassifications. The pixel-level RGB-IR semantic analysis motivates selective fusion to improve unseen-class recognition under challenging illumination. A vision-language fusion contribution bridging image fusion and open-vocabulary segmentation.

entry.title: Bias-Only Training Dynamics in ReLU Networks

author.name: Shreyas Chaudhari, Jose M. F. Moura

entry.summary: The paper characterizes training dynamics of one-hidden-layer ReLU networks with fixed random weights and trainable biases through activation codes, showing gradients depend on inputs only via these binary patterns and that training reduces to a sequence of linear least-squares problems while codes remain fixed. Given bias-only networks are universal approximators, this yields an unusually tractable window into nonlinear network training.

entry.title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations

author.name: Hongnian Huang, Andrew Stump

entry.summary: This paper establishes stability guarantees for parallel transport convolution on Riemannian manifolds, proving L2-continuous dependence of the convolution output on the metric in the C2 topology for continuous signals and localized kernels. The analysis develops perturbation estimates for geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and the exponential map. A rigorous mathematical foundation for robustness of geometric deep learning architectures.

entry.title: Agent Verifiers in Counterfactual Analysis: A Pilot Study Benchmarking Agentic Heterogeneous Treatment Effects

author.name: Satiyabooshan Murugaboopathy, Entejar Alam, Adel Daoud, Connor T. Jerzak

entry.summary: This pilot study explores using LLM agents to expand covariate space of randomized experiments by retrieving fast-moving local context for heterogeneous treatment effect estimation, and confronts the verification problem: retrieval and encoder leakage can pull post-treatment information into nominally pretreatment summaries. Guided by a two-channel information bound, it proposes a three-layer benchmark protocol covering retrieval admissibility, heterogeneity validation, and verification. An early but careful intersection of agentic AI and causal inference.

entry.title: When Normal-Only Updates Are Not Enough: Test-Time Adaptation in Reconstruction-Based Time-Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jianhuan Mao, Mengxiao Zhu, Yue Pei, Lei Li, Haogang Zhu

entry.summary: This paper asks whether test-time adaptation reliably improves reconstruction-based time-series anomaly detection even under idealized conditions where only samples labeled as normal are used for updates. Using controlled interventions across nine benchmark families, four optimizer configurations, and five random seeds, the study probes a basic assumption of online TTA for anomaly detection. The findings challenge the assumption that normal-only adaptation is sufficient.

entry.title: Algorithmic Market Making Can Lead to Rough Volatility Through the Order Book

author.name: Sai Niranjan Ramachandran

entry.summary: This paper presents a mechanism by which predominantly algorithmic market making can generate rough volatility in financial markets. It models each market maker as a desk applying a first-order gradient rule to move order distances toward oracle-provided targets, acting asynchronously as relevant information arrives. This explains how order flow near instability with power-law memory decay, previously assumed, can arise endogenously from order book dynamics.

entry.title: Zonotopic Analysis of Quantization Error in Neural Networks

author.name: Robert Debbas, \'Eric Goubault, Sylvie Putot

entry.summary: This work presents a zonotope-based abstract interpretation framework for verifying quantized ReLU feed-forward networks, introducing a unified round-clamp abstract transformer with proven soundness and optimality properties, extended to constrained zonotopes. Experiments on ACAS Xu benchmarks demonstrate tighter quantization error bounds.

entry.title: ConserveEdit: Source-Anchored Transactions for Drift-Bounded Iterative Image Editing

author.name: Shuyang Jiang, Fucheng Deng, Yuchuan Luo, Zhenyu Wu

entry.summary: ConserveEdit is an editor-agnostic controller for iterative instruction-driven image editing that treats each refinement step as a transaction against a contract compiled from the source image, separating authorized edit regions from protected content with explicit tolerances. Candidates from a frozen editor are committed only if target progress, drift, and quality checks pass.

entry.title: NOTREKS: Marginal Independence in Score-based Structure Learning

author.name: Fabian Bleile, Sarah Lumpp, Mathias Drton

entry.summary: NOTREKS introduces a way to incorporate prior knowledge that pairs of variables are marginally independent into score-based causal discovery, encoding it as a no-trek graphical constraint under faithfulness. The authors propose a power-series trek penalty for gradient-based optimization and a trek constraint for order-based search, with analysis of why such information helps in finite samples. This is a thoughtful contribution to the causal discovery methodology literature.

entry.title: ReflectRec: Cycle-Consistency Preference Verification for LLM-based Recommendation

author.name: Dae Kyoo Kim, Heejung Cho, Sungmoo Hong, Eunil Park

entry.summary: Proposes ReflectRec for LLM-based recommendation, built around a preference-to-history round-trip verifier whose recall score signals how recoverable a generated preference note is, enabling conditional regeneration. The pipeline adds a semantic Stage-1 prompt and retrieval of future watches from behaviorally similar users, improving results on MovieLens benchmarks.

entry.title: PRISM: Profiling and Representation of Individual Stereotypical Motion

author.name: Austin A. MBaye, Savik Kinger, Matthew S. Goodwin

entry.summary: PRISM characterizes repetitive (stereotypical) movement using tracked masks and dense optical flow rather than fixed joint landmarks, measuring intensity, spatial extent, frequency, and rhythmicity. Validated across 1,890 synthetic conditions plus a hand-motion experiment showing variation invisible to identical COCO-17 trajectories. Co-authored with Matthew Goodwin, it targets understanding of repetitive behaviors relevant to autism research and accessible health monitoring.

entry.title: Can AI Understand Indonesian Children's Book Illustrations? Compliance, Safety, and the Cultural Alignment Gap

author.name: Rian Adam Rajagede, Rochana Prih Hastuti, Fitri Hasanah Amhar

entry.summary: This study evaluates whether vision-language models can assess children's book illustrations against Indonesia's government-issued Book Leveling Guideline, covering guideline compliance, safety, and cultural alignment across four reading levels. It compares VLM assessments on real published pages and probes the cultural alignment gap between AI evaluation and local standards. It is a valuable culturally grounded audit of VLM reliability in a non-Western educational context.

entry.title: SIRAZ: Sparse Inter-Layer Residual Aggregation for Zero-Shot Visual Neural Decoding

author.name: Neha, Mudasir Ganaie

entry.summary: SIRAZ tackles zero-shot visual neural decoding by aggregating sparse inter-layer residuals from vision model representations to better match the brain's hierarchical visual processing. It aims to reconstruct or retrieve visual stimuli from neural activity while aligning machine representations more closely with biological ones. The work bridges brain-computer interfaces and representation learning.

entry.title: CURVTON-205K: A Mask-Free Difficulty-Stratified Synthetic Dataset for Robust and Scalable Virtual Try-On

author.name: Dipan Bartaula, Anuj Shrestha, Ankit Belbase, Anish Bishwakarma, Saroj Poudel, Samip Ghimire, Shashank Bhatta, Eric Arazo, Binod Bhattarai

entry.summary: CURVTON-205K is a synthetic dataset of 205K triplets for virtual try-on generated via a pipeline coordinating editing and generation models with VLM guidance, requiring no parsing masks or dense-pose annotations. It argues that VTON failure modes stem from dataset design and long-tail regimes, providing difficulty-stratified data covering occlusions, poses, and under-represented garments. A solid data-centric contribution to a practical application.

entry.title: DetailScale-SR: Decoupling Restoration and Continuous Detail Control for Real-World Super-Resolution

author.name: Shengchuan Gao, Zhongjie Duan, Yingda Chen, Jingjing Chen

entry.summary: DetailScale-SR is a preference-conditioned super-resolution framework that continuously controls reconstructed detail for a fixed low-resolution input without prompt rewriting or post-processing. It learns a smooth family of reconstructions from conservative restoration to richly textured output while keeping content recovery separate from detail preference.

entry.title: One Affinity, Two Axes: Bidirectional Slot Attention for Iterative Aggregation across the Structure--Detail Spectrum in Visual Retrieval

author.name: Zihang Wang, Wenkai Zhu, Lingdong Kong, Teng Yan, Alan Liang, Shuyuan Li, Xieyuanli Chen, Dong Kong, Guanyu Zong

entry.summary: BiSA reformulates visual retrieval aggregation as iterative bidirectional slot attention, where a shared token-slot affinity is interpreted along competition and consensus axes to jointly capture structural and fine-grained cues. The method progressively refines learnable slots into compact global descriptors from dense patch tokens. It targets non-redundant scene decomposition for retrieval.

entry.title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World

author.name: Chenjie Zhao, Zhiliang Zhu, Quan Chen, Yuquan Xue, Xingxue Shi, Puyue Wang, Zhiqiang Zhao, Kangye Zheng, Boyang Xu, Mingwei Lin, Dejun Li

entry.summary: NereidVLA is a vision-language-action model for underwater navigation that first trains a marine spatial knowledge model (Sea2Know) on ~2 million examples, then adapts it with expert trajectories under simulated underwater vehicle dynamics. Given RGB histories and language instructions, it predicts discrete motion tokens decoding into local 3D trajectories. This addresses the scarcity of paired robot trajectories in marine vision-language data.

entry.title: Incremental Speciation in Evolutionary Red Teaming of Large Language Models

author.name: Onkar Shelar, Travis Desell

entry.summary: Studies speciation design choices (embedding vs. NLI dissimilarity, representative vs. density-based grouping) in black-box evolutionary red teaming of LLMs, calibrating on a 3,139-prompt archive. Shows different compatible representations produce different species structures at the same threshold, informing diversity maintenance in automated red-teaming search.

entry.title: Navigating Robots from Unknown and Uncalibrated Exocentric Cameras via Map Estimation

author.name: Raul Steinmetz, Raphael Druon, Yusuke Yoshiyasu, Akihisa Ohya, Ayanori Yorozu

entry.summary: ROMUX enables point-goal navigation with obstacle avoidance from wall- or ceiling-mounted exocentric cameras that are unknown and uncalibrated, removing the need for time-consuming professional calibration prior to deployment. The agent estimates robot-centric obstacle maps directly from uncalibrated camera views.

entry.title: Dual-Actuation Emulation of Scaled Relative Orbital Dynamics on a Free-Flyer

author.name: Elias Krantz, Pedro Roque, Gunnar Tibert, Huina Mao, Christer Fuglesang

entry.summary: This paper presents a dual-actuation architecture on an open-source free-flyer testbed that physically emulates Clohessy-Wiltshire orbital dynamics on the ground, using two parallel model predictive controllers driving solenoid thrusters and bidirectional propellers. A dynamic similitude mapping scales orbital scenarios onto a limited testbed floor. This enables hardware-in-the-loop testing of spacecraft docking and rendezvous behaviors on Earth.

entry.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese

author.name: Carla Teixeira Lopes, Daniel F\'elix

entry.summary: LusoClin is a publicly released dataset of synthetic clinical notes in European Portuguese, generated by fine-tuning Llama 3.2 3B with QLoRA on preprocessed real clinical data. It addresses privacy-driven data scarcity that hampers clinical NLP research in low-resource languages. This enables privacy-preserving research on clinical note search and cohort identification for an underserved language.

entry.title: Searching the Pareto Front: Multi-Objective Retrieval for Heterogeneous Scientific Modalities

author.name: Song Young Oh, Nesar Ramachandra, Bin Xia, Ian Foster, Kyle Chard

entry.summary: This paper compares multimodal foundation models against independently trained per-modality embeddings fused via multi-objective Pareto optimization for scientific retrieval in cosmology, covering star formation histories, spectra, and multi-wavelength observations. It investigates whether late fusion provides an adaptive alternative to shared embedding spaces under uneven modality coverage. The findings inform architecture choices for heterogeneous scientific data.

entry.title: Training-Free Domain Generation for One-Shot Federated Learning with Server-Side Pre-trained Diffusion Models

author.name: Yixuan Tong, Yuanguo Bi, Mingjian Zhi, Wenchao Xu, Yuan Wu

entry.summary: Proposes FedDoG, a training-free framework for one-shot federated learning that uses server-side pre-trained diffusion models to synthesize data approximating heterogeneous client distributions. This reduces client computational burden and improves visual guidance compared to prior diffusion-based OSFL approaches. Addresses communication and computation constraints in federated settings.

entry.title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution

author.name: Wenhao Yuan, Longhui Yuan, Zexi Jia, Ningzhe Shi, Jingwei Li, Shipeng Cen, Pengcheng Luo, Jie Zhou, Jinchao Zhang

entry.summary: OpenKAGE is an agent-group evolution framework for open-ended lifelong learning in which agents autonomously explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities from their own and others' experiences. It uses a two-layer knowledge representation separating situated memories from shareable knowledge to enable continual self-improvement beyond predefined tasks and curricula.

entry.title: Vibe-Trading: Towards Agent-Native Trading

author.name: Haozhe Wu, Zhonghang Li, Chao Huang

entry.summary: Vibe-Trading is an agent-native framework and workspace for building, evaluating, and evolving financial trading agents, unifying market research, data, strategy generation, backtesting, and portfolio management. It targets the core problem that trading agents must preserve reliable state as prices, news, positions, and capital change continuously, so results must remain tied to the correct time and execution context. It is positioned as infrastructure rather than a single model.

entry.title: Image Watermarking With Memory Across Reissuance

author.name: Xinyuan Li, Yi Nian, Xiaoqin Feng, Tiankai Yang, Yue Zhao

entry.summary: The paper formalizes reissuable provenance for images: determining whether an image region is current, superseded, or unissued and recovering each region's last authorized revision, with abstention under insufficient evidence. Its Generational Stratigraphy Fields combine watermark evidence with an authenticated live reference, allowing replacement or retirement of watermarks without rewriting already-circulated copies.

entry.title: MEM-STRESS: Longitudinal Field Study of a Wearable-Informed AI Chatbot for Stress Management

author.name: Soorya Ram Shimgekar, Pragya Singh, Shivam Sharma, Chandrayee Roy, Koustuv Saha, Antti Oulasvirta, Talayeh Aledavood

entry.summary: MEM-STRESS is a stress-support chatbot that converts wearable ring physiological data into a layered memory (daily records, baseline deviations, LLM summaries) driving multi-session conversations grounded in Dialectical Behavior Therapy. A four-week non-randomized field study with 60 adults compared it against a chatbot remembering only past conversations. The work explores integrating physiological signals into chatbot memory for personalized mental-health support.

entry.title: TOMAS: Topology-Aware Operation Modeling and Adaptive Staging for Egocentric Hand Forecasting

author.name: Guanzhong Sun, Junyi Ma, Yuxuan Wu, Erhang Zhang, Chenyang Xu, Yanzi Miao, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TOMAS, a framework for forecasting hand trajectories from egocentric video that links hand skeletal topology and articulation dynamics with object semantics to capture operation-dependent motion patterns, plus adaptive staging of predictions. This targets the problem that different manipulation intentions yield different trajectories for the same object.

entry.title: Gaussian Primitive Fusion for Any-Resolution Multimodal Images

author.name: Baoshuo Cai, Xinrui Jiang, Bing Cao

entry.summary: Proposes Gaussian Primitive Fusion (GPF), which reformulates multimodal image fusion in a shared continuous Gaussian space so that source images of different native resolutions need not be resampled to a common grid. By fitting native-resolution observations with shared Gaussian geometry and modality-specific content, it avoids artifacts introduced by resampling. This is a technical improvement for infrared-visible and similar fusion tasks.

entry.title: OCTR2A: Real-Time RGB-to-BEV Trajectory Projection and Forecasting at Urban Intersections

author.name: Emanuele Iacobelli, Simone Teglia, Francesco Pro, Claudia Melis Tonti, Irene Amerini

entry.summary: Introduces OCTR2A, a modular pipeline that reconstructs and forecasts bird's-eye-view agent trajectories from paired opposite-corner RGB cameras on existing urban infrastructure, avoiding costly LiDAR, HD maps, or calibrated setups. It combines per-view detection, cross-camera geometric matching, transformer-based BEV projection, and forecasting, running in real time. Targets practical intersection safety analytics.

entry.title: Negotiating Control and Accountability among Stakeholders in High-Risk AI Use Cases: Development and Evaluation of the Method ALIGN

author.name: Lena Schneider, Daniel Boos, Gudela Grote

entry.summary: ALIGN is a scenario-based governance method, developed from human factors literature, expert interviews, and field observation in a high-risk railway AI use case, that helps stakeholders surface and negotiate accountability-control misalignments. It provides structured guidance for stakeholder involvement in AI development and deployment in safety-critical domains.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Cyber-Physical Attack Path Identification in Smart Grids

author.name: Amr Elshazly, Jesse Roberts, Rachad Atat, Muhammad Ismail

entry.summary: The paper presents a physics-grounded framework using LLMs to identify high-impact cyber-physical attack paths in power grids, combining cascading-failure-derived physical impact with LLM adversarial reasoning over topology and threat semantics. It aims to fill the gap between purely topological analysis and slow simulation-based offline methods for rapid evolving-scenario evaluation.

entry.title: Budgeted Proper Loss Design for Uncertain Decision Thresholds

author.name: Ankit Sharma (International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore)

entry.summary: This paper studies how to design a proper loss when multiple decision makers with different error-cost thresholds will consume the same probability estimates. Among integrable loss weights with a positive floor and fixed total mass, the authors derive the weight minimizing distribution-free worst-case regret from surrogate to threshold-averaged decision regret, with a closed-form clipping solution found via one-dimensional root search. A careful theoretical contribution to loss design under threshold uncertainty.

entry.title: Conformally Calibrated Adaptive Computation in Neural Operators

author.name: Abdul Qadir Ibrahim, Martin Burger, Abel Maviano Jonathan

entry.summary: The authors study adaptive computation in neural operators using conformal calibration to choose Fourier modes or channel width per input under a fixed error budget. They propose a triangle-inequality envelope and a direct-score rule with marginal guarantees, including abstention when calibration is infeasible. Notably, on Burgers and Darcy flow benchmarks, mode selection reduced active spectral support without a measurable latency reduction, candidly exposing the gap between computation savings and wall-clock speed.

entry.title: CAFE-AQI: Coverage-Aware Day-Ahead AQI Forecasting with Early Warning and Conformal Uncertainty in Bangladesh

author.name: Md Rafid Islam, Rafsan Jany, Rafid Bin Zaman, Mohammad Fahim Islam, Hafiz Abdur Rahman

entry.summary: CAFE-AQI is a coverage-aware framework for forecasting next-day maximum AQI in Bangladesh, with probability estimates for Unhealthy-or-worse conditions and conformal uncertainty quantification. The authors' audit revealed a sharp sensor coverage expansion after August 2022 and that 103 city labels correspond to only 61 unique AQI trajectories, which they address via trajectory weighting and chronological splits. The framework combines temporal and pollutant features with early warning capability.

entry.title: FDM+: A Framework for Constrained Control of the 2D Radiative Transport Equation

author.name: Hualing Zhong, Shuai Wang, Hui Xie, Heng Yong

entry.summary: FDM+ extends the frozen diffusion model approach to constrained control of the 2D radiative transport equation, addressing dimensional heterogeneity between control and state variables, resolution mismatch between numerical solvers and deep models, and solution non-uniqueness. It introduces a decoupled prediction architecture, an efficient parameterization strategy, and a total error bound combining parameterization and model estimation errors. This enables principled diffusion-based control for challenging PDE-constrained problems.

entry.title: UCLIR: Unsupervised Continual Learning using Independent Representations

author.name: Kamel Aouaidjia, Yanchao Duan, Zihui Zhen, Xin Li, Yongfei Lv, Chongsheng Zhang

entry.summary: UCLIR tackles the degradation of regularization-based continual learning as task count grows, caused by updates spreading across densely interconnected parameters. Inspired by the Exponential Distance Rule from neuroscience, it learns independent representations so that inter-area updates remain less task-dependent while learning is locally correlated. This preserves earlier-task knowledge more effectively in unsupervised continual learning.

entry.title: Tell Me How Sure You Are: Communicating Uncertainty in Auxiliary Evidence to Foundation Models

author.name: Soumyajit Chatterjee, Baturalp Buyukates, Abhirup Ghosh

entry.summary: This paper systematically demonstrates that communicating uncertainty about contextual auxiliary information to foundation models improves downstream decisions, formulating the problem as zero-shot foundation-model-assisted image classification with text-based auxiliary evidence. It shows that conventional prompting discards useful uncertainty cues that can be exploited.

entry.title: A Differential Theory of Quality-Resource Trade-offs for AI Model Selection: The Multiresource Frontier and Its Minimax Price

author.name: Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: This single-author theory paper develops a differential geometry of quality-resource frontiers relating model error to latency, parameter count, compute, and energy, introducing a price-independent plane-curve representation linking effective resource channels to remaining log-error depth. It aims to make scaling-law trade-offs explicit and comparable across resource channels.

entry.title: GRAFT: Graph-Regularized Prototype Fields for Realistic Test-Time Adaptation of VLMs

author.name: Maxx Richard Rahman, Wolfgang Maass

entry.summary: GRAFT improves test-time adaptation of vision-language models by modeling adapted prototypes as text anchors plus a displacement field partially pooled over a semantic class graph via a Gaussian Markov random field prior, with explicit class-occurrence handling. This addresses failures of transductive TTA when few vocabulary classes appear in a batch or streams are correlated.

entry.title: Two is better than one: optimizing binary rating scales for online platforms

author.name: Liren Shan, Alec Sun, Jingyan Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies rating-scale design on online platforms, proving that splitting a single rating scale into two user-specific scales can always improve item ranking quality, and characterizing optimal multi-scale designs as evenly spaced 0-1 step functions with an adaptive extension. It connects mechanism design to practical platform feedback collection.

entry.title: Sightline: Long-Window Speculative Decoding for Fast SVG Generation

author.name: Yanchao Li, Ben Gao, Jiaqing Xie, Yusu Zhang, Beilun Wang, Yanbo Wang, Xiaohua Xu, Nanqing Dong, Tianfan Fu, Zhongyu Huang

entry.summary: Sightline accelerates SVG generation models, which decode code token-by-token, using speculative decoding with unusually long verification windows. The key insight is that draft acceptance errors on SVG are rare and clumped rather than uniform, so a verification window matched to the drafter's horizon, filled by a wide draft tree, pays off. Experiments across text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG show lossless speedups, offering a transferable lesson about workload-specific speculative decoding design.

entry.title: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters

author.name: Mojtaba Asadollahi, Danial Khajehzadeh, Abolfazl Ramezanpour

entry.summary: The authors extend quantum annealing into a quantum neural network framework and evaluate it on prototypical hard optimization problems. They show that even a small network width of 2 can exponentially reduce the required annealing depth in the quantum search problem, mitigating the exponentially small energy gaps that plague standard annealing at discontinuous phase transitions. This suggests network width as a new resource for practical quantum optimization.

entry.title: ViLFlow: Parallel Vision-Language Generation with Continuous Latent Flows

author.name: Kevin Zhai, Bian Sun, Zhenyi Wang, Song Wang

entry.summary: ViLFlow is a continuous-flow vision-language model that jointly models output embeddings and decodes tokens in parallel, moving beyond sequential autoregressive generation and discrete diffusion. It adapts pretrained continuous language generation to visual question answering and image captioning using a visually adapted teacher providing image-guided denoising supervision. This offers a new architectural direction for faster parallel multimodal generation.

entry.title: Coverage Governs Accuracy: When to Expand the Lexicon and When to Fall Back in Low-Resource Manchu OCR

author.name: Ruixin Yu, Zifan Wang, Mingxin Ding, Xiaoxin Sun, Dongjie Wang, Suhua Wang, Minghao Yin

entry.summary: Studies lexicon-constrained decoding for Manchu OCR, using morphological expansion to generate roughly 510k word candidates and analyzing when to expand the lexicon versus fall back on confidence. The paper decomposes accuracy into coverage and in-lexicon precision, showing how expansion size and fallback interact for agglutinative low-resource languages.

entry.title: Constructing Dynamic Conversations with Neural Back-channel Generation and Voice-line Scheduling

author.name: Yifang Pan, Chris Landreth, Karan Singh

entry.summary: A neural scheduler combines two independently recorded or synthesized voice tracks into a unified dyadic conversation, inserting pauses, overlaps, and predicted back-channels. The back-channel predictor uses both audio and content of a turn to identify opportunities for listener responses. This targets game-industry voice production, where conversational dynamics between characters are currently assembled manually.

entry.title: EyeDiT: Anatomy-Grounded Multi-Modal Eye Generation and Simulation

author.name: Yonghan Lee, Zachary Willms, Kun Liu, Pushkar Anand, Ali Behrooz, Dmitri Model, Dinesh Manocha, Yatong An

entry.summary: EyeDiT generates anatomy-grounded 3D eye data for AR/VR eye-tracking development, trained on OCT, labeled anatomy point clouds, and near-eye images via a multi-modal anatomy VAE and an eye latent DiT generator. Unlike image-centric synthetic eye generators, it provides controllable 3D anatomy with anatomical labels. Synthetic data of this kind can accelerate eye-tracking research where real labeled data is scarce and privacy-sensitive.

entry.title: A Hardware-Aware Comprehensive Study of Edge Vision Deployment with A Unified Hardware-Model-Runtime Mapping Framework

author.name: Le Duc An, Le Duc Thanh, Vo Hoai Viet

entry.summary: This survey bridges edge hardware constraints, vision model architectures, and deployment toolchains, proposing a taxonomy that classifies edge hardware into GPUs/NPUs, embedded MPUs/SoCs, and microcontrollers. It aggregates multi-source benchmarks for image classification and object detection across the computing spectrum to guide model selection for resource-constrained devices. It is a practical reference for practitioners deploying computer vision at the edge.

entry.title: DORMS: Image Segmentation via Depth-Ordered Region Merge Trees

author.name: Furkan Mumcu, Yasin Yilmaz

entry.summary: DORMS is a fully algorithmic, training-free segmentation method that builds depth-ordered merge trees from monocular depth maps via deterministic union-find sweeps, using area, depth persistence, and spatial contact constraints. It requires no learned parameters in segmentation, only an off-the-shelf depth estimator, and shows competitive results on COCO Panoptic, Cityscapes, and ADE20K. A refreshingly classical counterpoint to learned segmentation.

entry.title: Stabilizing Neural-to-Image Retrieval with Frequency-Domain Priors and Adaptive Supervision

author.name: YaoYang Liu, ZhuoShi Tang, Haopeng Lai, Weijun Sun, Xiaozhao Fang, Jie Wen

entry.summary: This work improves visual neural decoding by aligning noisy EEG/MEG signals with pretrained vision-language embeddings in a shared semantic space, using frequency-domain priors and adaptive supervision. The goal is reliable neural-to-image retrieval despite trial variability and subject dependence.

entry.title: Psychometrics-Inspired Coreset Selection for Image Quality Assessment

author.name: Susu Jiang, Xuelin Shen, Baoliang Chen

entry.summary: GRAM is a quality-aware representation learning framework for image quality assessment inspired by the graded response model from psychometrics, modeling how latent quality drives probabilities of successive assessment grades. It improves coreset selection for reducing the annotation burden of subjective IQA datasets.

entry.title: AnchorUp: Anchoring Feature Upsampling on a Classical Interpolation

author.name: Kotaro Horikawa, Keisuke Toida, Junya Komori, Kazuhiro Hotta

entry.summary: The authors observe that learned feature upsamplers for dense prediction spend most capacity reproducing smooth content that plain bilinear interpolation already provides. AnchorUp anchors learned upsampling on classical interpolation so networks only refine edges and fine details. This simplifies upsampling modules built atop vision foundation model features.

entry.title: EgoJev: Finding Evidence in Egocentric Video by Reading VLM Decisions

author.name: Chunggi Lee, Hanspeter Pfister

entry.summary: EgoJev is a training-free frame selector for long egocentric video QA that reads the VLM's output distribution when choosing among labeled frames, exploiting the finding that VLMs locate evidence moments better by choosing than by writing timestamps. It compares all frame candidates in a single decision. The method targets wearable assistant applications.

entry.title: ReCoCo: From Patches to Compositions for Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Juan Guti\'errez, Saman Zadtootaghaj, Jos\'e Luis Blanco-Murillo, Sara Atito

entry.summary: ReCoCo extends self-supervised cross-view consistency from patch level to regional composition level without requiring explicit correspondence estimation or semantic grouping assumptions. It represents content shared between augmented views in a principled way to learn stronger dense features. This targets the known difficulty of self-supervised dense representation learning.

entry.title: UltraTex: Aligning Physical Knowledge for High-Fidelity PBR Texture Generation

author.name: Jingzhi Bao, Xiaohe Ma, Hong Li, Yuanming Hu, Xiaoguang Han

entry.summary: UltraTex is a cascaded multi-view diffusion framework for generating physically based rendering texture maps from a single reference image, jointly predicting albedo and world-space shading normals before inferring metallic-roughness maps. It moves beyond appearance matching by integrating physical knowledge for accurate relighting. This improves on generative methods that produce realistic albedo but poor material attributes.

entry.title: Joint Image Denoising and Interpolation via Mixed Graph Filtering

author.name: Gene Cheung, Niruhan Viswarupan, Romisaa Elsaidy

entry.summary: Models joint image denoising and interpolation with mixed graph filtering, using undirected graph filters for denoising and directed filters for interpolation, and proves that pseudo-linear denoisers and interpolators can be interpreted as MAP solution filters under corresponding smoothness priors. This yields principled joint formulations avoiding task-interaction artifacts.

entry.title: Learning and Control in Physically Coupled Dynamical Systems

author.name: Bao Trung Truong, Dat Thanh Nguyen, Thinh T. Doan

entry.summary: Introduces TAG, a low-cost robotic testbed combining a ball-in-maze board with a rotary inverted pendulum whose dynamics physically disturb each other, creating a benchmark for learning control in coupled dynamical systems. Presents complementary model-based and model-free reinforcement learning paradigms accounting for cross-subsystem interference.

entry.title: Radar-Native Control Barrier Functions: Doppler Range Rate as a Measured Barrier Derivative

author.name: Johannes Mootz, Hesam Mojtahedi, Reza Akhavian

entry.summary: This work uses FMCW radar Doppler measurements of radial relative velocity directly as the derivative of an ego-centered range control barrier function, yielding a closed-form filter on robot forward velocity for safe navigation around dynamic obstacles. Validation across 508 paired encounters with a sensor-error margin accounts for range, Doppler, ego velocity, and bearing errors.

entry.title: BiPathCPG: A Novel Load-Sharing Design Architecture for Compound Planetary Gearboxes

author.name: Deepak Kapa, Aman Singh, Saketh Vegesna, Suryank Joshi, Mayank Goswami, Shishir Kolathaya

entry.summary: The paper proposes BiPathCPG, a compound planetary gearbox architecture with an idle second-stage sun gear aimed at balancing torque density, efficiency, and stiffness for quasi-direct-drive legged robot actuators. It targets the width, mass, and torsional-stiffness problems of conventional 3D-printed compound planetary designs. This is relevant to legged robot actuator hardware development.

entry.title: When to Refine: Selective Search for Frozen Visual World Models

author.name: Jingni Huang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Selective CEM Refinement (SCR), a learned gating rule that decides whether to continue cross-entropy method search with a frozen visual world model based on action movement, terminal cost decline, and plan diversity, without additional rollouts. On PushT it nearly matches fixed 15-iteration search success while reducing computation. This is a compute-efficiency contribution for world-model-based planning.

entry.title: OmniFish: A Bioinspired, Modular, Reconfigurable Soft Robotic Fish Enabling Multi-Modal Swimming

author.name: Mathias Jensen, Saravana Prashanth Murali Babu

entry.summary: OmniFish is a modular soft robotic fish with a tendon-driven compliant segmented spine whose stiffness is reconfigured via mechanical jamming, enabling all five major body-and-caudal-fin swimming modes from a single actuator. Morphometric analysis across fish species guided the design. This demonstrates a single platform covering the spectrum of fish-like locomotion.

entry.title: Hierarchical Admittance-Impedance Control for Mobile Manipulator Load Transfer

author.name: Minghao Xu, Thushara Sandakalum, Christina Dao Wen Lee, Marcelo H. Ang Jr

entry.summary: The authors present a hierarchical controller combining an inner Cartesian impedance controller, an outer 6D admittance supervisor, and workspace-aware mobile-base assistance for human-guided load transfer, motivated by assistive tasks like airport baggage handling. The system was validated on a torque-controlled Franka Research 3 manipulator, demonstrating compliant load support while a human guides motion with small physical forces.

entry.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties

author.name: Yulia Alexandr, Moritz Grillo, Thiago Holleben, Guido Mont\'ufar, Teresa Yu

entry.summary: This paper gives a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties, proving that determinantal equations from rank constraints generate the defining ideals and thereby resolving a conjecture of Alexandr-Montufar. The proof uses orbit closures of matrix pencils characterized via the Kronecker canonical form.

entry.title: On exporting agency to Washington, DC

author.name: ethanelasky

entry.summary: Argues that AI safety researchers in the Bay Area wrongly treat US legislation as outside their locus of control, when upcoming low-salience, bipartisan AI safety bills have still-malleable text. The author catalogs pending bills (FRONTIER Act, AI Kill Switch Act, etc.) and urges technical people to engage directly in shaping legislative outcomes.

entry.title: AI Takeoff: Complex Tasks and Pacing

author.name: ronbodkin

entry.summary: Builds a quantitative model (with Claude Fable 5.2 assistance) of AI-driven research progress as a three-stage pipeline - small-scale experiments, scaled runs with transfer, and real value with validity - arguing that research taste (transfer and validity improvements) is hard-to-supervise and will lag easily-supervised optimization. Used to argue that rapid takeoff arguments based on the METR report may overstate near-term AI research automation.

entry.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications article applying satellite-derived learned representations to estimate malaria burden across sub-Saharan Africa under scenarios of intervention disruption. The work illustrates how geospatial foundation-model-style representations can support epidemiological monitoring in data-scarce settings; the supplied content field was empty, so the assessment relies on the title and venue.

entry.title: From real to synthetic: PSG-GAN learns sleep apnea signal dynamics for AI training

author.name: Riku Huttunen, Samu Kainulainen, Matias Rusanen, Sami Myllymaa, Juha T\"oyr\"as, Timo Lepp\"anen, Henri Korkalainen

entry.summary: The authors developed PSG-GAN, a generative adversarial network that co-synthesizes longer multi-signal polysomnography segments capturing inter-signal dynamics of obstructive sleep apnea, going beyond prior work on short single-signal segments. Synthetic EEG/EOG band powers match real distributions across sleep stages, enabling privacy-friendly training data for sleep medicine AI.

entry.title: Panini- Feasible Grammar For Robot Designs

author.name: Mayukh Debnath, Manan Roy Choudhury

entry.summary: Panini introduces a typed production grammar with case-role relations, parameter inheritance, and specificity-based rule arbitration to generate both robot manipulation skills and morphologies, with a geometric realization map translating grammar composition into SE(3) transformations. The paper shows arbitration decisions can be recovered from geometric containment, with agreement around 0.905 versus a 0.611 baseline.

entry.title: PGU-Decoder: Prior-Guided Unified Decoding for Industrial Road-Network Map Updating

author.name: Yuguang Ning, Bingbing Kang, Nan Zhao, Zhixuan Li, Ze Zhao, Dongdong Liu, Wenjian Zhu, Zekai Liu, Junhui Wang

entry.summary: PGU-Decoder is a unified decoding framework that handles three road-network map update tasks together: intra-intersection topology generation, merging/diverging detection, and drivable-area detection. Its Prior Query Module constructs point-level prior queries from sampled road-network geometry locations, preserving positional priors during decoding. This replaces separate pipelines and reduces operational costs for production map maintenance relevant to navigation and autonomous driving.

entry.title: TRESS: A Fixed-Size History Representation for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Shusen Ma, Yangchun Xie, Xudong Zuo, Haizhou Liang, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: TRESS is a forecasting model for irregular time series that retains the latest observations at their original timestamps while summarizing each variable's full history, keeping the representation a fixed size as records grow. Its query-conditioned event lifting module weights deviations from the latest value by observation age and forecast horizon, and a channel-specific decoder combines these features with historical statistics. This captures both recency and long-range context for irregularly sampled data.

entry.title: ICICLE: In-Context Inference for Curve-Learning Extrapolation

author.name: Laurits Fredsgaard, Michael Riis Andersen, Mikkel N. Schmidt

entry.summary: ICICLE is a prior-data fitted network surrogate for freeze-thaw Bayesian optimization that accepts a variable number of hyperparameters through a shared set encoder and trains on synthetic priors covering typed hyperparameters, heavy-tailed noise, quantization, and divergence. At 1.28M parameters—8.7% of FT-PFN's—it matches FT-PFN's mean-regret trajectories.

entry.title: mmTherm: Absolute 3D Human Pose Estimation from Low-Resolution Thermal Images and mmWave Radar

author.name: Zhaoxin Chang, Badii Jouaber, Daqing Zhang

entry.summary: mmTherm fuses privacy-preserving millimeter-wave radar with low-resolution thermal imaging for absolute 3D human pose estimation, motivated by the finding that feature-level fusion generalizes poorly to unseen subjects, sometimes worse than radar alone. The framework explicitly incorporates complementary geometric structure between modalities. It targets surveillance-free, privacy-respecting human sensing.

entry.title: R$^{3}$Sieve: Suppressing Unconditional Information from Attention to Answers for High-Resolution VQA

author.name: Yifan Cao, Yawen Zhang, Xiaocui Yang, Faxian Wan, Shi Feng, Daling Wang, Yifei Zhang, Shangshu Yu, Xianbing Zhao

entry.summary: R3Sieve improves high-resolution VQA by addressing how small-target visual evidence is used during inference, arguing that unconditional information persisting in attention obscures question-relevant evidence from image crops. It suppresses such unconditional information to sharpen attention on answers. A focused inference-time improvement for fine-grained multimodal perception.

entry.title: Fuse Before Reconstruct: A Novel Reconstruction Paradigm for Multimodal Industrial Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zhi Li, Hanyu Wang, Qiyu Chen, Fei Shen, Zhengtao Zhang

entry.summary: FBR proposes fusing multimodal features before reconstruction for industrial anomaly detection, avoiding intra-modal reconstruction's neglect of cross-modal information and cross-modal reconstruction's projection errors and ambiguous one-to-many mappings. By fusing first, the method sidesteps failure cases like identical textures mapping to multiple geometries. It targets precision manufacturing quality inspection.

entry.title: A$^3$Bench: Compositional Reasoning over Aggressive Interactions in Videos

author.name: Austin C Baker, Raiyaan Abdullah, Daniel Zeev Yoffe, Shruti Vyas, Yogesh S Rawat

entry.summary: A3Bench tests whether multimodal LLMs can reason about participant roles in aggressive video interactions: identifying aggressors, victims, and bystanders, and binding actions to participants. Existing violence datasets only detect whether aggression occurs, not compositional role understanding. The benchmark exposes a significant gap in current MLLM video reasoning.

entry.title: Old Matches, New Frames: Schedule-Gated Stereo Memory from Human Vision to Machine Matching

author.name: Ruiqi Liu, Yang Lu, Yanlan Kang

entry.summary: Investigates how stereo vision systems should decide whether temporal disparity matches remain valid after input refresh, testing nine temporal mechanisms against human psychophysical data from 10 observers. Identifies that down-weighting aged evidence lacking binocular support improves fits and reproduces a reversed-depth illusion, with formal propositions on scheduling rules.

entry.title: Scalable Iterative Multi-Agent Path Finding under Turn Constraints

author.name: Zheyu Tao, Chunlong Yu, Yicheng Hu

entry.summary: PIBT*_T extends priority-inheritance-based iterative MAPF solving to multi-agent path finding with turn actions and turn-induced delays, overcoming the broken node-vacation assumption that turn constraints impose on conventional priority inheritance. It preserves lightweight single-timestep mechanics for large-scale multi-robot coordination.

entry.title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability

author.name: Jialing Xie, Yifan Zhou, Yiwen Zhang, Junjun He

entry.summary: M2G-bench is a benchmark evaluating film-to-game adaptation by generative systems, combining general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting with three GUI model players across 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation fidelity, and player experience, plus a shared weakness.

entry.title: Entropy-Regularized Integrated Gradients for Stable Feature Attribution

author.name: Rukmangadh Sai Myana, Sumit Kumar Jha, Yanzhao Wu

entry.summary: ERIG is a path-based attribution method that stabilizes Integrated Gradients by attenuating gradient irregularities along the integration path using maximum-entropy softmax weighting with a temperature parameter. The authors provide Lipschitz-based theoretical bounds decomposing attribution change under input perturbation into model-response and path-weighting terms.

entry.title: SoU-RHS: Bayesian Structured Sparsity for Compact Architecture Recovery in CNNs

author.name: Rafael Mouallem Rosa (STATIFY), Julyan Arbel (STATIFY)

entry.summary: SoU-RHS is a Bayesian structured-sparsity method combining Regularized Horseshoe Shrinkage with a Sources of Uncertainty sparse global-local mechanism to recover compact CNN architectures from overparameterized reference models. It sharpens separation between active and inactive filters and exhibits stability across different starting widths and pruning thresholds. This offers a principled alternative to heuristic pruning for architecture recovery.

entry.title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Location Encoding Methods for Species Distribution Modelling

author.name: Christian Lange, Oisin Mac Aodha

entry.summary: This paper introduces a standardized evaluation framework comparing input features for species distribution modeling, spanning climate variables, learning-based encodings, earth embedding models, and raw transformed geographic coordinates. It clarifies which location encodings are most informative for generating dense spatial species range outputs from sparse observations.

entry.title: Where the Tokens Go: Heat, Entropy and Error in Agentic Coding

author.name: Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik, Varinia Bernales

entry.summary: This paper proposes a software thermodynamics framework that treats tokens generated by coding agents as a cost divided into work and heat, with test suites acting as a Maxwell's daemon. The theory is tested with coding/uncoding cycles analogous to single-molecule pulling experiments. It offers a conceptual framing for what token expenditure buys in agentic coding, though its practical implications remain speculative.

entry.title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance

author.name: Kaiwen Shi, Zheyuan Zhang, Changzhi Liu, Han Bao, Yanfang Ye

entry.summary: This paper applies multi-agent LLM systems to food insecurity assistance, connecting eligibility rules, access constraints, and dietary needs while handling uncertainty across agent handoffs. It introduces receiver-conditioned clarification so agents know when and whom to ask before making recommendations, preventing tentative interpretations from propagating as facts. It demonstrates socially beneficial AI with principled uncertainty handling.

entry.title: Fast Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Sparse AI Evaluation

author.name: Dario Deniz Ergun, Haohua Wang, Brendon Tao, Jonah Kollenberg, Chen Ye Gan

entry.summary: Shows that predicting AI benchmark performance can be done with a tiny Beta-Binomial approach: a weak prior built from public evaluation counts, updated from at most 31 revealed outcomes, with no model semantics or inference API. Achieved a 24.6 percent Brier ALC improvement over a constant baseline in the AIMS competition with a 7.7KB submission and microsecond predictions. A useful baseline demonstration that simple statistics rival heavy methods in sparse evaluation settings.

entry.title: CaDO: Formal Verification-Guided Multi-Agent Framework for Causal Dataset Repair and Generation

author.name: Songli Yu, Qi Luo

entry.summary: CaDO is a multi-agent framework for diagnosing and repairing causal reasoning datasets, with three stages: a Formalizer Agent translating natural language questions into formal causal queries, multi-level diagnosis, and automated repair and generation. It targets annotation errors and structural imbalances that degrade causal model training.

entry.title: The Illusion of Relief: How GenAI Redistributes Cognitive Workload in Software Organizations

author.name: Chamari Dasanayake, Vladimir Mandi\'c, Rahul Mohanani, Burak Turhan

entry.summary: Based on questionnaire responses from 44 practitioners across nine organizations, this study examines how generative AI reshapes cognitive work in software development.
