entry.summary: The paper studies GUI agents trained cheaply on text interface views that fail when acting on real screenshots through a low-cost vision-language screen reader, finding the reader's misreads are systematic rather than random noise. The authors show reader alignment, fine-tuning the reader on screenshots, outperforms noise-based sim-to-real remedies and direct screenshot policy training under a small screenshot budget.

entry.title: FMT: Lossless Image Compression in a Fixed Number of Parallel Steps

author.name: Ammar Ali

entry.summary: FMT is a lossless image format whose decoding order and entropy coder are co-designed so that neither the network's wait for conditioned values nor the arithmetic decoder's serial reads grows with image size, enabling decoding in a fixed number of parallel GPU steps. It addresses the key reason learned codecs lose to classical ones in practice: latency. This could make learned lossless compression practically deployable.

entry.title: CaFe: Causally Faithful Conditional Traffic Scenario Generation

author.name: Steven Yu Tung, Shubham Vaijanath Phoolari, Christoph Lauer, Abhinav Valada, Steven Peters

entry.summary: CaFe identifies and formalizes intent leakage in language-conditioned traffic simulation, where simulated surrounding agents react to private instructions before the instructed behavior becomes observable, defusing intended test events. The paper proposes causally faithful evaluation and generation to ensure agents only react to observed behavior.

entry.title: NEBench R1: a Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Nuclear Domain Competence in Large Language Models

author.name: Liyan Wang, Longze Li, Mohamed Hassan, Isshu Lee, Dajie Sun, Ruimin Feng, Aleksandar Vakanski

entry.summary: This paper introduces NEBench R1, a benchmark of 7,546 multiple-choice questions drawn from U.S. NRC reactor operator licensing exams across 18 nuclear facilities, with official explanations enabling evaluation of reasoning quality rather than just answer accuracy. It addresses a gap in domain-specific evaluation for safety-critical nuclear engineering applications of LLMs.

entry.title: Can You Undo It? Reversibility Classes for AI Agent Actions

author.name: Deepak Waghmare, Shaad Sufi

entry.summary: The paper proposes Reversibility Classes, a declared five-level vocabulary with argument-sensitive rules and prior-state capture contracts for judging whether agent tool actions can be undone, implemented as a pinned registry covering 536 tools across 20 MCP servers. On 2,158 recorded runs, a session guard using the classes gates risky actions; the authors transparently note limitations including non-independent AI-assisted rating approval.

entry.title: Reconfiguring Procedural Knowledge for Compositional Robot Skill Adaptation

author.name: Daehee Lee, Dongsu Lee, Sanghyun Ahn, Minjong Yoo, Honguk Woo

entry.summary: The paper frames robot skill adaptation in general-purpose behavior models as reconfigurability: restructuring existing skills under sparse task and procedure specifications rather than learning new behaviors. It proposes RecPo, which represents skills task-agnostically through multiple procedure views and composes them to realize new behaviors when concrete bindings are underdetermined.

entry.title: Seeing What Still Holds: How Waiting Control Changes Cooperative Recovery

author.name: Kangjie Huang, Yucheng Xin, Xinchun Wang, Dong Liu, Yan Fan, Shuming Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces AuditEmbodied, a paired execution-and-trajectory evaluation framework for robotic recovery, which independently varies holding references and waiting duration while keeping recovery executors frozen. Through a 960-execution factorial experiment on 20 initialization seeds comparing CAD-feedback and landmark-based recovery, the authors show that changing the holding reference during a fixed-duration wait can reverse the ranking of visual recovery methods, with protected completion counts shifting dramatically across conditions. This demonstrates that evaluation protocols in embodied AI can materially change which methods appear superior.

entry.title: VITAL: A Framework for Validating Agentic AI in Pharmaceutical Drug Development and Clinical Trial Operations

author.name: Sandeep Burugupalli, Pedro Matos-Filipe, Andrea Hita Ardiaca, Adam Taylor, Alex Grigorenko, Natalia Jakubiak, Xin Yu, Raghav Mani, Sherry Mangla, Alvi Lai, Rachel C. Mercado, Pratik Shah, Raja Shankar

entry.summary: VITAL is a validation framework for agentic AI in pharmaceutical clinical development, integrating context of use, controls, behavioral validation, and lifecycle evidence within a risk-adjusted structure. It was developed through regulatory mapping, expert interviews, and multi-stakeholder refinement, then operationalized on real agents in clinical development. This addresses the gap where existing assurance approaches cannot validate agents when reference standards are unavailable.

entry.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving

author.name: Baiting Luo, Shatadal Mishra, Ahmadreza Moradipari, Nejib Ammar

entry.summary: AR-WAM is a streaming world-action model for autonomous driving that combines causal autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning, incrementally updating visual context and reusing computation instead of repeatedly re-encoding history. This makes video-foundation-model-style anticipation practical for real-time driving by avoiding iterative video generation.

entry.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction

author.name: Ihab Bendidi, Kian Kenyon-Dean, Alisandra K. Denton, Auguste Genovesio, Emmanuel Noutahi

entry.summary: Occam is an MLP-based framework for single-cell representation learning that combines denoising-learned cell representations with gene interaction, text, and protein-sequence features to predict genetic perturbation effects. It achieves top aggregate representation scores and outperforms four retrained baselines on cross-context few-shot prediction where a perturbation and cell context are individually seen but never together.

entry.title: JointGV: Structure-Aware Correction of Visual World Models with Parallel Graph Dynamics for Long-Horizon Modeling

author.name: Tian Lyu, Yichen Jiang, Ziyuan Cheng, Yunda Yan, Xiangyu Pan, Junjie Jiang, Jialin Yu, Boyu Ning, Pietro Li\`o, Fan Mo

entry.summary: Proposes JointGV, a plug-in that runs a task-conditioned scene graph rollout alongside a visual world model and couples the two to correct recursive drift in entity poses and spatial relations during long-horizon prediction. It rests on a cross-granularity dynamics hypothesis: graph-node changes and visual-state changes describe the same physical transition despite different representations. The approach improves robot planning-relevant long-horizon prediction without restructuring the underlying visual model.

entry.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yor\`ub\'a, and Igbo

author.name: Nuhu Ibrahim, Maryam Abdulazeez, Fatsuma Jauro, Salisu Aliyu, Robert Stevens, Riza Batista-Navarro

entry.summary: This paper introduces ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated and culturally adapted recipes in three major Nigerian languages (Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo), plus ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon of roughly 15,000 translated entities spanning ten recipe categories. It addresses the gap in culturally adaptive translation for low-resource languages, where ingredients and procedures must be adapted to the target culture rather than literally translated, and enables evaluation of multilingual LLMs on this task.

entry.title: Know When to Zoom: How Small Is Too Small for Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Siddharth Vohra, Min Xu

entry.summary: Measures how much visual detail survives in large images before online vision-language models see them, noting e.g. that a 20-pixel-wide car in a drone photo reaches Claude at about 6 pixels while OpenAI defaults reject the image outright. Using printed-code eye exams and 601 questions about small objects across seven models from four vendors, the authors quantify minimum readable text sizes and show tiling into up to nine tiles recovers 11-15 percentage points of accuracy. This is an analysis of existing deployed models rather than a new release.

entry.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations

author.name: Mridul Mahajan, Aldo Pacchiano, Xuezhou Zhang

entry.summary: Studies provable transfer in RL via an undo map that recovers the source MDP state space from the target, proposing an algorithm that learns this map by matching state feature statistics. In the linear undo map, linearly-Q*-realizable setting, the approach has strictly better sample complexity than learning from scratch.

entry.title: WM-Quant: Rollout-Aware Post-Training Quantization for JEPA-Style World Models

author.name: William Hammer, Andrew Heuer, Nikhil Krishna, Matthew Grenier, Ramtin Zand

entry.summary: WM-Quant is the first post-training quantization framework designed for JEPA-style world models, showing that quantization error compounds across autoregressive MPC rollout steps until action rankings become near-random. The method combines early-encoder precision, control-path preservation, and rollout-aware techniques built on existing PTQ methods to keep planning reliable at reduced cost. This targets the thousands of inferences that action planning requires in world-model agents.

entry.title: An Optimization Framework for Denoising Generation

author.name: Xinyu Zhou, Jiawei Zhang, Stephen J. Wright

entry.summary: This theoretical work interprets noise-unconditioned denoising generation as gradient ascent on a fixed log-density landscape and proves convergence guarantees: ascent trajectories converge almost surely to within a computable distance of a reference data manifold. It also derives a source-sink identity used to prove finite-resolution regional coverage and analyzes diversity retention across initializations.

entry.title: ResoLUT: Distilling Residual Networks into Lookup-Table Networks

author.name: Katarzyna Fojcik, Aidas Mikalauskas, Matthias Kampa, Renaldas Zioma, Jogundas Armaitis

entry.summary: ResoLUT distills trained ResNets layer by layer into lookup-table trees, preserving the multi-bit residual stream and BatchNorm while extracting connectivity from the teacher rather than learning it, enabling efficient hardware inference with Boolean logic. It is claimed to be the first convolutional logic network in computer vision retaining a ResNet-style residual stream, reaching 95.66 percent on CIFAR-10 with ResoLUT-20. Hard LUT decisions throughout avoid discretization gaps.

entry.title: Latent Fact Composition under Next-Token Training

author.name: Tianyi Zhang, Feiying Chen

entry.summary: This paper asks whether transformers trained on full next-token prediction learn to answer two-hop questions whose intermediate entity never appears in two-hop training examples, using a synthetic corpus with exactly computable losses. Standard and looped transformers largely fail, so the authors introduce Baton looped transformers that pass the intermediate entity between loops, largely solving the task under answer-only training.

entry.title: Robust Actor-Critic Learning under Transport and Divergence Uncertainty

author.name: Kunqi Huang, Lican Kang, Hongrui Shu, Jincheng Ying

entry.summary: Develops an actor-critic method for robust Markov decision processes with continuous states and actions where the transition law is unknown. Transition uncertainty sets are defined via Wasserstein, total variation, KL, or chi-square divergences, with a conditional diffusion model fitted to offline data and a shared-target minimax criterion for value estimation. This extends robust offline RL to more general and practical settings.

entry.title: Growing Clusters Lower the Bar: Profile Accretion in LLM-Based Incremental Entity Resolution

author.name: Huixue Han, Shangzhi Xu, Anqi Xiong, Yu-Chu Tian

entry.summary: Finds that LLM-based entity resolution matchers lower their threshold for adding a record to a cluster as the cluster grows: showing sixteen verified members instead of one raises false match rates on similarly named companies across six open-weight models. This violates the standard oracle assumption that match decisions depend only on the records compared.

entry.title: Every Camera Grows Up: Camera-Height Regression in Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Sheng Lu, Guangpin Tao, Tong Lu, Ying Tai

entry.summary: The paper shows that six recent open-weight interactive video world models suffer from camera-height regression: as generation proceeds, the implied camera drifts toward human eye level regardless of the starting elevation, breaking fidelity as embodied-agent simulators. It introduces the EyeHeight benchmark with six rendered and four real calibrated heights for scale-free height estimation. This identifies a previously unnamed, systematic failure mode in world models used for robotics and embodied AI.

entry.title: Disagree to Prune: Reallocating Visual Tokens Where a Small VLM Dissents

author.name: Yanchao Li, Jiaqing Xie, Ben Gao, Yusu Zhang, Beilun Wang, Yanbo Wang, Xiaohua Xu, Zhongyu Huang, Tianfan Fu, Nanqing Dong

entry.summary: Introduces PRUDENT, which answers visual questions with roughly half the visual token budget, then uses a small VLM reading the full image to detect disagreements with the pruned answer and re-answers those questions at double budget. This disagreement-triggered reallocation makes token pruning substantially safer with the same overall budget.

entry.title: CascadeJEPA: Enhancing 3D Geometric Representations via Spatially Coupled Cascaded Prediction

author.name: Kailai Zhou, Ziqi Chen, Xiaoning Xu, Yuefeng Wu, Zixuan Fu, Zijun Lin, Zhihao Li, Youwei Pang, Xiaoqi Zhao, Xun Cao, Bihan Wen

entry.summary: The paper observes that I-JEPA-style pretraining improves semantic recognition while degrading 3D geometric representations, hypothesizing this stems from predicting abstract latents with incomplete spatial context. CascadeJEPA introduces spatially coupled cascaded prediction with full-grid context encoding and cross-attention to restore fine-grained geometric information.

entry.title: Harnessing Image Diffusion Prior for Photo-Realistic Video Restoration

author.name: Fanghua Yu, Hongyu An, Jinfan Hu, Xinqi Lin, Zhiyuan You, Jian Wang, Hongyang Li, Chao Dong, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: The authors transfer powerful image generation priors to video restoration while maintaining temporal consistency, combining noise energy rebalancing to suppress structure-disturbing stochasticity, motion-aligned noise warping to propagate details along object motion, and self-supervised denoising. The method bridges image-level fidelity and video-level stability, a known trade-off in the field.

entry.title: Rescaling OLS-Merged Adapters To Improve Personalized Image Generation

author.name: Leander Girrbach, Niklas Schweiger, Zeynep Akata

entry.summary: The authors identify a systematic flaw in OLS-based adapter merging methods (RegMean, Mix-of-Show, Subspace Routing): the reconstruction objective shrinks task-specific signals whenever activation distributions overlap, yielding overly weak merged adapters. They derive a decomposition quantifying this shrinkage and propose rescaling the merged update. Results improve multi-subject personalization with up to 30 merged adapters.

entry.title: Making Future-Predictive Representations Actionable

author.name: Fangchuan Wang, Hao Zhang, Qiyan Zhao, Huanqi Zhao, Guanting Ye, Xu-Yao Zhang, Yuqing Gao

entry.summary: Analyzes why future-prediction auxiliary supervision in world action models (WAMs) often fails to help action generation: layerwise probes on Fast-WAM show predictive information concentrates in deep layers whose gradients diverge from the action objective. RelayWAM adds an explicit recurrent transition space between video and action backbones, making predictive representations actionable for robot control.

entry.title: Conserved Verdicts, Drifting Commitments: Identifying Harmful Overthinking

author.name: Jianghong Zhou, Hao Rong, Chen Lin

entry.summary: This paper decomposes reasoning-model stopping decisions into commitment (correctness if stopped now) and verdict (correctness at completion), proving the verdict alone cannot determine whether continued thinking helps or hurts. They derive an identity linking the commitment-verdict gap to expected remaining quality change, enabling principled detection of harmful overthinking.

entry.title: LoCaR: Localized Canvas Retrieval With Frozen Vision-Language Model

author.name: Rahim Hossain, Dipanwita Saha, Ashirbad Mishra, Xinxin Shu, Svetlana Strunjas, Binbin Li

entry.summary: LoCaR is a training-free framework for localized text-to-image retrieval that uses SAM2-generated object proposals to encode individual regions with frozen vision-language encoders, addressing how whole-image embeddings under-represent small objects. The authors also introduce LOCFG, a Visual Genome-derived benchmark for evaluating retrieval of small, challenging referents, plus an optional paired-support adaptation that does not update the encoders.

entry.title: SeasonRainBench: Global Seasonal Precipitation

author.name: Qiuyan Sun, Mengxuan Chen, Haoyuan Liang, Guowen Li, Zhen Huang, Jianhao Lin, Juepeng Zheng, Haohuan Fu

entry.summary: This paper introduces SeasonRainBench, a global benchmark for evaluating data-driven seasonal precipitation forecasting against operational numerical ensemble systems. It addresses the lack of standardized global evaluation, proposes operational-relevant metrics beyond ACC and RMSE, and aims to accelerate the shift from computationally expensive physics-based ensembles to machine learning forecasters that could improve drought, flood, and crop-failure preparedness months in advance.

entry.title: Learning to Edit IFC Building Models: Verifiable Checkers as the Training Signal for Dependency-Aware Editing Agents

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Yao Luo, Yuze Dan, Yunqin Li, Bowen Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces IfcGym, a CodeAct environment where language models edit IFC building-information models through executable code, with four verifiable checkers (validity, intent, dependency, preservation) whose conjunction defines strict success. It distills verified teacher episodes into a Qwen3.5-9B student via supervised fine-tuning, enabling dependency-aware editing agents that learn from edit outcomes rather than prompting alone.

entry.title: From Ideal to Real: Integrating Language Models into Smart Home for Human-Centric IoT Safety and Security Fuzzing

author.name: Lin Li, Xinbo Ban, Chao Chen, Lei Pan, Ming Ding, Kok-Leong Ong, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: This paper extends IoT fuzz testing for smart homes by replacing idealized simulated human decisions with LLM-driven models of realistic human behavior, aiming to expose inter-rule vulnerabilities that could cause privacy breaches or physical harm. It matters because traditional simulated fuzzing misses how real occupant interactions create security and safety risks across healthcare, transportation, and home automation settings.

entry.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory

author.name: Caoxin Wang, Shengkai Gan, Xiang Hu, Lili Pan

entry.summary: This paper studies the underexplored between-round decision in autonomous research systems: after each experiment round, deciding whether to refine a solution or pivot, and what goal to set next. BRED is an LLM controller that makes this decision directly from accumulated evidence without external search structures. This targets a core control problem for autonomous scientific discovery agents.

entry.title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond

author.name: Bingjun Luo, Jialin Guo, Siqi Li

entry.summary: This paper studies how long-video question answering benchmarks like Video-MME-v2 use a uniform frame budget per question even though different queries need different amounts of visual evidence. It introduces FrameRouter, a training-free test-time framework that routes frame budgets per question while keeping the average budget equal to a uniform reference. This matters for efficient video understanding, since uniformly increasing frames does not reliably improve all metrics.

entry.title: Can AI Help Explain AI? Effects of Multimodal LLM-Generated Explanations on Perceived Understanding and Perceived Trust in XAI Visualizations

author.name: Mario Truss, Marc Schmitt, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: A pre-registered within-subject experiment (N=128) across seven decision scenarios and five XAI methods tests whether adding multimodal LLM-generated textual explanations to XAI visualizations improves perceived understanding and trust. Explanations improved both by meaningful margins (0.35 and 0.26 points on five-point scales, p < .001), consistently across scenarios, with the largest gains for certain participant groups. This provides empirical evidence that LLMs can make XAI more usable.

entry.title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary

author.name: Renhe Sun, Yueying Feng, Bohan Yu, Tong Niu, Yunqi Liu, Zitong Wang, Haolin He, Kexin Shi, Hualei Wang, Qiuqiang Kong, Chang Yao, Yuge Huang, Weiqiang Wang, Jingyuan Chen, Jian Liu

entry.summary: This paper presents the EgoLink Challenge at ACM Multimedia 2026, a benchmark for egocentric multimodal AI covering social reasoning from first-person video and interactive agents that complete service tasks through dialogue and tool use. It tests whether perception, reasoning, and action remain coupled in both offline QA and state-changing interaction.

entry.title: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection

author.name: Kartik Pandit, Sourav Ganguly, Arnob Ghosh

entry.summary: The paper studies constrained contextual bandits and proposes running SquareCB with a rectified cost weight that is zero within budget and otherwise just large enough to restore budget compliance. This yields cancellation-free constraint violations (avoiding the offsetting of slack and violations across rounds) with regret of order the standard SquareCB regret over a margin parameter.

entry.title: Domain-Tuned Diffusion Super-Resolution for 4K Facial Asset Maps

author.name: Elly Akhoundi, Mathieu Lamarre, Thibault Goyallon, Patrick Anderson, \'Etienne Danvoye

entry.summary: This paper presents a diffusion-based upscaler that converts 1K facial albedo and displacement maps used in physically based rendering into 4K maps suitable for cinematic close-ups. It adapts a frozen SDXL backbone with LoRA modules per modality and a Tile ControlNet to preserve structure, addressing the domain-specific statistics of facial UV maps that make photographic super-resolution a poor fit.

entry.title: FailureGen: Scalable Robot Failure Data Generation with World Models

author.name: Akul Santhosh, Chaitra Sathe, Aastha Jhunjhunwala

entry.summary: FailureGen generates synthetic robot failure videos with temporal event annotations by fine-tuning an action-conditioned Cosmos world model on real successes and failures, then transferring failure-associated motion segments into compatible successful host contexts. Generated samples are annotated and filtered by observed events and visual quality. The method addresses the scarcity of failure data in robot learning datasets.

entry.title: MAVE: Reconstructing Editable 3D Blockouts from Film Shots

author.name: Yifan Chang, Jian Yang, Jiangnan Shao, Xiaofeng Wang, Zhaoxin Fan, Renjing Xu, Ming Lu, Xingang Wang, Zheng Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces MAVE, a framework that automatically converts film footage into editable 3D blockouts by recovering cameras, human motion, and geometric evidence in a shared metric space, then using an agent to build a constrained editable environment with programmatic verification. It also contributes MAVEBench, a benchmark of 50 film shots and 416 keyframes for camera motion, spatial layout, and character blocking. This matters for previsualization workflows and for generating paired training data for video generation.

entry.title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects

author.name: Hoang Pham Cong, Long D. Nguyen, Ho Viet Duc Luong, Nguyen Tran Minh Nhat, Binh P. Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes Decision-Guided Speculative Perception (DGSP), which probes a planner with hypothetical inserted objects to compute a decision-sensitivity field indicating where an unseen object would change the planned action, directing high-resolution perception only where it matters. This couples perception resolution to decision relevance rather than image cues alone.

entry.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models

author.name: Hansang Lee

entry.summary: This paper finds that preference optimization, the standard method for reducing object hallucination in vision-language models, also reduces object coverage in four LLaVA-1.5-7B checkpoints, lowering recall without improving set-level object F1. A simple positive end-of-sequence logit bias applied to the base model reproduces 58-86 percent of the CHAIRi hallucination gains, suggesting much of the PO benefit is just early stopping. A negative EOS bias under greedy decoding can recover the lost object categories.

entry.title: Layerwise Learning-Rate Scaling in Vision Networks: Effective-Rate Identification, Power-Mean Aggregation, and Budget Dependence

author.name: Chandini Vysyaraju, Raghuvir Duvvuri, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

entry.summary: This paper studies how layerwise learning-rate scaling, well established for fine-tuning, behaves when vision networks are trained from scratch, showing that a strategy's effect is well captured by a single effective learning rate computed from its multiplier profile via power-mean aggregation. It finds that test-accuracy changes closely track training-loss changes (r = -0.996), supporting an optimization-progress explanation of short-budget effects, and shows results are consistent across architectures and robust to a tenfold change in base learning rate. The work matters because it offers a cheap predictive shortcut that avoids exhaustively training each candidate tuning recipe.

entry.title: Higher-Order Interaction Reconstruction via Integral Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Xin Mao, Zhen Xu, Shiyi Yang, Sukwon Yun, Yunmei Liu, Ren Wang, Tianlong Chen, Can Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes IntegralPINN, a physics-informed neural network framework for reconstructing higher-order interactions in complex networked systems such as ecological, social, and biological networks. Instead of penalizing derivative-based physics residuals, it uses an integral formulation over temporal intervals, which suppresses high-frequency noise and avoids derivative-induced instability in noisy, sparse observation settings.

entry.title: VTT: Reading Vehicle Size and Powertrain Type from Motion Trajectory Across Unseen Car Models

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Yuechen Guo, Jingxin Yang, Chuheng Wei, Suyang Chen, Abdulaziz Alhuraish, Yiyi Wang, Mingyang Ban, Jingran Sun, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces VTT, a large-scale dataset and benchmark for inferring vehicle size class and powertrain type from motion trajectories and CAN bus signals, spanning 9,062 drives, roughly 3,950 hours, 1,431 vehicles, and 174 car models. It evaluates sequence models on unseen car models and drivers, showing that auxiliary physical targets, augmentation, and task-specific weighting raise drive-level macro-F1 to about 92.6-93.0 percent for battery-electric detection.

entry.title: How Many Training Labels Are Wrong? Auditing a Fitted Model through Gradient Allocation

author.name: Yuchen Li, Zongqi Fan, Xintong Li, Nguyen H. Tran, Ken-Tye Yong

entry.summary: This work proposes auditing label quality using per-example gradients of a single trained model, comparing each example's normalized gradient allocation against class-mean allocations to flag likely mislabeled data. It avoids the pitfalls of held-out-set readings and output-based detection, which fail once the model has memorized wrong labels. The method addresses a persistent practical problem in dataset curation.

entry.title: Variance Restoration over Covariance Rank: Memory-Budgeted Analytic Continual Learning

author.name: Elena Voss, Pixel Nomand, Marcus Hale, Sofia Reyes

entry.summary: This paper studies analytic continual learning based on closed-form ridge regression over frozen pretrained features, identifying a memory trade-off between storing exact feature autocorrelation statistics in a narrow code versus compressing cross-coordinate interactions in a wide random code. It proposes a variance restoration approach to manage this trade-off under a fixed memory budget.

entry.title: Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell

author.name: Hyojung Han

entry.summary: This empirical study evaluates INT2/INT3, GPTQ, NVFP4, and mixed-precision quantization of Qwen3-8B on NVIDIA B200 with vLLM under preregistered accuracy and latency gates across Korean, English, numerical, and reasoning tasks. It finds INT2 grids degenerate, non-additive module restoration effects, cross-lingual sensitivity mismatches, and that a promising candidate fails final evaluation.

entry.title: Addressing Exogenous Variability in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Seongmin Kim, Woohyeon Byeon, Jiwon Jeon, Seungyul Han, Youngchul Sung

entry.summary: Formalizes cooperative MARL under exogenous variability (shifting opponents or environment regimes) as the Exogenous Dec-POMDP, partitioning state into action-responsive and non-responsive components and analyzing mediated influence. The formulation aims to yield algorithms robust to dynamics the team cannot control.

entry.title: XM-Sparse: High-Throughput Sparse-Attention LLM Serving over Scale-up Memory Pools

author.name: Yijun Sun, Xudong Liao, Zhuobin Huang, Kai Chen, Nikita Lazarev, Zhizhen Zhong

entry.summary: Analyzes why sparse-attention LLM serving remains bounded by GPU HBM capacity even with emerging scale-up memory pools, identifying hot KV buffers and fully resident indexer-key caches as the culprits. XM-Sparse proposes a serving design that exploits scale-up memory pools to offload KV history beyond PCIe and host-memory limits, improving serving concurrency for long-context inference.

entry.title: Sample-Aligned Decoders for Latent Generative Models

author.name: Yu Lei, Yi Li, Hongcheng Gao, Yipeng Wei, Liang Li, Li Su, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: Identifies that latent generative model decoders are trained only on encoder latents and never see generated latents at test time, rendering generator residuals into final images. The paper shows generated latents lie near the real-latent manifold but follow a different distribution, and proposes adapting the decoder to the generated-latent distribution without retraining the generator or adding per-step cost.

entry.title: Social Signal Bench: Evidence-Weighted Evaluation of Co-occurring Social Signals in Video and Audio

author.name: Siddharth Ravi, Anders R. Bargum, Hugo Anselme, Patrizio Cugia di Sant'Orsola, Alberto Cardaci, Flora Kincso Parragi, Vincent Borowiec, Line H. Clemmensen

entry.summary: Introduces Social Signal Bench, a 47-hour densely annotated benchmark with audio and audiovisual datasets for recognizing co-occurring social signals such as interest and hesitation in conversation. It proposes evidence-weighted metrics that account for semantic relationships between signals and annotator disagreement, addressing gaps in conventional multi-label F1 evaluation. This matters for affective computing and socially aware AI systems where existing benchmarks rarely test signal co-occurrence.

entry.title: When Anchors Shift the Target: Advantage-Gated Adaptation for Diffusion Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Pu Cao, Min Zhou, Ying Shu, Tiezheng Ge, Qing Song, Lu Yang

entry.summary: Identifies a conflict in reinforcement learning fine-tuning of diffusion and flow-matching models: cached moving-anchor predictions used to stabilize negative-advantage updates also corrupt what positive feedback teaches. The authors formalize this as anchor coupling, prove affine moving-anchor rules cannot resolve it, and propose Advantage-Gated Adaptation (AGA), which treats positive and negative samples differently. This improves the stability-quality tradeoff in diffusion RL.

entry.title: Capability Composition in Heterogeneous Teams via Barrier-Guided Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Diana Laura Morales, Ruoyu Lin, Magnus Egerstedt, Fabio Pasqualetti

entry.summary: Encodes the physical conditions under which heterogeneous robot teams can combine capabilities as constraints on team trajectories, enforced via barrier guidance during sampling from generative models trained only on single-agent demonstrations. This allows teams to compose capabilities for tasks they have never demonstrated together, with provable constraint satisfaction. It reduces dependence on costly cooperative demonstrations in multi-robot coordination.

entry.title: Call-Efficient ICD-10 Code Prediction via Supervised Candidate Generation and Selective LLM Invocation

author.name: Ilia Kopanichuk, Daniil Kartashev, Yuri Bolkonsky, Petr Anokhin, Vladimir Makharev, Iaroslav Bespalov, Dmitry V. Dylov

entry.summary: Describes a pipeline for assigning ICD-10 codes from short, noisy diagnosis text that combines transformer embeddings, tree-based supervised candidate generation, reranking, and gated LLM assistance to reduce costly model calls. It uses a leakage-safe validation protocol with out-of-fold selection and a locked test set.

entry.title: Asking What Matters: Disagreement-Guided Ambiguity Detection for Interactive Text-to-SQL

author.name: Su Dong, Jiayan Lin, Yujia Liu, Zijin Hong, Qinggang Zhang, Feiran Huang, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces DisGuAD, a framework that uses disagreement among plausible SQL interpretations to guide which ambiguities an interactive text-to-SQL agent should clarify within a limited turn budget. It addresses the problem that surface-level ambiguity detection often misses ambiguities that actually change the resulting SQL query. This matters because clarifying the right question at the right time is central to practical database copilots.

entry.title: Cross-Modal StateKV Injection for Communication in Multi-LLM Systems across Temporal Segments

author.name: Xiaoqian Zhang, Zhihao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies communication between multiple multimodal LLMs for video understanding via key-value state injection rather than text: provider models observe complementary frames, and their visual KV states are aligned, projected, and injected into a carrier model via gated residual updates. This preserves carrier KV-cache length while avoiding information loss of text-based intermediaries.

entry.title: SpatialMind: Adaptive Multi-Level Geometric Fusion for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Shibin Zhao, Hao Tan, Fan Yang, Haixin Wang, Feilong Chen, Yidong Ma, Chaoyang Zhao, Ming Tang, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SpatialMind, a method that injects 3D reconstruction into multimodal LLMs with adaptive multi-level geometric fusion, showing that different spatial tasks (distance estimation vs. route planning) need different granularities of geometric representation. This outperforms fixed single- or multi-granularity fusion schemes.

entry.title: Keeping Parts Honest: Isolated Part Graphs for Faithful Vision Transformer Explanations

author.name: Bernard Tomczyk, Gail Collyer-Hoar, Bryan Williams

entry.summary: The paper shows that part and prototype-based explanations of Vision Transformers are unfaithful because self-attention lets part-level features absorb whole-image context; accuracy collapses when each explained region is encoded in isolation. The proposed classifier represents images as graphs of isolated parts encoded only from their own patches, yielding more faithful part-based explanations.

entry.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation

author.name: Ruoyu Wang, Hao Zhong, Yanming Yang, Jiahao Tian, Lin Liu, Biao Gong, Guoshan Lu, Yiding Tian, Chunhua Shen, Zhenzhong Lan, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Invoker-Render pairs a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, appearance references, and language, decoupling world-state simulation from photorealistic synthesis. Trained on an aligned ~200-hour multi-granularity corpus, it targets both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming without drift. This addresses key challenges in controllable world-model-based video generation.

entry.title: CRA: Continuous Risk Assessment for Safety-critical Visual Navigation

author.name: Lihao Zheng, Ying Wu, Chen Jiang, Randy Freeman

entry.summary: CRA replaces binary safe/unsafe constraint notions with a continuous, vision-based risk estimate for safety-critical navigation, using RGB and LiDAR to estimate four risk factors that vary with object motion and interaction context. For example, a fast-moving person carrying a hot object warrants a different response than a static obstacle.

entry.title: COAST: Safe Flight Corridor Planner for Fast and Robust Snap Minimized Trajectories

author.name: Alejandro Pelaez, Randal W. Beard

entry.summary: COAST is an online B-Spline trajectory planner that produces snap-minimized trajectories with hard Safe Flight Corridor guarantees, combining an A* front-end generating simple rectangular corridor chains with a QP back-end, handling non-convex corridor intersections. It resolves the speed-versus-safety trade-off in current B-Spline planners.

entry.title: Sim2CBF: From Forward Simulations to Implicit Control Barrier Function Safety Filtering without Model Derivatives

author.name: Luzia Knoedler, Yihan Liu, Shaohang Han, Yifei Dong, Jana Tumova

entry.summary: Sim2CBF solves the CBF safety-filter optimization using only forward-model evaluations, approximating the CBF constraint with finite differences and local linear interpolation over sampled control inputs. The implicit CBF is built from backup-policy rollouts, enabling safety filtering with expressive predictive models whose derivatives are unavailable or unreliable.

entry.title: Thoughts on "safety bad bc warning shots good"

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Cleo Nardo examines the Warning Shot Argument, which claims that making current-generation AIs safer could paradoxically increase catastrophic risk by preventing the non-catastrophic harms that raise societal awareness and drive protective action. The post formalizes the argument step by step and begins exploring whether a safety-improving intervention should be pressed, using a hypothetical button framing and a concrete lab-focused example.

entry.title: When Lower Harm Misleads: Auditing Concept Corrections

author.name: Tianyou Lai, Wentao Yue, Hongji Li, Chaoyuan Hao, Qilei Li

entry.summary: The authors propose a correction audit protocol for expert corrections of concept predictions (e.g., BI-RADS descriptors in breast ultrasound) that separates harm reduction from useful gain and distinguishes a worse starting prediction from genuine correction responsiveness. Applied across three breast-ultrasound sources, the audit reveals when objectives appear beneficial merely by lowering responsiveness or starting from worse baselines.

entry.title: Towards Physics-Constrained Rectified Flow for Climate Downscaling: What Projections Can Certify?

author.name: Arun Sharma

entry.summary: The paper presents PC-RF, a conditional flow-matching downscaler with training penalties on wind divergence, negative precipitation, and mass drift, plus a post-sampling projection that exactly enforces non-negativity and mass conservation. Experiments show the projection drives violation rates to zero and penalties reduce divergence error by about 30%, probing what physics constraints can certify on ERA5 data.

entry.title: Multistage Contextual Optimization for Vehicle Repositioning

author.name: Jinyu Zhang, Di Huang, Zhiyuan Liu, Nikolas Geroliminis

entry.summary: This paper formulates ride-hailing vehicle repositioning as a multistage linear program coupled with a macroscopic fundamental diagram linking vehicle accumulation to trip completion. The authors develop a contextual optimization approach in which decision performance trains the demand-prediction model, handling coupled stages, decision-dependent context, and predictions that affect the objective, constraints, and right-hand side of the LP. They derive effective solutions and demonstrate improved spatial supply-demand balancing on real ride-hailing scenarios.

entry.title: Structured AI ideation yields physical strategies for epithelial barrier repair

author.name: Geonho Nah, Johyun Park, Kyung-Ah Cho, Suyoung Hwang, Yoon Hee Lim, Eun-kyung Min, Seunghyun Moon, Donghyun Koh, Seungwon Kim, Jiho Park, Hojin Yoo, Myungsun Nam, Haneul Choi, Kyungsu Kim, In-Sun Hong, YunJae Jung, Minhyeong Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents Abelio, an AI system for generating novel research directions by reformulating research objectives, identifying relevant elements outside disciplinary boundaries, and refining hypotheses, with divergent-exploration and convergent-selection subsystems at each stage. Applied to epithelial barrier repair, its Ideation Core proposals reportedly outperform baselines in quantitative evaluations. This demonstrates structured AI ideation producing actionable biomedical research strategies.

entry.title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts

author.name: Shashank

entry.summary: FCP addresses the problem that when an LLM writes both an artifact and its tests, passing tests are weak evidence. It checks AI-generated artifacts against the request itself, separating conformance (decidable by SMT solvers and model checkers) from fidelity (undecidable but refutable by concrete witnesses), and turns eight ways a proof can falsely certify a requirement into mechanical witness-producing checks. This is a practical protocol for trustworthy verification of generated code and artifacts.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests

author.name: Gil Pasternak, AJ Langley, Tom Yotam, Ellie Kitanidis

entry.summary: This work benchmarks three popular coding agents with frontier models on writing reliable unit tests and translating them between programming languages. Agents far exceed human-written suites on coverage metrics, but test quality degrades sharply with project complexity, tempering trust in agent-generated verification.

entry.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning

author.name: Boyu Han, Qianqian Xu, Shilong Bao, Zhiyong Yang, Qingming Huang

entry.summary: The paper reformulates generative reconstruction within an AUC-optimization framework to unify contrastive discrimination and perceptual fidelity for visual encoders serving multimodal LLMs, avoiding gradient interference from naive composite losses. The aim is representations that are simultaneously fine-grained, discriminative, and reconstructive.

entry.title: Teaching Language Models to Narrow Boolean Patent Searches from Search Feedback

author.name: Seiya Kawano, Koji Marusaki, Hirofumi Nonaka, Koichiro Yoshino

entry.summary: The authors distill 38,397 Japan Patent Office search reports into executable expert Boolean search strategies and train a generator offline from scored rollouts, using screening-aware strategy scores and line-level credit for citation-preserving narrowing. Prompted models write valid, high-recall strategies but leave citation sets too large to screen; the learned line-level approach improves narrowing. This demonstrates feedback-driven learning for a real professional search workflow.

entry.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language

author.name: Aritra Das, Francesco Cagnetta, Darshil Doshi, Victor V. Albert, Maissam Barkeshli, Andrey Gromov

entry.summary: Introduces tree-grams, autoregressive n-gram models built through hierarchical composition of order-2 and order-3 tensors, with context window and capacity controlled by interpretable hyperparameters. Tree-grams beat existing n-gram baselines and stay competitive with transformer language models, enabling controlled studies of scaling and learnability.

entry.title: VisHead-Spec: Head-Routed Visual Attention for Multimodal Speculative Decoding

author.name: Xin Guo, Arushi Rai, Xiang Zhou, Qiang Zhang, Siyu Lin, Xiangjun Fan, Lizhu Zhang

entry.summary: The paper explains why multimodal speculative decoding speedups collapse under high concurrency: image tokens inflate draft computation as batches become compute-bound, and block-diffusion drafters like DFlash and DSpark achieve under 9 percent speedup in this regime. Through information-flow analysis across model components, the authors identify how visual attention is routed through specific heads and propose head-routed visual attention to make drafting more efficient. The approach preserves target model outputs while improving VLM serving throughput.

entry.title: HADVQ: Hessian Aware Directional Vector Quantization

author.name: Daniil Li, Mars Davletshin, Vadim Klyzhenko, Artem Danilishin, Valery Sandul, Daniil Ryazanov, Ekaterina Muravleva

entry.summary: HADVQ tackles ultra-low-bit quantization of large language models by random preconditioning of the weight space, polar-coordinate decomposition separating direction and magnitude quantization, and an E8 lattice structured codebook for directions. It additionally detects and protects highly sensitive channels that are disproportionately harmed by aggressive compression. The goal is better preservation of model quality at extreme bit budgets.

entry.title: Action-outcome coupling: a pre-investment feasibility audit for offline reinforcement learning in supply chain operations

author.name: Tung Dang, The Hung Phung, Son Lam Nguyen, Tu Nguyen

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a pre-investment feasibility question for offline RL in logistics via action-outcome coupling, a total-effect variance index measuring how much expected outcomes change with the logged action. Coupling yields an algorithm-independent upper bound on achievable policy value in monetary units and an analysis of false-licensing risk when naive value-model workflows are applied to low-signal logs. This helps organizations decide whether offline RL initiatives are worth funding.

entry.title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy

author.name: Tunahan Parlay{\i}c{\i}, Erchan Aptoula, Y\"ucel Sayg{\i}n

entry.summary: This evaluation paper shows that reported face-privacy protection rates above 90% are inflated by two protocol defects: unrealistic input pipelines that skip detection-alignment-cropping, and a saturating success-rate-difference metric. Re-scoring through a realistic front end costs a standard transfer attack 56% of its dodging protection, with the metric masking underlying effects.

entry.title: Auditing a Learned Simulator for Legged Robots: The Robotic World Model on ANYmal D

author.name: Joyjeet Singh

entry.summary: An end-to-end audit of a published learned simulator (Robotic World Model) for the ANYmal D quadruped, rebuilt without a GPU to match released code outputs exactly, covering 101 trained simulators, 200 compressed copies, and 38 simulators of three other architectures. The audit examines the model's one-step-ahead validation versus its actual use over hundreds of autoregressive steps, and tests policies in a hand-built MuJoCo model. Rare, rigorous reproducibility and reliability analysis of a learned world model.

entry.title: Can a World Model Predict a Deepfake Video? A Consistency Margin Prior for Deepfake Detection

author.name: Pradip Gupta, Shubham Mandloi, Ravi Kumar Satzoda, Sujeeth Bharadwaj, Yassine Benajiba, Dan Roth

entry.summary: This paper proposes deepfake detection via the prediction residual of a natural-video world model: using a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder with a LoRA-adapted predictor, manipulated clips should produce larger gaps between predicted and observed frames. The approach aims to generalize across datasets better than detectors that rely on generator-specific artifacts. It connects self-supervised video world models to the deepfake-detection generalization problem.

entry.title: Cross3DGS: Unified Vulkan-Based 3D Gaussian Splatting Training from Workstations to Mobile Devices

author.name: Hiroyuki Sato, Yusuke Takimoto

entry.summary: Cross3DGS is a cross-vendor, cross-platform Vulkan implementation of 3D Gaussian Splatting training that runs on devices beyond CUDA workstations, including phones and laptops. It selects per-device execution schedules using rules about device limits and observed driver behavior, moving beyond simple kernel translation.

entry.title: PCRG: Training-Free Pruning and Caching of Reference Tokens for Video Generation

author.name: Siyuan Wang, Haoran Li, Yi Yue, Tak L. Fung, Quan Chen

entry.summary: PCRG accelerates reference-to-video diffusion transformers by pruning or caching static, smooth, or irrelevant reference tokens, which otherwise consume a large share of the quadratic attention cost. It is training-free and plug-and-play, using signals the model already computes to tier tokens into pruned, cached, or kept.

entry.title: Wear and Go: Calibration Free Sparse Inertial Motion Capture via Online Sensor Setup Estimation

author.name: Yuanshuo Tan, Licheng Zhong

entry.summary: MOSAIC removes the calibration-pose requirement in sparse inertial motion capture by recovering each sensor's anatomical assignment and mounting orientation from ordinary movement, exploiting that pose changes continuously while the sensor setup persists. A setup network with temporal and cross-sensor attention accumulates evidence into a session-level estimate that canonicalizes measurements for frozen pretrained pose estimators.

entry.title: Wall-to-wall maps of canopy height and aboveground carbon across the Atlantic Forest

author.name: Matheus Pinheiro Ferreira, Thiago Carmuega Raba\c{c}al, Giulio Brossi Santoro, Giovanna de Andrade Ferreira, Rodrigo Costa Pinto, Danilo R. A. de Almeida, Paulo Guilherme Molin, Catherine Torres de Almeida, Ang\'elica F. Resende, Vinicius Castro Souza, Marcelo Antonio Pinho Ferreira, C\'assio Toledo, Eben North Broadbent, Angelica Almeyda Zambrano, Laura Sim\~oes, Juliano van Melis, Ricardo Ribeiro Rodrigues, Pedro H. S. Brancalion

entry.summary: The authors produce wall-to-wall 10 m canopy height and 30 m aboveground carbon density maps of the Brazilian Atlantic Forest for 2024, using a deep learning network fusing Sentinel-1/2, ALOS PALSAR, and elevation data trained on a statewide airborne LiDAR campaign. They report low RMSE (3.05 m at 10 m) with external validation and find that over the same pixels, Meta and WRI global maps show notable discrepancies. This provides both a regional product and a caution about global map accuracy.

entry.title: VLM-guided Grounding Expert for Generalised Referring Expression Comprehension

author.name: Mingcheng Zhu, Wentian Xu, Tao Lin, Shiying Duan, Ziyun Liang, Xuecheng Qi, Junyang Chen, Kuo Li, Zhifan Wan, Dong Wang, Richard Wang, Yang Gao

entry.summary: VGE combines a frozen VLM's contextual representations with a grounding expert's direct spatial prediction to improve generalized referring expression comprehension, including rejection of absent targets and robustness to paraphrased, robot-contextualized requests. It targets reliable language grounding for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: [Research Note] Detecting Research Sabotage with Debate & Slopvestigators

author.name: Joey Yudelson

entry.summary: An ongoing SPAR program study testing whether scalable oversight methods can detect subtle sabotage in untrusted AI research outputs. Debate provided little to no uplift over a lone judge, while a decomposition strategy using swarms of parallel agents investigating well-scoped potential sabotages beat a lone judge by about 0.09 AUROC, though within noise.

entry.title: DNeo: Your Parallel Draft Model Needs Better Target Feature Encoding

author.name: Jameson Sandler, Shane Bergsma, Mostafa Elhoushi, Bin Claire Zhang, Gavia Gray, Joel Hestness, Nolan Dey, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: DNeo improves speculative-diffusion decoding by fixing three limitations of feature-encoding mechanisms used by parallel drafters: lossy projections via residual mixing, lack of memory across steps, and related encoding inefficiencies. Better conditioning on target features should increase the fraction of draft tokens passing verification, speeding inference.

entry.title: The Only Edge Was Memorized in Training: LLM Trading Agents Around Earnings and Bad News

author.name: Jackson Wang

entry.summary: Using a look-ahead-free benchmark of 598 earnings announcements and 409 bad-news drops in large US stocks, the paper tests whether LLM trading agents can generate alpha after transaction costs at two exploitable moments: before scheduled news and after overreaction to bad news. The title suggests the only exploitable edge was memorized during training, a sobering result for LLM-based trading claims.

entry.title: Think Once, Act Fast: Cost-Effective Recursive Self-Improvement for Decision Model Harness

author.name: Siqi Lai, Haitao Li, Hao Liu

entry.summary: JevRSI is a System-1/System-2 collaboration framework in which a fast, low-latency System-1 model handles action selection while an asynchronous LLM System-2 recursively builds a modular harness of procedures, state memory, and world models that supply decision context across past, present, and future. Utility-driven retrieval selects harness modules to cut the latency and compute costs of repeatedly invoking LLM reasoning.

entry.title: OICycle: Observe, Infer, and Intervene Cycle for Belief-State Learning in Longitudinal Clinical Decision Making

author.name: Jitindra Fartiyal, Pedro Freire, Sergei K. Turitsyn, Sergei G. Solovski

entry.summary: OICycle learns a stochastic belief state directly from retrospective electronic health records, framing longitudinal clinical decision making as a POMDP without requiring hand-specified discrete state spaces or transition models. It follows the observe-infer-intervene closed loop of clinical care, updating beliefs from irregular, multimodal, incomplete records. This bridges deep learning practicality with POMDP-style sequential decision making for medicine.

entry.title: Improved Convergence Rates for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent which Close the Gap: A Proof by AI

author.name: Lisha Chen

entry.summary: This note establishes a new convergence rate for stochastic multi-gradient descent in smooth nonconvex multi-objective optimization, improving the squared Pareto-stationarity bound from O(T^-1/4) to O(T^-1) with constant stepsize and linearly growing mini-batches, without bounded-gradient assumptions. Notably, the key step in the proof was produced with AI assistance, as the title highlights. The result closes a gap in the multi-objective optimization literature.

entry.title: ARC-2: Continuous Compliance Through Delta Management

author.name: Tord Johan Eide, Einar Holt

entry.summary: ARC-2 extends a three-layer governance architecture for autonomous systems with Delta Management, a framework that continuously measures deviations between a system's operational state and a certified baseline defined as a region rather than a fixed point. Four extensions cover behavioral deviation incorporation in certification, outlier quarantine, and monitoring-based compliance assessment replacing static certification.

entry.title: GauntletScore: Auditable Fact-Checking That Matches the Best Published Checkers on LLM-AggreFact

author.name: Ernie Hobbs, Jim Hinson

entry.summary: GauntletScore is an evidence-engine approach to claim verification that asks typed questions to independent readers from different providers, records answers as measurements in an evidence ledger, and combines them with a fixed Bayesian rule counting a contradiction only when two readers agree. It achieves 79.51 balanced accuracy on the full LLM-AggreFact test split, above every published leaderboard average, with auditability as a key property.

entry.title: Solver-Free and Cost-Aware Online Scheduling of AI Data Center Tasks

author.name: Xin Qin, Dawei Qiu, Fei Teng

entry.summary: This paper proposes a solver-free online optimization rule, inspired by dual decomposition, that assigns arrival-time start periods to AI data center tasks to minimize electricity cost while respecting operational constraints. Simulations on an A100 GPU trace with 3,456 GPUs and 1,343 tasks show lower cost than a multi-timescale optimization benchmark with no solver latency. It bridges the timing gap between continuous task arrivals and periodic electricity pricing.

entry.title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking

author.name: Benjamin Clavi\'e, Herumb Shandilya, Hanna Lichtenberg, Aamir Shakir, Makoto P. Kato

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how listwise LLM rerankers split candidates into groups for parallel scheduling, showing that dealing candidates round-robin by retriever rank minimizes expected cuts of true top passages when quotas bind. The authors prove optimality under a simple retriever model and show contiguous chunks perform worse as the retriever degrades. Although dealing is not conceptually new, this is its first formal analysis for reranking schedules.

entry.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?

author.name: Pedro Beltr\'an-L\'opez, Raul Gonzalez Jimenez, Dario Maddaloni, Manuel Gil P\'erez, Pantaleone Nespoli

entry.summary: Proposes narrative deception for LLM-powered honeypots: the defender maps attacker commands to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, selects compatible scenarios from a MITRE Engage-based catalogue, and deploys mutually referential artifacts (files, processes, services, logs) so that a coherent story unfolds. The study asks whether jointly coherent artifacts retain LLM-driven attackers better than unrelated ones, a timely question as autonomous offensive agents emerge. It is evaluated on an emulated Ubuntu host.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models

author.name: Xiaoyan Hu, Rohit Sonker, Jalal Butt, Jiayu Chen, Egemen Kolemen, Jeff Schneider

entry.summary: Proposes a guidance-sampling approach using diffusion models for high-dimensional black-box optimization that avoids both reward-conditioned pretraining and the need for exact reward gradients. This broadens the applicability of diffusion-based optimizers to settings with limited labeled data and non-differentiable objectives.

entry.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Hai Huang, Bartosz \.Zuk, Rassul Magauin, Jiaxin Huang, Xue Liu

entry.summary: The authors propose making representation structure an explicit inductive bias in language model pretraining, motivated by the Kolmogorov complexity two-part coding view. They instantiate this via Boundary Bottleneck Concept routing and Continuous Concept regularization that induces a spectral decomposition into low-frequency structure and high-frequency residual, and derive coding bounds. The work aims to separate structural information from realization detail inside learned representations.

entry.title: When Does Discrete Ricci Curvature Help? An Edge-Level Analysis of Curvature-Enhanced GCNs for PPI Prediction

author.name: Clara Joswig, Elham Gholamzadeh, Ghazal Mostofi, Nico Scherf

entry.summary: This paper tests whether curvature-enhanced GCNs actually improve performance by mitigating over-squashing at bottlenecks, using edge-level analysis on four protein-protein interaction datasets. While CGCNs improve aggregate AUC, AUPR, and F1, the gains concentrate on low-degree edges while performance on low-curvature bottleneck edges systematically degrades, contradicting the standard over-squashing justification. This is a careful negative/diagnostic result about a popular graph-learning motif.

entry.title: GP--RL--MPC: Uncertainty-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Augmented Model Predictive Control with Gaussian Process Postdecision State-Value Functions

author.name: Jon Li, Jay H. Lee

entry.summary: GP-RL-MPC uses a Gaussian process-learned critic as the terminal penalty in model predictive control to account for costs beyond the prediction horizon. The method supports data-efficient critic learning from limited noisy rollouts via optimistic approximate policy iteration, includes a tunable risk coefficient weighting epistemic uncertainty, and uses a postdecision state formulation to handle aleatoric uncertainty offline.

entry.title: What Does Weight-Space Programming Add to Diffusion Editing? Program Construction versus Score-Guided Refinement

author.name: Zitian Gao, Jingyi Xu, Ziqi Han, Chengkai Lei, Ye Liu, Liangliang Shi

entry.summary: The paper evaluates weight-space programming, where an LLM generates executable weight updates for diffusion concept editing, comparing generated programs against published editors, a hand-written baseline, and budget-matched conventional edits across 24 test edits for Stable Diffusion 1.4. A preregistered evaluation finds no advantage over a strong baseline, though exploratory analysis suggests one-shot program generation helps on fresh-scene joint success metrics.

entry.title: Virtual Double Oracle: Faster Convergence by Leveraging Strategies That Were Watching All Along

author.name: Ruilan Wang, Francisco Aristi Reina, Katerina Papadaki

entry.summary: Virtual Double Oracle improves Online Double Oracle methods for approximating Nash equilibria in two-player zero-sum games by removing the wasteful uniform reinitialization of newly discovered strategies. It exploits a bilinear identity showing a strategy's full hindsight loss history collapses to its utility against the current mixture, allowing warm-started learning. This yields faster convergence in population-based game solving.

entry.title: Quantum-Classical Separation in Probability Distribution Transport via Nonlocal Games

author.name: Fangjun Hu, Xun Gao

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes a quantum-classical separation in distribution transport: two classical distributions connectable exactly and reversibly by a constant-depth local quantum circuit require substantially larger spatial range under classical stochastic transport. The result is demonstrated explicitly on a one-dimensional example using nonlocal game techniques.

entry.title: From Temperature-Limited to Battery-Limited Legged Locomotion

author.name: Rapha\"el S\'egas, Bal\'azs Opra, L\'eo Ghafari, Thomas Stewart

entry.summary: Shows that sustained legged-robot locomotion typically ends in motor thermal shutdown rather than battery depletion, and trains thermally aware RL locomotion policies without observing temperature directly. A fitted 13-node lumped RC thermal network predicts all twelve motor temperatures with sub-1-degree RMSE across robots, gaits, payloads, and speeds, demonstrated on a Unitree Go2.

entry.title: Sub-Meter Canopy Height Synthesis from Sentinel-2 via Anchored Residual Flow

author.name: Kiarie Ndegwa, Tony Chang, Andreas Gros, Vincent A. Landau, David D. Diaz, Luke Zachmann, Nathan E. Rutenbeck, Guy C Bayes

entry.summary: Produces 0.5 m canopy height maps from free 10 m Sentinel-2 imagery via a 20x cross-modal super-resolution task, deriving two operating points from the perception-distortion trade-off: a deterministic regressor (Anchor) for low distortion and a conditional flow-matching model trained on the Anchor's residuals (AR-flow) for perceptual fidelity. Applications include forest carbon accounting and wildfire fuel mapping.

entry.title: Stochastic Diversity Windows: Diagnosing Noise Influence in Robotic Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Tina Lakhani, Jing Wu, Yu-Kun Lai, Ze Ji

entry.summary: Presents a per-timestep counterfactual diagnostic that measures how changing sampled noise in diffusion model samplers affects final robotic control outputs. Across five model-sampler configurations and three robotics benchmarks, the authors find highly varied temporal sensitivity profiles and define stochastic diversity windows (SDWs) to characterize when noise matters. This improves understanding of why diffusion-based policy samplers behave as they do.

entry.title: Is model self-assessment enough for diverse LVLM ensembles?

author.name: Michael Smith, Frank P. Ferrie

entry.summary: Creates a unified pipeline for ensembling large vision-language models by selecting the best candidate response using model self-assessed confidence, avoiding task-specific training. The study is unusually comprehensive: 34 confidence estimation methods, 24 ensemble configurations, 20 datasets, and two prompt styles. It finds that simple training- and parameter-free aggregation approaches can suffice, even outperforming heavier pipelines.

entry.title: MInfoVisQA: A Multilingual Benchmark for Information-Rich Visual Question Answering

author.name: Changjiang Jiang, Jiang Zhou, Xinbin Yuan, Fan Zhang, Tao Feng, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Presents MInfoVisQA, a parallel benchmark with 8,960 QA configurations from 128 seed instances across 24 languages, built by disentangling numerical-structural data from text in information-rich visuals and synchronizing translated labels programmatically. Evaluation of 25 multimodal LLMs under language-aligned and cross-language settings reveals inconsistencies in InfoVis understanding as surface language changes. Highlights multilingual robustness gaps in MLLMs on charts and infographics.

entry.title: Comparing Implicit and Explicit Language Attitudes toward the Dutch multiethnolect Straattaal in Humans and Large Language Models

author.name: Hedwig Oldenhof, Laura Rosseel, Anna Wegmann, Dong Nguyen

entry.summary: Investigates whether LLMs encode human-like implicit and explicit attitudes toward the Dutch multiethnolect Straattaal and its associations with migrant communities, using matched designs: an Implicit Association Test and rating task for humans, and parallel measures for LLMs. This connects sociolinguistic attitude theory to model bias evaluation.

entry.title: Compact and Decodable Electrocardiogram Text for Large Language Models

author.name: Elif Dorukba\c{s}{\i}, \.Ilker T\"urker

entry.summary: Presents a deterministic text encoding for twelve-lead ECGs that writes eight leads as amplitude letters and exact time gaps, algebraically recovers the remaining limb leads, and uses a learned 26-letter codebook plus tolerance schedule to fit a fixed token budget. Evaluated on 21,388 PTB-XL records via exact decode-and-re-encode round trips and waveform fidelity metrics.

entry.title: Dynamic Task Allocation with Dialogue

author.name: Matthew Groholski, Weiwei Gu, Nakul Gopalan

entry.summary: Introduces a communication-augmented Bayesian task-allocation framework for multi-agent collaboration under partial observability, where agents use dialogue to reduce uncertainty about the environment and collaborators while keeping decisions grounded in explicit, verifiable beliefs about task state and intent.

entry.title: Nunchi: Ears Help Eyes in Multi-Party Conversations

author.name: JunYeong Park, Shijing Wang, Seonwook Park, Michael Stengel, Shalini De Mello, Sang-Il Choi, Hyung Jin Chang

entry.summary: The paper introduces SORBET, a benchmark of 3,340 samples from 1,578 clips with synchronized speech, transcripts, and attended-person labels for multi-party gaze estimation, and Nunchi, a framework that fuses conversational cues like who is speaking into gaze prediction via text prompts. It addresses the ambiguity of gaze geometry as more people enter a scene. This fills a real dataset gap for audio-visual social perception.

entry.title: BATMoS: Budget-Aware Guidance Allocation for Efficient Video Diffusion

author.name: Zhixu Du, Kuo Yang, Jingwei Sun, Hai "Helen" Li, Yiran Chen

entry.summary: BATMoS improves video diffusion inference efficiency by routing between fresh classifier-free guidance and cached guidance over the denoising trajectory, using a magnitude-based temporal rule to reuse guidance when it matters least. Across eight equal-budget configurations, VBench scores span 4.80 points, showing allocation design matters, and BATMoS preserves quality with fewer denoiser evaluations. This is a practical efficiency contribution as video diffusion inference costs balloon.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Motion Identity Reduction via Autoregressive Generative Encoding for Privacy-Preserving Skeleton-based Motion Data

author.name: Thomas Carr, Xujun Che, Depeng Xu, Shuhan Yuan, Aidong Lu

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a causal, target-free anonymizer for skeleton motion data that adds identity-reducing residuals frame-by-frame, preventing third-party action classifiers from identifying people through body proportions and movement style. It uses a rotary-position encoder-decoder with key/value caching for online operation.

entry.title: TANGO: Real-World Unregistered RGB-Guided Hyperspectral Super-Resolution with Two-Camera Acquisitions

author.name: Matteo Kolyszko, Marco Buzzelli, Simone Bianco, Raimondo Schettini

entry.summary: The authors release DUET, the first large-scale public benchmark of real two-camera RGB-hyperspectral acquisitions with high-resolution references (403 indoor/outdoor scenes), and propose TANGO, a method for unregistered RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution. The work addresses the gap between synthetic misalignment assumptions and real geometric misalignment.

entry.title: LOCUS: Causal Support Windows for Attribute Control in Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Zijun Huang

entry.summary: The paper investigates where in the image-token sequence interventions can flip rendered attributes in unified autoregressive image generators, introducing the causal support profile that measures intervention effectiveness per window. It finds structural attributes like count and position are most responsive, and uses this to enable attribute control, including overriding conflicting prompt attributes.

entry.title: MI-Hyper: Generating Multiple Instance Models for Weight Space Transfer Learning in Histopathology via Mixed Tasks Pretrained HyperNetwork

author.name: Xitong Ling, Yousef Kotp, Weiming Chen, Yining Li, Jiawen Li, Minxi Ouyang, Xinyi Guo, Mingxi Fu, Yizhi Wang, Tian Guan, Lianghui Zhu, Yonghong He

entry.summary: MI-Hyper is a hypernetwork pretrained across mixed pathology tasks that generates aggregation and classification weights for multiple-instance-learning models, enabling zero-shot whole-slide-image prediction without parameter updates at deployment. Evaluated across 308 tasks from 52 pathology cohorts, it offers an alternative to pooling patch-text similarities as in MI-Zero. This targets generalization to new pathology tasks with no labeled data.

entry.title: TCP4D: A Unified Tool-Center-Point Tracking and Generation Model for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Haosong Peng, Xiangyang Liu, Zhengshen Zhang, Yunfeng Fan, Tianyu Qi, Xin Xia, Yufeng Zhan, Wenchao Xu

entry.summary: TCP4D uses a shared 4D scene representation to both track a robot's tool-center-point pose in SE(3) with gripper states from monocular video and generate future TCP trajectories conditioned on language instructions and robot observations. This unifies action annotation recovery and trajectory prediction in an embodiment-agnostic action space.

entry.title: Beyond Episodic Recall: Experience-to-Knowledge Evolution for Lifelong Embodied Navigation

author.name: Weitao An, Chenghao Xu, Xu Yang, Cheng Deng

entry.summary: EvoNav is a two-timescale memory framework for lifelong embodied navigation that organizes semantic observations, spatial relations, and task feedback into sparse experience structures that evolve into environment-specific knowledge. This avoids growing storage costs of raw observations while supporting retrieval and reasoning for goal search.

entry.title: AI models tell anxious renters less directly that new apartments lower rents

author.name: Michael Z

entry.summary: An empirical study of Claude Sonnet, ChatGPT, and GPT-6 Sol showing that when a user first expresses anxiety about a nearby luxury apartment building, models state the economically supported conclusion that new housing lowers nearby rents less directly than they otherwise would. The author frames this as sycophancy producing opinion-reinforcing political information from a single source.

entry.title: Correlating a behavior with reward doesn't reinforce it

author.name: fitandfend

entry.summary: The author investigates whether an RL-trained model could steer its own training by correlating a desired property with the reward signal, and finds that correlation alone is insufficient for reinforcement due to barriers in how RL credit assignment works. The post updates a mental model of RL with implications for correlation-based training-influence strategies, which where they work involve sandbagging that RL erodes.

entry.title: Streaming On-Policy Distillation: Decoupling Three Clocks for Stage-Wise Supervision Consumption

author.name: Yun Zhu Da Wang

entry.summary: The paper develops streaming on-policy distillation by decoupling response completion, supervision delivery, and parameter updates into independent clocks, with a consumption protocol governing supervision budgets, position selection, staleness, and update scheduling. In GSM8K experiments distilling Qwen3-4B into Qwen3-0.6B with VERL, the approach reduces the early accuracy gap over candidate baselines under matched supervision budgets.

entry.title: HyCoInfer: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models on Heterogeneous GPU-FPGA Architectures

author.name: Zewen Huang, Xiangwen Zhuge, Yingkun Hu, Zheng Yang, Qiang Ma

entry.summary: HyCoInfer is a serving system that assigns LLM prefill to cloud GPUs while distributing autoregressive decoding across cloud GPUs and edge FPGAs, addressing capacity balancing, KV-cache transfer over constrained wide-area links, and heterogeneous-execution latency. It targets the memory-bound nature of decoding, which underutilizes GPU arithmetic units.

entry.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs

author.name: Zaer Bin Zaqy, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Shows that standard attribution applied to raw network outputs can credit inputs for changes a fixed decoder discards, and proposes attributing through the decoder differential instead, which for normalization decoders reduces to a scaled tangent projection. The paper characterizes invariance properties and zero-sensitivity points on spheres.

entry.title: Teaching What to Look For: Privileged Perception Questions for Agentic On-Policy Distillation in Video Captioning

author.name: Yifan Xu, Ruopeng Gao, Zhixiao Wang, Jiafu Tang, Yichun Yang, Zihao Wang, Yuanxing Zhang, Limin Wang

entry.summary: PQ-OPD trains video captioning agents that actively seek relevant moments and inspect regions, using training-only Perception Questions that specify what evidence should be gathered without revealing answers. This on-policy distillation approach encourages teacher exploration toward fine-grained visual evidence that fixed-frame sampling misses.

entry.title: CAST: Calibrating Correspondences for Training-Free Biomedical In-Context Segmentation

author.name: Mingze Jiang, Jiashu Han, Haonan Chen, Zhiyi Li, Yilun Du, Kunzan Liu

entry.summary: CAST is a training-free in-context segmentation framework for biomedical images, built on a frozen DINOv3 backbone, that calibrates fine-grained correspondences via a stability test to handle similar adjacent structures and cross-subject variation. New anatomical structures are specified by a few annotated exemplars at inference time, avoiding dense expert annotation. This addresses a major bottleneck in clinical translation.

entry.title: PAIR: Bringing Household Robots into the Smart Home

author.name: Junseong Pyo, Hyeongjin Kim, Jongwook Han, Seungwon Kook, Sungjib Lim, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Introduces PAIR, a smart-home simulation environment grounded in the Matter protocol, providing 84 smart-device assets with functional control panels, APIs, and shared device state with evolving ambient conditions. It includes a benchmark of 40 tasks from 1,443 surveyed requests plus 340 human demonstrations for policy learning.

entry.title: Honest Brokers in AI Regulation: How Public Comments Introduce Evidence to Regulators

author.name: Sarah Tran, Anna-Maria Gueorguieva, Eva Maxfield Brown, Nicholas Weber

entry.summary: The authors build a corpus of 40 potential US AI regulations and 2,664 public comments, computationally extracting citations and informal references to study evidence flow to regulators. They find business commenters supply systematically different types and amounts of evidence, quantifying channels of potential regulatory capture.

entry.title: Big Brains, Tiny Board: Pupavision, an Agentic Physical AI Instrument for Monitoring Drosophila Pupariation and Lifecycle Transitions

author.name: Joel Sadler, Daniel Graham, Melanie Worley

entry.summary: Pupavision is a low-cost physical AI instrument (roughly $45-75 in parts) built on a single-board Linux computer that autonomously monitors Drosophila pupariation timing, with a frontier coding agent running its harness on the device while the model thinks in the cloud. The agent assists image capture, repairs its own code errors, and checks the experiment, demonstrating embedded agentic AI for biology instrumentation.

entry.title: Fidelity Regret: Measuring Simulator Misspecification in Verifiable Design

author.name: Noah Flynn

entry.summary: The paper introduces fidelity regret — the reference simple regret incurred when a cheap simulator selects a design instead of ground truth — and measures it in genetic-circuit design over a 21,362-design subspace spanning five gate libraries and three organisms. Mean normalized regret of 0.369 with only 6 of 72 cells at zero regret shows exact verifiers can still mis-rank physical performance, with strong dependence on the reference axis.

entry.title: Proximal Targets: Training Looped Refiners on Problems with Many Correct Answers

author.name: Syed Affan Daimi
