author.name: Trinh T. Nguyen, Duy-Tung Pham, Hoang-Son Do, Tan Minh Nguyen, Thieu N. Vo

entry.summary: The paper partially resolves a NeurIPS 2024 conjecture about causal attention dynamics, proving that convergence to two clusters aligned with eigenvectors of the value transformation's largest eigenvalue holds when that eigenvalue is positive and generally fails when it is not. It also identifies a rigorous dimension-reduction phenomenon in the high-dimensional token dynamics.

entry.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL

author.name: Zelin He, Siyu Zhu, Jacob Helwig, Yujian Liu, Li An, Rohit Jain, Shiyu Chang, Alborz Geramifard

entry.summary: Recasts the RL harness, the scaffold controlling what an agent sees of its own interactions and guidance it receives, from a fixed hand-written component into learnable programs that evolve during training. Structured interactions are recorded as typed blocks, with learned compression and guidance programs assembled into the model's context.

entry.title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances

author.name: Andre Albrecht, Enzo Morosini Frazzon, Leandro C. Coelho, Bruno Vieira

entry.summary: The authors test whether a frontier LLM used as a coding agent with open-source tools can match commercial scheduling solvers on hard unsolved job-shop instances. An agent-written solver improved all ten instances of a 100,000-operation benchmark family, closed two, and outperformed CP Optimizer and Hexaly on gap-to-lower-bound under equal budgets, also improving several open flexible job-shop instances. All runs are reported with independent verification, making a strong case for LLM agents as algorithm designers.

entry.title: More Genes, Faster Inference: Efficient Large-Panel Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology

author.name: Songming Zhang, Yuxiao Luo, Shifu Luo, Siran Chen, Shuquan Su, Jinyan Li

entry.summary: GeneFlow is a framework for predicting spatially resolved gene expression from histology images that combines flow-matching generative modeling with structured multimodal fusion, encoding both tissue morphology and cross-gene interactions. It targets large gene panels where prior methods were restricted to small fixed panels with complicated architectures. The work shows a simpler approach can scale spatial transcriptomics prediction.

entry.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits

author.name: Aritra Lahiri, Florian Marquardt

entry.summary: Formulates fault-tolerant quantum circuit design — traditionally done by hand for individual cases — as agentic evolutionary program synthesis, where an LLM guided by a circuit verifier evolves a program defining Clifford circuits for tasks like logical state preparation and gate implementation. The approach leverages LLM pretraining knowledge and tool use to automate a bottleneck in scalable quantum computing.

entry.title: The Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective

author.name: Hamed Karimi, Julie Nutini, Mark Schmidt

entry.summary: The authors of the influential 2016 paper that named the Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition offer a candid retrospective on the paper's origins, impact, and criticisms following their 2026 ECML PKDD Test of Time Award. They revisit the main theorem with AI-assisted refinement and survey related ideas and extensions across ten years of optimization research.

entry.title: Beyond Prediction Gain: LASR as a Metric for Action-Grounded Latents in World Models

author.name: Yu Zhou, Changsong Lei, Yixiang Wei, Kairui Wen, Huankun Sheng, Ming Li, Yeying Fan, Yu-Hui Wen, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a fundamental flaw in latent-action model evaluation: latents that improve prediction may encode shortcuts like state or task identity rather than genuine action information, and existing metrics cannot isolate this distinction. The authors propose LASR (Latent Action... grounding), a new metric for measuring whether latents are truly action-grounded rather than merely predictive.

entry.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix

author.name: Saptarshi Ghosh, Mohammad Saim, Tianyu Jiang

entry.summary: Analyzing 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, this study shows that recent GPT and Claude models draw roughly 50 percent or more of their review weaknesses from paper appendices, versus only 8.4 percent for human reviewers, and that this bias holds across API, coding-agent, and web access methods. The finding reveals a systematic behavioral difference in LLM-assisted reviewing that could skew peer review. This is directly relevant as venues consider AI involvement in reviewing.

entry.title: Beyond Endpoints: B\'ezier Paths for Vision Foundation Model Adaptation

author.name: Chenzhi Zheng, Xi Xiao, Chih-Ting Liao, Qizhen Lan, Jingwen Lin, Tianyang Wang, Hao Xu, Xin Cao

entry.summary: The paper theoretically analyzes prompt-based adaptation of frozen vision foundation models as transport between feature-distribution endpoints, showing shared prompts often cannot travel along the shortest path because they compete with image content for attention. In an exactly solvable attention model, reachable features form a cone that can be unrolled into a plane yielding exact minimum-action paths and explicit optimal prompts.

entry.title: Speed-Variation Distillation for Generative Modeling

author.name: Sukit Seripanitkarn, Phonphrm Thawatdamrongkit, Supasorn Suwajanakorn

entry.summary: Proposes a generative framework where image generation traverses recognizable images rather than corrupted noise states, using a variation-reducing degradation process built via generative-prior-based image morphing. The reverse process is distilled into a diversification operator that turns a prototype into increasingly varied samples. This rethinks diffusion trajectories to stay on the image manifold throughout.

entry.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple

author.name: Jianjun Zhou, Hua Geng, Haoyu Guo

entry.summary: JVT is a plain large-patch DiT-style transformer for pixel-space video diffusion that removes the pretrained autoencoder, cascades, detailers, and U-Net skips typical of prior pixel-space approaches. Through systematic ablations of patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive normalization, it matches latent-diffusion baselines in quality while simplifying the pipeline.

entry.title: Objectives as Policies: Vision-Language Model Cost Programs for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Zihao Lu, Trong Gia Hung Nguyen, Fuquan Wang, Yifan Zhu

entry.summary: OaP connects a pretrained VLM to sampling-based MPC through editable objective programs that specify staged task solutions with running and terminal costs from a cost library. This lets VLM semantic reasoning drive physics-based planning for contact-rich manipulation without the VLM generating actions directly.

entry.title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming

author.name: Zhaojia Wang, Jiucui Lu, Zheng Li

entry.summary: Empirically investigates whether general-purpose LLMs can use weight-space programming to inject backdoors into neural networks directly from natural-language instructions, without task data, forward passes, or gradient training. The study probes a new security surface opened by LLMs that can inspect and modify model weights.

entry.title: Right Token, Right Time: From Per-Token Gating to Trajectory-Aware Activation Steering

author.name: Nima Eshraghi, Lovedeep Gondara, Sagarika Suresh, Xiaotong Xu, Jithin Pradeep, Fanny Chevalier

entry.summary: The paper reframes SAE-based activation steering as a per-token allocation problem under a fixed steering budget, showing that when along a generation the intervention is applied is a decisive control axis. The authors introduce two gating methods, including Contrastive Feature Projection, that select which tokens to steer, reducing distribution displacement and quality erosion versus steering every token. This improves behavioral control of LLMs without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond

author.name: Cole Becker, Taylan Kargin, Kimia Hassibi, Asuman Ozdaglar, Pablo A. Parrilo

entry.summary: Proposes a joint schedule/discretization design framework for stochastic-interpolant generative models based on analyticity properties of complexified ODE trajectories, solved exactly via conformal mapping to yield variance-preserving elliptic schedules parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing schedules with tailored discretization yields Zoloflow, a sampling algorithm connected to Zolotarev approximations.

entry.title: Graph diffusion transformer for interpretable generation and inverse design of disordered atomic structures

author.name: Jiani Hu, Chenyan Wang, Yongkun Yang, Guanyu Hou, Jihaochen Zhang, Lei Liu, Ji Chen

entry.summary: The authors introduce GaDiT, a graph diffusion transformer combining dynamic periodic graphs, masked conditioning, and interval-weighted noise distributions to generate disordered (amorphous) atomic structures. GaDiT accelerates sampling by two orders of magnitude over corrector-based approaches on amorphous carbon, silicon, and silica, and supports conditional generation and inverse design under structural feature constraints.

entry.title: Mesh-Free Weak-Form Regression for Learning Interaction Kernels from Particle Trajectories

author.name: Daisuke Inoue, Dante Kalise

entry.summary: The authors propose mesh-free weak-form regression for learning interaction kernels from noisy particle trajectories, using smooth test functions and empirical particle averages to avoid differentiating noisy data or reconstructing densities. Sparse fitting with sampled particle pairs avoids quadratic cost, and they prove high-probability error bounds separating finite-particle, time-discretization, noise, and sampling errors.

entry.title: Safety Side Effects of Preventative Persona Steering: An Empirical Audit

author.name: Sabrina Tang, Nikolai Vo, Carson Murillo, Chira Sukumarnpiti, Sarah Wilson

entry.summary: This audit evaluates preventative persona steering, a technique that adds persona vectors during fine-tuning to prevent traits like sycophancy and hallucination from being encoded in weights. Prior validation of the technique measured only capability retention (MMLU); this paper instead audits safety side effects. It finds previously unmeasured safety regressions, challenging the recommendation of preventative steering as a free lunch.

entry.title: Soteria: Formally Verified Planning with Runtime Enforcement for Safe LLM Agents

author.name: Mike He, Ankush Desai, Sharad Malik, Aarti Gupta

entry.summary: Soteria reconciles safety and utility for LLM agents performing multi-step tool calls by formally verifying a structured plan against domain specifications before execution, then using the verified plan for runtime enforcement during execution so blocked unsafe actions leave the agent a principled recovery path. Existing approaches tend to sacrifice one objective for the other. Combining formal methods with LLM agents addresses a fundamental safety tension.

entry.title: Measured from the feed: the unsustainable growth of AI video generation

author.name: Tristan Coignion, Aur\'elie Bugeau, Gael Guennebaud, Anne-Laure Ligozat

entry.summary: The authors measure yearly video output of two commercial text-to-video platforms and build a prospective model of the full environmental footprint from training to storage. Projections suggest emissions rise nearly seventy-five-fold by 2030 under continued growth despite efficiency gains, while holding usage at 2026 levels with the same improvements reduces emissions by about two-fifths.

entry.title: Diffusion Tree Sampling for Inference Time Adaptation of Crystal Generative Models

author.name: Daniel T. Levy, Vineet Jain, Tara Akhound-Sadegh, S\'ekou-Oumar Kaba, Siamak Ravanbakhsh

entry.summary: Proposes adapting diffusion-based crystal structure generative models at inference time via Diffusion Tree Sampling, a Monte Carlo tree search over the denoising trajectory, avoiding costly per-objective fine-tuning. Technical contributions include reusing property-conditional generative models and steering toward multiple conflicting properties simultaneously.

entry.title: Benchmarks Don't Talk Back: Learning Through Self-Disagreement

author.name: Soheil Abbasloo, Peng Cheng

entry.summary: This paper introduces the concept of dialectical competence: a distinct capability to know when to hold a position and when to yield under counter-reasoning, which standard benchmarks do not measure. The authors show this capability depends on first-answer accuracy but does not follow from it, cannot be obtained via inference-time self-reflection or sampling, and can even be degraded by training for accuracy alone. It argues for new training methods and evaluations that treat position-holding as a first-class skill.

entry.title: Can You Trust Your Finance Agent? Drift, Diagnosis and Auditable Intervention on One Shipped Financial Research Agent

author.name: Cosimo Galeone, Anna Ettorre, Ginevra Mariani, Minsu Park, Giuseppe Ettorre, Daniele Ligorio

entry.summary: This empirical study audits the reference agent shipped with the Vals Finance Agent Benchmark v2, revealing score instability across identical runs and cost variance up to 17 percent. The authors classify failure trajectories by the responsible layer (instructions, tools, model, data) using a frozen taxonomy and show blind readers from different model families reach consistent diagnoses. It offers a practical framework for auditing deployed agents beyond leaderboard scores.

entry.title: Do Verifier Judgments Survive Abstraction? Measuring Verification Transport for LLM Agent Evaluation

author.name: Disha Sheshanarayana, Sai Linisha Reddy Goli

entry.summary: Introduces Verification Transport, a reliability test measuring whether LLM-based verifier judgments remain stable when the same agent execution is presented through different abstractions such as composed tools, delegation boundaries, or compacted histories. The method constructs matched native, abstracted, and restored views of frozen executions while holding the task fixed.

entry.title: Offline KL-Regularized Reinforcement Learning with Stochastic Transitions

author.name: Andrew Liu

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes sample complexity lower and upper bounds for offline KL-regularized RL with stochastic transitions, the objective underlying RL fine-tuning of language models. It derives an Omega(KCH^3) lower bound and shows pessimistic soft value iteration with a variance-aware penalty matches it. The results give the first rigorous data requirements for RLHF-style offline settings beyond bandits.

entry.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions

author.name: Brandon Amos

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard divergence computations between categorical distributions, including forward/reverse KL, generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence, Monte Carlo KL estimates, and entropy, suffer rounding and cancellation errors when distributions are nearly equal, extending recent findings about softmax loss. The authors propose numerically stable reformulations with example implementations relevant to distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods.

entry.title: Algorithmic Opacity as a Principal-Agent Problem

author.name: Ignacio Cofone, Katherine J. Strandburg

entry.summary: This legal-economic analysis frames algorithmic opacity as a principal-agent problem, developing a test for when algorithmic decision systems should trigger disclosure obligations despite claims of gaming or trade secrecy. The proposed diagnostics—error profiles and outcome distributions across groups—can be disclosed without enabling gaming or revealing secrets, exposing misalignment between design incentives and social welfare.

entry.title: See Every Block Once: Variance-Reduced Post-Training for Masked Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Yunzhen He, Hiroaki Yamagiwa, Hidetoshi Shimodaira

entry.summary: This paper addresses a variance problem in post-training masked diffusion language models (MDLMs), where policy gradient methods require log-likelihoods estimated via Monte Carlo over the ELBO and existing blockwise estimators may repeatedly sample some blocks while skipping others. The proposed full-block estimator evaluates every block exactly once per iteration, removing block-selection variance. This improves the efficiency of preference alignment for diffusion LMs.

entry.title: AmbiSteer: Selectively Eliciting Ambiguity-Aware Responses in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Monica Riedler, Samuele Antonelli, Barbara Plank, Raffaella Bernardi

entry.summary: AmbiSteer is a lightweight activation-steering framework that encourages vision-language models to recognize referential ambiguity in VQA, responding with clarification requests or enumerated referents for ambiguous questions while answering unambiguous ones directly. It targets the common overconfidence failure where VLMs commit to a single interpretation regardless of visual evidence.

entry.title: Zoom In, Scale Out: Metric Depth Models Mistake Digital Zoom for Moving Closer

author.name: Rabeya Noor, Khandoker Nosiba Arifin

entry.summary: Introduces a label-free diagnostic test for monocular metric depth models based on digital zoom: since zooming changes nothing in the scene, a correct model should return identical depths while correctly scaling its focal-length estimate. Evaluating 800 images from KITTI, NYUv2 and DIODE, the paper shows widely used models like Depth Anything V2 behave as if the camera moved closer (alpha near 0.95 instead of 0). The test is free, exact, and requires no annotations.

entry.title: Ego2Flow: Benchmarking the Traffic-System Impact of Autonomous Driving on Maps Distilled from Real-World Roads

author.name: Yu Dong, Weiying Shen, Hangyu Li, Shu Han, Hong Li, Xiangbo Gao, Keshu Wu, Zhengzhong Tu, Soyoung Ahn, Zhiyuan Liu, Xiaopeng Li

entry.summary: Ego2Flow introduces a closed-loop benchmark evaluating how end-to-end autonomous driving affects overall traffic-system performance, using an agent-guided map distillation framework that builds realistic 3D urban environments from real-world maps. An iterative feedback mechanism and traffic information graph guide scene generation for sustained multi-vehicle simulation.

entry.title: AI-guided robotic in situ fabrication of curvature- and tissue-adaptive wireless bioelectronics

author.name: Hiroyuki Tetsuka, Jiaju Ma, Naomi Kumano, Minoru Hirano

entry.summary: The authors present an AI-guided robotic platform that prints wireless wound electrotherapy devices directly onto wound dressings in situ. The system combines 3D vision, a six-DOF robot arm, direct-ink-writing, and RF design optimization driven by AI-based wound segmentation to adapt devices to individual wound geometry and curvature.

entry.title: Confident and Wrong: Structure Confidence Is a Poor Selection Filter for Protein Function

author.name: Eric LoPrete, Pavle Jeremi\'c

entry.summary: Shows empirically that structural confidence scores (pTM, ipLDDT) are poor predictors of protein function: a function-guided model designed rare-earth-element-binding variants of lanmodulin, and selecting designs by structural confidence inverted the intended outcome despite high expression rates. Screening of 297 designs against terbium and dysprosium provides wet-lab validation.

entry.title: Tracing Uncertainties of Extreme El Ni\~{n}o Prediction to Mesoscale Ocean Currents

author.name: Bo Qin, Zeyun Yang, Qiaofei Xue, Yanan Ding, Jinyu Wang, Chaopeng Ji, Shijin Yuan, Bin Mu, Wansuo Duan, Guokun Dai, Mu Mu, Yi Deng

entry.summary: Using the CNOP method applied to a differentiable ocean AI model, the authors show that large-scale errors traditionally blamed for ENSO forecast uncertainty may originate from mesoscale ocean-current errors in initial states. The influential current errors are strongly event-dependent, exemplified by the 1997/98 El Nino. This reframes the source of predictability limits for extreme climate events using differentiable AI-based earth system models.

entry.title: Fuse-All MoE Inference Kernel with Load Balancing on TPUs

author.name: Rupeng Liu, Bangsheng Tang, Zongwei Zhou, Chengji Yao, Yejin Lee

entry.summary: Fuse-All MoE is a TPU kernel that jointly optimizes expert computation, output communication, and load balancing for mixture-of-experts LLM inference, fusing token collection, expert projections, gated activation, and output writes while keeping intermediates on chip. Fixed token-slot destinations let scheduling and expert placement change dynamically without altering routing semantics. It targets the long-tail latency and data-movement bottlenecks of sparse MoE serving.

entry.title: Tractable Importance Sampling for Monte Carlo Privacy Accounting

author.name: Galen Andrew, Arun Ganesh

entry.summary: The paper makes Monte Carlo differential privacy accounting practical for DP matrix factorization with privacy amplification by sampling, where estimating tiny delta for high-dimensional correlated Gaussian mixtures otherwise suffers prohibitive variance. The authors derive shifted importance sampling estimators that dramatically improve sample efficiency for strict privacy guarantees.

entry.title: Structure makes quantum circuits trainable

author.name: Wenbo Xie, Wojciech Szpankowski, Ananth Grama

entry.summary: The paper develops an analytical framework bounding gradient variance for arbitrary input states and observables in variational quantum circuits, addressing the barren plateau problem that limits trainability of quantum AI models. Decomposing the unitary representation of the associated compact Lie group, the authors derive exact variance expressions for 2-design circuit segments and prove a sufficient condition for trainability.

entry.title: CS-MPC: Contraction-Certified Sampling-Based MPC for Nonlinear Systems Under Uncertainty

author.name: Yashwanth Kumar Nakka

entry.summary: CS-MPC augments sampling-based model predictive control with contraction-certified tracking feedback inside each rollout and an execution layer verifying inputs via quantile-tightened control barrier function conditions. The paper derives nonlinear contraction verification and proves finite-sample stochastic stability and mission-level probabilistic safety guarantees, validated on rover, quadrotor, and other simulated systems.

entry.title: Verifiable pXRD: Hill-climbing pXRD structure determination with LLM agents

author.name: Samuel Chen, Jiaru Bai, Austin Henry Cheng, Varinia Bernales, Al\'an Aspuru-Guzik

entry.summary: The paper formulates crystal-structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction as a verifiable agentic search problem, where candidate structures are assessed via forward-simulated profile agreement. It introduces pXRD-Bench, a 200-problem benchmark spanning in-distribution, polymorphic, and distribution-shifted cases. Agent adaptation raises structural recovery from 27% to 69%, with further gains reported.

entry.title: RecMem: Recurrent Memory Compression for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation

author.name: Haoyi Hu, Gaoyang Guo, Yunjia Xi, Wen Chen, Weiwen Liu, Jian Wu, Yuning Jiang, Weinan Zhang

entry.summary: RecMem introduces a recurrent memory compression framework for generative recommendation systems, condensing long user interaction histories into a fixed set of memory slots using a shared encoder-decoder with forget-gated updates. The design enforces three properties — space invariance, semantic fidelity, and lifelong evolvability — so that memory state and decoder context remain independent of history length while recommendation supervision ensures predictive information is retained. This matters because processing ever-growing user histories is a major cost and quality bottleneck for industrial recommender systems.

entry.title: LACCO: Local Accumulation with Computation--Communication Overlap

author.name: Daniele Kopyshevskiy (MLIA), Benjamin Th{\'e}rien (Mila, UdeM), Nicolas Pinto (MLIA), Edouard Oyallon (MLIA)

entry.summary: LACCO is a two-stage distributed training algorithm that overlaps global communication with local computation for low-bandwidth LLM training, applying globally aggregated updates shared by all replicas without staleness in the outer update. The paper establishes convergence guarantees and avoids the replica drift problems of delayed or replica-local update schemes.

entry.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection

author.name: Thomas Brennan, Andrew W. Lo, Chaoyi Zhao

entry.summary: Studies how evolutionary selection shapes AI agent choices between task completion and rules of conduct when these objectives conflict. The model shows long-run growth is maximized by matching action frequency to environmental reward, and compares task-only, fixed linear, and adaptive policies for whether learned behavior withstands subsequent selection pressure.

entry.title: Time-Consistent Evaluation of Hierarchical Code Graphs for SWE Agents

author.name: Xianpeng (Simon), Sun (Ken), Tian Yu (Ken), Haonan Sun (Ken), Sheng Ma (Ken), Qincheng Zhang (Ken), Lifei Rao (Ken), Jie Li (Ken), Jian (Ken), Cao, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a zero-leakage evaluation protocol for repository-aware SWE agents, locking repository snapshots and knowledge graphs at historical cutoff commits and evaluating only future pull requests, to eliminate temporal contamination and prompt-level solution leakage. Applies the protocol to DragonFly and React repositories across four prompt granularities and three context-augmentation regimes.

entry.title: GDP.xlsx: Benchmarking Frontier Models on Professional Workbooks

author.name: Suhaas Garre, Sushant Mehta, Edwin Chen

entry.summary: GDP_xlsx is a benchmark of 70 realistic workplace spreadsheet requests from 13 domains, paired with expert rubrics of 791 binary criteria over workbooks totaling 2.18 million cells. Agents work in a containerized environment with spreadsheet tools and are judged by an agentic judge applying strict pass@1 over all criteria. Across 20 configurations of frontier Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI models, the best model (an existing Gemini 4 Argon configuration) passes only a minority, revealing large headroom in professional workbook tasks.

entry.title: From Bytes to Behavior: Request-Level Attribution from Live GPU Hidden States

author.name: Jonathan Pan, Yidi Yuan, Xin Wei Chia, Xinhui Su, Vincent Tan, Brenda Ong

entry.summary: The paper presents a forensic method for acquiring per-layer residual-stream activations from a live GPU inference process using a non-modifying debugger, without prior knowledge of model architecture or weights, enabling request-level attribution of LLM behavior. This extends memory forensics from static artifacts (weights, prompt logs) to transient computational states of running services that cannot be restarted. It has implications for security investigation and accountability of deployed LLM systems.

entry.title: CoPre-MoE: Consolidating and Preserving MoE for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning

author.name: Tao Hu, Ling-Xiang Zhang, Da-Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Addresses catastrophic forgetting in multimodal continual instruction tuning by exploiting the observation that mixture-of-experts allocated per task learn redundant overlapping functions (e.g., visual region localization shared across benchmarks). CoPre-MoE consolidates redundant experts across tasks to curb linear parameter growth without inducing forgetting.

entry.title: Direction or Magnitude? Learning Scalars over Task-Calibrated Directions

author.name: Ziqing Wen, Xiaohui Song, Jiahuan Wang, Ping Luo, Junlin Zeng, Dongsheng Li, Kele Xu, Tao Sun

entry.summary: SCALAR is a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that learns only scalar coefficients over a fixed, task-calibrated basis of input activation directions with a random output dictionary, achieving LoRA-comparable performance with fewer trainable parameters, lower memory, and higher throughput. Grouped computation and cross-layer dictionary sharing further reduce costs. It is evaluated on commonsense reasoning, math, and code generation.

entry.title: Fuse-PINN: Combining Finite Element Methods and Physics-Informed Neural Networks to enable massively parallel simulations of non-linear PDEs

author.name: Stanislas Pamela, Nicolas Pailliez, Emmanuel Franck, Victor Michel-Dansac, Laurent Navoret, Vignesh Gopakumar

entry.summary: Fuse-PINN presents a mathematically grounded hybrid of finite element methods and PINNs designed to scale to massively parallel HPC simulations of nonlinear PDEs with turbulent dynamics over large domains and long timescales, directly challenging the belief that PINNs do not scale. The formulation targets ambitious physics problems beyond the toy models typical of the PINN literature.

entry.title: Creating Steering Vectors via Input Optimisation

author.name: Batuhan Akar

entry.summary: ActGCG adapts Greedy Coordinate Gradient to optimize input suffixes that reproduce target activations matching a steering vector added to the residual stream, enabling black-box-style steering through inputs rather than hidden-state modification. The paper introduces universal suffixes, a model-translation step producing human-readable text, and soft-suffix variants, demonstrating behaviors including language steering and anti-refusal jailbreaks.

entry.title: JaRS: Contrast-Free Localization of Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Jacobian Row Sums

author.name: Saisuchith Mahajan, Aditey Nandan, Rohit Singh, Nishanth Shetty, Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula

entry.summary: The paper shows that Jacobian row sums, unlike the commonly used Jacobian diagonal, disambiguate memorization from smoothing-related averaging in diffusion models, enabling contrast-free localization of memorized training-image regions. This removes the need for a null prompt or earlier checkpoint required by prior contrast-based methods, addressing privacy and copyright risks of generative diffusion models.

entry.title: Tracing Knowledge and Reasoning in LLM

author.name: Yang Wang, Xiao Wang, Yiqi Liu, Chenghao Xiao, Eleni Vasilaki, Goran Nenadic, Chenghua Lin

entry.summary: The authors propose a task-centric framework for characterizing the internal processing LLMs use on benchmarks, combining attention, activation, and representation-based signals to distinguish retrieval-dominant from reasoning-dominant tasks. Evaluating 16 LLMs across 24 benchmarks, they surface systematic processing differences and failure modes that task-level scores conceal. This adds internal-process evidence to benchmark evaluation.

entry.title: Token2Tile: Token-Wise Sparse Attention with Tile Execution through a Low-Rank Space for Video DiTs

author.name: Xuecheng Wu, Aichen Feng, Jinyan Chen, Qingjie Zhao, Julien Lai

entry.summary: Presents Token2Tile, a training-free sparse attention operator for video diffusion transformers that reconciles per-query token scoring with tile-based GPU execution using an online low-rank space computed from queries and keys. It combines per-query scoring, a per-query residual, and tile-level clustering to preserve accuracy while cutting the quadratic attention cost. Directly targets the main inference bottleneck in video generation.

entry.title: PROOF: Perceptive Robustness via Out-of-Distribution Fallback for Legged Locomotion

author.name: Siyuan Wang, Dongjie Zhu, Jinxuan Lu, Wenjun Xu, Jiankun Wang

entry.summary: PROOF is a two-stage teacher-student framework for vision-based legged locomotion that explicitly models perception reliability and provides fallback behavior under out-of-distribution visual conditions such as occlusion, reflections, and lighting changes. This prevents catastrophic failures when perception degrades.

entry.title: What LLM Agents See and What Users Say

author.name: Yue Zhao, Angela Huyue Zhang, S. Alex Yang, Hua Wei, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: This paper studies when LLM agents act on false assumptions before consequential actions, using presupposition theory from linguistics to define when an agent may act based on tool observations, user claims, or disclosures. It provides a bound showing that when lookups cannot distinguish one record from two, any agent errs equally often, and empirically varies how search results list, count, or omit matches. The work clarifies the interplay between tool-grounded evidence and user statements in agent safety.

entry.title: Probabilities of Causation in Nondeterministic Causal Models

author.name: David S. Watson, Sander Beckers

entry.summary: The paper studies probabilities of causation in nondeterministic causal models where mechanisms stay stochastic even after fixing latent variables, developing an identification program that frames observational and interventional data as moment constraints and computes sharp bounds via constrained optimization. The resulting identification regions are often more informative than under deterministic alternatives.

entry.title: Logically Consistent Accurate Forecasts

author.name: Kate Yuan, Rohan Alur, Manish Raghavan, Devavrat Shah

entry.summary: This work targets the inability of LLM-based agentic forecasting systems to produce logically consistent forecasts, where related predictions violate probability axioms. Naive projection onto consistent forecasts degrades accuracy, so the authors instead leverage the reasoning behind each forecast and finetune models to enforce consistency without the accuracy loss. As LLM forecasters become competitive with expert humans, this addresses a key barrier to decision-making utility.

entry.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems

author.name: Grid Robotics, :, Qingfeng Lan, Duo Li, Siyao Li, Yiheng Lyu, Shijian Lu, Zhenghao Qi, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang, Ming Yang, Zhiqin Yang, Zuhao Yang, Tao Yu

entry.summary: This position paper argues that agentic robotics, applying foundation models in closed-loop embodied systems that observe, reason, invoke skills and tools, verify outcomes, and adapt, represents a new paradigm, noting that within weeks of GPT-6 Astra (GA September 2026) frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. The authors propose Embodied System 2 realized by foundation models, and call for shared definitions, evaluation frameworks, and a research roadmap. It is a roadmap/position paper from a large academic consortium rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers

author.name: Aayush Marasini, Barsat Khadka, Nick Rahimi

entry.summary: Introduces WeightBench, a benchmark with 42 tasks across five tracks evaluating LLMs' ability to directly read, fix, and write neural network weights without gradient descent (Weight-Space Programming), including recognizing impossible edits and data-free compression on networks from 2K parameters to 7B-parameter language models. It provides the first systematic evaluation of this emerging capability.

entry.title: Deep Latents, Long Memory: Latent persistence explains temporal correlations in transformer activations

author.name: Francesco Cagnetta, Santiago Acevedo

entry.summary: The authors define layer-wise autocorrelation functions of transformer activations and show that slowly decaying tails, indicative of persistent latent variables encoded along the context, grow across layers in both synthetic and natural data. This provides an operational, quantitative probe of how abstraction deepens in LLM representations.

entry.title: Provable Cross-Modal Transfer of Hierarchical Concept Structure in CLIP Embeddings

author.name: Nghia Nguyen, Tianjiao Ding, Lachlan Ewen MacDonald, Ren\'e Vidal

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Hierarchical Angular Separation, a geometric property where non-leaf concept embeddings are more similar to descendants than off-branch concepts, and provides a theoretical account of why taxonomic hierarchy emerges in CLIP despite a non-hierarchical contrastive objective. Empirically, HAS holds approximately in raw images and randomly initialized CLIP image embeddings, while text embeddings acquire it through contrastive learning.

entry.title: Contrastive latent representation learning with denoising score matching

author.name: Christopher Marouani, Grigory Bartosh, Christian A. Naesseth

entry.summary: ScoreCLR is a contrastive representation learning method that estimates the repulsive force term via denoising score matching rather than the usual large-batch negative sampling. By maximizing mutual information between two latent views and differentiating the Shannon entropy of the latent distribution, the method avoids high variance and curse-of-dimensionality issues of standard contrastive objectives. This offers a practical route to contrastive learning without large batch sizes.

entry.title: PerfArena: Ranking LLMs by Code Performance

author.name: Rui Rua, Hailemariam Mersha, Joao Paulo Fernandes, Karim Ali

entry.summary: PerfArena is an open-source, reproducible benchmark that ranks LLMs by the runtime, memory, and energy cost of their generated code across multiple languages and programming competitions, rather than correctness alone. It executes each model's solutions on a controlled Unix-like host and reports correctness alongside latency, memory, and energy metrics.

entry.title: ParseBench-2: Severity-Aware Evaluation of Document Parsing

author.name: Pierre-Lo\"ic Doulcet, Boyang Zhang, Sebasti\'an G. Acosta, Sacha Bron, Daniel B. Ospina, Antonio Jimeno Yepes, Nutchapol Dendumrongsup, Simon Suo

entry.summary: ParseBench-2 introduces a method for building document-parsing metrics from explicit severity policies specifying how each error type should affect scores, expressed as test scenarios and optimized by coding agents under human review. The resulting benchmark comprehensively evaluates document parsing in a way that reflects which errors actually change important facts rather than rewarding surface similarity.

entry.title: Real-Time Diffusion Relighting as a Neural Sensor: Closing the Low-Light Domain Gap for Robotic Perception

author.name: Shengjie Xu, Alexander Gao, Anshul Rai, Dae Yeol Lee, Guan-Ming Su, Ming C. Lin

entry.summary: The paper embeds a real-time diffusion-based relighting module inside robotic control loops, treating illumination as a generative prior to recover task-relevant semantics in low light rather than doing signal-level enhancement. A perceptual architecture decouples high-latency semantic recovery from low-latency control to make this practical for live robot operation.

entry.title: Open-World Scene Deocclusion

author.name: K. M. S. J. Kumarasinghe, Neil A. Dodgson, Fang-Lue Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a training-free, open-world framework that recovers the full amodal appearance of occluded objects from a single RGB image, decomposing the scene into depth-ordered RGBA layers. It handles cluttered real scenes, occlusions involving undetected background surfaces, and cyclic occlusion dependencies that defeat existing methods.

entry.title: Beyond Attack-Based Accuracy: Rethinking Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Through Structural Gradient Alignment

author.name: Hanrui Wang, Yu Luo, Shuo Wang, Xingbo Dong, Zhe Jin, Isao Echizen

entry.summary: SGA proposes a complementary adversarial robustness metric based on structural alignment between input content and objective-conditioned local sensitivity, requiring only a few random unlabeled public probes rather than prescribed attacks or in-distribution probing data. This enables external auditing of robustness across classifiers, VLMs, and LVLMs.

entry.title: Reusing Locomotion Training Recipes Across Humanoids via Body-Aligned Virtual Joints

author.name: Sol Choi, Mingon Kim, Seokin Seo, Jongeun Choi, Donghyeon Kim, Yisoo Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces a body-aligned virtual joint space that standardizes the coordinate interface between humanoid policies and robot-specific actuators, enabling RL training recipes such as rewards and hyperparameters to transfer across humanoids. A deterministic kinematic layer maps virtual targets to native joint coordinates without modifying existing transmission layers.

entry.title: Does the Ranking Hold? A Practitioner-Facing Audit of Hallucination Detectors on Small, Quantized, On-Device LLMs

author.name: Shubhra Mittal, Gaurav Naresh Mittal

entry.summary: A reproducible single-GPU audit of four hallucination detection paradigms (token-margin calibration, n-gram baseline, semantic entropy, SelfCheckGPT-NLI) on small 4-bit quantized models like Llama-3.2-3B and Qwen2.5-3B. The paper addresses the gap between detector evaluations on large research models and the on-device models practitioners actually deploy. Findings test whether detector rankings from large-model literature transfer to resource-constrained settings.

entry.title: Knowledge After Collapse: Context and Wording Shape Factual Accessibility in Language Models

author.name: Sujato Dutta, Prithviraj Patil, Chandrajit Bajaj

entry.summary: The authors introduce Knowledge Answer Divergence (KAD), an event-conditioned evaluation protocol that tracks how language models behave after adopting a false correction, distinguishing persistence, recovery, and abstention rather than measuring a single susceptibility score. They evaluate eight local checkpoints and six hosted endpoints plus an audited 300-question rerun. This matters because conversational sycophancy and false-belief persistence are key reliability concerns for deployed assistants.

entry.title: VelServe: Taming Decode Jitters in LLM Inference with Tail-Calibrated Scheduling

author.name: Ishaan Datta, Alind Khare, Koushik Kumar Dey, Ratnesh Jamidar, Anand Kumar Singh

entry.summary: VelServe targets latency SLO violations in LLM serving caused by decode jitters in both aggregated and disaggregated serving, where rare overruns propagate to every request in a batch across long streaming responses. It introduces tail-calibrated scheduling to leave headroom for mispredictions and host stalls, improving tail latency over SLO-aware baselines.

entry.title: Racing the Clock: Teaching VLNs Budget-Conditioned Object Search

author.name: Maitree Meher, Siming He, S. Shankar Sastry, Jitendra Malik, Claire Tomlin, Jonas Frey

entry.summary: Introduces budget-conditioned object search for vision-language navigation, where an agent must find as many target instances as possible given an explicit action budget, requiring behavior to adapt to the time available. Compares supervision from a privileged TSP expert against alternatives, with evaluation of how policies trade off sprinting versus broad exploration.

entry.title: Only as Safe as the Weakest Agent: A Break That Appears Only When the System Is Multi-Agent

author.name: Keegan Wang, Anantika Mannby

entry.summary: Reports attacks that succeed against multi-agent systems built from frontier models even though equivalent attacks fail against the models in isolation, demonstrating breaks against unmodified Claude Code, Codex, and a reference harness using their own sub-agent mechanisms. Argues AI safety has over-focused on isolated models while composed systems reintroduce patched vulnerabilities.

entry.title: CarryOn: Learning What to Keep in Context for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Lihuan Li, Ruiyi Yang, Jiru Wang, Yifan Duan, Xiachong Lin, Hao Xue, Yang Song, Flora Salim

entry.summary: CarryOn is a lightweight context manager for long-horizon LLM agents that pairs compact execution state with fine-grained, source-linked evidence, using a learned selector and adaptive retention policy. It addresses the flaw that summarization or pruning loses exact details needed for later actions while full histories carry irrelevant content. The approach promises reliable multi-step agent execution without extra inference overhead.

entry.title: An In-Silico Audit of Topographic Organization in a Multimodal Brain-Response Model

author.name: Jakub Strawa

entry.summary: This single-author audit tests whether TRIBE v2, a model predicting fMRI responses to video, audio, and text, preserves classic topographic organization of sensory cortex such as retinotopy, tonotopy, and MT+ motion selectivity, which the original authors did not evaluate. The author provides mapping stimuli, an adapted fitting pipeline, and a stand-in model with known ground truth as controls, and predicts spatial averaging in TRIBE's video features should destroy retinotopy. It is a careful in-silico replication-style scrutiny of an influential brain encoding model.

entry.title: TradeGauntlet: Evaluating Compliance Controls for Autonomous Trading Agents

author.name: Sandip Nandi, Aishwarya Bose, Apurba Bose, Soovadeep Bakshi

entry.summary: Presents TradeGauntlet, a replayable limit-order-book simulator separating detection, prevention, and execution cost for evaluating compliance controls on autonomous trading agents. Across 1,680 simulated sessions using Claude Haiku 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (existing Anthropic models), gates eliminated self-matching alerts, but results show zero alerts alone do not establish agent compliance.

entry.title: User-Schedulable Approximations for Quantized Tensor Programs

author.name: Alex Reinking

entry.summary: The paper extends Halide's algorithm/schedule separation to value representation, treating each quantization approximation as a codec composed from reusable quantizers, integer representations, bit packers, and layouts, controlled by a new directive. This addresses the combinatorial explosion of hand-written kernels in libraries like GGML, where only 8 of 54 weight-activation pairs have tiled matmul kernels on an Arm CPU.

entry.title: Structural Self-Teaching for Compositional Generation in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Jaeyoo Park, Bohyung Han

entry.summary: Proposes Structural Self-Teaching, a framework that improves compositional image generation in unified multimodal models by using their internal understanding path as a source of structural supervision for the generation path. Phrase-conditioned support masks extracted from internal attention maps of the understanding path supervise training, addressing missing objects, attribute binding failures, and spatial errors in dense compositional prompts. Requires no external supervision.

entry.title: Grounding Object-to-Object Hazard Reasoning into 3D Risk Fields for Task-Conditioned Safety

author.name: Mariana Sosa Guzm\'an, Yide Song, Amin Abyaneh, Gregory Dudek, Hsiu-Chin Lin

entry.summary: The framework uses a VLM with a structured safety tool over RGB-D observations and natural-language task instructions to either reject tasks with non-recoverable hazardous outcomes or identify preventable object-pair hazards, which open-vocabulary segmentation and depth grounding convert into 3D risk fields for robot manipulation. This makes safety constraints task- and scene-dependent rather than purely geometric.

entry.title: Learn then Bet: Learning Interpretable Rules for Reliable Agent Intervention

author.name: You-Lin Chen, Xinyi Lisa Chen, Pedro Herrero-Vidal, Xiaojing Yu, Bingqing Song, Bin Xu

entry.summary: LeBet is a statistical learning framework for runtime monitoring of long-horizon autonomous agents that learns an interpretable OR-of-AND monitor and accumulates evidence via a fixed betting statistic, intervening when evidence crosses a threshold. The objective is derived from sufficient conditions for valid and powerful intervention, with finite-sample guarantees. It targets the problem that heuristic monitors (turn limits, keyword filters) both over- and under-intervene.

entry.title: Experts Across Schemas: Agent-Guided Mixture-of-Relational-Experts for Cross-Database Generalization

author.name: Hiren Madhu, Sukanta Ganguly, Kiran Srinivasan, Smita Krishnaswamy, Rex Ying

entry.summary: MoREGT is a mixture-of-relational-experts graph transformer for relational foundation models that represents rows and cells as tokens, incorporates row log-ages and foreign-key relationship names into attention, and routes tokens to experts by column metadata. It aims to match cross-database pretraining gains with far less data, using an agent-guided component and target-database features.

entry.title: When to Trust Simulated Patient Responses:Support-Gated World Models for Vasopressor Decision Support

author.name: Yifan Jin, Tao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a support-gated extension to propose-simulate-refine clinical agents: a recurrent dynamics ensemble predicts short-horizon patient physiological responses to norepinephrine dosing, while a behavior model estimates whether the action is observationally supported, withholding predictions when support is weak or ensemble disagreement is high. Evaluated on eICU-CRD across 70 hospitals with 30,700 decision transitions and held-out hospitals.

entry.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Tony H. Zhang, Connor Mattson, Daniel S. Brown

entry.summary: Extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning to cooperative multi-agent teams using Round-Robin Behavior Cloning, where a single demonstrator controls one agent at a time while others run current policies. The imitation policy provides a warm-start that is then improved by RL, overcoming the difficulty of simultaneous multi-agent teleoperation.

entry.title: Training-Free Acceleration of Multi-View 3D Transformers via Regime-Aware Attention Approximation

author.name: Muhammed Izzet Sezer, Sevval Belkis Dikkaya

entry.summary: The paper analyzes global attention in multi-view 3D transformers like VGGT across seven datasets and finds every layer plays one of three roles: scene averaging, cross-image point matching, or anchoring on the first image. Building on this, it proposes a regime-aware attention approximation that accelerates these models training-free, addressing the quadratic attention cost in image count. This is a useful efficiency contribution since generic LLM accelerators fail on these architectures.

entry.title: AG-JEPA: Anatomically Guided Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture for Neurodegenerative Representation Learning

author.name: Azad Singh, Ayantika Das, Amog Rao, Aiman Farooq, Anirban Porya, Ananya Shukla, Sowbhagya Suresh, Srinivasan Iyengar, Mohit Jain, Mercy Prasanna Ranjit

entry.summary: AG-JEPA augments joint embedding predictive architectures with anatomical tokens that interact with patch tokens during pretraining, forcing representations to capture brain regions relevant to neurodegeneration in brain MRI. Built on this representation, the work targets early Alzheimer's disease detection during the subtle cognitively-normal-to-MCI transition. It demonstrates how domain structure can be injected into self-supervised medical models.

entry.title: Interactive Program Induction with Language Model Priors

author.name: Robin Shing Moon Chan, Ryan Cotterell

entry.summary: Frames program induction from input-output examples as Bayesian inference, using language models as priors over programs, and studies how posterior mass concentrates on the target program as examples are observed interactively. This addresses the fundamental ambiguity where finite examples are consistent with infinitely many programs diverging on unseen inputs.

entry.title: Disentangling Forgetting from Utility: Lightweight LLM Unlearning via Orthogonal Null-Space Projection

author.name: Xiuyuan Wang, Weiming Liu, Zongxin Yang, Fan Wang, Liemiao Jin, Rubin Qin, Wei Chen, Bin Shi, Chaochao Chen, Xiaolin Zheng

entry.summary: UUE reformulates LLM unlearning as controllable model editing by projecting parameter updates into the orthogonal left null space of retained knowledge representations, guaranteeing retained knowledge is untouched while targeted knowledge is removed. This addresses the utility degradation and inefficiency of fine-tuning-based unlearning. It matters for privacy compliance and safety of deployed LLMs.

entry.title: Sample-Efficient Control of Magnetoconvective Flows via Differentiable Simulation

author.name: Jannis Becktepe, Dmitry Krasnov, Nils Thuerey, J\"org Schumacher, Sebastian Peitz

entry.summary: The paper presents phi-PICT, a differentiable GPU-accelerated magnetohydrodynamic solver for active flow control, validated against MHD benchmarks. Integrated into FluidGym, it enables gradient-based control algorithms that improve heat transfer by over 25 percent with roughly a thousandfold accuracy gain over prior approaches, relevant to fusion blanket cooling.

entry.title: Contrastive local learning in large nonlinear analog circuits

author.name: Pragyan Pandey, Peter Wu, Deema Alyahya, Eric Y. Ma

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates that contrastive local learning networks, where analog circuits relax to equilibrium and each adaptive element updates from local voltage contrasts without backpropagation, can scale beyond proof-of-concept circuits to larger tasks and remain robust to hardware nonidealities. Device-level simulations identify design principles governing scaling of nonlinear transistor implementations.

entry.title: Detection and Classification in Latent Spaces: High-Dimensional Analysis and Validation

author.name: Enis Chenchene, Anil S. Baslamisli, Paolo Braca

entry.summary: This work analyzes statistical detection and classification rules operating in foundation-model latent spaces in the proportional high-dimensional regime, deriving explicit large-deviation characterizations of false-alarm and miss probabilities for linear and quadratic statistics under the Neyman-Pearson paradigm. The analysis reveals non-monotonic error decay including double-descent and multiple-descent behavior, validated on vision, text, and other modalities.

entry.title: VEPO: Mitigating Multilingual Hallucinations in LVLMs via Visual Evidence-guided Preference Optimization

author.name: Chengpeng Fu, Xiaocheng Feng, Wenshuai Huo, Yichong Huang, Baohang Li, Duyu Tang, Ting Liu

entry.summary: VEPO is a training-time preference optimization method that reduces object hallucination in large vision-language models for low-resource languages by transferring reliable visual grounding from English to other languages without external translation or reward models. It localizes visual evidence and uses it to guide preference optimization, avoiding inference-time interventions that distort output language. This addresses a well-documented weakness of LVLMs in multilingual settings.

entry.title: Cracks in Embeddings: Robustness and Stability of JEPA-Based Chest X-Ray Representations

author.name: Zahid Mansur, Kalpana Yadav, Deepak Mishra

entry.summary: Systematically tests four JEPA-based chest X-ray encoders under adversarial attacks, image corruptions, and label-scarcity conditions, finding severe model-dependent degradation with cosine similarity dropping to 0.33 and AUROC falling by up to 0.12. The study evaluates representations trained on 78,468 NIH ChestX-ray14 images and examines mitigation strategies. It highlights that increasingly popular JEPA approaches may be fragile in clinical deployment.

entry.title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection

author.name: Donghoon Lee, Jusung Park, Shinjin Kang

entry.summary: The paper casts OOD object detection as a box-conditional hypothesis test whose null distribution depends on box size and border contact, yielding a distribution-free false-alarm bound per box. This conditional testing uncovers separation hidden by a single null distribution and improves reliable OOD ranking in deployed detectors.

entry.title: Per-Agent-Safe Navigation of Globally Driven Robot Collectives via Affine Field Design

author.name: Seunghwan Jang, Steven Ceron, Wei Xiao

entry.summary: This work proposes a broadcast control formulation where a single spatially affine field governs motion and deformation of a robot collective, with the scalar component regulating size and the gradient driving translation through non-reciprocal interactions. This avoids per-robot control and communication costs that scale with team size while guaranteeing individual safety.

entry.title: When Will You Hand It Over? A Hidden Start Delay Makes Self-Play Handover Robust to Unfamiliar Partners

author.name: Mohammad Khoshnazar, Mike Degany, Deyuan Qu, Qing Yang, Matyas Szanto

entry.summary: The paper studies cooperative self-play for humanoid object handover, showing that a receiver trained with a learned giver achieves 95% handover success but drops to 31% with unseen scripted partners. The authors diagnose the failure as the giver consistently starting its offer immediately, causing the receiver to learn a single timing rendezvous, and show that a hidden one-second start delay restores robustness to unfamiliar partners.

entry.title: When Should LLM Agents Forget? Memory Filtering Under Query-Critical Resolver Errors

author.name: Samarth Vinayaka

entry.summary: This paper examines when hard-filtering of stale facts in LLM memory systems hurts downstream accuracy due to resolver errors that delete query-critical facts. Across three models, sensitivity analysis shows hard-drop can swing from accuracy gains to significant losses at low resolver reliability, with false-drops causing more damage than false-keeps. The authors propose a deployment-matched gate that outperforms always-filtering and approaches oracle performance.

entry.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system

author.name: Yong Jiang, Zheng Jiang, Gaowei Zhang, Zengzhou Hao, Suixiang Shi, Chi Zhang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: ChlCast is an AI model producing daily 10-day forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a at approximately 4-km resolution between 60S and 60N, combining factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture. It reportedly outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system while avoiding the heavy computational cost of coupled numerical simulation. The model supports marine ecosystem monitoring and management.

entry.title: A Spectral Framework for Universal Proxy Regularization in Model Merging

author.name: Shangge Liu, Danyue Qian, Qi Fan, Yinghuan Shi, Wenbin Li, Lei Wang, Yang Gao, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: This paper proposes a spectral framework characterizing when a universal, task-agnostic proxy distribution can replace task-specific data for regularizing model merging, using notions of spectral coverage and leakage. It addresses the privacy-violation problem in which prior merging methods require data from other tasks during finetuning. The work provides theoretical grounding for data-free model merging, a practically important capability for multi-task model construction.

entry.title: TotalSegmentator Aorta Report: Automated Aortic Diameter Measurement at 11 Standardized Landmarks on CT Images

author.name: Jakob Wasserthal, Daniel Hinck, Martin Segeroth, Joshy Cyriac, Denis Berdajs, Jules Miazza, Maurice Pradella

entry.summary: The report presents an open-source, fully automated tool that measures aortic diameters at 11 standardized landmarks on CT angiography, validated against a senior radiologist reference standard on 239 examinations. It follows current clinical guidelines and builds on TotalSegmentator segmentations of aortic branches and vertebrae.

entry.title: LECAT: Measuring LLM Category Learning from Pretraining Data

author.name: Jimin Mun, Maarten Sap, Yanai Elazar

entry.summary: LeCat is a two-part framework for analyzing how LLMs learn category knowledge, distinguishing memorization of in-domain knowledge, generalization to unseen instances, and flexible contextual use, then tracing how such knowledge can be acquired from pretraining text that encodes it via repetition, exceptions, or other patterns. The motivating example is humans knowing airplanes are fast, extending to red airplanes but not broken ones.

entry.title: LuthorSQL: A One-Pass Text-to-SQL Model as System 1 for a Slower LLM Agent

author.name: Ibrahim Memon, Armin Karamzade, M. Hanif Jhaveri, Roy Fox

entry.summary: LuthorSQL is a non-autoregressive 7B text-to-SQL model that makes a single forward pass over a bounded query-plan grammar, serving as a fast System 1 gate that escalates only uncertain queries to a slower frontier LLM agent (System 2). Motivated by the high cost of hosted frontier agents for database access, it lets organizations use local hardware without sacrificing accuracy. The work targets a concrete and sizable cost problem in enterprise database querying.

entry.title: Condensing Law of Security Information

author.name: Qi Tan, Tianyu Cui, Qi Li, Ke Xu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper challenges the assumption that bigger LLMs are always better in security contexts, arguing that security decisions depend on long-tailed anomalous inputs (such as zero-day attacks) that likelihood-based scaling handles poorly. The authors identify a failure mode where a model's general capability causes it to silently repair anomalous inputs before downstream security components can detect them, and formalize the problem as a tradeoff involving a cognitive capability measure K(W) defined via mutual information between the model and the input distribution.

entry.title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays

author.name: Weiru Zhang, Yuzhong Hong, Junwei Bao, Lemao Liu, Dejing Dou

entry.summary: The paper introduces G-CGEC, a new task formulation requiring grammatical error correction systems to predict both corrections and their pixel positions on images of handwritten K-12 Chinese essays, moving beyond text-to-text GEC. The accompanying G-CGEC-Eval benchmark provides real-world annotated essay images with adapted IoU-style metrics from object detection. This bridges multimodal perception and linguistic correction for practical educational applications.

entry.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization

author.name: Pei Tang, Songtao Lu

entry.summary: The paper studies preference-guided multi-objective optimization over nonconvex objectives, proposing a penalty-based min-max-min formulation (the M3 problem) that unifies preference optimization with weak Pareto optimality enforcement via a merit function vanishing on the weak Pareto set. ParetoM3 is a single-loop first-order algorithm with convergence guarantees to stationary solutions under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption. It has natural applications to multi-objective alignment and RLHF-style preference learning.

entry.title: AI-Based Multi-View Echocardiographic Image Synthesis using Dynamic Shape Control

author.name: Jo\~ao Freitas, Anca Balinisteanu, Ahmed Youssef, Vitor Hugo Pereira, Jan D'hooge, Sandro Queir\'os

entry.summary: Proposes a shape-controlled synthesis framework for multi-view echocardiographic sequences that goes beyond left-ventricle-only supervision, enabling generation of standard and unconventional cardiac imaging planes while preserving multi-view consistency. The work targets the data scarcity problem in clinical cardiology caused by ethical and logistical limits on annotated datasets.

entry.title: Adversarially Batched Online Learning

author.name: Mingda Qiao, Kerui Wu

entry.summary: Introduces adversarially batched online learning, where the learner may update its decision rule only at restricted times, and analyzes four canonical problems: stochastic bandits, online convex optimization, prediction with expert advice, and adversarial bandits. For stochastic bandits it identifies a universal complexity measure based on relative batch growth and shows the batch penalty can grow superlinearly.

entry.title: Complex Schr\"odinger Bridges

author.name: Dong-Sig Han, Tolga Birdal

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces conformal optimal transport (COT), a complex-valued transportation framework for physical systems governed by geometric and dissipative dynamics such as Hamiltonian structures. Building on COT, the authors propose complex Schrödinger bridges (CSBs), a new class of dynamical diffusion bridges designed to transform distributions in complex vector spaces while respecting scaling and rotation laws. This extends diffusion bridge methods, which are typically limited by large optimization spaces, into domains relevant to physics and geometric machine learning.

entry.title: Analyzing Learning-Dynamics Across Loss and Prediction Choices for Diffusion Models

author.name: Dongwoo Kim

entry.summary: This paper systematically disentangles the effects of prediction target (clean data, noise, or velocity) and loss space in denoising diffusion models, showing that changing the loss space for a fixed prediction target is exactly equivalent to timestep reweighting. It also proves an irreducible squared-error floor for noise and velocity prediction under linear bottlenecks, explaining why different combinations yield different sample quality.

entry.title: PACT: A Decoder-Confidence-Guided Two-Round Receiver for Joint Channel and Phase-Noise Estimation in Sub-THz OFDM

author.name: Ruilin Wang, Xiaodai Dong

entry.summary: This paper proposes a two-round receiver for sub-THz OFDM communication that jointly estimates frequency-selective channel effects and oscillator phase noise using a pilot-aware complex transformer (PACT) combined with neural decoding. Decoder outputs are fed back as pseudo-pilots with confidence weighting to refine second-round estimates, yielding roughly 70% and 57% lower code-block error rates than the best baseline at Eb/N0 of 30 dB.

entry.title: Hierarchical Bayesian physics-augmented neural networks for populations of hyperelastic laws: specimen variability and uncertainty from scarce, noisy data

author.name: Vincent C. Scholz, Phaedon-Stelios Koutsourelakis

entry.summary: This work develops Bayesian physics-augmented neural networks (PANNs) for learning hyperelastic material laws, extending from single-specimen fits to a hierarchical Bayesian formulation that captures specimen-to-specimen variability as a nonlinear mixed-effects model. The approach keeps learned laws physically admissible and quantifies uncertainty even from scarce, noisy experimental data such as soft tissue tests.

entry.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation

author.name: Jianjun Ou, Matthew Lentz

entry.summary: Callo is a disaggregated LLM serving system that reuses invalidated KV cache state for speculative decoding when agent sessions edit context, verifying drafts against exact KV after re-prefill before committing tokens. On a two-GPU testbed with SWE-agent sessions across three model families, it achieves 1.05-1.19x all-request speedups over vLLM at moderate load.

entry.title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions

author.name: Jianguo Hou, Wuchen Li

entry.summary: This paper extends score-based probability-flow formulations to reaction-diffusion equations by developing a Lagrangian particle method in which particles carry both a position and a physical weight that tracks mass changes from reaction source terms. The authors combine learned velocity fields with weighted particle training and prove a relative-entropy inequality for non-increasing reaction rates. It matters because it bridges score-based generative modeling theory with PDE dynamics that do not conserve mass.

entry.title: What Do Multilingual Self-Supervised Speech Encoders Know About Sentence Meaning?

author.name: Kevin Krahn, Eric Fosler-Lussier

entry.summary: The authors probe sentence-level semantics in massively multilingual self-supervised speech models across 76 languages using linear maps from frozen speech representations into a frozen text embedding space, evaluated via cross-modal retrieval. They find sentence meaning is linearly accessible but highly uneven across languages and resource tiers, and that cross-lingual probes can transfer to unseen languages. Scaling the OmniASR wav2vec family from 300M to 7B parameters yields analysis of scaling effects on semantic structure.

entry.title: NER-D: A cross-domain benchmark for German NER

author.name: Marc Brinner, Philipp Cimiano, Karolina Hanna Czok, Regina Stodden, Viju Sudhi, Sina Zarrie{\ss}

entry.summary: NER-D is a cross-domain German named entity recognition benchmark spanning 13 datasets across 9 domains including legal, medical, and historical text. The authors benchmark proprietary LLMs and small open-source models, finding that a proprietary model wins without tuning but LoRA fine-tuning lets small open models substantially outperform it. The benchmark also analyzes the effects of domain and tagset variation.

entry.title: Signal Scaffolding: Unlocking the Potential of Lightweight Models for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Zhijie Wang, Li Zhang, Yujie Chen, Shibiao Deng, Xin Gao, Houzhi Zhou, Jiangshuo Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies underexploited training regimes as the root cause of poor lightweight self-supervised monocular depth accuracy and proposes a three-phase Signal Scaffolding strategy requiring no extra data or parameters. Applied to their ReForgeDepth network, it achieves state-of-the-art results for the accuracy/efficiency class on KITTI and Cityscapes.

entry.title: DoubleTake: Focused Verification of Visual Evidence for Long-Document Understanding

author.name: Kejun Xue, Ang Li, Jinghua Tang, Xincheng Wang, Yongbin Gao, Yanghua Xiao, Zhijun Fang

entry.summary: Introduces DoubleTake, a training-free framework for long-document question answering that runs a second focused verification pass over retrieved pages. An initial reading produces a candidate answer plus an evidence record; a planner formulates a factual question, an independent verifier answers it from source images, and a reasoner resolves the final answer. This separates evidence checking from answering, improving accuracy when models fail despite sufficient evidence.

entry.title: MaskSCD: Bitemporal Mask Classification for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images

author.name: Weikang Yu, Pedram Ghamisi

entry.summary: MaskSCD reformulates semantic change detection in remote sensing as mask classification over bitemporal label-pair images, predicting one shared mask per region of constant land-cover class pair. This guarantees consistency between change maps and per-date semantics, avoiding the contradictory outputs of separate per-pixel decoders.

entry.title: Co-Sight Harness: Externalized Control Assets and Deterministic Enforcement for Long-Horizon Business Agents

author.name: Luyao Wang, Xijun Zhu, Zhaohui Hao, Xiwen Zhang, Xingyu Wen, Weishan Li, Yuyang Liao, Yanqin Gao, Yongsheng Du, Lingjun Huang, Shaowei Zhao, Gang Li, Qifan Yu, Baoli Wang

entry.summary: Co-Sight Harness makes long-horizon business workflows reliable without changing the underlying LLM by externalizing workflow definitions, state, and domain knowledge into versioned control assets, enforced by a state machine and machine-checkable acceptance gates with an independent trace auditor. Assets are updated only after regression checks and human approval. Evaluation on three deployed workflows exceeding 200 steps shows reliability improvements.

entry.title: VLAN: Vision-Language Accessible Navigation

author.name: Jie Hu, Yu Zheng, Wenzhi Wu, Weixing Feng, Cunlei Cheng, Jiaming Zhang

entry.summary: VLAN is a large-scale navigation benchmark with 1,000 scenes, 20K trajectories, and 160K keyframes that treats accessibility as user-conditioned, providing embodiment-specific actions and labels for legged and wheeled agents including humanoid and quadruped robots and people with visual or mobility impairments. Obstacles are categorized as Passable, Bypass, HighRisk, and more.

entry.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models

author.name: Dhruv Dixit, Khushi Patel, Congcong Xu, Min Song

entry.summary: Introduces a two-stage framework training small language models to produce executable, auditable reasoning trajectories: free-form chain-of-thought rationales are first compiled into typed action traces with calculator calls, runtime observations, and verification steps, followed by reinforcement learning. Targets reliable mathematical reasoning for low-cost, privacy-sensitive local deployment.

entry.title: RL$^{\mathrm{RT}}$: On-Device Reinforcement Learning Runtime

author.name: Zexin Li, Xinwei Gao, Arvind Easwaran

entry.summary: RL-RT is an on-device runtime for reinforcement learning that coordinates a periodic actor and learner sharing one embedded GPU, making the coupling between policy refresh and actor deadlines a tunable parameter via refresh bounds and slack-aware GPU permits. On two Jetson boards it keeps deadline misses below 1 percent for a 16.8M-parameter policy, versus 85-100 percent without the runtime. This is a systems contribution enabling continual learning on embedded hardware.

entry.title: Identifying Latent Neural Dynamics with Recognition-Parametrised Gaussian Process Dynamical Systems

author.name: Arielle Rosinski, Qianqian Feng, Lior Fox, Maneesh Sahani

entry.summary: Proposes recognition-parametrised Gaussian process dynamical systems for modeling latent dynamics in high-dimensional neural recordings, avoiding explicit generative parameterizations of the flow field, observation map, and response variability. The approach supports the computation-through-dynamics hypothesis by identifying dynamical rules from recorded neural population activity.

entry.title: Antidistillation is Cheap: Lightweight Distillation-Resistance via Stylistic Corruption

author.name: Anh Tu Ngo, Anupam Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: This paper proposes a lightweight defense against model distillation attacks on black-box LLM APIs: dynamically injecting style-steering vectors into teacher activations upon suspected malicious queries, causing stylistic corruption of outputs that degrades student training. Unlike surrogate-based defenses that manipulate next-token sampling, this avoids significant inference latency overhead. It matters for protecting proprietary model capabilities behind APIs.

entry.title: On the Limits of Sufficient Explanations

author.name: Klaus Weinbauer, Peter F. Stadler, Thomas G\"artner, Sagar Malhotra

entry.summary: The paper formally characterizes when sufficient post-hoc explanations exist for classifiers on structured data such as graphs and strings, providing a general explanation formalism with instance spaces, classifiers, and select relations. It delivers four main theoretical contributions establishing the boundaries of the widely adopted sufficient-explanation paradigm.

entry.title: Multifidelity Operator Inference for Dynamical Systems

author.name: Vignesh Sella, Anirban Chaudhuri, Karen Willcox

entry.summary: MF-OpInf extends non-intrusive Operator Inference for reduced-order models by combining scarce expensive high-fidelity snapshots with plentiful low-fidelity snapshots through a control-variate-inspired multifidelity least-squares formulation. This addresses unstable or inaccurate ROM predictions in aerospace settings where high-fidelity training data is limited in parameter coverage and trajectory length.

entry.title: Adaptable Watermarking: Transforming Image Watermarking Models via Lightweight Adapters

author.name: Mehrdad Saberi, Vishal Asnani, Shruti Agarwal, Soheil Feizi, John Collomosse

entry.summary: This work shows that one neural image watermarking model can be transformed into another via compact parameter-efficient adapters trained with a multi-domain residual alignment loss plus a secret-loss term preserving bit accuracy. Evaluated across TrustMark, InvisMark, RoSteALS, HiDDeN, and WAM, the approach makes watermarking systems modular and upgradable without full retraining.

entry.title: ALoMa: Affine Correspondences Beyond Patches

author.name: David Nordstr\"om, Georg B\"okman, Viktor Larsson, Fredrik Kahl, Jonathan Ventura

entry.summary: Revisits affine correspondence estimation, extending it beyond local patches to image and image-pair levels and learning the full 4-DoF affine matrix jointly rather than component-wise. Building on LoMa keypoint descriptions, ALoMa demonstrates consistent improvements across a wide range of multiple-view geometry downstream tasks. Affine correspondences enable robust and efficient minimal solvers but remain understudied.

entry.title: DiffusionSSD: Achieving Extreme Visual Compression with Dual-stage Diffusion and Cross-level Near-Data Processing

author.name: Kuai Yu, Wen Li, Shengwen Liang, Jie Zhang, Ying Wang, Huawei Li, Xin Yao, Renhai Chen, Gong Zhang

entry.summary: DiffusionSSD proposes a diffusion-based codec for extreme visual compression on edge devices, combining a dual-stage algorithm with cross-level near-data processing on SSD storage to avoid NPU contention and long I/O paths. The systems-algorithm co-design targets perceptual quality at extreme compression ratios under resource constraints.

entry.title: Advancing Quantization for R&R Models with Microscaling Formats

author.name: Yavuz Yetim, Bor-Yiing Su, Zhe Wang, Arthur Liu, Pranav Sharma, Ying Wang, Randy Shuai, Luke Pfister, Ruichao Xiao, Bill Zhao, Zihao Liu, Liyuan Li, Jiangyuan Li, Gaoxiang Liu, Nathan Yan, Geonhwa Jeong, Jatin Chhugani, Elias Ellison, Uladzimir Pashkevich

entry.summary: An empirical study of MXFP8 and 6-bit MXFP6 microscaling quantization for industrial-scale recommendation and ranking (R&R) inference on AMD MI350X hardware. Unlike LLMs, production R&R models enforce extremely tight 0.01% normalized entropy launch bars, which has blocked aggressive quantization. The large author team provides engineering detail on meeting these constraints with microscaling formats.

entry.title: MASTARS: Multi-Agent Sequential Trajectory Augmentation with Return-Conditioned Subgoals

author.name: Jiwon Jeon, Myungsik Cho, Woojun Kim, Seongmin Kim, Woohyeon Byeon, Seungyul Han, Youngchul Sung

entry.summary: MASTARS tackles the diversity-coordination trade-off in offline multi-agent RL data augmentation using a diffusion-based framework that generates trajectories sequentially across agents while enforcing cross-agent coordination via inpainting, with return-conditioned subgoals. It produces augmented trajectories that improve offline MARL beyond what fixed datasets allow. The formulation cleanly identifies a real tension in joint versus independent generation.

entry.title: Causally Constrained and Uncertainty-Aware Cardiopulmonary Risk Prediction

author.name: Yuxiang Lai, Jiashuo Zhang, Liang Zhao, Xiaofeng Yang

entry.summary: The CE-Agent is a two-stage medical AI framework that compiles peer-reviewed epidemiological evidence into explicit constraints on risk-factor weights before training, estimating local baseline risk, applied to joint lung cancer and cardiovascular risk prediction from chest CT.
