It aims to avoid confounded risk directions and hidden uncertainty in small hospital cohorts. This addresses well-known reliability failures of unconstrained clinical ML.

entry.title: When evaluation becomes intervention in clinical AI

author.name: Anthony Abou Mrad, Aviona Conti, Samuel Schmidgall, Jayanth Pratap, Ruhika Iyer, Joseph Kim, King Shi, Yann Sakref, Luis M. Ahumada, Lisa Knowlton, Andrew M. Cameron, Khyzer Aziz, Jeffrey K. Jopling

entry.summary: This position-style paper examines how LLM judges used to select prompts or train clinical models become part of the intervention, potentially favoring errors the judge overlooks. It specifies what a judge's report must contain and what independent clinical testing each judge-driven change requires.

entry.title: From Local Prediction Error to Final Outputs: A Theory of Expert Sharing in Multi-Step Reasoning

author.name: Tiantong Wang, Zhiren Gong, Yixin Wang, Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: The paper develops a theory of when expert sharing across layers or steps in mixture-of-experts models helps final outputs rather than just local prediction error, deriving exact sharing and merging criteria in linear regression settings. It characterizes final-output risk and constructs cases where sharing lowers average local error yet increases final-output error. This provides principled guidance for MoE weight sharing in multi-step reasoning systems.

entry.title: MineralExp: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Experimental Design in Real-World Mineral Exploration

author.name: Bing Wang, Mingyang Wang, Yuanhang Mi, Yue Xu, Kaibo Su, Li'ang Xiao, Chunguo Wu, Changchun Li, Ximing Li, Kun-Feng Qiu, Bo Yang

entry.summary: MineralExp is a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on automated geochemical experimental design in mineral exploration, a capability upstream of the data-analysis tasks agents already automate. The benchmark handles methodological diversity and subjectivity in experiment choice, where no single reference protocol exists. It fills a gap in assessing agentic scientific reasoning in an applied geoscience domain.

entry.title: Alignment with Reflect-Reasoning: Learning How To Follow Principles

author.name: Henry Bell, Caroline Zhang, Dhaval Potdar, Mohammed Mobasserul Haque, Brandon Fain

entry.summary: Proposes Reflect-Reasoning, a training method that teaches LLMs to follow contextual norms and principles supplied at inference time via post-generation critique-and-revision, improving on system prompting while generalizing beyond fixed training-time constitutions. The approach addresses the reality that governing norms vary by cultural context and deployment application.

entry.title: Joint World Action Models through Differentiable Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Mintae Kim, Koushil Sreenath

entry.summary: The paper proposes WATO, which improves joint world-action models by treating generated actions and future states as references in a dynamics-constrained trajectory optimization problem, backpropagating a task loss through the optimizer during training. This makes generated trajectories task-effective and dynamics-consistent while optimization is needed only at training time. Deployment remains direct generation, preserving inference speed.

entry.title: Which Model, For Which Variable? Per-Variable Forecast Combination in Sparse ICU Time Series

author.name: Marius Fracarolli, Stefan Riezler

entry.summary: Across five ICU databases and 94 physiological channels, the authors show no single forecasting architecture is best for every variable, and per-variable weighted combinations of 14 models beat the best single model by 6.1 to 11.0 percent mean squared error. Gains concentrate in the sparsest channels, where clinical data is thinnest.

entry.title: A thorough review on Deep Learning approaches to 2D-to-3D Registration in Medical Imaging

author.name: Andrea Borghesi, Julia van Beurden, Maarten van Alphen, Michiel van den Brekel, Luc Karssemakers, Jan-Jakob Sonke, Baris Karakullukcu, Jonas Teuwen, George Yiasemis

entry.summary: This is a comprehensive review of deep learning methods for 2D-to-3D image registration, a key enabler of intraoperative guidance that aligns preoperative 3D volumes with real-time 2D images. It covers how core DL concepts are adapted to registration and analyzes recent methodological advances addressing non-convexity, initialization sensitivity, and computational demands of classical optimization-based methods.

entry.title: Explanations that Transfer: Interpreting Medical Retrieval with Sparse AutoEncoders

author.name: Diane Bouchacourt, Ga\"etan Brison

entry.summary: This paper applies sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to medical information retrieval, converting dense text embeddings into semantically interpretable representations via a reconstruction-plus-InfoNCE objective. The goal is to explain retrieval behavior while preserving transferability to new clinical corpora, addressing the opacity of finetuned dense retrievers in medical AI systems.

entry.title: FEND: Far-End Detection in Outbound Voice AI Calls

author.name: Abhishek Kumar, Suraj Agrawal, Aashraya Sachdeva

entry.summary: FEND reframes answering-machine detection for outbound Voice AI agents, arguing that a single human-versus-machine bit is insufficient because the far end may be a live person, voicemail, an IVR system, or another AI agent, each requiring different agent behavior. Drawing on 1,000 sampled calls from a real deployment (48.1 percent answered by a live person), the paper motivates and presumably builds a richer far-end detection taxonomy. This reflects the emerging reality of AI-to-AI phone calls.

entry.title: GT-FENG: General Theory of Factual Evaluation and Normative Grounding in Language Models *Author(s)

author.name: Jiayu Feng

entry.summary: GT-FENG proposes a unified framework for evaluating LLM answers against context-dependent rules in law, policy, and other rule-governed domains, where correctness varies by jurisdiction, date, or definition. The framework performs rule-based error attribution and proves that when multiple rules yield the same value, the answer alone cannot reveal which rule was used. It demonstrates the approach on Medicaid income-limit questions.

entry.title: LitArc-Bench: Disentangling Text-Specific Reader-Response Dynamics from Position and Lexical Affect

author.name: Mingming Su, Yushan Wei, Sen Song, Xinche Zhang

entry.summary: LitArc-Bench evaluates whether model predictions of human affect over literary texts reflect genuine reader-response dynamics or merely narrative position and lexical affect. Using 39 Chinese literary excerpts with 430 questionnaires and over 9,000 VAD ratings, it shows position alone explains substantial alignment, but text-specific dynamics remain above control thresholds.

entry.title: Marimba: A System One Model for Speech

author.name: Solano Amadori

entry.summary: Marimba is a lightweight interface for typed speech decisions such as term presence, turn completion, and language identification, built on frozen features from a small ASR model. It combines zero-shot transcript scoring, a question-conditioned head, and a layer-18 turn-end readout, achieving solid AUROC and calibration on private conversational and public read speech, plus strong PII detection via a downstream pipeline.

entry.title: HarmonyText: Harmonious Scene Text Editing via Reverse-to-Refined Pair Synthesis and Region-Decoupled Frequency Learning

author.name: Ziqi Yi, Huiguo He, Guitao Xu, Peirong Zhang, Cheng Da, Xinyao Yu, Zhanpeng Wang, Changqian Yu, Huan Yang, Kun Gai, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: HarmonyText is a mask-free, instruction-driven scene text editing framework that addresses unreliable pseudo-ground-truth supervision and over-smoothed text generation. It introduces Region-Decoupling Optimization to align edited regions with pseudo-targets and frequency-aware supervision to preserve high-frequency text details lost under standard velocity regression.

entry.title: VACO: Vertex-Aligned Decoding for Dense Hand Contact Estimation from a Single Image

author.name: Binhong Ye, Jin-Chuan Shi, Tao Liu, Xin Wang, Hao Chen, Chunhua Shen

entry.summary: VACO improves dense hand contact estimation by having each MANO hand vertex sample image features at its own projected location instead of decoding the whole contact map from one shared query. A jointly trained hand-reconstruction backbone predicts vertex locations at inference, and noise-perturbed training improves robustness.

entry.title: InfiHall-Bench: A Benchmark for Hallucination Evaluation in Autoregressive Text-to-Image Generation

author.name: Yuxia Qiao, Xinhao Zhong, Junhao Li, Yi Sun, Jiaxin Hong, Shuoyang Sun, Bin Chen

entry.summary: Introduces InfiHall-Bench, a 411-prompt benchmark specifically designed to evaluate hallucination in visual autoregressive text-to-image models, where existing diffusion-centric benchmarks lose diagnostic value. It composes five foundational skills - attribute binding, spatial relation, action relation, part correspondence, and more - into prompts that test interactions among multiple visual requirements within a single image. Addresses stale prompts and template-heavy category construction in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: X-Strata: Separating Aneurysms and Overlapping Vessels into Layers from 2D X-ray Angiography

author.name: Zhihong Wen, Congzhou Chen, Hucheng Li, Xun Han, Jianning Zhang, Yakun Chen, Hao Gao, Hao Zhao, Yudong Ma, Guanqiao Li, Yongping Liang, Shengli Guo

entry.summary: X-Strata decomposes a cine X-ray angiogram into three layers: complete aneurysm sac, front vessels, and rear vessels, exploiting contrast timing and parallax between two views to resolve occlusion and layer ordering, then lifting layers into 3D. It trains on labels projected from same-session 3D rotational angiography.

entry.title: ERA: Error-Resistant Autonomous Object Navigation with Predicted Depth

author.name: Shunyang Huang, Shuo Wang, Wenyuan Xie, Mingyu Lin, Yue Ding, Hongtao Lu

entry.summary: ERA is a training-free object navigation system that replaces depth sensors with RGB-predicted depth, introducing a Move with Error paradigm where new viewpoints correct accumulated map errors. Revisable occupancy maps and exploration from reachable viewpoints prevent premature search termination caused by depth prediction errors.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Risk Evaluation with Low-Rank Perturbations

author.name: Linglingzhi Zhu, Dongze Wu, Yao Xie

entry.summary: This paper studies distributionally robust risk under perturbations restricted to low-rank matrices with shared row and column spaces, quantifying the gap between unrestricted and low-rank worst-case risk under moment or Wasserstein budgets. It derives computable risk certificates via projected gradient ascent on a curvature-corrected problem with convergence guarantees.

entry.title: When Cooperation Must Change: Semantic Strategy Unlearning in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Wenhan Wu, Linghan Chen, Yudong Gao, Fan Yang, Honglong Chen, Kai Yin, Jiawei Jiang, Chuang Hu

entry.summary: This paper introduces semantic strategy unlearning for cooperative MARL: removing a specific learned coordination convention when it becomes obsolete or unsafe while preserving overall cooperation, a harder problem than runtime shielding which leaves underlying coordination intact. Motivating examples span web caching permissions and multi-robot coordination. It connects machine unlearning ideas to multi-agent settings, an underexplored intersection.

entry.title: Neural Classifiers as Error-Correcting Codes

author.name: Sergey Salishev, Anton Makarov, Oleg Granichin, Renata Avros, Zeev Volkovich

entry.summary: The authors establish a unified framework characterizing supervised deep classification as decoding of error-correcting codes, showing cross-entropy optimization aligns softmax classifiers with maximum-likelihood decoding where logits map to Hamming distances. The framework geometrically explains standard divergence objectives and identifies Neural Collapse and LeJEPA geometries as optimal decoding constellations.

entry.title: Learning Latent Goal Costs for Visual World-Model Planning with an Expanding Curriculum

author.name: Konstantinos Mylonas, Thrasyvoulos Spyropoulos

entry.summary: The work improves image-goal planning with frozen visual world models by fitting a small residual adapter on frozen I-JEPA embeddings to learn better latent goal costs, avoiding MSE's failure to penalize states behind obstacles that look similar to the goal. An expanding curriculum of initial states and order-based learning from successful and failed rollouts requires no task-specific progress labels.

entry.title: D2ToF: One-Step Diffusion for Depth Super-Resolution from Lightweight Single-Photon LiDAR Waveforms

author.name: Pallabjyoti Deka, Lewis Wilson, Stephen McLaughlin, Jonathan Leach, Abderrahim Halimi

entry.summary: D2ToF distills a diffusion model into a one-step framework for depth super-resolution from very low-resolution single-photon LiDAR arrays, using amortized variational distillation that embeds a measurement-based data consistency term directly in the training objective. This brings generative fidelity to real-time depth imaging on cheap sensors.

entry.title: LoRAWeaver: Directional Adapter Routing in LoRA Representation Space

author.name: Inish Melroy D Souza, Tom Jackson, Vitor Castro, Rebecca Higginson, Andrea Soltoggio

entry.summary: LoRAWeaver treats LoRA adapter routing as a representation alignment problem, selecting adapters training-free by matching adapter-conditioned query representations against task prototypes via cosine similarity. This avoids the retraining that existing routing and encoder-based methods require when new adapters are added. Experiments on LLaMA-2-7B and 13B across a 48-task FLAN-v2 benchmark demonstrate the approach's effectiveness.

entry.title: AscendGYM: A Cost-Aware Kernel Optimization Benchmark for Real-World Workloads on Ascend NPUs

author.name: AI Training Platform Team, Bingwei Zhang, Jing Li, Amir Abdullin, Sihang Chen, Xin Chen, Liangjun Feng, Yingmeng Gao, Tao Guo, Junjie Huang, Dongfang Li, Zhanglian Lin, Jiajun Liu, Zekun Liu, Zhengxuan Lu, Xiaodong Luo, Jian Meng, Ivan Nosov, Linyuan Qiu, Weijian Sun, Wanrui Yan, Binfan Zheng, Zhicheng Zhou, Baotian Hu, Min Zhang, Haizhou Li, Zhiquan Luo

entry.summary: AscendGYM is a benchmark of 48 kernel-optimization tasks across three difficulty levels for Ascend NPUs, with test cases drawn from real training and inference workloads. Unlike prior Ascend kernel benchmarks focused on code generation, it evaluates agents optimizing existing implementations under realistic configurations. It supports multiple evaluation modes and maps performance directly to workload improvements.

entry.title: Certified Improvements to Best-Known Thomson-Problem Configurations with a Search Pipeline Built with Large Language Model Agents

author.name: Hui Shao, Tao Wang, Xiaotian Liu, Yijie Peng

entry.summary: Using a search pipeline assembled from LLM agents combined with replica-exchange basin hopping, the authors certify new best-known configurations for the Thomson problem at N = 912, 1382, and 2502, with energies below the Cambridge Cluster Database values verified by exact integer arithmetic. This is a concrete instance of LLM-agent-assisted scientific discovery on a decades-old mathematical optimization problem.

entry.title: FlexCast: Flexible Context Learning for Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Zuyang Shen, Luqi Gong, Fanda Fan, Bingsong Wang, Xiang Ao, Yahui Wei, Minghao Liu, Chunjie Luo, Jianfeng Zhan

entry.summary: FlexCast disentangles variable-context conditioning from autoregressive factorization in time series foundation models by reformulating forecasting as variable-length masked prediction over patches, dynamically sampling context-target configurations during pretraining. This clarifies where AR next-token forecasting gains come from and enables more flexible context learning. It is relevant to the fast-growing time series foundation model area.

entry.title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams

author.name: Issa Sugiura, Taro Makino, Takashi Ishida

entry.summary: JFinBench is a Japanese financial benchmark of 321 examples from 2026 editions of six certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking, with a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline for constructing and refreshing it. The design directly addresses country-specific coverage and training-data contamination from leaked questions.

entry.title: PhysDox: Benchmarking LLMs on Physical Feasibility Auditing of Physiological Sensing Protocols

author.name: He Liu, Boyuan Gu, Shuaiqi Cheng, Haiyang Sun, Siyu You, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PhysDox, a benchmark for auditing physical feasibility of biomedical sensing protocols, with a 683-sample expert-curated gold set and 5,000-sample silver set across six sensing domains. Evaluating six LLMs under four inference strategies yields only 53.0 macro-F1 on severity detection, with strong oracle diagnosis collapsing in end-to-end settings due to correlated cascade errors.

entry.title: CoTTAGE: An Explainable Judge for Text-to-Audio Generation

author.name: Yu-Xiang Lin, Yun-Man Hsu, Bo-Ru Lu, Kuan-Po Huang, Wenze Ren, Ming-To Chuang, Chun-Yi Kuan, Jiawei Du, Byeonggeun Kim, Qingming Tang, Chieh-Chi Kao, Ankur Gandhe, Chao Wang, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: CoTTAGE is a reasoning-based evaluator for text-to-audio generation that scores text relevance and audio quality via a reason-then-predict paradigm, generating audio-grounded rationales before assigning scores. It is supported by over 10K new human quality annotations and trained with supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. The work addresses a real bottleneck in TTA development where existing metrics lack both human correlation and explainability.

entry.title: Photogrammetric 3D Model-Based Animal Behavior Classification

author.name: Olaf Hellwich, Moritz Heine, Patrik Reiske, Sole Traverso, Katharina Hohlbaum, Henning Sprekeler, Christa Th\"one-Reineke, Lars Lewejohann, Roman Bhuiyan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage approach to video-based animal behavior classification: first reconstruct 3D body and object geometry via photogrammetry, then classify behavior from the 3D representation rather than going end-to-end from 2D image sequences. This makes ambiguities in the ill-posed 2D-to-3D inverse problem explicit and correctable. The method is demonstrated on simulated interacting mice with an extension to real video.

entry.title: Who Should Be on the Panel? Task-Conditioned Persona Selection for LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Boming Yang, Yuquan Wang, Jiaxian Guo, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo

entry.summary: The paper studies task-conditioned persona selection for multi-agent LLM systems, instantiating FinPanel, a trading system in which a recruiter selects trader personas per stock based on a direction-blind statistical sketch of its trading behavior. Each persona gives independent daily calls that are aggregated. This challenges the default practice of reusing a fixed cast of agents across all tasks.

entry.title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review

author.name: Hua Yang, Aditya Bhardwaj, Shidong Pan, Bowen Xu

entry.summary: PrivacyPR is a dataset of 4,131 merged GitHub pull requests from 1,469 repositories (2018-2024) with commits, diffs, review discussions, and LLM-generated labels for privacy relevance, fix type, and GDPR principles, including 1,169 high-confidence privacy fixes plus manually verified and small evaluation splits. It enables benchmarking whether coding agents catch legally required privacy defects during code review. This addresses a gap between code-review automation and regulatory compliance.

entry.title: Between Obligations and Evidence: A Participatory Study of Translating the EU AI Act into Technical Requirements

author.name: Helma Torkamaan, Masoud Mansoury, Yanan Xin, Oscar Oviedo Trespalacios, Roberta Savella, Andrej Zwitter, Maria Heuss, Huy Son Nguyen, Marie-Therese Sekwenz, Moyi Li, Roberta Tamponi, Megha Khosla

entry.summary: A participatory workshop study with 32 researchers, policymakers, and practitioners examining how EU AI Act obligations for high-risk AI systems are translated into measurable technical requirements and compliance evidence, using healthcare, recruitment, and public transport scenarios. Thematic analysis identifies recurring tensions in translating legal obligations into system properties and assigning responsibility.

entry.title: SURFACE: Preference Distribution Matching on Pareto Fronts via Scalarization Steering

author.name: Liuyuan Jiang, Prasanna Sattigeri, Lisha Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SURFACE, a method that adaptively updates scalarization weights in multi-objective optimization so that a finite set of Pareto solutions is allocated along the Pareto front according to a desired preference distribution, correcting for the nonlinear and unknown weight-to-solution distortion. It uses chart estimation to redistribute finite Pareto approximations.

entry.title: Beyond a Single Sign: BiTE for Branch-Preserving Binary Threshold Expansion

author.name: Siddharth Gupta, Mikail Yayla, Akash Kumar

entry.summary: This paper introduces BiTE, an extension to binary neural networks that evaluates each preactivation against K ordered thresholds rather than a single sign function, preserving multiple binary responses as separate inputs. This raises the representational capacity of BNNs from two activation states to K+1 ordered states while retaining bitwise efficiency. It matters because the single-sign bottleneck is a core limitation of binarized networks.

entry.title: Electrocardiographic Imaging via Posterior Sampling under Operator Discrepancy

author.name: Ricarda Buttmann, Andreas M. Lehrmann

entry.summary: OpDis-PS is a diffusion posterior sampler for electrocardiographic imaging that models the discrepancy between the assumed and true forward operator (arising from respiration, posture, and unknown body composition) as signal-dependent rather than treating it as independent noise. It learns how the discrepancy depends on the heart signal and folds it into a corrected forward model. This addresses a key failure mode of posterior samplers on ill-posed inverse problems.

entry.title: Conflict, Feasibility, Faithfulness, Displacement: Four Quantities That Come Apart in Federated Dual-Cone Aggregation

author.name: Grzegorz Gwardys, Karol Wojciechowski, Mateusz Gwardys, Bartosz {\'S}widerski

entry.summary: This work critically examines multi-objective gradient aggregators in federated learning (FedFV, FedGH, FedMGDA+) using UPGrad, showing that conflict, feasibility, faithfulness, and displacement are distinct properties that prior work conflated. Experiments show modest accuracy gains that often vanish or shrink under more careful experimental protocols.

entry.title: f-Divergence Self-Play for Tabular Anomaly Detection via Large Language Models

author.name: Hoang Tran Vuong, Linh Ngo Van, Dang Nguyen, Thin Nguyen, Phuoc Nguyen, Mehrtash Harandi, Trung Le

entry.summary: DiSPaT proposes a self-play fine-tuning framework grounded in f-divergence minimization to strengthen LLM-based tabular anomaly detection beyond one-shot supervised fine-tuning. The derived training objective tightens the model's description of normality across heterogeneous numerical, categorical, and textual attributes.

entry.title: Sample-efficient prediction of high-entropy alloy strength through outcome-aware robust sequential learning

author.name: Ahmed Shoyeb Raihan, Md Habibor Rahman, Ashish Nimbarte, Imtiaz Ahmed

entry.summary: ROSE-HEA is a sequential experimentation framework that predicts ultimate tensile strength of high-entropy alloys from composition and processing conditions while minimizing costly tensile tests. Its acquisition policy anticipates how possible outcomes update Gaussian process models and selects candidates by reassessing worst-case expected predictive risk, validated retrospectively on 501 alloy records.

entry.title: RaFL: An Empirical Study of Random Filter Losses for Image Reconstruction

author.name: Ruibo Wang, Fengbei Liu, Aleksei Tiulpin, Mert R. Sabuncu, Heejong Kim

entry.summary: RaFL is a loss function comparing predictions and targets through random convolutions, random Fourier features, and random wavelet filters with gradient-norm-based automatic balancing, avoiding both domain-specific pretrained perceptual features and manual loss tuning. The systematic empirical study investigates filter family, weighting, and design choices for image reconstruction tasks.

entry.title: A Generalizable Approach to Safety-Aware Robotic Behavior Planning with an Explicit Constraint Space

author.name: Xianxu Wu, Shang-Ching Liu, Zhaocong Liang, Hengxiang Chen, Yujian Ma, Shenwen Deng, Qiang Li, Jianwei Zhang

entry.summary: This work proposes a safety-aware behavior planning framework for robots driven by language and vision models, built on an explicit Constraint Space of reusable textual safety rules. A lightweight query-conditioned dual-tower model learns task- and environment-conditioned applicability of constraints rather than relying solely on semantic retrieval, improving safe manipulation in tabletop environments.

entry.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon

author.name: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

entry.summary: This hardware study builds an FPGA tile computing one full layer of a 369M-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet (linear-attention) model, measuring the cost of paging its fixed-size recurrent state to external memory on an edge device. The finding that paging adds at most 11.2 percent of decode cost shows the recurrent state is not the decoding bottleneck, informing edge deployment of linear-attention LLMs.

entry.title: Evaluating Feedback-Driven Black-Box Processes via Stochastic Modeling and Simulation

author.name: Mengfan Xu, Zirui Liu, Juan Zhai, Shiqing Ma, Barry Nelson

entry.summary: The authors introduce a stochastic framework using Markov chains and simulation to evaluate feedback-driven black-box policies, such as mutation-based fuzzing and analogous iterative processes in machine learning. The framework connects empirical practice with theory by modeling the sequential loop of generating inputs, observing feedback, and adapting. This provides a unified evaluation methodology where none previously existed.

entry.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations

author.name: Genki Kinoshita, Ko Nishino

entry.summary: BAL is a self-supervised framework for human movement representation that exploits the natural temporal ordering of everyday behavior, autoregressively predicting in a semantically abstract latent space rather than at precise joint-configuration level. This avoids the heuristic augmentation and masking hyperparameters of prior self-supervised approaches. The work is relevant to human behavior modeling and action anticipation.

entry.title: Learning Word-Level Explanations of Text Reuse in Latin Literature with Little Annotation

author.name: Julian Schelb, Michael Wittweiler, Marie Revellio

entry.summary: The paper develops a method for explaining intertextual reuse in Latin literature at the word level, aligning each word of a reusing passage to its source and labeling the transformation operation. To avoid expensive annotation, synthetic pairs built from known operations train an initial model, and active learning selects pairs for expert correction.

entry.title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts

author.name: Daniel Reichenpfader (Institute for Patient-Centered Digital Health, Bern University of Applied Sciences, Bern, Switzerland, Faculty of Medicine, University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerland), Kwaku Appiagyei (F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG, Basel, Switzerland), Manovah Nadarajah (Kantonsspital Aarau, Aarau, Switzerland), Ahmed Reda Bahr (University of Alexandria, Alexandria, Egypt), Irina Filchenko (Department of Neurology, Inselspital, Bern University Hospital and University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland), Fabio Dennst\"adt (Data Semantics and Decision Making Institute, Department of Digital Medicine, Inselspital, Bern University Hospital and University of Bern, Bern, Switzerland)

entry.summary: The paper explores whether LLM agents can automatically derive a common data element (CDE) schema for sarcoma research from over 24,000 PubMed case report abstracts, proposing nearly 73,000 candidate CDEs consolidated down to 1,570. Human reviewers approved most retained CDEs for relevance, and the system attempted evidence-linked extraction across the full corpus with detailed agreement analysis.

entry.title: Where to Predict in Retinal OCT? Anatomy-Guided Target Selection for I-JEPA

author.name: Yunchu Feng, Wai Tak Lau, Kaveri A. Thakoor

entry.summary: The authors adapt the I-JEPA self-supervised framework to retinal OCT by replacing uniform target-region placement with anatomy-guided selection using image intensity and predicted retinal segmentation, while keeping the architecture unchanged. The goal is better representations of subtle anatomical variation with less labeled data.

entry.title: QCAP-VQA: Question-Conditioned Capped Prior-Mass Supervision for Medical Visual Question Answering

author.name: Yining Zhao, Catarina Moreira, Mukesh Prasad, Ali Braytee

entry.summary: QCAP-VQA supervises a subset of cross-attention heads in medical VQA models with a question-conditioned prior built from ranked segmentation proposals, using a capped prior-mass objective that penalizes insufficient attention inside the prior only below a threshold. Evaluation separates attention on the named anatomy from how attention shifts between questions, using structure boxes that play no role in training.

entry.title: See and Detect: Image-Driven Open-Vocabulary Multi-View 3D Object Detection

author.name: Yating Xu, Na Zhao, Chenhan Jiang, Qingwen Zhang, Jiankang Deng, Jifei Song

entry.summary: Presents an image-driven framework for open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D detection that uses multi-view images, rather than reconstructed point clouds, as primary evidence for generating 3D boxes and semantic labels. Discovering object candidates from individual images lets it detect objects missing from point clouds. This addresses localization and open-vocabulary weaknesses of point-cloud-driven pipelines.

entry.title: KnowVis: Dual-View Evaluation and Diagnosis of World-Knowledge Grounding in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Yonghang Yu, Ruoyu Wang, Haoyu Zhang, Lin Qi, Yawei Zhou, Changqian Yu

entry.summary: Introduces KnowVis, a benchmark for evaluating world-knowledge grounding in text-to-image models, covering prompts that require implicit facts, structured knowledge, and domain-specific commonsense beyond explicit visual descriptions. Built on a hierarchical knowledge taxonomy with case-level annotations, it combines two complementary evaluation views with a structured MLLM-based VQA judge for diagnosis. Fills a gap left by alignment-only evaluations.

entry.title: DIRT: Depth-completed Image-based Rendering using Two-band Blending for Live Novel-view Synthesis

author.name: Mathias Harrer, Laura Fink, Noah Lewis, Paul Himmler, Tim Weyrich

entry.summary: DIRT targets live novel-view synthesis from posed depth-sensor and image captures without per-scene optimization, using sparse point-based geometry whose depth buffer is completed in the target view screen-space with two-band blending. This addresses the latency and generalization gap that limits standard optimization-heavy NVS methods for live capture scenarios.

entry.title: Natural Swing-Up of an Underpowered Double Pendulum

author.name: Arne Sachtler, Manuel Keppler, Florian Loeffl, Alin Albu-Sch\"affer

entry.summary: The authors swing up a direct-drive two-link robot whose motors provide only about 6 percent of the shoulder gravity torque by riding its nonlinear normal modes, splitting torque into power-neutral steering and a scalar pumping input solved as a linear program under torque limits and a control-Lyapunov constraint. This demonstrates energy-efficient control that exploits rather than fights robot dynamics.

entry.title: PoliMop: Policy-in-the-Loop Motion Planning in 3D Spaces for Mobile Robots

author.name: Yael Fassbind, Valentin N. Hartmann, Huang Su, Yijiang Huang, Stelian Coros

entry.summary: PoliMop is a kinodynamic RRT planner that uses physics simulation of control-policy rollouts to expand the tree, allowing planning that respects the robot's actual locomotion capabilities in complex 3D environments. Sampling is guided by a preplanned mass-point path to focus exploration on promising regions.

entry.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem

author.name: Jia Shen, Junhyoung Ha, Yue Chen

entry.summary: This work proposes a friction model for continuum robots based on complementarity constraints under Coulomb friction assumptions, capturing static friction, sliding friction, hysteresis, and environment-induced deformation. Existing approaches only model internal friction bounded by the Coulomb cone, missing these environmental interaction effects.

entry.title: Aligned, Conflicting, or Unspecified? A Diagnostic Benchmark for Multimodal Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xintong Wang, Haihan Nan, Ruidong Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces the first real-world diagnostic benchmark for multimodal time series forecasting, with 1,762 text-window pairs across weather, web traffic, and finance, each labeled by whether text aligns with, conflicts with, or is unspecified relative to sensed history. It evaluates ten pretrained models zero-shot on text selection and combination under these relationships. The benchmark reveals how unreliably models use text that contradicts sensor data.

entry.title: Adversarially Attacking Symbolic Vocabulary Vulnerabilities In LLM Planners

author.name: Stephen Obadinma, Xiaodan Zhu

entry.summary: This paper uses an adversarial attack framework to probe whether reasoning-model improvements in LLM planning persist when commonsense cues in symbolic planning vocabularies are obfuscated, testing joint symbolic interpretation and planning robustness. It reveals that despite recent reasoning model gains, LLM agents remain unreliable relative to symbolic planners under vocabulary obfuscation. This is a useful robustness check on claims about LLM planning competence.

entry.title: OutfitterBench: Evaluating LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Resource Allocation and Commitment Coordination

author.name: Jie Huang, Yuecheng Hong, Yao Chen, Shengding Jiao, Xudong Liu, Qiang Ye

entry.summary: OutfitterBench evaluates LLM agents on commitment feasibility and opportunity-cost-aware resource allocation, simulating 200 days of managing an equipment-rental business with roughly 1,100 reservation requests and a 46-product catalog. It highlights a neglected capability — keeping one's own commitments feasible while reassessing allocations as opportunities change — beyond existing continuing-operation benchmarks. This probes a core skill for real-world long-horizon agents.

entry.title: T2ST: Data-Efficient Spatio-Temporal Foundation Models via Temporal Data and Knowledge Transfer

author.name: Yue Xu, Kaiyun Wei, Wenying Duan, Zichen Xu, Shuai Ma, Xiaoxi He

entry.summary: T2ST is a data-efficient training framework that augments scarce spatio-temporal observations with abundant auxiliary time series and transfers knowledge from a frozen time-series foundation model, motivated by the insight that temporal pattern learning can benefit from pure temporal data. This reduces the costly curation burden for spatio-temporal foundation models. It targets climate, traffic, and related forecasting domains.

entry.title: ERGo: Energy-Efficient Hybrid Graph Neural Network Training on Processing-In-Memory Architectures

author.name: Pratyush Dhingra, Chibuike E. Ugwu, Janardhan Rao Doppa, Partha Pratim Pande

entry.summary: Proposes ERGo, a hybrid training framework for GNNs on processing-in-memory architectures that automatically switches from a full-parameter phase to a parameter-efficient phase using low-rank weight representations, reducing off-chip memory access with negligible accuracy loss. This addresses the energy and performance costs of off-chip access in PIM-based GNN training.

entry.title: Quantum Graph Neural Networks: Architectures, Trainability, and Applications

author.name: Zeinab Sharifi, Hossein Shirazi

entry.summary: This survey systematizes quantum graph neural networks with a unified formalism (encoder, graph-conditioned circuit, observables, classical head), a permutation-equivariance condition at the circuit level, and a resource model for cost comparison. It organizes the literature into five architecture families and critically assesses the evidence behind scalability and expressivity claims since 2019. It provides a needed critical map of a hype-prone field.

entry.title: NeoResearch: Literature- and Experience-Guided Autonomous Time Series Model Discovery

author.name: Ze Guo, Mingyue Cheng, Xiaoyu Tao, Shuo Yu, Shangtong Ye

entry.summary: NeoResearch uses LLMs as autonomous researchers to discover lightweight, domain-specific time-series forecasting models, coupling hypothesis-driven architecture exploration with iterative training and validation in a dual-loop workflow. The framework aims to translate web-scale literature knowledge and research experience into applicable model designs.

entry.title: Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC

author.name: Syed Haider Ali, Nouhaila Innan, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: The Manifold Helical-IN is an Interaction Network architecture for particle track reconstruction that embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold with curvature-aware features, unrolling tightly curled trajectories of low-momentum particles. This geometric projection improves discrimination of true tracks from combinatorial noise on the TrackML challenge dataset, targeting HL-LHC occupancy scales.

entry.title: Efficient Genotype Classification from 3D MRI in ADPKD via Density-Aware Point Sampling and E(3)-invariance

author.name: Kwanghee Lee, Hyeongsub Lee, Youngwoo Kim, Hyunji Jeong

entry.summary: The paper presents a method for inferring ADPKD genetic mutations (notably truncating PKD1) from abdominal 3D MRI as a low-cost complement to genetic testing, using density-aware point sampling to handle large abdominal volumes and E(3)-invariant networks to exploit kidney geometry. This addresses both the scale of abdominal MRI and the scarcity of labeled genotype data.

entry.title: A systematic comparison of physics-informed neural networks and mechanistic models for epidemic modeling and forecasting

author.name: Martina Rama, Yuhan Li, Bruno Lepri, Nicola Perra, Michele Tizzoni

entry.summary: This study systematically compares a PINN-based epidemic framework against a stochastic mechanistic model sharing the same age-structured SEIRD core and forecasting pipeline, in synthetic scenarios and London's first COVID-19 wave. Interestingly, PINNs underperform on synthetic scenarios yet achieve comparable or better results on real data, offering a nuanced picture of when physics-informed learning pays off.

entry.title: Stage-wise Lineage-aware Dropout for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yan Xing, Zhi Chen, Fanglue Zhang, Junhong Zhao, Bing Xue, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces a lineage-family concept for 3D Gaussian Splatting primitives, grouping Gaussians descended from the same founder, and drops whole families rather than individuals to counteract neighbor compensation during regularization. Applied to sparse-view 3DGS, this stage-wise lineage-aware dropout reduces overfitting from limited training views.

entry.title: nnAEU: a Simple and Efficient CNN-Autoencoder for Hyperspectral Unmixing

author.name: Edgard Dabier, Christophe Kervazo, Pietro Gori, Florence Tupin

entry.summary: Derives a lightweight CNN autoencoder for hyperspectral unmixing by pruning the Mamba component entirely from UNMamba, a recent state-of-the-art model. The resulting model uses over ten times fewer parameters while outperforming UNMamba and other transformer- and GAN-based methods in accuracy. Includes complete reproducible code and challenges the trend of increasing architectural complexity in HSU.

entry.title: When Does Cross-View Consistency Matter in Multi-View Appearance Augmentation? A Controlled Study for Visuomotor Policies

author.name: Zixuan Jiang

entry.summary: Using simulation-state replay to control cross-view coupling while holding perturbation distributions and action labels fixed, this controlled study shows that inconsistent global appearance, ghost injection, and color changes barely hurt late-fusion Diffusion Policy success across seven LIBERO tasks. In contrast, geometrically anti-coupled views reduce success by about 3.3 percentage points, delineating which consistency actually matters.

entry.title: Alignment 'train/test splits' should be sacred

author.name: draganover

entry.summary: Argues that alignment techniques must be partitioned into those used for training and those reserved exclusively for evaluation, mirroring the sacred train/test split in machine learning. Training against all misalignment detectors risks producing covert misalignment invisible to users, the same failure mode as overfitting to validation data.

entry.title: Can Agents Keep Up with Time? An Empirical Analysis of Temporal Adaptation After a Conversational Hiatus

author.name: Hongguan Su, Ming Wang, Shun Zhang, Yifan Wang, Rong Yin, Zhiming Ma, Mengzheng Yang, Peng Chen

entry.summary: This empirical study examines whether long-horizon personal-assistant agents perceive the passage of time during conversational hiatuses and adapt advice accordingly, a capability the authors call temporal state perception and use. Existing evaluations focus on fact retention and explicit state updates, leaving temporal awareness unexamined. The finding that agents may give stale advice after stale bookings pass is an important, previously unmeasured failure mode.

entry.title: Smart Home Agents Make Capable but Unpredictable Grid Operators

author.name: Christopher Terrazas, Eduardo Cotilla-Sanchez

entry.summary: The authors conduct the first resilience analysis of smart home agents across a full power outage, using outage simulations in a live environment to measure behavior before, during, and after failures. They show agents can act as grid operators but identify several new failure categories, highlighting unpredictability where cascading grid-edge failures matter.

entry.title: WETW: Learning Pair-Specific Weighted Euclidean Distances for Efficient DTW Search

author.name: Christos Panourgias, Qitong Wang, George Tzagkarakis, Themis Palpanas

entry.summary: Observes that once aligned, DTW over long time series reduces to a Euclidean distance over pair-specific coordinates, and proposes WETW, a learned distance that adapts fixed-length embedding comparisons to each pair via a small symmetric module. Targets efficient similarity search over large collections of long time series.

entry.title: Towards Seconds-level Video Representation: Quadratically Gated Feature Grid with Adaptive, Prediction-free Sampling

author.name: Tie-Yun Li, Hao-Ran Wang, Chao Wang, Zhiyong Yin, Yiming Xu, Zhenwei Cai, Li Li, Rongzhi Lin, Feng-Lei Fan

entry.summary: Q-GAS is a coordinate-queryable implicit video representation combining multi-resolution explicit 3D feature grids with a compact SwiGLU-style quadratic-gating decoder and an error-aware, prediction-free sampler to reach seconds-level fitting times. The design avoids hash-collision coefficient sharing and improves nonlinear feature response via low-rank second-order interactions. It addresses the chronic slowness of implicit neural video representations, a practical blocker for industrial use.

entry.title: Protection-Oriented Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in Power Systems

author.name: Julian Oelhaf, Georg Kordowich, Changhun Kim, Christian Bergler, Andreas Maier, Johann J\"ager, Siming Bayer

entry.summary: The authors provide a protection-oriented evaluation of three ML fault detectors (gradient-boosted trees, CNN, logistic regression) against a sequence-current baseline on PROTECT-90, a dataset of 9,022 simulated fault episodes on a 90 kV line. The assessment uses window conditions, causal labeling, episode-grouped cross-validation, and operating-point selection under a security budget, reporting security, dependability, and timing rather than just AUC. This promotes safety-aware evaluation standards for ML in critical infrastructure.

entry.title: When Copying Is Hard to Beat: A Negative Result in Clinical Assessment Forecasting

author.name: Marius Fracarolli, Stefan Riezler

entry.summary: This paper reports that models forecasting next-day clinical assessment items on ICU data show no consistent advantage over simple persistence baselines that copy previous questionnaire answers. Careful patient-disjoint evaluation across 29,715 ICU day-pairs reveals that apparent gains shrink or disappear under stricter scoring conditions.

entry.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling

author.name: Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: The authors study Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes driven by finite-speed Kac processes rather than Brownian motion, deriving explicit Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation solutions via Legendre polynomials and analyzing the processes through piecewise-deterministic Markov process tools. The framework is positioned as a foundation for generative modeling where finite-speed transport may offer advantages over diffusion.

entry.title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Andrea Marelli, Alessandro Ardenghi, Giacomo Boracchi, Luca Magri

entry.summary: Proposes MemCAM, a weakly supervised video semantic segmentation transformer that learns temporally consistent masks from video-level labels by supervising internal cross-attention memory rather than relying on external optical-flow priors. The paper shows that naively training temporal cross-attention under weak supervision is unstable and can fall below single-frame baselines. Avoids noisy, expensive, non-semantic flow cues.

entry.title: TetraCoder: Adaptive Tetrahedral Encoding for Neural Fields

author.name: Daniele Della Pietra, Antonella Rech, Nicola Conci, Nicola Garau

entry.summary: TetraCoder provides a hash-free adaptive tetrahedral encoding linking explicit tetrahedral spatial structure to an implicit signed distance field, yielding a continuous piecewise-affine hybrid space with exact correspondence between implicit SDF and explicit mesh. This eases conversions between explicit surface sampling and implicit spatial queries.

entry.title: What Futures Do AI Models Want? An Exploratory Character Evaluation of AI for AI Strategy

author.name: Hans Gundlach

entry.summary: Develops an exploratory character evaluation probing what long-term futures AI models themselves prefer, covering questions like digital mind proliferation, racing versus pausing AGI, and loss of human control. Motivated by the observation that models can influence pivotal decisions through advice and recommendations even without full delegation.

entry.title: Tabular Population Priors as Structured Retrieval for EHR Medication Set Prediction

author.name: Animesh Agarwal, Meysam Ghaffari, Nina Fatehi, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: The paper argues that clinical RAG for medication prediction from EHRs retrieves the wrong object (similar patient records) when the target is a discrete medication label set. It proposes a tabular population prior built from condition-medication co-occurrence statistics as a more task-aligned retrieval object. Swapping only the retriever in the PACERAG pipeline improves F1 from 0.303 to 0.338.

entry.title: OCTAVE: A Capability-Resolved Benchmark for End-to-End HTML5 Game Generation

author.name: Kehang Li, Xinlan Xu, Yulin Jin, Heng Cao, Xuchen Li, Houxian Ren, Zihao Ji, Qiang Luo, Yadong Mao, Qilin He, Jian Zhang, Jian Zhao, Zihao Wang

entry.summary: OCTAVE is a benchmark for complete HTML5 game generation organized around eight capability dimensions with 180 tasks and 1,800 evaluation requirements drawn from player requests, commercial mechanics, and expert design. It distinguishes completeness from richness of implementation and supports static source-code requirement-level diagnosis across PC, mobile, 2D, and 3D settings. The design aims to expose which capabilities agents implement rather than a single aggregate score.

entry.title: G-CAST: Governed Continual Self-Training for E-Commerce Agents under Evolving Demands

author.name: Yuechun Yu, Wenzheng Kong, Xiaofeng Mao, Jin Zhang

entry.summary: G-CAST addresses continual adaptation of LLM-powered e-commerce shopping agents facing demand drift and evolution of the execution harness (tools, skills, procedures), proposing a governed self-training approach that adopts new capabilities without losing established behavior. It targets a real production problem where models trained once fall behind changing user needs. The dual challenge framing is practically grounded.

entry.title: Toward Interference-Agnostic RF Source Separation

author.name: Maxence Albert, Rapha\"el Duroselle, Thibaud Ehret, Olivier Boeffard, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Bonastre

entry.summary: This work shows that specialized RF source separators trained on one interference type fail badly on unseen interference, often performing worse than no processing. The authors train a single interference-agnostic separator over all interference pairs on two disjoint architectures, a convolutional WaveNet and a band-split transformer, without test-time labels.

entry.title: Dancing Tokens on the Vocabulary Network from LLM Generation

author.name: Yuan-Chao Hu

entry.summary: The author builds token-embedding similarity networks for six open LLMs and maps generations onto them, finding the networks scale-free and heavy-tailed but more fragmented than matched random embeddings, with distillation barely changing topology. Consecutive generated tokens are rarely graph neighbors, no more than in shuffled order, suggesting generation is not a walk on the embedding network and probing LLM explainability.

entry.title: Typing Matters: Muscle, Language and Typing Behaviour in Live Keystroke Decoding from sEMG

author.name: Abhilash Durgam, Nyle Siddiqui, Mubarak Shah, Qiushi Fu

entry.summary: Argues that wrist sEMG keystroke decoding should be framed as a live, context-dependent problem shaped jointly by muscle signals, language, and typing behaviors like typos and backspaces, rather than offline windowed signal inference. The paper identifies shortcomings of fixed-window systems that discard session context and lack linguistic modeling.

entry.title: Adversarial Tracking: Attacks on Image Sensors for Object Tracking in Autonomous Vehicles

author.name: Han Wu, Alex Chan, Ekin Can Erkus, Tousif Rahman, Rishad Shafik

entry.summary: Evaluates image-specific and image-agnostic adversarial attacks on YOLOv3/YOLOv4 detectors paired with SORT, Deep SORT, Strong SORT, and OC-SORT trackers in the CARLA simulator, measuring impact on downstream trajectory estimation via MOTA-style metrics. Characterizes how detection perturbations propagate through tracking-by-detection pipelines.

entry.title: Imitation Policies Learn a Proprioceptive Anchor: A Predictive Law for Perception Noise and Its Closed Loop Cost

author.name: Christopher Malili

entry.summary: The paper shows that imitation policies trained on noisy object positions learn to combine the noisy reading with an implicit proprioceptive anchor derived from the robot's own state, weighting it by an analytically characterized factor. A single measured quantity predicts held-out sensitivities across robomimic tasks, outperforming classical errors-in-variables regression. This provides a predictive law for how perception noise affects closed-loop robot imitation policies.

entry.title: SceneAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Portable Game Scene Generation

author.name: Xingyi Li, Jiahao Yang, Yiqin Zhu, Jingwen Ye, Yang Sun, Weidong Zhang

entry.summary: SceneAgent is a multi-agent framework for game scene generation that makes the construction process portable across game engines via a canonical SceneContext state and backend adapters isolating conventions, asset bindings, and export. It distills human-approved construction traces into reusable Layout and Content skills and introduces the GameScene benchmark. The key contribution is process-level reuse rather than just exporting final outputs.

entry.title: RACE: Ranking-Uncertainty Aware Capacity-Adaptive Customization for Efficient Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Tianqi Liu, Kaipu Sun, Kairui Fu, Wenkai Wang, Sihao Liu, Hui Zang, Ran Chen, Tao Wang, Shengyu Zhang

entry.summary: RACE is a framework for efficient sequential recommendation that dynamically adapts both model structure and input sequence length per instance based on ranking uncertainty, replacing uniform compression ratios that waste compute on simple queries or under-serve complex ones. It addresses a capacity-complexity mismatch in resource-constrained recommendation deployment. This is applied industrial ML research.

entry.title: LightTAR: Light and Fast Target-Aware Representations for Multimodal Tabular Learning

author.name: Eilam Shapira, Alan Arazi, Shoham Grunblat, Roi Reichart

entry.summary: LightTAR improves multimodal tabular learning by augmenting PCA-reduced encoder embeddings with target-aware features extracted via regularized partial least squares from final and intermediate encoder layers. This aligns dimensionality reduction with the prediction target rather than input variance. It was evaluated across 21 tabular tasks, suggesting broad applicability.

entry.title: RiverScan: Learning to Accumulate on River Networks

author.name: He Zhu, Zhiyi Gao, Youhuan Yang, Han Quan, Ming Li

entry.summary: RiverScan introduces a spatial operator for runoff prediction that uses river-network connectivity, combining local temporal representations with accumulated upstream states via area-weighted selective state-space recurrence processed in topological order. Learned retention and contributing-area fractions let the model handle subcatchments of different sizes.

entry.title: Emulating physics-based XCO2 retrievals across OCO-2 viewing modes with compact neural networks

author.name: Xianlei San, Chengxing Zhai, Hui Su, Kuai Dai, Shuangchen Du

entry.summary: The paper uses SVD-compressed OCO-2 satellite spectra feeding compact MLPs to emulate computationally expensive full-physics CO2 column retrievals, predicting corrections to operational priors. Trained on 2015-2019 data and validated on held-out years through 2025, the models achieve low errors relative to the reference retrieval product across viewing modes.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Continual Learning for 2D XRD Interpretation Using Simulated and Experimental Data

author.name: Zihan Wang, Hyun Sang Park, Ali Rachidi, David Elbert, Todd C. Hufnagel, Wei Chen

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept framework enables continual interpretation of 2D X-ray diffraction data for autonomous experimentation, combining MMD-based domain adaptation to close simulation-to-experiment gaps with a CNN-SNGP model for calibrated uncertainty, addressing overconfidence on unfamiliar inputs and catastrophic forgetting during sequential updates.

entry.title: Efficient and Practical Clustering of Variables in Causal Graphs

author.name: Otto Tabell, Jani Nyk\"anen, Santtu Tikka, Juha Karvanen

entry.summary: This paper introduces a new class of clusters called conduits in causal graphs and presents a sound, complete, and efficient algorithm to detect all of them. Clustering variables into conduits can substantially reduce graph size for visualization and enable known identifiability results, as demonstrated in simulation studies with real-world graphs.

entry.title: LaMe: a Joint Latent Mediation Framework for High-Dimensional Systems

author.name: Ga\"el Poux-M\'edard, Kaniav Kamary, Yohann De Castro, Vivian Viallon

entry.summary: LaMe is a joint linear-Gaussian framework for mediation analysis in high-dimensional settings, summarizing exposure-mediator-outcome systems through a small number of latent variables to overcome overparameterization, bias, and scalability limits of existing latent mediation methods. The framework identifies natural direct and indirect effects under explicit structural assumptions.

entry.title: Bregman geometry in regular exponential families: dual representations and relative smoothness

author.name: Mame Diarra Fall, \'Eric Barat, Nicolas Dobigeon

entry.summary: This work systematically develops the Bregman-geometric structure of regular exponential families with respect to expectation parametrization, establishing equivalent dual Bregman representations with normalization and uniqueness results. It also derives relative smoothness and convexity properties, connecting statistics, convex analysis, and information geometry. The results provide geometric tools likely useful for optimization and sampling on statistical manifolds.

entry.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory

author.name: Mojtaba Soltanalian

entry.summary: This single-author theory paper formalizes how finite representations can succeed in unbounded environments by introducing future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value across tasks. It shows under compactness assumptions that any retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on a joint decision-regret state that preserves task regrets without increasing information. The result yields an information-regret framework for understanding generalization.

entry.title: RAG-FGO: Dynamic Optimization of Query-Rewriting Agents for Generative RAG

author.name: Qigan Sun, Xudong Wang, Chaoning Zhang, Chenghao Li, Jiaquan Zhang, Jiehui Xie, Sungyoung Lee, Jie Zou, Ning Xie, Peng Wang, Yang Yang, Heng Tao Shen

entry.summary: RAG-FGO is a framework that dynamically optimizes query-rewriting agents for generative retrieval by formulating rewriting as a black-box optimization problem over mixed discrete prompt templates and continuous decoding parameters, using feedback to handle noisy retrieval signals. It targets three deployment challenges: retrieval feedback noise, joint discrete-continuous optimization, and poor generalization of static rewriting strategies. This improves real-world RAG system performance.

entry.title: In the Eye of the Beholder: Human Label Variation in Textual and Visual Entailment

author.name: Monica Riedler, Jasmin Orth, Raffaella Bernardi, Barbara Plank

entry.summary: The paper introduces VariNLI-VE, a dataset for studying how human label variation differs between paired natural language inference and visual entailment instances, re-annotating originally neutral SNLI items and their visual counterparts with the same annotators providing labels, confidence scores, and explanations. This paired design isolates the effect of swapping a textual premise for an image on annotator disagreement. It extends the growing human-label-variation literature into multimodal entailment.

entry.title: A Multi-Layered AI Pipeline for BPMN Generation from Natural Language

author.name: Alexandru Rancea, Ionut Anghel, Tudor Cioara, Ovidiu Anchidin, Ancuta Nemes

entry.summary: The paper presents a pipeline that converts natural-language process descriptions into BPMN diagrams by combining fine-tuned RoBERTa entity extraction, LLMs, control-flow relation extraction, ontology population, and structural validation. It targets the persistent challenge of linguistic ambiguity and non-adjacent control-flow dependencies in business process modeling.

entry.title: MamaReason: Unfinished Reasoning and Answer Recovery in Clinical Language Models

author.name: Thanni Adewuyi, Adepoju Jeremiah Moyondafoluwa, Dorcas Amapu, Dieko Whenu, Sylvia Essessien, Sandra Oko-Oba, Pelumi Onafadeji, Lily Aimas-Love, Samuel Omolaiye, Abiodun Adereni

entry.summary: This study examines whether failed clinical reasoning passes in a fine-tuned Gemma-based maternal-health model already contain an implicit diagnosis that simple answer continuation would recover. An explicit-commitment extractor identifies diagnoses in most failed RL and SFT passes, and reading those commitments without extra generation recovers a large fraction of pairs restored by continuation. The work also includes recurrence controls and a second-commitment trigger analysis.

entry.title: Evaluating Human Sensitivity to Gender Biased AI-Generated Content through Human Assessment of Google's Autocomplete Function

author.name: Tamara Serrano, Nikoleta Pantelidou, Raquel Montero, Natalia Moskvina, Paolo Morosi, Evelina Leivada

entry.summary: This human-subjects study tested whether telling Spanish-speaking participants that some gender-biased statements were AI-generated (sourced from Google autocomplete) changed their reaction times or agreement judgments. AI attribution had no effect on either measure, suggesting AI-generated content may be evaluated with less skepticism rather than more.

entry.title: RecurIR: Learning When and How to Revise Restoration Policies via Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Hu Gao, Haoran Zhang, Yulong Chen, Lizhuang Ma

entry.summary: Proposes RecurIR, a recursive self-improvement framework for agent-based image restoration that learns when existing restoration strategies become invalid and how to revise decision rules as degradation severity, coverage, or interactions change. It goes beyond accumulating past successes and failures by explicitly modeling the conditions under which learned policies apply. Targets heterogeneous, coupled degradations.

entry.title: Lens: Training-Free Semantic Search for Cross-Tile Object and Scene Retrieval in Satellite Imagery

author.name: Ata Akbari Asanjan, Anit Upadhyaya, Jeremy Kravitz, Subash Yeggina

entry.summary: Presents Lens, a training-free system for semantic search across large satellite mosaics using frozen DINOv3 features. It removes positional bias by projecting dense features onto the subspace orthogonal to a positional basis estimated from a constant image, centers debiased features, and matches neighborhood- or tile-level query embeddings by cosine similarity. Enables object and scene retrieval without training a detector for the class of interest.

entry.title: Do Underwater Image Quality Metrics Agree with Human Perception? A Benchmark with Human Choices, Simple Edits and Generative Drift

author.name: Rishii Kumar Singh, Abhinav Rajput, Dinesh Kumar Vishwakarma

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates 73 handcrafted, learned, vision-language, and general-purpose no-reference quality metrics against human preferences on underwater image enhancement, using published opinion-score sets plus a new paired-comparison study. It probes whether simple edits and adversarial perturbations can inflate metric scores above human-preferred enhancements, exposing reliability gaps in metric-based evaluation.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models as Spatial Priors for Object-Goal Navigation

author.name: Jun Miura

entry.summary: This paper evaluates whether open-weight LLMs can provide explicit spatial priors for object-goal navigation by eliciting distributions over target object positions in a room. Testing on CubiCasa5K and ScanNet layouts, it finds models capture object frequencies and room size patterns but fail to reproduce wall-proximity differences across room types.

entry.title: Toward Resilient Self-Driving Laboratories through Telerobotic Interventions

author.name: Ziheng Wu, Adrian Vecina Tercero, Andre A. Fatehi, Abhik Sarkar, Brian Giera, Eric B. Duoss, Christopher M. Spadaccini, Nikhil Deshpande, Aldair E. Gongora

entry.summary: This work addresses fault recovery in self-driving laboratories by developing a teleoperation interface that lets human operators intervene and resolve disruptions during automated experiments. The system provides precise control of a six-DOF UR3e arm via a 3D mouse, and the authors evaluate intervention effectiveness across two experimental setups, arguing that human-in-the-loop teleoperation is key to SDL resilience.

entry.title: Disturbance-Aware Informative Planning in Spatiotemporal Environments

author.name: Kaleb Ben Naveed, Haejoon Lee, Anouck Girard, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-stage informative planning approach for persistent monitoring that accounts for spatially varying external disturbances without estimating them everywhere. It focuses disturbance estimation on regions relevant to monitoring trajectories, improving information gain predictions during execution.

entry.title: Generated Evaluation Suites as Diversity-Driven Search for Real Agent Regressions

author.name: Pulkit Yadav

entry.summary: The paper reframes generated evaluation suites as archives from diversity-driven search and derives a coverage ceiling: a defect whose trace footprint contains b passing scenarios can contribute at most b/N to a suite of size N. Injecting 7 controlled defects into a tau-squared-bench agent, it shows that for most traceable defects the ceiling falls below the detection threshold, explaining why aggregate pass rates miss regressions. The analysis motivates footprint-aware evaluation design.

entry.title: DECODE: Diagnosing Interpretability Failures in Automated Interpretation Process

author.name: Dohyun Kim, Jaeung Lee, Donghee Hong, Jaemin Jo

entry.summary: DECODE is a visual analytics system that reintroduces human oversight into LLM-driven mechanistic interpretability pipelines, where LLMs both generate and evaluate explanations with minimal human validation. It helps attribute interpretation failures to the extracted representations versus the LLM used in the process. This addresses a genuine reliability gap in increasingly automated interpretability research.

entry.title: Active Learning of Temporal Specifications through Distinguishing Queries

author.name: Rajarshi Roy, Xiaowei Huang

entry.summary: The paper presents an active-learning framework for LTLf specification learning in which the teacher only labels traces and answers natural-language questions, avoiding equivalence queries and SAT-based restarts. The learner maintains an enumerated version space of candidate formulas and generates distinguishing traces. This makes formal specification mining more practical for verification and monitoring, potentially bridging natural language and temporal logic.

entry.title: AI for Parameter Selection in Sample-based Quantum Diagonalization

author.name: Doriela Grabocka, Dimitrios Christofidellis, Federico Zipoli, Anna van Elst, Patrick Ruch, Antonio Foncubierta-Rodr\'iguez, Siddhartha Mishra, Matteo Manica

entry.summary: The paper explores whether learned oracle models can predict quantum runtime and approximation error for sample-based quantum diagonalization (SQD) methods directly from a Hamiltonian and candidate configuration, using synthetic Hamiltonians with controllable spectral properties. The models map Hamiltonians to best-ranked configurations for the SKQD algorithm, validated against classical counterparts. This comes from an IBM-affiliated team working at the AI-quantum interface.

entry.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration

author.name: Ivana Ragusa, Lorenzo Guiducci, Filippo Cavallo

entry.summary: A structured scoping review of AI-enabled remote patient monitoring evolving toward agentic systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action in domestic and clinical settings. The review finds mature agentic care has not yet emerged — most systems remain human-led — and uses healthcare robotics to surface embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance challenges.

entry.title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture

author.name: Han Zhang, Mehrisadat Makki Alamdari, Babak Shahbodagh, Mohammad Vahab, Cosmin Anitescu, Timon Rabczuk, Elena Atroshchenko

entry.summary: This work presents a mesh-free deep energy method using multiresolution neural representations to simulate thermally driven brittle fracture, predicting spontaneous crack nucleation, spacing, and crack arrest without pre-placed defects. Separate networks represent displacement, phase-field, and transient temperature with variational energy functionals. It advances neural PDE solvers for challenging multiscale physical simulation.

entry.title: Enrichment-Oriented Virtual Screening of Perovskite Solar Cells through Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yezeyuan Zheng, Ziyang Hu, Maojun Sun. Ruijian Han, Jian Huang, Guanhua Chen, Jie Liu

entry.summary: The authors cast perovskite solar cell recipe generation as enrichment-oriented virtual screening, using a frozen TabPFN surrogate to guide reinforcement-learning policies toward high-performing experimental neighborhoods. Five-fold evaluation on 1,846 measured devices shows top-ten selection raises mean power conversion efficiency from 19.68 to 23.74 percent.

entry.title: Performance-Portable Exact Gaussian Process Regression in Python via SYCL and oneMath

author.name: Alexander Strack, Marcel Graf, Alexander Van Craen, Dirk Pfl\"uger

entry.summary: GPRat is an open-source Python library for exact Gaussian process regression built on the HPX asynchronous many-task runtime, extended here with a hybrid HPX/SYCL oneMath backend supporting AMD and Intel GPUs. The SYCL backend comes within 3% of native CUDA on an NVIDIA A30 and outperforms GPflow and GPyTorch by up to roughly 1.75-2.17x and 1.79-4.62x on A30 and MI210 hardware respectively.

entry.title: Beyond Bot Labels: Retrospective Consequence-Grounded Ranking of Attributed Cache Harm in E-Commerce Logs

author.name: Jisoo Kim, Youngwoo Seo, Seonghoon Jeong

entry.summary: The paper reframes bot detection for e-commerce web caches: instead of classifying sessions as bots from UA strings or behavior, it ranks sessions by the actual eviction damage they cause to other shoppers via a chronological replay that attributes cache misses to culprit sessions. A behavioral model predicts harm from session behavior alone, and flagged sessions bypass the cache while remaining origin-served.

entry.title: Vessel2Brain: Edge-Aware Multi-Scale Flow Matching for 3D Brain Image Generation from Vessel Masks

author.name: Zhi Chen, Tianyang Zhang, Theodoros N. Arvanitis, Le Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Vessel2Brain, an edge-aware multi-scale conditional flow matching framework that synthesizes full 3D brain MRI volumes conditioned only on sparse vascular label maps. Vascular structures provide strong anatomical cues but cover a tiny fraction of brain volume, making the task highly ill-posed. Applications include data augmentation, simulation, and downstream neuroimaging analysis.

entry.title: Pose-based Neural Clothing for Animated Characters

author.name: Julian N. Heidenreich, Vinicius C. Azevedo, Jakob Buhmann, Lento Manickathan, Arnold Moon, Paul Kanyuk, Amit H. Bermano, Jingwei Tang

entry.summary: This work extends data-driven neural clothing simulation to stylized, non-SMPL animated characters, addressing the gap where existing neural garment methods trained on realistic human models fail. A lightweight network enables real-time inference so artists can interactively pose characters with high-quality folds during animation.

entry.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks

author.name: Kenyu Ikeuchi, Tomoaki Ohtsuki, Michelle Cohn, Alyssa Weakley, Yui Ishihara, Joseph Hoang, Taishiro Kishimoto, Sarah Tomaszewski Farias, Jet M. J. Vonk, Chen-Nee Chuah

entry.summary: The paper performs a cross-linguistic, cross-task acoustic analysis for dementia detection across Spanish, Mandarin, English, and Japanese, combining conversational data with structured speech tasks. It applies statistical and clinician-guided interpretable methods rather than black-box models, examining how task type and language affect acoustic biomarkers of cognitive impairment. The work supports scalable and equitable multilingual screening.

entry.title: SWIFT: Sample-Wise Instance Fine-Tuning of Time-Series Foundation Models for Forecasting

author.name: Yang Chen, Feifan Tian, Cong Wang, Cheng Feng, Wenbin Li, Yang Gao

entry.summary: SWIFT proposes sample-wise instance fine-tuning of time series foundation models, replacing dataset-centric few-shot adaptation with per-instance adaptation using structural priors from the target series' own history, combining self-retrieval and a frequency-aware loss. This makes adaptation transparent to end users, removing the need for additional datasets. It addresses a real adoption barrier for forecasting foundation models.

entry.title: GraphScent: Calibrating Directional Relevance Signals for Bounded-Context Code Localization

author.name: Ramesh Arvind Naagarajan

entry.summary: Studies stateless code localization with frozen local models on single consumer GPUs, finding a systematic directional asymmetry: zero-temperature relevance scores on enclosing scopes and upstream callers reliably separate true structural neighbors from lexical distractors, while downstream scores do not. Evaluated on Gemma 4 models across 211 real Python issues in 86 repositories.

entry.title: DySENSE: Dynamic Spatiotemporal ENergy Synthesis and Emulation with Satellite Imagery

author.name: Kailai Sun, Zijie Gao, Mingyi He, Can Rong, Alok Prakash, Baoshen Guo, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: DySENSE is a multimodal generative framework that synthesizes city building-energy consumption aligned with satellite imagery, generating dynamic monthly energy data for future-city scenarios rather than only predicting for existing cities. It targets gaps in fine-grained aligned energy data relevant to net-zero and SDG goals. The work advances generative modeling for urban energy planning.

entry.title: MarathonTS: a benchmark of long synthetic time series from window assembly and long-series generators

author.name: Ilyas Varshavskiy, Sergey Shulgin, Shuhrat Khalilbekov, Bonu Boboeva, Azizjon Azimi

entry.summary: MarathonTS is the first open benchmark comparing window-assembly versus direct long-series generation for synthesizing time series much longer than training windows, evaluated on 9 hourly datasets with 83 fidelity metrics against three real references. It also assesses downstream utility of the generated long sequences under one unified protocol.

entry.title: Online Switching Control as Learning with Experts

author.name: Masataka Nakamura, Kaito Ito, Hideaki Ishii

entry.summary: The paper reduces online switching control of discrete-time nonlinear systems—sequentially selecting controllers from a finite set under unknown disturbances—to the experts problem with switching costs. Using counterfactual costs from historical data, the authors propose an adaptive Hedge-based algorithm with switching suppression and derive performance guarantees.

entry.title: RSSA: Robust Semantic and Spatial Aligner for Collaborative Perception

author.name: Zhihao Yang, Zhiyu Xiang, Peng Xu, Tianyu Pu, Kai Wang, Eryun Liu, Dongping Zhang, Yong Ding

entry.summary: Introduces RSSA, a plug-in module for V2X collaborative perception that replaces simple spatial warping with combined semantic and probabilistic spatial transformations for robust feature alignment. A Semantic Transformation block corrects channel-level inconsistencies based on relative pose, followed by a probabilistic spatial component that tolerates positional noise. Improves robustness of multi-agent feature fusion.

entry.title: SemRAG: Semantic-Guided Sentence-Level Retrieval-Augmented Sign Language Production

author.name: Xiao Liu, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Peishuo Liu, Bowen Guo, Kuizhuang Liu, Cong Wang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Proposes SemRAG, a retrieval-augmented sign language production method that retrieves sentence-level signing priors guided by semantics rather than gloss- or word-level dictionaries. This avoids costly annotations and better preserves continuous sentence-level rhythm and coordination when generating sign pose sequences from text. Targets semantic inaccuracies in long or complex sentences.

entry.title: Model Annealing: Data-Efficient Learning through Review and Consolidation

author.name: Ali Mohammadi Ruzbahani, Rezvan Abouzadeh

entry.summary: Model annealing divides training into episodes where the learning rate is raised and cooled, with each cooled state joining a memory of past selves that provides tempered prediction targets and adversarial 'dream' examples where student and memory disagree. The memory averages predictions rather than weights so inference incurs no extra cost. Results across CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet show data-efficient learning from small labeled datasets.

entry.title: Large Language Model-Empowered Intelligent Agent for Adaptive Fast-Charging Control of Lithium-Ion Batteries

author.name: Joey Chan, Haoyu Pan, Zhen Chen, ErShun Pan

entry.summary: The authors develop an LLM-based agent for closed-loop adaptive fast-charging control of lithium-ion batteries, where the agent interprets structured battery states and generates executable control policies that balance charging speed, energy throughput, degradation, and safety. This avoids the accurate models or task-specific policies required by conventional approaches.

entry.title: Superfluid: Local AI Server for Distributed LLM Inference

author.name: Prabod Rathnayaka, Isura Manchanayake, Srikandabala Kogul, Steve Siu, Fabian Waschkowski, Lukas Wesemann

entry.summary: Superfluid is an open-source LLM server for local inference addressing two scenarios: multiple agents sharing a locally served model alongside an interactive user, and small teams pooling several idle machines across vendors for distributed serving. It orchestrates runtimes like llama.cpp, MLX, and BaseRT through a single scheduler with interactive priority. The system targets privacy, cost, latency, and offline availability of LLM inference.

entry.title: PUMA-Former: Uncertainty-Aware Agentic Computation Offloading in MEO-LEO Satellite Networks With Incomplete Information

author.name: Yi Jing, Chunxiao Jiang, Jiawei Wang, Jiachen Sun
